01HHZZ8CiATCVr7v47tP: DME works in the UHF band, 962-1213 MHz, i.e. approximately 1000 MHz. The 252 channels are paired with VOR/ILS frequencies so that tuning the VHF nav box automatically selects the associated DME channel. 110 MHz is VOR/ILS, and 300 MHz and 600 MHz carry no aeronautical navigation service.
01MLDvhGEudCrhZL39vp: The constant speed drive holds the generator's input speed constant, which fixes the output FREQUENCY at 400 Hz. Voltage is a separate matter: it falls as load increases, so a voltage regulator is still required, controlling the field excitation current to hold the output at 115 V whatever the load.
01VM9GBAJEvuUdLJSYL5: Cabin humidity in a modern jet runs at about 5-15 percent, nowhere near the 50-60 percent claimed, and drinking plenty of water builds no 'resistance' that can be lost - so statements 1 and 4 are false. Thirst really does lag behind dehydration, and dehydration really does produce dizziness and fatigue, so 2 and 3 are the correct pair. Drink on a schedule rather than waiting to feel thirsty.
025uduFYum72OBSQEyc8: Spatial disorientation is a conflict between what the instruments say and what the vestibular and seat-of-the-pants senses say, and it only becomes dangerous when the pilot resolves that conflict in favour of the senses. A good instrument cross-check does not cause it, it is the cure.
02yuZDoSMN3e8xZcdgat: JAR-OPS 1.655 ties the audio selector panel to IFR operation: an operator shall not operate an aeroplane under IFR unless an audio selector panel accessible to each required flight crew member is fitted. It is not a VFR or passenger-carrying requirement, so the trigger is simply IFR.
03ELEPzbj7PWo1nq65PI: A difference of opinion means someone in the crew has information or a reading of the situation the others do not, so it is a safety resource. The CRM aim is to surface disagreement early and resolve it explicitly; a crew where nobody ever disagrees has usually stopped monitoring rather than achieved consensus.
03OyXQDbdtwlrl0xqbH7: Locked down means mechanically locked, not merely fully extended. Side stays or drag struts are folded slightly past their aligned position so that the air and ground loads act to hold the joint closed rather than to fold it - an overcentre lock. Reaching the end of the actuator travel or getting a green light is evidence of the lock, not the lock itself.
03Q8ZkggrAmDfDEMcSoR: Aircraft approach categories are set by VAT (1.3 x VSO at maximum certificated landing mass): A below 91 kt, B 91-120 kt, C 121-140 kt, D 141-165 kt, E 166-210 kt. 121-140 kt therefore falls in Category C, which drives the circling and approach minima applied to the aircraft.
03sJPEOPCg3InGqK6dCj: CS-25.107 sets two floors on VR: it may not be less than V1, and not less than 105% of VMCA. The V1 floor prevents rotation before the decision speed, and the VMCA margin guarantees directional control is available if an engine fails at rotation. The 1.05 multiplier attaches to VMCA, not to V1 - reading it the other way round is the usual trap.
04Swvku0Iu8YELBscSAS: Friction in the boundary layer backs the surface wind relative to the gradient wind in the northern hemisphere and slows it. Over the sea, where friction is light, the rule of thumb is back about 10 degrees and reduce speed to roughly 70-80%: 350 backed 10 degrees gives 340, and 24 kt reduced gives about 20 kt, so 340/20. Over land the effect is roughly double: back 30 degrees and halve the speed.
05FLTZYsycg746fGkldM: The subtropical jet (around 30 degrees latitude, near FL390) and the polar front jet (around 40-60 degrees, near FL300) are permanent features present all year, though both are stronger and displaced equatorward in winter. The arctic jet is essentially a winter feature, and the equatorial easterly jet only appears in the northern-hemisphere summer over southern Asia and Africa in connection with the monsoon.
05Xn9499Hp5NrOAXOHTS: The indifferent stage runs from sea level to about 3000 m (10 000 ft), where the fall in oxygen partial pressure is small enough that performance is essentially unaffected apart from night vision. Above that the compensatory stage begins, with rising pulse and breathing rate.
05dAqakpS4wZq0seVYrz: Organisational factors are the decisions the COMPANY makes: fuel policy and rostering both shape the pressures the crew flies under. A technical malfunction and the weather are not organisational; they are conditions the organisation must plan for.
05nDeG4OdTZhQdG9ayxd: The otoliths respond to the resultant of gravity and acceleration, and cannot tell one from the other. A forward acceleration tilts that resultant backwards, which the brain reads exactly as if the body had pitched up - the somatogravic illusion. On a night or IMC take-off it produces a powerful and dangerous urge to push the nose down.
05wEx55x7izyBBzKZDE8: JAR-OPS 1.770 Table 1 for unpressurised aeroplanes requires 10% of passengers to be supplied for the entire flight time after the first 30 minutes at cabin pressure altitudes above 10 000 ft but not exceeding 13 000 ft. Above 13 000 ft the requirement jumps to 100% of passengers, so the 10% band is exactly 10 000-13 000 ft.
06Sv1I5NeBbwi9O6D0er: A demand regulator delivers gas only when the wearer inhales, which is what makes the supply last; the 100% selection simply cuts out the dilution air so that pure oxygen is delivered on each breath instead of an altitude-scheduled mixture. It is selected for smoke as well as for hypoxia, but the flow remains demand-driven.
06V9D30L1SVicImWkvYI: JAR-OPS 1.775(a) is the trigger: a pressurised aeroplane may not be operated above a pressure altitude of 10 000 ft unless supplemental oxygen capable of storing and dispensing the required supplies is carried. The percentage of passengers to be supplied then varies with cabin altitude, but the 10 000 ft threshold is what makes the reserve mandatory in the first place.
06aWHm4Bg6leFig6VCFZ: A slat opens a slot ahead of the wing that ducts high-energy air from beneath onto the upper surface, re-energising the boundary layer and delaying separation to a much higher angle of attack - typically an extra 5-10 degrees of stalling angle. CLmax therefore rises without changing the basic aerofoil. Note that slats raise the critical (stalling) angle, whereas trailing-edge flaps normally lower it.
06h9gkmC9178d2bmsqRE: Time of useful consciousness at 35 000 ft is 30 to 60 seconds, and a RAPID decompression roughly halves even that because the pressure differential drives oxygen back out of the blood. That is why the drill is mask on first, before anything else.
07pytacnEzsSIFrp4lTO: ICAO Doc 4444 sets separate thresholds for what counts as a significant change in wind components on final approach: 10 kt for mean headwind, 2 kt for mean tailwind, and 5 kt for mean crosswind. The crosswind threshold is tighter than the headwind one because crosswind directly affects directional control and drift at touchdown.
07z536E3Be7h7KBk6iNL: Geostrophic wind is the theoretical wind that results when the pressure gradient force is exactly balanced by the Coriolis force. That balance is only possible with straight, parallel isobars and no friction, so the wind blows parallel to the isobars at constant speed. Curved isobars introduce centripetal acceleration and give the gradient wind instead; friction gives the surface wind.
089A9zyu43Ils6952zl5: Modern human factors thinking treats error as a normal by-product of how cognition works - the same mental shortcuts that make people fast and flexible also make them occasionally wrong. Errors therefore cannot be trained or willed away; the aim is a system that tolerates and traps them.
08Rza4qKTlzlAaoiXPkO: Range varies with the square root of transmitter power, so power varies with the square of range. Doubling the range from 10 NM to 20 NM therefore needs 2 squared = 4 times the power. The same rule explains why very large power increases buy only modest extra coverage.
09JOhEQrDGyZgtyHUhNC: The Rome Convention (1952) covers damage caused by foreign aircraft to third parties on the surface. Do not confuse it with the Warsaw Convention, which governs the carrier's liability to passengers and cargo, or the Tokyo Convention, which deals with offences committed on board aircraft.
09KvJV1X1Abmd6ttYZEk: After an act of unlawful interference the commander submits a report without delay to BOTH the designated local authority (the State where the event occurred) and the Authority of the State of the operator. Reporting to only one of the two leaves either the scene-of-event State or the regulator that oversees the operator uninformed.
09L1Hc1trPaCsW8ZlqMw: CS-25 requires the stall warning to begin far enough above the stall to allow recovery, and the margin is specified as 5 kt or 5% of CAS, whichever is the GREATER - so the percentage governs at high speed and the fixed 5 kt at low speed, which is where the absolute margin matters most.
0AYfGHoFCyJ6wYmOeZAl: Skip distance is the gap on the surface between the point where the ground wave dies out and the point where the first sky wave returns after refraction in the ionosphere - so it is measured from the transmitter to that first sky-wave arrival. Within it no signal is received at all, which is the dead space of HF communication.
0B7ryPmxklYysrPH4dyr: The commander must produce the aeroplane's documents to an authorised representative of an Authority within a reasonable time of being asked. The documents are carried precisely so that they can be inspected; there is no right of refusal, no fixed 48-hour delay, and no requirement to consult the operator first.
0C9hr7it37neN83Oa1RZ: Drift is 313 - 307 = 6 degrees right, so the wind must come from the left of the heading. Resolving the air vector (307T/230 kt) against the ground vector (313T/210 kt) gives a wind blowing towards about 081 degrees at 30 kt, i.e. a W/V of about 261/30. Note the aircraft has slowed from 230 kt to 210 kt, confirming a headwind component.
0CSeZi5tFuTkVZ3YDcKj: Exhaust gas temperature peaks at the chemically correct mixture, a fuel-to-air mass ratio of about 1:15, because that is where combustion is most complete and the least heat is carried away by unburnt fuel or excess air. Both richer and leaner settings reduce EGT, which is why leaning past peak is used to cool the engine.
0D8XXI2w0XCQ54qBbBNz: The FMC computes position by blending radio and inertial sources: DME-DME (or DME and VOR) fixing, GPS where fitted, and the IRS as the smooth continuous reference between updates. SATCOM is a communications system and contributes nothing to position.
0EGLH1bSrarzMn7wIWIu: A squall line is a non-frontal line of active thunderstorms and is one of the phenomena for which a SIGMET is mandatory, along with severe turbulence, severe icing, severe mountain wave, volcanic ash, and tropical cyclone. A SIGMET is a warning of en-route weather hazardous to aircraft; a TAF is a routine aerodrome forecast and is not the vehicle for hazard warnings.
0EYA09p3HkzgXZ8MF5l8: A thermocouple generates an electromotive force proportional to the temperature difference between its hot and cold junctions, so E = K x T with K depending on the metals used. The relationship being linear is what makes the output usable on a simple moving-coil instrument scaled directly in degrees.
0FIwqCGBWx7OxsznGY78: Internal leakage - past seals, within a pump or actuator - returns fluid to the low-pressure side of the system rather than losing it overboard, so the quantity stays the same and the system may still hold pressure. What changes is temperature: the work done in forcing fluid through the leak path appears as heat, so a rising fluid temperature is the symptom to look for.
0G0IwG5PW3BQdEPMSMhc: RVR is normally greater than the reported meteorological visibility because it is assessed against high-intensity runway lights, which remain visible through obscuration long after unlit dark objects have disappeared. RVR is reported in METAR/SPECI only (never TAF), is triggered when visibility or RVR falls below 1500 m, and is measured by transmissometers or forward-scatter meters; a ceilometer measures cloud base, not visibility.
0G1nkJJHEKVUI8WlQhwT: Cooling makes the body shiver and raises the metabolic rate, so oxygen demand goes UP at exactly the moment the crew member can least afford it, and tolerance to hypoxia falls rather than improves. The reduced-demand effect only appears in deep, deliberately induced hypothermia, not from a loss of cabin heating.
0G5GRRNcK6cthdNEDMM3: ICAO Annex 1 requires an ATPL(A) applicant to have completed at least 75 hours of instrument time, of which no more than 30 hours may be instrument ground time (simulator or FSTD). The cap exists so most of the instrument experience is gained in an actual aircraft rather than on the ground.
0G64jD9HktUpK3QrHnc7: The atmosphere is about 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen by volume, and those proportions stay constant to about 70 000 ft. What changes with altitude is the total PRESSURE, and therefore the partial pressure of oxygen, not the percentage.
0Gf8pmb4PTH6AL7OJcMg: The stem is the ICAO definition of airside: the movement area together with adjacent terrain and buildings to which access is controlled. Of the options given, the aeronautical part is the term for that controlled area. A terminal is only a building within it, and the manoeuvring area is narrower still, covering runways and taxiways but excluding aprons.
0IYXPW72B1iLJRz0CAmm: JAR-OPS 1.135 lists what must be preserved on the ground for each flight: a copy of the operational flight plan, copies of the relevant parts of the aeroplane technical log, route-specific NOTAM documentation if the operator issued it, mass and balance documentation if required, and special loads notification. Statements 2, 3, 4 and 5 match that list. The day's weather and the performance charts are used in preparation but are not on the retention list.
0IfTYBrAG8lYrzFAlLVY: Crash axes and crowbars scale with the maximum approved passenger seating configuration: one is required up to 200 seats, and two once the configuration exceeds 200. With 201 seats the aeroplane is just over the threshold, so two are required.
0K8rqxeMI5gGAKHtx1Bd: The altimeter is calibrated to the standard atmosphere, so it reads true altitude only when the real atmosphere matches it - correct sea-level pressure AND the standard temperature profile. Setting the right QNH removes the pressure error but not the temperature error, which is why cold weather leaves the aircraft lower than indicated.
0KchFWLwUsdP4XUvjUoZ: ICAO Doc 8168 sets maximum holding speeds by altitude band. At or below 14,000 ft the limit for jet aircraft is 230 kt IAS, and FL 110 falls within that band. The limit is expressed as indicated airspeed, not true airspeed, because the protected holding area is based on IAS.
0KdNKNzLkK3BJFugU9mg: On the ground the altimeter reads the height of the aircraft above whatever datum is set on the subscale. Setting 1013 when the actual QNH is 993 is 20 hPa too high, and at about 27 ft per hPa that adds 540 ft to the reading. The airfield elevation is 540 ft, so the altimeter shows 540 + 540 = 1080 ft. With 1013 set on the ground the reading is by definition the pressure altitude of the airfield.
0L7tjnxprupXc7UZMb3l: Short-term memory is limited in BOTH ways: about 7 items, and only 10 to 20 seconds without rehearsal. It is also highly vulnerable to disturbance, which is exactly why an interruption wipes a clearance. Procedural knowledge - how to fly the aeroplane - lives in long-term memory.
0LgZ3E2XBMtZBPpGnunL: Yellow fever is a viral disease spread by the bite of an infected mosquito, which is why the vaccination requirement is tied to particular tropical regions rather than to food or water hygiene. Malaria and dengue share the same vector, so mosquito avoidance covers all three.
0Nw0Dm4uySBnNnUfaI4W: The mean sun is a fiction used to make civil timekeeping uniform. It travels along the CELESTIAL EQUATOR, not the ecliptic, at a constant rate, and coincides with the apparent sun at the equinox. Placing it on the equator removes the obliquity effect; moving it uniformly removes the elliptical-orbit effect.
0OHme2ex36EDNwedS6Ju: The requirement is based on the seating installed, not on the passengers actually carried, and there must be at least 10% more dispensing units than seats so that a unit is available wherever a passenger or crew member happens to be. With 200 seats fitted that gives 220.
0PFLw31Fn2JVa669hMHa: This is confirmation bias, and it gets STRONGER once a plausible explanation exists: the mental model becomes a filter, information that fits is accepted and information that contradicts is discounted or simply not noticed. Experience makes it worse rather than better, because experienced pilots form their model faster.
0Q5mnW9oR4oTV1JbDkQd: Halon 1211 (BCF) works by chemically interrupting the combustion chain reaction rather than by cooling or smothering, so it is effective across the range: paper, fabric and wood (class A), hydrocarbons (class B) and live electrical equipment, since it is non-conductive. That is why it became the standard hand extinguisher for aircraft cabins.
0QAT6DJcWVW3rWzSztBH: At low RPM the rear stages choke and the front stages stall, because the compressor is running away from its design point. Bleed valves opened between the spools dump some of the flow overboard, which reduces the mass flow through the rear stages while allowing the early stages to pass more air - restoring the axial velocity and unstalling them.
0QW52e6aikKs75YMlzZ7: In a steep wind gradient the headwind decreases rapidly as the aircraft descends. The aircraft's inertia means that lost headwind comes straight off the airspeed, so IAS decays on final. Unless speed is deliberately controlled, the result is a low, slow approach that undershoots the aiming point - or, if the loss is severe enough, a stall. The standard defence is to add a margin to the approach speed when a marked gradient is reported.
0Qj30BGAvhh1Krrp1I22: RVR groups in a METAR always represent the touchdown zone, which is the most operationally critical part of the runway for landing. Where mid-point and stop-end sensors exist they are used for low-visibility operations and passed by ATC, but they do not appear in the routine METAR group. The METAR gives a one-minute or ten-minute representative value, with a tendency indicator (U, D or N) when it has been changing.
0QlLVgXOf3zPsBmWQL1e: Annex 8 requires the State of Design to ensure a continuing structural integrity programme, including corrosion prevention and control, for aeroplanes over 5,700 kg maximum certificated take-off mass. Note the criterion is take-off mass alone; options phrased as take-off and landing mass are distractors.
0Rx4PHFUam8IMs55c1qG: The MEL is a dispatch document and stops applying once the aeroplane moves under its own power, so a failure discovered during taxi is handled by the abnormal and emergency procedures in the Operations Manual. The commander then decides whether to continue or return to stand - and back on stand the MEL governs again, because the aeroplane is once more being dispatched.
0T07KpReeGaWD9LNiem2: An automatic landing means the automatics fly the aeroplane onto the runway: the autopilot stays coupled to the localiser and glideslope until the flare (3), the autothrottle retards the thrust at about 30 ft (4), and the flare and roll-out are completed automatically (5). Statements 1 and 2 describe an autocoupled approach disconnected at decision height, which is not an automatic landing.
0TeCHSmuhHnlq3h7DNFZ: A cantilever wing carries its loads entirely through its own internal structure to the fuselage attachment, with no external struts or bracing wires. It costs more in structural weight but removes the drag of the bracing, which is why it is universal on transport aircraft. It says nothing about where the wing is mounted or its planform.
0VqrpAffE8ScrWohsclC: The standard constant-pressure charts and their approximate ISA heights are 850 hPa near 5000 ft (FL50), 700 hPa near 10,000 ft (FL100), 500 hPa near 18,000 ft (FL180), 300 hPa near 30,000 ft (FL300) and 200 hPa near 39,000 ft (FL390). A pressure level of 4781 ft therefore corresponds to the 850 hPa chart.
0WmpNzfoo6BkSMKnHrHR: When both aircraft carry TCAS II the two units exchange intentions over the Mode S data link before issuing their resolution advisories, so the manoeuvres are coordinated - one climbs, the other descends - and complementary. Against a target with only a transponder, no such coordination is possible.
0X3g98qQELi2dJOjn4wO: A ring laser gyro has no moving parts, so there is nothing to wear out: life is long, reliability high, power consumption low and there is no spin-up time - it is available almost immediately. Those characteristics, rather than any gain in accuracy alone, are what displaced the spinning-mass gyro.
0XNqbVx6qDu1cV275ubd: Freezing fog (FZFG) consists of supercooled water droplets: liquid water existing below 0 C. It is reported when those droplets freeze on contact with a surface, which is why it is a serious airframe and runway icing hazard. If the droplets had already frozen the fog would be ice fog, which is a different phenomenon and is far less hazardous for icing.
0XPPFdjSFJiHeI7e7m5n: FADEC governs the engine within its limits, so overspeed protection and EGT (or turbine temperature) limiting are core functions - the unit will schedule fuel to prevent the limit being exceeded regardless of thrust lever position. Fire detection loops are an airframe system, entirely separate from engine control.
0YR7dZTHwMSaION20qof: Below about 200 ft the glideslope beam becomes unusable, so vertical guidance for the flare is taken from the radio altimeter, which measures actual height above the surface. Barometric height is not accurate enough near the ground on any setting, which is why radio altimeter serviceability is a condition for a Cat II or III approach.
0YeDIqUZLEwLmjCQYRLY: ICAO Doc 4444 states that during a radar approach, the pilot should be advised to consider a missed approach if the aircraft's position or identity is in doubt, or if the aircraft is not visible on the radar display for a significant interval during the last 2 NM of the approach. The 2 NM threshold ensures reliable guidance through the most critical segment close to the runway.
0YiuEnOTDJSY59Sxt4YP: Airborne weather radar and most ground ATC radars use SHF, 3-30 GHz. The short wavelength gives the narrow beam needed for good bearing resolution from a small antenna, and it is short enough to be reflected by water droplets, which is what makes weather returns possible at all.
0ZOU2aZTfIiW33DbHMsR: Sound decision-making starts with understanding the process itself - which biases you are prone to, how stress narrows your options, and how you weigh risk. Deferring to the captain's authority, avoiding situational awareness or suppressing non-verbal cues all make decisions worse.
0ZfpFNn40bVaMV3vhR3a: In a high bypass engine most of the air passes around the core, and that cold stream produces roughly 75-80% of the total thrust. The core exists largely to drive the fan. Moving a large mass of air slowly is more efficient than a small mass quickly, which is why bypass ratios rose as fuel prices did.
0aMnox4UhDFM4hmbeP0l: Nickel-cadmium cells hold their terminal voltage nearly constant until they are almost flat (4) and accept a high charging rate, so they recharge quickly (3). Their internal resistance is LOW, not high, and it is precisely that low resistance which makes them vulnerable to thermal runaway - the opposite of statement 1.
0aPlr5WpX3ZJVxeu8MLd: The chain of responsibility starts with the shipper. When completing the shipper's declaration for dangerous goods the shipper certifies that the article is not forbidden for air transport and is correctly classified, packed, marked and labelled. The operator's acceptance check and the commander's notification come afterwards, and neither replaces the shipper's initial certification.
0aWiHDJeIeM3YNY6hrWo: For unpressurised aeroplanes, JAR-OPS 1.770 requires all occupants of flight deck seats on flight deck duty to be supplied with supplemental oxygen for the ENTIRE flight time above a cabin pressure altitude of 10 000 ft. There is no 30-minute grace period for flight deck duty occupants; that concession applies only to the 10% passenger case.
0bDVZuEX3xFfIudTqoO6: In mid-latitudes the tropopause sits near 11 km (about 36,000 ft), and the stratosphere extends from there up to the stratopause at roughly 50 km. Above that lies the mesosphere (50-85 km) and then the thermosphere. Note the tropopause height varies with latitude: about 8 km over the poles and 16-18 km over the equator.
0bPzRYY4qe8LWNPvO6uC: The instruments are the only reference that cannot be fooled by an illusion, so the response is to go on instruments and believe them. Scanning outside or dimming the lights does nothing about a vestibular illusion, and looking for outside cues at night is what generated it in the first place.
0bZ8BD1Lpzo6FEaUXAXl: Aviation phraseology is deliberately restricted: a small standard vocabulary, fixed formats and readback exist precisely because ambiguity is what kills. Communication is not something to minimise, nor does it outrank flying the aircraft, and syntax matters as much as the individual words.
0cRQjvSNAZO0EDJdqGES: A fixed-pitch propeller is optimised for exactly one combination of airspeed and rpm and its efficiency falls away rapidly either side of that point. A constant-speed unit varies blade angle to hold the chosen rpm, so the blades stay near their optimum angle of attack across the whole speed range - climb, cruise and descent - giving near-maximum efficiency throughout. Its peak efficiency is no higher than a fixed-pitch prop's; it simply holds it over a far wider range.
0cdAY0zSIpY427W1aJCF: True altitude needed is 8000 + 2000 = 10 000 ft. In colder than standard air the aircraft is lower than the altimeter reads, so the indicated altitude must be increased. Using 4 ft per 1000 ft per degree C, ISA-10 gives 4 x 10 x 10 = 400 ft of correction, so the lowest permissible indicated altitude is 10 400 ft.
0cwQEI1TE86kq5ptb2bz: Convert to true first: heading 355(M) with 15E variation gives 010(T). The feature lies 30 degrees left of the nose, so its true bearing from the aircraft is 010 - 030 = 340. The question asks for the bearing of the AIRCRAFT FROM the feature, which is the reciprocal: 340 - 180 = 160 degrees.
0dKHUEFyxy7WbRyoYxbD: A decision is made against the situation as it was understood at that moment, and the situation moves on. That is why decisions have to be reviewed as new information arrives - a plan that was right at top of descent may be wrong ten minutes later, and treating it as fixed is how crews fly into a deteriorating situation.
0denp2OSHeg4TstZCtKg: On a Lambert conformal conic chart the convergence between any two meridians is constant across the whole sheet and equals change of longitude x sin(parallel of origin). Earth convergency also equals dlong x sin(latitude), so the two agree exactly at the parallel of origin. Chart convergence is too large south of it and too small north of it.
0dsXl7z7uOvCImBps4No: On an AC primary system the battery is charged through a transformer rectifier unit, which steps the 115 V AC down and rectifies it to about 28 V DC. A static inverter does the reverse - DC to AC - and is used to feed essential AC loads from the battery when generation is lost.
0e6z3lDnzp62Dzg5RDj8: Statements 3, 4 and 5 are correct: the pilot in command may deviate from the rules when safety requires it, and may request an amended clearance if the one issued is unsatisfactory. Statement 1 is wrong because compliance with ATC is not absolute; the PIC retains final authority for the safety of the aircraft. Statement 2 is wrong because the PIC is responsible for the aircraft regardless of who is acting as pilot flying.
0eCFXuHoFpdwNMmJ2QFE: Short-term (working) memory holds about 7 plus or minus 2 items for around 10 to 20 seconds without rehearsal. That is why clearances are given in chunks, why readback matters, and why an interruption during a long clearance so reliably destroys it.
0fFKwD6ItMxelvePDRA6: This is the double-the-angle-on-the-bow method. Relative bearing 315 is 45 degrees off the nose and 270 is abeam, so the angle on the bow has doubled from 45 to 90 degrees. When that happens the range at the second bearing equals the distance run: 10 minutes at 240 kt = 40 NM.
0fQzO7ODIM4s97odv3Lv: The environmental lapse rate (ELR) is the actual measured temperature profile of the real atmosphere at a given place and time, so it varies continuously with time, location and height, and can even be negative through an inversion. The fixed figures quoted in the distractors belong elsewhere: 0.65 C/100 m is the ISA lapse rate and 1 C/100 m is the dry adiabatic lapse rate.
0fXfIPuyEdIFWxPbodSC: Wing loading is weight (a force, in newtons) divided by wing area, so N/m2. Dynamic pressure q = 1/2 rho V2 is a pressure, and a pascal is by definition one newton per square metre, so it is also N/m2. Both quantities share the same units, which is why wing loading and dynamic pressure can be compared directly in the lift equation.
0g4FTiR2w82ZBp4420xs: The names and titles of persons authorised to exercise operational control must be listed in the certificate holder's manual. The manual is the operator's controlled document for crew and dispatch procedures, whereas Operations Specifications record the authorisations granted by the authority, and the load manifest covers only that individual flight.
0gA3SBkfeKh6Trt30hmU: The apparent solar day varies because the Earth's orbit is elliptical, so its orbital speed changes, and because the axis is tilted 23.5 degrees to the orbital plane, so the sun's apparent motion is not parallel to the celestial equator. The equation of time is the NAME for the resulting difference, not its cause.
0gBGElfqcLvR0U9oMTx8: A circling approach is the visual phase flown after an instrument approach to position the aircraft for landing on a runway not aligned for a straight-in approach. It is flown visually with the runway kept in sight, so it requires visual conditions rather than IMC, and it is not dependent on radar vectoring.
0gJzZkl9iqXhqSiIWHH5: Ice accretes first and fastest where the airflow strikes the airframe head-on and the radius is small: the frontal areas, i.e. wing and tail leading edges, engine intakes, antennas, windscreen and probes. Upper and lower surfaces well aft of the leading edge see far less impingement because the supercooled droplets have already been swept out of the local flow.
0hPTJF5xeFkePVUhv6wr: Mach number is the ratio of dynamic to static pressure, so a machmeter is built from both an airspeed capsule sensing pitot minus static and an aneroid capsule sensing static alone; the linkage combines them so that the pointer reads M directly. Nothing in it measures the speed of sound.
0hcSjp9b8AazLwhvOWHj: About 97 percent of the oxygen carried is bound to haemoglobin inside the RED blood cells, with only a small fraction dissolved in the plasma. White cells fight infection and carry no oxygen, and haemoglobin is not found in plasma.
0j7WkE8F36qu1tsnPzaO: Red cells carry oxygen on haemoglobin, white cells provide immunity, and platelets clot the blood. Anaemia - too few red cells or too little functional haemoglobin - therefore reduces oxygen-carrying capacity and makes a crew member far more susceptible to hypoxia.
0jAEuszphgt7EyckiRbg: Night vision is the first thing hypoxia degrades, and the loss is measurable from about 4000 to 5000 ft. At 10 000 ft at night the rods are already significantly impaired, and the fix is supplemental oxygen, which restores acuity within minutes. Scanning technique helps you USE what vision you have; it does not restore it.

0jPIfeFcJkuYFXwBLVOU: Work the two errors in turn. Pressure: with QNH 1003 but 1013 set, the datum is 10 hPa (about 270 ft) below sea level, so the altimeter over-reads by 270 ft. Temperature: 15 C colder than ISA means the aircraft is lower than indicated, so indicated = true / (1 - 4 x 15 / 1000) = 15000 / 0.94 = about 15,960 ft. Adding the 270 ft pressure error gives roughly 16,230 ft. Remember: cold air and low pressure both make the altimeter read high.
0joVirZTDqHvDkMwAPvn: Divided attention means genuinely running more than one activity at once, either by rapid switching or by letting a well-learned motor programme run subconsciously while attention goes elsewhere, so 1 and 2 are right. Statement 3 describes SELECTIVE attention, which explicitly excludes other operations, and 4 describes delegation, not division.
0k7UmJlOzQo9ZEIEMkQf: An interruption breaks the thread of whatever the other pilot was doing, and the commonest consequence is an omitted item. Closing the loop by reminding them where they had got to is what stops the interruption becoming an error. Interrupting for a sound reason is always legitimate; failing to restore the sequence afterwards is not.
0lfw6se01Qq66VP5fwqq: Under the AIP structure this question is drawn from, meteorological information including the SIGMET service is published in the MET part. Note the option list also offers AGA (Aerodromes and Ground Aids), which places the question in that same structure; in the current GEN/ENR/AD layout the equivalent material sits in GEN 3.5, Meteorological Services.
0m0hYY3FXSOQH0M2vDs5: Direct Mercator scale expands as the secant of the latitude, so a fixed chart length represents a distance proportional to the cosine of latitude. Distance = 90 x cos30 / cos45 = 90 x 0.866 / 0.707 = about 110 NM. Lower latitude means less scale expansion, so the same chart length covers MORE ground.
0nIk3kAqicOkeI7hQspt: A rapid airspeed increase with thrust and attitude unchanged is an increasing-performance shear, and its danger is that it usually reverses into a decreasing-performance shear seconds later. The correct response is therefore to hold the flight path, tolerate the positive speed excursion and watch the trend, keeping the energy in hand. Chasing the speed by pulling thrust off leaves the aircraft low on both speed and thrust exactly when the shear reverses.
0nLCOAv6TRQw39GoF1U6: Whole-body resonance occurs in the low frequency band, roughly 1 to 100 Hz: the abdomen resonates around 4 to 8 Hz, the head and shoulders around 20 to 30 Hz, and the eyeball around 60 to 90 Hz, which is why vibration in that range blurs instrument reading.
0nho3BQjXe8bLOZ18gax: MMO and VMO cross at a particular level, typically in the high twenties. Above it a constant Mach number corresponds to a CAS below VMO, so the Mach limit governs; below it VMO is reached first. Descending from FL390 the aircraft is therefore Mach-limited initially and speed-limited from the crossover down.
0nrQhy6TcpYbHHNQbYT1: Short-term memory is limited in BOTH capacity and duration: about 7 items for 10 to 20 seconds without rehearsal, and easily destroyed by an interruption. Procedural knowledge, the skill of flying, is held in long-term memory instead.
0oFNufjpRg6H4KCa1VOy: Pre-ignition is ignition of the charge by a hot spot in the cylinder - a glowing carbon deposit, an overheated valve or plug electrode - before the spark occurs. The charge burns while the piston is still rising, so peak pressure arrives too early and the piston is fighting it, which produces very high temperatures and rapid damage.
0oGOCZfGwvoNFuZUKPjX: By WMO convention low cloud has its base between the surface and 6500 ft, medium cloud between 6500 ft and about 23,000 ft, and high cloud above that. The classification is by base height, not by top, and the medium and high boundaries vary with latitude (they are lower over the poles and higher over the tropics).
0oLyE7DpZSkeglaIRGXN: A trough is an elongated extension of low pressure. Air spirals inward toward low pressure, so along the trough line the flow converges, and because that converging air cannot go into the ground it must rise. The lifting is why troughs are associated with cloud, precipitation and thunderstorms. A ridge is the opposite: divergence with subsidence and generally fine weather.
0pmFmrEhDl1s4BEbZU27: Fuel is jettisoned in straight and level flight at a relatively high level so the fuel atomises and evaporates well before reaching the surface, and so that the jettisoned fuel is not drawn back over the airframe. Dumping low down, in a holding pattern or on final approach concentrates fuel near the ground and near the aircraft's own path.
0pqBxnUQRlnd1LH7XsjV: A departing aircraft may be radar identified when its radar position indication is observed within 2 km (1 NM) of the end of the departure runway. Keeping the limit that tight ensures the observed return can only be the aircraft that just departed, avoiding a mistaken identification.
0ptnvvkynoJ9JytT6FaU: A flight level is measured from the 1013.2 hPa datum, so it only sits at or above its nominal altitude when neither pressure nor temperature pushes it down. QNH at or above 1013 puts the datum at or below sea level, and temperature at or above ISA expands the air so each level is physically higher. Both conditions together guarantee the flight level is at least at the stated height. A 'warm high' is not a safe substitute, because a high-pressure area is high only relative to its surroundings and can still have a QNH below 1013.
0qvTR1ovuwzesOuEpdfP: An EFIS installation consists of the symbol generators, which build the picture from the aircraft's data sources, the display units on which it is drawn, and the control panel through which the crew selects ranges, modes and overlays. The FMS and the air data computer supply data to it but are not part of it.
0r0IW68OpK4xL5U48kcc: JAR-OPS 1.110 is absolute on this point: the operator shall not permit, and shall take all reasonable measures to prevent, the use on board of any portable electronic device that could adversely affect the performance of the aeroplane's systems and equipment. Once a device is suspected of interfering there is no discretionary exception the commander can grant.
0rp8b2p70KFJ30AI92Wh: The five classic GPWS modes are excessive descent rate (1), excessive terrain closure rate (2), altitude loss after take-off or go-around (5), unsafe terrain clearance for the gear and flap configuration (6) and excessive deviation below the glideslope (7). Angle of attack and pitch attitude are not GPWS inputs.
0sYcep4gHioPHMYSFkV4: ICAO PANS-OPS lists the circumstances in which noise abatement may NOT drive runway selection, and all three named here are on it: crosswind including gusts above 15 kt, tailwind including gusts above 5 kt, and a runway that is not clear and dry. Windshear reported or thunderstorms expected are on the same list. Safety-of-operation criteria always outrank noise.
0t7Zb8eV5Hjzf8qc6fxE: At or below the transition altitude the vertical position is reported as an altitude, because the aircraft is flying on QNH and its height is referenced to mean sea level. Above the transition level the altimeter is set to the standard pressure of 1013.2 hPa and the position is reported as a flight level.
0tyst444Sr3iLr2e8wHc: Diving on compressed gas saturates the tissues with nitrogen, and climbing to cabin altitude straight afterwards drops the ambient pressure again before that nitrogen has washed out - which is the exact mechanism of decompression sickness. A wait of at least 24 hours is required after a dive of this kind. Note the risk is DCS, not hypoxia.
0u4z1pMTY8PgxSHoXqxx: The AIP is divided into three parts: GEN (General), ENR (En-route), and AD (Aerodromes). Holding, approach and departure procedures are published in the ENR section because they govern the en-route and terminal phase of flight between aerodromes.
0usX4C3eJPwe2FEDJnLT: Boost pressure is the pressure the turbocharger delivers to the induction manifold, so the instrument that measures it is the manifold pressure gauge and nothing else. RPM tells you engine speed and cylinder head temperature tells you how hot the engine is; neither indicates how much boost is being produced.
0vU4qdXLaMJJ3iFZr5PL: Air bled from the compressor has already had work done on it, so taking it for pressurisation, anti-icing or engine starting reduces the mass flow available to produce thrust and increases specific fuel consumption. That is why bleed-off performance penalties are tabulated, and why bleeds are shut off for a maximum-performance take-off.
0vbYDdjmuBh9kfR7SWqe: The lowest usable flight level must be safe under the worst combination of conditions, and both low pressure and low temperature push a flight level physically downward. So you need the lowest QNH expected along the route and the largest negative (coldest) deviation from ISA. Correcting for the best-case conditions instead would leave the aircraft below the minimum safe altitude.
0wTXCxHq3mFzt0bxk6ww: The adult brace position is designed to stop the upper body flailing and to keep the head from striking a hard surface: bend fully forward with the head down as low as possible and the arms wrapped round the legs behind the knees. The knee-cushion variant is the position taught for children, and crossing the arms in front of the face restrains nothing.
0wbfj19JQWoeVzWrh6JM: The yaw damper senses yaw rate with a rate gyro and applies rudder to oppose it, damping Dutch roll. It works through the rudder alone, and its inputs are not fed back to the pedals on most types, so the crew normally sees no control movement at all.
0zj8ie1Rua9s2824y2vN: The periphery of the retina is almost all rods: poor at detail and blind to colour, but very sensitive to low light and to MOVEMENT. That is why an aircraft on a constant collision bearing, which by definition does not move across your field of view, is the hardest of all to detect.
0zwLWNNFjzeAjQC5kJh1: ATIS broadcasts are updated upon receipt of any official weather observation, regardless of whether the content has actually changed. This ensures the information identifier advances and pilots always work from the latest available data.
0zzjYWvjmIGh1YyjG1G9: Track 353 against heading 002 is 9 degrees of port drift, so the wind is from the right, and the groundspeed of 132 kt slightly exceeds the TAS of 130 kt, so there is a small tailwind component. 10gjfuJBBzVrfKPsPerY: Semantic memory holds meanings and general knowledge - what a stall is, what the word 'cleared' means - and because it is rehearsed constantly it lasts longer and is more accurate than episodic memory, which stores particular events and decays. Both are parts of long-term memory.
11IYWN8Xf4kwsCWcDgOR: The probe is immersed in the airflow, so what it senses is total air temperature - the static temperature plus the kinetic heating produced as the air is brought to rest against it. The air data computer subtracts that ram rise, using Mach number and the probe's recovery factor, to recover the static air temperature the crew and the systems actually need.
11txKpJkqtLhMPfne7Z0: Anti-icing fluid is only protective within its holdover time. Once that time has been exceeded the fluid film has absorbed contamination and can no longer be relied upon, so the surface must first be de-iced (the used fluid and any contamination removed) before fresh anti-icing fluid is applied. Simply re-spraying anti-icing fluid over a lapsed film is not acceptable.
12ItvunkqwZvasu5gs1m: A checklist only works if it is given attention, so it must not be run in parallel with another task: doing so is how items get called without being checked, or checked without being called. Nor is it made redundant by a later list.
12NYuSJCn5o89KVIKfCi: Endurance in Item 19 of the ICAO flight plan is the airborne endurance of the usable fuel, so it must include the reserve. Reserve is 30% of trip fuel, which is 30% of the 2 h 45 min trip time = 49.5 minutes. Endurance = 2 h 45 min + 49.5 min = 3 h 34 min. Taxi fuel is burned before take-off and is not part of the airborne endurance.
12jGOaW9T5j5RqCx9i3I: Class B is a flammable-liquid fire, so the agent must smother or break the chain reaction: CO2, dry chemical and halon all qualify. Water is excluded because it is denser than most hydrocarbons - it sinks, flashes to steam and spreads the burning liquid.
14u4YtZSlZv1k6xzNTiA: Machines are better at everything that is dull, precise and continuous: waiting indefinitely for a rare event, holding a value for hours, and watching limits. People remain better at QUALITATIVE judgement - deciding what a novel situation means and what matters about it - which is why item 4 stays with the crew.
15Gt5NNgFbroYMRmtNKl: Take the pressure error first: FL160 is 16,000 ft above the 1013 datum, and with QNH 1003 that datum sits 270 ft below sea level, so the altitude above sea level in ISA terms is 15,730 ft. Now the temperature: ISA at 16,000 ft is about -17 C, so -27 C is a deviation of -10 C. True altitude = 15,730 x (1 - 4 x 10 / 1000) = about 15,090 ft. The aircraft is lower than the flight level suggests, which is the classic cold-weather hazard.
15QOgDV6TeEaH2GMvT7F: All four apply. The choice depends on the goal, on the risks each option carries, on objective and subjective criteria together, and on the decision-maker's own personality and risk appetite - which is why two competent crews can reach different, defensible answers from the same facts.
15rDcKjPB4N9Val3i5sJ: The full chain is IAS, corrected for instrument error to give IAS proper, then for position error to give CAS, then for compressibility to give EAS, then for density to give TAS. All four corrections apply; at low speed and low level the last two are small, which is why they are often ignored in light aircraft work.
16LrQGXKVo00hYAJzvXe: With independent spools only the high-pressure spool has to be turned to start the engine, so a much smaller and lighter air starter will do the job. The other options overstate the case: multi-spool engines can still surge, they are not shorter, and a seized spool is a catastrophic failure.
16srVwjYE6wRGkuEaXFo: Auto trim runs the elevator trim to null out the steady elevator deflection the autopilot is holding, so that the autopilot's servo is left working near the middle of its authority. Without it the autopilot would be holding an increasing out-of-trim force, and a disconnect would produce a large sudden pitch change.
17CnOmHngxkBVCKyQObj: Circling (visual manoeuvring) minima are set by aircraft category, and the minimum visibility runs 1500 m for Category A, 1600 m for B, 2400 m for C and 3600 m for D. A Category B aeroplane therefore needs at least 1600 m.
17Va1CkJ6W44uEfM5kYz: Turning onto north in the northern hemisphere, a direct reading compass lags, so the turn must be stopped before the compass reads north - undershoot north, overshoot south. Turning left the heading is decreasing towards 360, so the roll-out is at a heading still to the east of north, and at 50°N the lead is of the order of 30°.
18F3htKvyBU8PnqSsmyu: TCAS interrogates the transponders of other aircraft and works out range from the reply delay and closure from its rate of change, with altitude taken from the Mode C or Mode S reply. It therefore sees only transponder-equipped traffic, and an aircraft with its transponder off or unserviceable is invisible to it.
18mCQpZJ2slMnWTnfFVt: Feedback closes the communication loop: the receiver returns the message so the sender can compare what was heard against what was meant and correct the difference. That is exactly what a readback is for, which is why it is required routinely and not just in special cases.
194R2U0KinzQgmhm3UIP: Descending air is compressed and warms at the dry adiabatic rate. Its actual moisture content is unchanged, but warmer air can hold far more water vapour, so the saturation capacity rises while the amount present stays the same, and relative humidity falls. This is why subsidence in a high-pressure area dissolves cloud, and it is also the mechanism behind the dry, warm Foehn wind.
19RyMKLYkgLP4dbjXnrn: At about 50 ft the glideslope is abandoned - the beam is unusable that close in - and the flare law takes over, flying a pitch and rate-of-descent schedule from the radio altimeter to touchdown. The localiser remains coupled until roll-out, which is why it is the glideslope mode specifically that drops out.
19tiAW3BC8eSG5deFsFC: ICAO Annex 2 and Doc 4444: if two-way communication fails during an IFR flight in VMC, the pilot shall continue to fly in VMC, land at the nearest suitable aerodrome, and report arrival by the most expeditious means to the appropriate ATC unit. This differs from the procedure in IMC, where the pilot maintains the assigned route and level.
1AKlbmZgxVRyoMhrSSQW: Roughly 70 to 80 percent of the information a pilot processes arrives through the eyes, which is why visual illusions and any degradation of vision matter so much. Hearing is second, and the kinesthetic sense is the least reliable of all in flight - it is the one that produces spatial disorientation.
1ATDdQHJBGah7XbwUWYr: The four strokes are induction, drawing the charge in as the piston descends; compression, as it rises with both valves closed; power, as the burning charge drives it down again; and exhaust, as it rises to expel the products. Only one stroke in four produces power, which is why a flywheel is needed to carry the engine through the other three.
1Auex94B6AvJMoE6Uc1Z: An INS flies great circles, whose true track changes continuously with longitude. Convergency over each 10 degree leg is dlong x sin lat = 10 x sin60 = 8.7 degrees. Arriving at WPT 2 the track is about 094 and leaving it the track is about 086, so the autopilot commands a track change of roughly 9 degrees DECREASE.
1BRnxSdzdolSydD2W5db: Hydraulic fluid must be thermally stable, must not emulsify with water, must not corrode the system and must resist burning, since it operates at high pressure near hot components. It must also be as INCOMPRESSIBLE as possible - a compressible fluid would make the controls spongy - and both high volatility and high viscosity are undesirable.
1BrG7Fl7ASPy1rTG5d6h: JAR-OPS 1.430 requires the operator to account for all of these when establishing aerodrome operating minima: navigation equipment available, runway dimensions and characteristics, obstacles in the approach and missed approach areas, the means available to determine and report the meteorological conditions, and the composition, competence and experience of the flight crew. Crew composition is genuinely part of the list, which is why the all-inclusive combination is correct.
1C1pDYMMTVsH5JWZM0YF: Apply variation before the relative bearing: heading 290(M) with 10E variation is 300(T). The island is 30 degrees right of the nose, so its true bearing from the aircraft is 300 + 030 = 330 degrees. East variation is added to a magnetic heading to obtain the true heading.
1C8v3k3dSWsGIvP1cJLZ: CAS is a measure of dynamic pressure. Descending into denser air, the same dynamic pressure is produced by a lower true speed, so holding CAS constant means TAS falls steadily - roughly 2% per 1,000 ft. The relationship reverses in the climb, which is why a constant-CAS climb gives an increasing TAS.
1CFdpuTfeY1IWRXDw8CD: JAR-145 sets the requirements for approved maintenance organisations. JAR-66 covers certifying maintenance staff licensing, JAR-25 is the airworthiness code for large aeroplanes, and JAR-AMO does not exist as a code.
1CWfEmY5rYv8dulGNvbX: Above 3050 m (10,000 ft) AMSL, ICAO requires a flight visibility of 8 km and cloud clearance of 1500 m horizontally and 1000 ft vertically for VFR flight in all classes of airspace. The higher visibility requirement compared to lower altitudes compensates for greater closing speeds at higher levels.
1DXDAX5ixpINvt2shAoT: Maximum taxi or ramp mass is a structural limit: it is the greatest mass the airframe and landing gear are certificated to support while manoeuvring on the ground, and it exceeds the maximum take-off mass by the fuel expected to be burnt in taxiing. Pavement strength and tyre limits are operational restrictions, not the definition.
1DngZ5dY3rbwVRTQoZS4: Alignment has two parts. Levelling establishes the local vertical by driving the accelerometer outputs to zero, and gyrocompassing then finds true north from the sensed rotation of the earth. Only when both are complete does the platform know its orientation, which is why the aircraft must be kept still and the process takes several minutes.
1EB0WRg99uogWVMJVLks: Cabin air comes from the engine compressors as bleed air, hot enough that the problem is cooling it rather than heating it: it is passed through the packs and then mixed back with hot bleed air in the mixing manifold to give the selected temperature. Turbine gas is contaminated with combustion products and is never used.
1FtaheZvXsf1kJRKrUOu: Departure = change of longitude in minutes x cosine of latitude. 900 = dlong x cos60 = dlong x 0.5, so dlong = 1800 minutes = 30 degrees. Applying 30 degrees east of 160E gives 190E, which is expressed as 170W because longitude is only counted to 180 degrees.
1GK9lSi4id4VEFxlPurs: A series actuator is fitted between the pilot's controls and the surface, so it moves the surface without moving the control column, and its authority is deliberately limited. Its inputs are the small, rapid corrections of stability augmentation, so there is nothing for the crew to see and nothing is displayed.
1GaKujnydz225ctTldFO: At a normal cruising angle of attack an efficient aerofoil generates far more lift than drag - lift-to-drag ratios of 15 to 20 are typical for a transport aeroplane. Since both forces share the same 1/2 rho V2 S term, the ratio of the coefficients equals the ratio of the forces, so CL is much greater than CD. Only near the stall, where CD climbs steeply, do the two approach each other.
1HL9ebwDWRdHvXEX45HO: The accessory gearbox is driven from the high-pressure spool and carries whatever the aircraft needs: fuel and oil pumps, the generator, the hydraulic pump, the starter, tacho and other sensors. On many installations it is also a structural member, providing an engine mounting point.
1HSGPMOC31RDqVPPGPBY: Modern transport aircraft use a phosphate-ester synthetic fluid such as Skydrol - fire-resistant, thermally stable over a wide range and compatible with the seals used with it. It attacks paint and some plastics, which is why spillages matter, and it must never be mixed with mineral fluid.
1IINjetaFv9P07TT8mBk: In noise abatement departure procedure B (NADP 2) the aeroplane climbs at V2 + 10 to 20 kt to 1000 ft, then reduces to climb thrust and accelerates while retracting flap, reaching en-route climb speed by 3000 ft. Procedure A is the one that holds the take-off configuration and speed up to 3000 ft with a thrust cutback at 800 ft.
1Ik07QBo9MQkMAXjnQMZ: Beyond Mcrit a shock wave forms on the upper surface, and the separated flow behind it produces the airframe shaking known as Mach buffet. The shock also moves the centre of pressure aft and reduces the downwash reaching the tailplane, and both effects generate a nose-down pitching moment - Mach tuck. The insidious part is that the nose-down pitch increases the Mach number further, so the tendency is self-reinforcing.
1J9hNYz7W2O1GqdZePG8: A tyre's speed limit is a structural limit on how fast the carcass can rotate, so it is governed by how fast the wheel is actually moving over the ground - the GROUNDSPEED. Airspeed of any flavour is irrelevant to the tyre. This is why a strong tailwind or a hot-and-high aerodrome, both of which raise the groundspeed for a given IAS, can make tyre speed the limiting factor for take-off.
1JQTE4cWoay5S9MEjlez: The two switches are wired in series and must both be made for the trim to run, so a single stuck or shorted switch cannot drive the trim on its own. Trim runaway is a serious failure - it loads the controls progressively and can become unrecoverable - so the split switch is a cheap and effective guard against it.
1JUqzQCcdHSsynvhjDjA: Output voltage is controlled by controlling the field: the voltage regulator senses the generator output and adjusts the excitation current supplied to the rotor field, raising it as load increases. The exciter and its permanent magnet generator provide the power, but it is the regulator that decides how much of it is used.
1JqXlrk6F9uuVMmsq9yN: This question cannot be answered without the track chart, but the reasoning is worth knowing. With a 1 h 45 min single-engine diversion capability at 420 kt the ETOPS-style rule circle around each alternate has a radius of about 735 NM, and only a track that stays inside the combined circles of Shannon, Santa Maria and St John's is legal. Of the tracks that satisfy that constraint you then pick the shortest flight time, not the geographically shortest line.
1K7GrH6him1dHfTaPuvZ: Blowing off carbon dioxide raises the blood pH, making it more alkaline (respiratory alkalosis). That shifts the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve to the LEFT: haemoglobin binds oxygen more tightly at the lungs, but for the same reason releases less of it to the tissues, which is part of why hyperventilation feels like hypoxia.
1Kn6tNm8lCRAr4hJ6UtU: The colour code reserves red for warnings requiring immediate action and amber for cautions requiring awareness and possibly later action. An advisory is neither, so it must not use red and should avoid amber as well, which leaves green, white, cyan or magenta for information that simply tells the crew what the system is doing.
1KusprLL1dpp6omc5OJX: Learning is defined as a relatively permanent change in behaviour resulting from PRACTICE AND EXPERIENCE. Changes from physical maturation, from drugs or from innate reflexes are excluded precisely because they do not come from experience.
1L5pzvfRqjHkymz1IibU: Turning error arises because the compass needle hangs off the horizontal, so that its dip component is dragged round by the turn. The dip angle increases with magnetic latitude, so the error grows as latitude increases - it is negligible at the magnetic equator and unusable in high latitudes.
1LCGDlouqu6ZGX4qcloi: Hydrocarbons in contact with high-concentration oxygen can ignite spontaneously, without any spark, and the reaction is violent. That is why oxygen systems are assembled with oxygen-clean tools and components and why servicing is never done with greasy hands or lubricated fittings.
1MRMAsThEg4jWI5pEgtQ: Transport aircraft generators are normally run in parallel so that the whole electrical load is shared between them and the loss of one generator does not drop any bus. Parallel operation requires the outputs to be matched in voltage, frequency and phase, which is the job of the real and reactive load-sharing loops.
1NIzIrFLWaZ9LPChyLRE: The PFD carries what is needed to fly the aeroplane: attitude, speed, altitude, heading, the flight director, the autopilot and flight director mode annunciations, altitude capture, and TCAS resolution advisories, which must be flown immediately. Engine parameters and system alerts belong on the ECAM or EICAS display instead.
1O4gbY9Id2vaqjFdAYHo: CO2 extinguishes by displacing oxygen and leaves no residue, which makes it the classic agent for flammable liquids and for live electrical equipment. It can be used on class A material as well, though its lack of cooling makes it poor at preventing re-ignition of a deep-seated fire. It must not be used on burning metals, which sustain their own oxygen supply.
1OD7EonE7MSpgxlIbUy3: The INS/IRS aligns by sensing the earth's rotation while stationary, so alignment must be completed and NAV mode selected BEFORE the aircraft moves off the gate. Any movement during alignment corrupts it. Loading passengers and freight rocks the airframe but does not translate it, so alignment can proceed during loading.
1OjbQe5l8ufOV1qbRpXZ: In the SHELL model, Software means the non-physical part of the system: procedures, manuals, checklists, symbology and their organisation. A manual you cannot find things in is a Liveware-Software mismatch. Hardware would be the physical controls and displays.
1QEbIkZTVCVwW26Dcl7c: The row for this question is corrupted in the source data - the tail of the stem has been parsed into option D - so the options as displayed cannot be matched to the question. The underlying point, confirmed by the intact sibling qDiwJtdgs0Pmh6jRqmMS: all four agents may be used on a class A fire. Water is the agent of choice because it cools; dry chemical and halon interrupt the chain reaction; CO2 smothers the flame but, lacking any cooling effect, leaves a deep-seated fire able to re-ignite.
1QZMo8vN5uwm4PmkNQxv: Dry chemical powder interrupts the combustion chain reaction and is non-conductive, so it works on class A solids, class B liquids and electrical fires. Burning metals need a dedicated class D agent: ordinary dry chemical can react with them, so the special-fires case is excluded.
1QZPMpyda5OWbTRj9dah: On a transverse Mercator the cylinder touches along a chosen meridian, so only that central meridian and the Equator project as straight lines. Every other parallel of latitude projects as an ellipse (and the other meridians as complex curves). The stem excludes the Equator precisely because it is the one straight parallel.
1QgmQEhELwZqCKiWzvpg: Anti-icing fluids are designed to shear off progressively during the take-off roll, and the requirement is that the aerodynamic surfaces are clean of fluid by rotation - the moment the wing has to produce lift at high alpha. Brake release is far too early a milestone; the fluid is deliberately still present then.
1RhomxOIwI5DbrmaF6TE: The ground run shortens if the aircraft is lighter (less inertia and a lower lift-off speed), if the air is denser (more thrust and more lift at a given TAS), and if flap is increased (a higher CL means lift-off at a lower speed). All three of those act in the same direction here. High pressure altitude, high temperature and high mass all lengthen the run.
1SB9563azFRusexEL5Gq: UTC+13 and UTC-11 give the same clock time but differ by a whole day in date. Territories choose the sign that keeps them on the same calendar date as the country they belong to or trade with, which is why some islands sit on the far side of the date line from their nominal longitude.
1SeCcLAXFxw8uo4MYa7i: At high power and low forward speed - take-off and the initial climb - the engine demands more air than the intake can capture, and the resulting depression opens the spring-loaded blow-in doors to admit extra air. As forward speed rises the ram pressure closes them again.

1Vn0PMmJdoApPMC4QdXk: The flight director computes and displays the attitude required to fly the selected mode; whether an autopilot is following that guidance is a separate matter. 1WPj582oCfXkeAc29XFz: GR is the METAR code for hail (diameter 5 mm or more), and hail requires the strong, deep updraughts that only cumulonimbus can produce, so it is reported almost exclusively with CB (or towering cumulus in the case of small hail, GS). 1WdpLh9udyFAitkElw0F: At a high angle of attack the propeller disc is inclined to the airflow, so the descending blade meets the air at a greater angle of attack and higher relative velocity than the ascending blade. 1XoHazcqbn6xX1rNJ091: A stationary anticyclone is maintained by convergence aloft feeding subsidence through the depth of the troposphere. 1XpaY4PrEZoecTOjiRqf: Air is supplied to the cabin at a roughly constant rate, so cabin pressure is set by how fast it is allowed to escape. 1YZBRWt85AEPZvHhqCKX: Flight envelope protection keeps the aeroplane within its aerodynamic and structural limits - stall, overspeed, bank and pitch angle, load factor - by limiting what the control laws will allow the pilot to command. 1Yem22mlKb66QPJF7hks: An Aerodrome Flight Information Service (AFIS) provides information useful for the safe conduct of flights at and around an aerodrome but cannot supply ATC services — it has no authority to issue clearances or instructions. 1YgCyKvLh7OJZsIuSg2A: The recency requirement is three take-offs and landings within the preceding 90 days, and they must be on the same type or class, or in a flight simulator of the type to be used. 1Zqrp4tC2H5W5j92rU2v: The Rome Convention of 1952 established uniform rules governing liability for damage caused by aircraft to third parties on the surface. It does not cover mid-air collisions (governed by general tort law) or dangerous goods (covered by other instruments).

1bHQPbCDVNWQCLq5vITn: The torque link, or scissor, connects the fixed upper part of the oleo to the sliding lower part, so the strut can telescope freely but cannot rotate. 1ccJZBowvlMlqGl2wjCa: Power is the rate of doing work: work is force times distance (newton-metres, or joules), so power is newton-metres per second - equivalently the watt or joule per second. 1dqAaqzGUwXlo6jV7Mv4: The wind from 165 blows towards 345, almost straight along the heading of 355, so it is nearly a pure tailwind with a tiny crosswind component from the right of the nose. Groundspeed rises to about 215 kt and the small crosswind gives about 1 degree of port drift.
1ebh2gSQFzfDJsf9wyPR: Oxygen is 21 percent of the air by volume at every altitude, including inside the cabin; that percentage never changes. What falls with cabin altitude is the total pressure, and hence the PARTIAL pressure of oxygen, which is what actually determines how much reaches the blood.
1etCdcHkSXbM0fA2spXX: In MNPS airspace the basic longitudinal separation is 10 minutes, but it may be reduced to 5 minutes where the Mach number technique is applied and the leading aircraft is maintaining the higher speed, because the gap is opening rather than closing. 1glRrRo3M1aruDyX7rLT: CS-25.113 requires the certified take-off distance to be the GREATER of the one-engine-inoperative distance and 115% of the all-engines-operating distance. 1iwhRI8oTFKVNkiJxKtK: An index is simply a moment scaled down: moment divided by a constant, and usually with a further constant added to keep the numbers positive. 1jXKjUNBEoWcAqpkUiwD: Water is lost continuously through the skin and the lungs - the so-called insensible losses, which rise sharply in dry cabin air - as well as through the kidneys. Both routes matter, which is why fluid intake has to be deliberate on a long sector.

1nyrjezxGnOWBKohi0mr: A deep winter trough near Iceland draws cold polar maritime air southward over a relatively warm ocean. 1opk2pFN5wOymqMp5gu9: Refuelling is controlled by level or quantity: each tank's shut-off valve closes when the preselected volume or mass has been loaded, so the operator sets a figure rather than watching gauges. 1puaWhvVjeRZmZhDfxH5: Selecting fine (decreased) pitch with the engine at idle makes the propeller windmill faster and presents a larger effective disc to the airflow, so it generates considerably more drag. 1sQkJFJOcpNFNp2JS0Tj: Under ICAO Annex 7 Article 3, the common mark for aircraft on a common or international register is assigned by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), which is the UN agency responsible for allocating radio call signs and registration marks to avoid conflicts with national marks.
1tRwXxisKfVx6LOH7l0I: JAR-OPS 1.520 requires the dry landing distance to be increased by 15% when the runway may be wet at the estimated time of arrival and the Flight Manual gives no specific wet-runway data. The 15% is applied on top of the dry factored distance, not instead of it.
1tlKvPaC5LI5ZHHStQMC: The stall recovery is: unstall the wing first by moving the stick centrally forward to reduce the angle of attack, keeping the ailerons NEUTRAL because aileron input at high alpha can provoke a wing drop or spin; apply full power to minimise height loss; and level the wings with RUDDER, since rudder remains effective when the ailerons are not. 1wWioHapc7uyV1Yawktl: Viscosity falls as oil warms and rises sharply as it cools, which is the whole reason for multigrade oils, oil coolers and cold-weather warm-up procedures. Pressure, quantity and ambient pressure do not change the fluid's resistance to shear for a given oil.
1wnt7YrOEpoe5IUtzdYx: The bends, joint pain from nitrogen bubbles forming in and around the joints, is by far the commonest first symptom of decompression sickness. 1y0BLUmaxRoy7f9lO144: The liver metabolises alcohol, at a roughly fixed rate of about one unit an hour that nothing - coffee, food or exercise - will speed up. That fixed rate is why the only reliable way to be sober for a duty is to allow enough time.
1y27ykCCvLQGjIA3jVAL: The cabin climbs too, but much more slowly than the aeroplane - typically 300-500 ft/min against a rate of climb several times that - so the differential builds progressively. 1ydkP4P9RfKXHMiLiVzw: With the packs still supplying air and no outflow, the cabin pressure rises until the differential reaches its maximum, at which point the safety relief valves open to prevent the structure being overstressed. 22EqbziIWkDK5HSIWcwT: Mode 1 gives a two-stage alert: a 'SINK RATE' caution when the descent rate is excessive for the height, escalating to the 'WHOOP WHOOP PULL UP' warning if the situation is not corrected. 260cq5yM20nx1uHjrb6R: The wake turbulence category filed in Item 9 of the flight plan is M (Medium) for a maximum certificated take-off mass of 7000 kg or more but less than 136 000 kg. H (Heavy) is 136 000 kg or more and L (Light) is 7000 kg or less; S is not a wake category at all.
26Q5H8BiXuva2IRynrKW: Drift down is the procedure following an engine failure at cruise level, where the aeroplane can no longer hold altitude and descends at the speed for best gradient until it reaches the level-off altitude. 27MZA5LJmhnJowd2eNqS: The constant-speed unit holds RPM at the selected value by changing blade pitch, so RPM does not vary. Manifold pressure, however, is limited by the ambient pressure available at the induction system, so in an unsupercharged engine it falls steadily as the aircraft climbs.

289n6QGJFubEv25jnQAQ: Personality is the stable, characteristic pattern of behaviour that makes an individual recognisably themselves. It is largely fixed by adulthood, which is why selection screens for it while training targets ATTITUDES, which can be changed.
2A1045VlMttI83kSgqJQ: An NDB radiates equally in all directions in the horizontal plane, which is what allows an aircraft anywhere around it to take a bearing. 2AjXhuVMOJvMZ29i09Vt: At the equinoxes the sun's declination is passing through zero and changing at its fastest, about 0.4 degrees per day, so day length changes most rapidly then too. 2AxvM5v5RxgK6Hct2x1c: Vapour lock is fuel boiling in the line: heat, low pressure or a volatile fuel produces bubbles that the pump cannot shift, and the flow to the engine is interrupted. 2Bm10WTMyexytctRdXJp: A bimetallic switch closes on a rapid rise in temperature, and vibration or a momentary hot gas puff could close it briefly. 2CPP1cQGZKaRZdmpldNF: Primary flight controls are those that control the aircraft about its three axes - elevator, aileron and rudder, and roll spoilers where they act as ailerons. 2CmtKVmHL78GPGMHGOlZ: A 2D RNAV system navigates in the horizontal plane only. Adding vertical navigation makes it 3D. Adding a time function on top of that makes it 4D. Speed or cruise management alone does not add a dimension.

2DnzT1JhsCErnjETjYWa: Aircraft tyres are designed to be retreaded: the carcass long outlasts the tread, so a worn tyre goes back to the manufacturer for a new tread and can be through the process several times before the carcass is rejected. 2DpCZA8VkdKOSnrYRdmu: Skill is regular practice, self-management and keeping capacity in reserve for the unexpected. Statement 3 fails on the word ALL: nobody holds every piece of knowledge about a modern aeroplane, which is why manuals and cross-checking exist.
