5KAPsupn0SdimMJGICCW: Steaming fog, also called arctic sea smoke, forms when a very cold air mass moves over much warmer water. Rapid evaporation saturates the shallow layer immediately above the surface and it condenses as it mixes upward. It therefore requires cold air mass properties and a strongly unstable, not stable, low-level lapse rate, which is why the fog appears to steam upward.
5KMavpA122wjCTm8Fk3K: A flashing red light from the control tower to an aircraft in flight means the aerodrome is unsafe and the aircraft should not land. This is distinct from a steady red light, which means give way to other aircraft and continue circling.
5KMihX4NwsiVSXevKfrb: The equator is a great circle, because its plane passes through the centre of the earth, and that plane is perpendicular to the axis of rotation. Every other parallel of latitude is a small circle whose plane is parallel to the equator and does not contain the earth's centre.
5Kf84974r0e6uCjxnecv: The Chinook is the Foehn wind of the eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains: air forced over the range loses its moisture as precipitation on the windward side, then descends the lee side warming at the dry adiabatic rate, arriving warm and very dry. The Bora is a cold fall wind, the Harmattan is a dry dusty north-easterly off the Sahara, and the Scirocco is a warm southerly off North Africa.
5Kha7IItwJCanTqi83Ee: A copilot who is inexperienced and insecure but keen needs his motivation protected and his confidence built. The captain should let him fly and make it explicit that support is available on request, so the copilot practises while knowing he is not on his own. Flying the leg himself denies the copilot the practice, and simply watching without any comment leaves an insecure pilot unsupported and is the least appropriate response.
5KqxjTtsybHUh7jhDsNP: The low-range radio altimeter transmits a continuously frequency-modulated signal and compares the frequency of the returning echo with the frequency being transmitted at that instant. The difference is proportional to the round-trip time and therefore to height, which allows very accurate measurement at the few feet that matter in a flare.
5LLmgh4Ea4Wm6bqCQqpI: The MEL is the operator's own document, derived from the manufacturer's MMEL and approved by the Authority the operator answers to. It may be more restrictive than the MMEL but never less.
5M28Nvr1RhKAhc4B9lP8: Work back from track to compass. True heading = true track minus right drift = 180 - 8 = 172. Magnetic heading = compass heading plus deviation = 195 + (-2) = 193. Variation = true minus magnetic = 172 - 193 = -21, and a negative result means WEST, so 21W.
5MCT2h9gCMw2n8rojAWB: JAR-OPS 1.990 sets both thresholds: cabin crew are required when the maximum approved passenger seating configuration is MORE than 19, and one or more passengers are carried. So a 20-seat aeroplane carrying a single passenger needs at least one cabin crew member; the same aeroplane carrying none does not.
5MFe4GfiUCwydGT8zNaG: The Tokyo Convention (1963) deals with offences and certain other acts committed on board aircraft, including offences against penal law. The Rome Convention covers surface damage, and the Warsaw/Montreal Conventions cover carrier liability.
5MrTiUh414EuQvQjFHrN: Antihistamines act on the central nervous system as well as on the allergic response. Drowsiness and dizziness, a dry mouth, headache, blurred or impaired depth perception and nausea are all recognised effects, so all five items apply. This is why sedating antihistamines are incompatible with flying duty.
5N1OG2fIn0gDZdAP1jVI: Eastward flight shortens the day and demands a phase advance of the body clock, which has a natural free-running period slightly longer than 24 hours and therefore resists being brought forward. Westward flight lengthens the day (a phase delay) and is easier to adapt to. North-south flights cross few time zones and cause little circadian disruption.
5NRNJ67KZqpbeDEwszTd: Future Air Navigation Systems is built on digital data link: controller-pilot data link communications and automatic dependent surveillance replace voice position reporting and HF relay in oceanic and remote airspace, which is what allows the separation minima to be reduced.
5NlXyjE6SYa1t3tmcq84: The magnetic poles wander, and the field they produce changes shape year by year, so charted variation drifts. Whether the numerical value at a given place grows or shrinks depends entirely on where that place is relative to the moving pole, which is why the annual change is published per chart and why old charts must not be used for variation.
5O8tIyGlp12MaVjOPWJw: Mach number is true airspeed divided by the local speed of sound, and the local speed of sound depends only on temperature. Indicated and calibrated airspeeds are measures of dynamic pressure and cannot be compared with a speed of sound directly.
5OfVsdVBh9ry44jF81d3: ICAO Annex 14 states that runway lead-in lighting shall consist of groups of lights forming a straight or curved line towards the runway. The basic requirement is a row of lights leading to the runway threshold to guide pilots during approach.
5Oft8oq7WaiTL5Mxi24i: With the diluter-demand regulator in NORMAL, the proportion of oxygen in the delivered mixture rises with altitude and reaches 100% at approximately 32 000-34 000 ft. Below that some cabin air is always mixed in, which is why the 100% selection exists for smoke or for an immediate need for undiluted oxygen.
5PcNSkDP778qCUykRvl9: In the cruise, ram air is forced through the pack heat exchangers by forward speed alone. On the ground and at low speed there is no ram effect, so electrically driven fans draw cooling air through the exchangers instead - which is why they run during taxi and are shut down as the aircraft accelerates.
5PsQSPp2BmxfCkFWQo0G: Clearway may be counted toward the take-off distance available only up to a maximum of HALF the take-off run available. With a 3000 m runway, at most 1500 m of the 2000 m clearway may be used, giving a TODA of 3000 + 1500 = 4500 m. Clearway is also counted at one end only, for the direction of take-off - it is not added twice.
5R50Mfk6JmqD6aV8DCO9: As Mach number rises the centre of pressure moves aft and the aircraft develops a nose-down tucking tendency, which reduces its longitudinal stability. Mach trim senses Mach number and moves the stabiliser progressively to counter it, restoring the stick-force gradient the pilot expects.
5R561CebJK8VTdxuVfaf: The legs page shows what is planned for each leg: the track to fly, the distance to run and the speed and altitude constraints. Present latitude and longitude is aircraft state rather than flight plan data and appears on the position pages instead.
5RidEu99rV9qiOG0f2E7: The autothrottle is independent of the autopilot, so it can hold the approach speed while the pilot flies the aeroplane by hand - which is exactly how a manual ILS is normally flown on a large aircraft. The thrust modes such as N1 or EPR belong to the climb and cruise rather than to the approach.
5SX1TV64YHdUMFOd502j: Gyrocompassing finds latitude for itself by sensing the earth's rotation, so the entered latitude is used as a check against the computed value and a large discrepancy stops the alignment (1). Longitude cannot be determined inertially at all, so the entered value is simply accepted as the starting point (3).
5ScQo6JrRviOT2NGAzfE: A float gauge measures the height of the liquid surface, so it reads volume and not mass, it is thrown off by any pitch, roll or acceleration, and it is least accurate near the top and bottom of its travel. What is true of it is that the transmitter and indicator run on the DC system.
5TFuEgONt79JnZ4yIFUU: A mechanical latch or detent in the gear selector prevents the lever being moved to UP unless it is first deliberately released, so a knock or a careless hand cannot select it on the ground. It works with, rather than instead of, the weight-on-wheels squat switch that inhibits the retraction circuit electrically.
5TRwdKv1ise4QfJppA60: On the ground the aeroplane is yawing but not banking, so the needle shows the yaw to the left while the ball, thrown outwards by the centrifugal effect of the turn, moves to the right. The result is a fully deflected needle with the ball out - the classic skidding indication, which on the ground is entirely normal.
5UEj3Jwuwtws7o8Qjsoq: The transition level is the lowest flight level available for use above the transition altitude. It is not a fixed value published in the AIP but is calculated based on the current QNH, and ATC declares it for each approach. It ensures vertical separation between aircraft using QNH and those on standard pressure.
5VOhSZzzWMvg8j0OmYdz: The certification scale runs minor, major, hazardous, catastrophic. A hazardous failure is one short of catastrophic: it produces a large reduction in safety margins and physical distress or a workload so high that the crew cannot be relied on to perform their tasks accurately or completely. Fatalities define the catastrophic case.
5VV74juG1ppI8zT3EPGp: Dihedral is the upward angle of the wing measured between the quarter-chord line and the lateral (pitch) axis, i.e. the spanwise horizontal. Its purpose is lateral static stability: in a sideslip the lower wing meets the relative airflow at a greater effective angle of attack, generates more lift, and rolls the aircraft back toward wings-level. Sweep and high wing position produce a similar effect.
5WOSWwSjnlXtZ0DZvIyG: MNPS airspace is RVSM airspace between FL290 and FL410 inclusive, so approved aircraft are separated vertically by 1000 ft. Above FL410 the minimum reverts to 2000 ft.
5WdMmkIt1GrNrlNB7l4E: Item 15 of the ATS flight plan takes the planned TRUE airspeed for the first or whole cruise portion, expressed in knots with the prefix N, or as a Mach number above the transition. Groundspeed cannot be used because it depends on wind, and indicated or equivalent airspeed would vary with altitude.
5WfvaqKRfBPiLaalLGGD: For a turbojet the dry landing field length required is the demonstrated landing distance divided by 0.6, i.e. plus 67%. For a WET runway a further 15% is applied on top: 1.67 x 1.15 = 1.92, so the required field length is the demonstrated distance plus 92%. Note that this factoring is a dispatch requirement, assessed before departure.
5WjNpVUKCcriqieLG55h: A microburst is a concentrated downdraught that strikes the surface and spreads out radially, producing a strong headwind, then a downdraught, then an equally strong tailwind in a matter of seconds - severe vertical and horizontal wind shear. It is a performance problem, not an icing or wake problem.
5XELQNACC9f2nFViDXlP: The induction tachometer transmits engine speed as a frequency, so line resistance does not affect the reading (1), the tachogenerator makes its own power so the indication survives an electrical failure (2), and because the signal is a frequency rather than a current, several indicators can be driven in parallel without loading it (4). It is not immune to temperature.
5XHa6G8ROYw3iosn4asM: VAT of 141-165 kt places the aeroplane in Category D. The bands are A below 91, B 91-120, C 121-140, D 141-165 and E 166-210 kt, and the category chosen drives the applicable minima including the circling visibility.
5XOqtQR46R9gDPRQUazS: Above a pressure altitude of 25 000 ft the time of useful consciousness after a decompression is too short to fit a conventional mask, so quick-donning masks - fitted and delivering oxygen with one hand in less than 5 seconds - are mandatory for the flight crew.
5XecDFeFGoe5DZDy7jtI: Presbyopia is the age-related stiffening of the crystalline lens that reduces accommodation for near vision. It becomes noticeable from the mid-forties and is essentially universal beyond about 50, which is why reading glasses or bifocals are a licensing condition for older pilots. It has nothing to do with intra-ocular pressure or noise exposure.
5XhtoRBpAhOrGwYB1QH1: Deviation is the compass error caused by the aircraft's own magnetism, so it varies with heading (which changes the geometry of the aircraft field against the earth field), with magnetic latitude (which changes the strength of the earth's horizontal component), and with what electrical equipment is switched on. Altitude has no effect.
5YMLEzyagv2xjmeKGh8U: Distance covered is 890 x 1.5 = 1335 km = 1335 / 1.852 = 721 NM. One degree of latitude is 60 NM, so that is 12 degrees of latitude. Starting at 10S and going north, 12 degrees takes the aircraft through the equator to 02N.
5YUlkbndYKxOAvfk0EMh: The outer loop provides guidance - taking the aircraft to a selected heading, level or path - and it commands through parallel actuators with full control authority, which move the control runs and the cockpit controls together so the crew can see what the autopilot is doing. Inner-loop stabilisation uses limited-authority series actuators instead.
5YasUMVOV9DJYfQWdStx: With the CG aft, the moment arm to the tailplane is short, so a small elevator deflection produces a large pitching moment and the aeroplane responds quickly - manoeuvrability is at its best and trim drag at its least. The price is reduced longitudinal stability and lighter, less informative stick forces, which is why certification sets an aft limit. A forward CG gives the opposite trade: very stable but sluggish and draggy.
5ZJFEJWrXQ12rLyQIEcV: Contamination spoils the boundary layer over the wing: maximum lift coefficient falls, so the stalling speed rises; the aeroplane must accelerate to a higher speed and drag is greater, so the take-off distance increases; and with less lift and more drag the climb gradient falls. Nothing about contamination shortens the take-off run.
5ZLsHjtC3ZJJMpr3LYUv: In a steady glide tan(glide angle) = CD/CL, so the shallowest glide - and therefore the greatest distance covered per unit of height lost - occurs at the angle of attack giving (CL/CD)max. Note the contrast with minimum SINK rate, which is a different condition, (CL^3/CD^2)max, flown at a lower speed and used when the aim is to stay airborne longest rather than to go furthest.
5a8UijHsc6NFMKVk9na6: Terrain look-ahead compares the aircraft's position and predicted flight path against a stored digital terrain elevation database, so it can warn about ground that is ahead rather than only about ground already beneath the aircraft. That is the whole advance of EGPWS over the older radio-altimeter-only modes.
5aKjpMhgPK26gaBZzuJ0: Atmospheric composition is nearly constant up to about 80 km, so each gas keeps a fixed percentage of the total. Total pressure falls with altitude, and because partial pressure is that fixed percentage of a falling total, every partial pressure falls with it. That falling partial pressure of oxygen - not a change in the percentage of oxygen - is what causes altitude hypoxia.
5asQr2JHgqLlV3dSML7j: The pump is where the energy goes in, so it is where a fault first shows as heat - a failing pump, or one running against a blocked or closed system, will overheat long before anything else does. Overheat detectors are therefore fitted at the pumps and their outlets, and the warning is usually accompanied by a pump-off drill.
5b5N6pD6S0FFY4GYCYqs: Track 240 against heading 233 is 7 degrees of right drift, and the groundspeed of 523 kt exceeds the TAS of 480 kt, so the wind is on the port quarter. Resolving the vectors gives a wind from about 111 degrees at 75 kt, i.e. 110/75.
5bZO3KG1DN78MtDQ0tsH: Anti-icing protects the surfaces that meet the airflow first and collect ice: the fixed leading edges and the leading edge devices - slats and Krueger flaps - where an accretion would destroy the lift the wing needs most. The upper surface aft of the leading edge and the trailing edge flaps are not protected.
5bo6UkXurRS3B7kqWSVO: Special VFR is flown clear of cloud and in sight of the surface, with a flight visibility of not less than 1500 m. It is a clearance to enter a control zone when the aerodrome is below VMC, and the 1500 m floor is what keeps it visual.
5c2R4W0a8jUgS2xW8Vmk: The slipstream is a corkscrew of air thrown back by the propeller, and its effect on the fin depends on how strongly the propeller is working relative to the aircraft's forward speed. At low speed and high power the helix is tight and the yawing effect is at its greatest - take-off and the initial climb.
5cVrRl1x12OE7pkCwyw6: A fuel jettison system is required only if the aeroplane cannot meet the certification climb gradients at the mass it would reach after a take-off followed by an immediate return: the approach climb with one engine inoperative (2.7% for a four-engined aeroplane) and the landing climb with all engines operating (3.2%). If it can meet both, it is allowed to land overweight rather than dump.
5ccL7QikOULi7D5XEMsH: JAR-OPS 1.515 requires a turbo-jet to be able to stop within 60% of the landing distance available at the destination, assessed at the flight-preparation stage. The equivalent figure for a turbo-propeller aeroplane is 70%, and both are increased by a further 15% if the runway may be wet.
5ci2hY850YfmWa3uC11H: A stimulus has to exceed the absolute threshold of the sense organ before anything can be perceived at all, and differences must exceed the difference threshold before they can be told apart. Stimulus intensity is therefore treated here as the foundation on which all later perceptual processing is built; the memory-based options describe interpretation, which is a later stage.
5dGEvMjd58ABRAKmi2kz: Can-type chambers are connected by interconnector tubes, so flame spreads from one to the next once combustion is established. Only two chambers therefore need igniters - two rather than one for redundancy - and the rest light from the flame propagating round the ring.
5dJwkPPcb04OzBXXPr7h: A second-in-command may log instrument flight time only for the time they are actually controlling the aircraft solely by reference to flight instruments. Simply being on an IFR flight plan does not qualify — actual instrument control is required.
5eotRTjzvJdVBuQuyA5o: The 200 hPa surface lies at roughly 39,000 ft (FL390) in temperate latitudes, which is why the 200 hPa chart is the standard upper-wind chart for long-haul cruise levels and for locating jet cores. Its height varies with the mean temperature of the layer beneath: higher over warm air, lower over cold air.
5fQWo8RFpGXEMpf0jD81: Pressing the test switch passes a current through the whole sensing loop and back, so a break in the wire or a failure of the warning circuit both show up. It is a continuity and function test of the complete chain, which is what makes it worth doing before every flight.
5gACFXdNtrCz9FiZqK8i: Moving the head - particularly out of the plane of rotation - while the aircraft is turning stimulates a second set of semicircular canals and produces the powerful, disorienting Coriolis illusion. The defence is to keep the head still during turns and while the fluid in the canals is still settling. Breathing technique addresses hyperventilation, not vertigo.
5iSyrY5dlG3Lttcakx43: The primary duty of a radar unit in an ATS context is to provide radar separation between aircraft. Assisting with navigation, equipment failures, or weather avoidance are secondary services that radar may provide.
5iY5TVHpmbLJExFCKjke: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) specifies that published missed approach procedures are based on a minimum climb gradient of 2.5%. This is the standard gradient used to calculate obstacle clearance in the missed approach segment unless a higher gradient is specifically noted on the chart.
5ifkE0NQGmSvfFmZGYHv: The two procedures differ in when take-off configuration is abandoned. Procedure B reduces power and accelerates earlier, so its noise relief falls close to the aerodrome, while procedure A holds take-off configuration and V2 + 10 to 20 kt up to 3000 ft, gaining height over the more DISTANT areas. Note that the modern PANS-OPS NADP 1 / NADP 2 pair is described the other way round, so check which convention a question is using.
5k2cNC11r05xXzlNpYn4: In a level turn the lift must support n times the weight, and since lift varies with the square of speed, the stalling speed rises with the SQUARE ROOT of the load factor: Vs(turn) = Vs x sqrt(n). At 60 degrees of bank n = 2, so the stall speed rises by sqrt(2), about 41%. Flap extension does the opposite - it raises CLmax and therefore lowers the stall speed.
5kBSQDaQs0ED7migyaWi: Hypnotics and tranquillisers work by depressing the central nervous system, and that depression outlasts the desired sedative effect: reaction time lengthens and perceptual awareness and judgement are degraded, often into the following day and often without the individual noticing. Sleep produced under these drugs is also of poorer quality than natural sleep, and an apparent absence of visible reaction is no evidence of fitness to fly.
5kMkCGz3OGu7HR8Hu0hY: A heavy landing on a short runway puts a large amount of kinetic energy into the brakes, and the risk that follows is brake temperature - fuse plug melting, tyre deflation, wheel fire and a subsequent take-off attempted with brake energy already absorbed. Brake cooling times must be observed before the next departure.
5kUmkLQzQj8DXcN13y40: The starter drives the high pressure spool through a clutch whose pawls are held in engagement by springs. Once the engine accelerates past the starter, centrifugal force throws the pawls clear and the drive disengages automatically, so the starter is not driven by the engine.
5lkZCK0t0EGPA5eQcj15: On a Direct Mercator the cylinder is tangential at the equator and the meridians are drawn as parallel lines, so the spacing of the parallels must expand as the secant of latitude. Secant 90 is infinite, so the poles would be infinitely far up the sheet and cannot be shown. Both polar stereographic and transverse Mercator handle the poles without difficulty.
5lq48f0Meh2O8BD4uvTK: An aileron deflected downward increases the lift near the trailing edge well aft of the wing's torsional axis, so it applies a twisting moment along the span. At high speed that twist can be enough to reduce or even reverse the aileron's effect, which is why outboard ailerons are locked out in the cruise on large aircraft.
5mhte6JejqZ0oqzWn1DG: The CVR is a microphone and pick-up system feeding a recorder built to survive impact, fire and immersion, with an underwater locator beacon. The flight data recorder is a separate unit recording parameters rather than audio, and the CVR is powered from the aircraft, not from its own battery.
5muJKo0s8jQvZSszrN6B: The flux valve senses magnetic heading and the error detector compares it with the gyro's heading; where they differ, the torque motor applies a torque to the gyro, which precesses slowly onto the magnetic heading. The combination gives the steadiness of a gyro with the long-term accuracy of a magnetic reference.
5n15QRTOcF7ZpKBALG6X: Saturation is reached by cooling the air to its dewpoint (or by adding moisture). Adiabatic expansion is exactly that: the parcel rises, expands against falling ambient pressure, does work and cools, so its relative humidity rises to 100%. Raising the temperature or compressing the air adiabatically warms it and lowers relative humidity, and reducing pressure at constant temperature does not lower the temperature, so none of those can saturate it.
5nIVuReTVVmwl0QqosP7: Heavy sweating in a hot climate loses salt as well as water. The classic early consequence of that salt loss is heat cramp - painful spasm of the heavily used muscles and of the abdominal wall. It is treated by replacing salt and fluid; the problem is a deficit of body fluid, not an excess, and dysentery is an infection unrelated to exercise.
5njAJ8smUSZ3IbmDDDiD: The offset level change follows the separation regime you are moving into. Below FL410 levels are 1000 ft apart, so 500 ft puts you midway; above FL410 they are 2000 ft apart, so 1000 ft puts you midway. Exactly at FL410 you are on the boundary: climbing enters the 2000 ft regime (climb 1000 ft) while descending stays in the 1000 ft regime (descend 500 ft).
5nzqVk8yK5LbNuEyTFwq: The Eustachian tube runs from the middle-ear cavity to the nasopharynx and exists to equalise middle-ear pressure with ambient pressure. It opens readily on climb as expanding middle-ear air escapes, but tends to act as a one-way valve on descent, which is why blocked ears and barotrauma are descent problems.
5oYeMGAgDtti6GQSZcFg: Aerotitis occurs when the Eustachian tube cannot admit air to the middle ear fast enough during descent, so the higher ambient pressure forces the eardrum inward. An upper respiratory infection swells the tube lining and makes this far more likely. Climb is normally safe because expanding air vents itself, so a descent is exactly the wrong remedy.
5qS5wkGJGRCdNb3QjJ32: Mercator scale expands as the secant of latitude, so the scale denominator SHRINKS by the cosine. At 60 degrees the denominator is 3 704 000 x cos60 = 3 704 000 x 0.5 = 1 852 000, giving 1 : 1 852 000. A smaller denominator means a larger scale, which is what expansion away from the equator produces.
5r4jYqfjh5x4oLjOM0ae: The inverted-U relationship means performance peaks at moderate arousal. Beyond the peak, attention narrows onto one or two salient cues - attentional tunnelling - so information outside that narrow band is missed. On a complex task, which needs a wide span of attention, this degrades rather than improves decision-making.
5r8NO8cPatmylZxkh35u: Air distance is what the aircraft flies through the air, and ground distance is what it makes good over the earth, so the two are in the same ratio as groundspeed to TAS. GD = AD x GS / TAS. With a tailwind, GS exceeds TAS and the ground distance is the greater of the two.
5r9Yahnvd3OKQKrp6zTq: Tropopause height follows the mean temperature of the troposphere beneath it: about 8 km over the poles, about 11 km (36,000 ft) in mid-latitudes such as 50 N, and about 16-18 km over the equator. The tropopause temperature runs the other way, roughly -45 C over the poles, -56.5 C in mid-latitudes and -75 C or colder over the equator.
5rwqxldEQMlsese9zlpT: Air is drawn in axially at the centre - the eye - of the impeller, flung outwards by the vanes and leaves at the periphery tangentially at high velocity, after which the diffuser converts that velocity into pressure. A centrifugal stage gives a large pressure rise in a single stage but a large frontal area.
5slpzrg1dukTL5xOy7PJ: Air is being supplied continuously, so holding a steady cabin altitude means letting exactly that much air out - the outflow valve sits partly open and the controller modulates it. Fully closed would let the cabin descend and fully open would let it climb; the valve is only fully closed on the ground in some configurations.
5smbih5XOWwZaEa1XdtW: ICAO Doc 4444 states that when vectoring an aircraft to intercept the ILS localizer course, the final vector shall enable the aircraft to intercept at an angle not greater than 30 degrees. This prevents overshooting the localizer and ensures a smooth capture.
5tzgGuZrorV2fZHm0SR0: Work from track to compass in order. True heading = true track minus right drift = 352 - 10 = 342. Magnetic heading = true heading plus west variation = 342 + 11 = 353. Compass heading = magnetic heading minus deviation = 353 - (-5) = 358.
5uImuugwe3CfKbHYsjjI: Acceleration errors appear on east and west headings, where the pendulous magnet system is displaced by the fore-and-aft force. In the northern hemisphere acceleration gives an apparent turn to the north and deceleration an apparent turn to the south - remembered as ANDS.
5vBKBxuKnZ6lrmC3E09p: In the current ICAO AIP structure, SIGMET information is found in the GEN part (GEN 3.5 Meteorological Services). Note that some older question banks reference a separate MET section, but the modern three-part AIP structure (GEN/ENR/AD) places this in GEN.
5vPGH8PzuuQK9WYvsenV: ICAO grades icing in three intensities. Light icing is no problem unless encountered for more than an hour, so no change of heading or level is needed. Moderate icing makes even short encounters potentially hazardous and a diversion is desirable. Severe icing requires immediate diversion because de-icing and anti-icing equipment can no longer cope.
5wc0kBTAMUxcJjqTnH2M: A positively cambered aerofoil carries more of its lift toward the rear of the chord, so even when the net lift is zero the pressure distribution still produces a couple. That couple is nose-down, so Cm at CL = 0 is negative - and because it is essentially independent of angle of attack it is a fixed characteristic of the section. A symmetrical aerofoil has Cm0 = 0, and a reflexed section can achieve a positive value.
5yJybK8XJydU0jiTN0XS: The wind from 030 is about 55 degrees off the port bow of the 085 course, giving a crosswind of 100 x sin55 = 82 kt from the left, so the heading must be turned about 10 degrees left to 075. The headwind component is 100 x cos55 = 57 kt, so the groundspeed is about 405 kt and 265 NM takes about 39 minutes.
5yMynINMivrmXLLWFD9c: When a DME is associated with a VOR the two share one identifier, transmitted in sequence: the VOR ident at 1020 Hz several times, with the DME ident at the higher pitch of 1350 Hz coming up roughly once every 30 seconds. So in any 40 second period the DME ident is heard once. The higher pitch is how you confirm the DME, and not just the VOR, is serviceable.
5yN2X8VzIfPpapbqqmtS: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that a Category I precision approach lighting system consists of a row of lights on the extended centreline extending 900 m from the threshold, with a crossbar at 300 m from the threshold. Category II/III systems are more elaborate with additional crossbars and barrettes.
5yvy9BWBdDKMT6Ch2xJJ: Use the 1-in-60 rule twice. Track error = 4 NM over 60 NM run = 4 degrees. Closing angle = 4 NM over the 120 NM remaining = 2 degrees. Turning by the track error alone only parallels the intended track, so the total alteration to reach B is 4 + 2 = 6 degrees right.
5zKSkGUoil800OsEaZyC: Long range cruise deliberately gives up 1% of the maximum specific range in exchange for the HIGHER of the two speeds that deliver 99% of it. That buys typically 3-5% more speed for a 1% fuel penalty, which is almost always worth it once crew time, maintenance and schedule are costed in. Maximum range cruise itself is rarely flown, because near the optimum the specific range curve is very flat.
5zMBWWOT4ZRb2Miz7yNv: VMO is a structural limit set by the dynamic pressure the airframe can take, and dynamic pressure is what calibrated airspeed measures - so the limit is fixed in CAS and shown to the pilot as a fixed indicated speed regardless of altitude. MMO takes over higher up, where compressibility rather than dynamic pressure sets the limit.
5zRAJZGTH2DWCTg6pkYl: The flight deck extinguisher must be halon or an equivalent agent, because most flight deck fires involve live electrical equipment: halon is non-conductive, leaves no residue on instruments and does not obscure the panel the way powder or foam would.
5zmkRU54v903sVvJ3sJB: High manifold pressure with low RPM means a large charge burnt slowly with the crankshaft turning slowly, so peak cylinder pressures are high and are applied for a long part of the stroke - the classic over-square condition that produces detonation and bearing damage. Power changes are made RPM first up, throttle first down.
60slsJxQpBs9tuFKZqD5: The rate of pressure change is metered through a calibrated leak, and the viscosity of the air through that leak varies with temperature. A bimetallic element in the capsule linkage compensates, and in doing so it sets the instrument's lag characteristic - the deliberate delay that gives the vertical speed indicator its steady but slow indication.
60wRs190wqWs70yckCRx: A constant speed propeller is worked by engine oil: the governor meters boosted oil to a piston in the hub which acts against a spring and the blades' own counterweights and centrifugal twisting moment. 61Z0s1McpwxU5ajiAJl1: Aerodromes use a long-grass policy - keeping grass around 15-20 cm - precisely because flocking birds avoid it: they cannot see approaching predators and cannot forage easily. 61kiZNzy6o0H2ED5Vh9S: Stress affects all four. 62VBgTWrdyXaLZdL4IOs: Selye distinguished eustress - the moderate, motivating arousal that improves performance - from distress, the harmful state produced when stressors are too intense or too prolonged for the individual's coping resources. Stressors are the causes rather than the perception, so the state perceived in the question is distress.
63N3f4CeRCtG3jcBlibb: The lateral axis runs spanwise, from wingtip to wingtip, and rotation about it is PITCHING, controlled by the elevator. For completeness: rolling is rotation about the longitudinal axis (nose to tail, controlled by ailerons) and yawing is rotation about the normal or vertical axis (controlled by the rudder).
63emiVC8fj4viZWVwnKm: GPS satellites sit at about 20 200 km in a 12 hour orbit, half a sidereal day, so each satellite passes over the same point on the earth twice a day. 658PRlNVLZjH3htc5G6T: A missed approach procedure has three phases: initial (the transition from approach to climb), intermediate (the climb to a safe altitude), and final (the segment to the missed approach holding fix or point). These correspond to the go-around, climb, and routing phases.
659UtssGIGCLYgwpp7cv: Cone density and therefore visual acuity are high only in the fovea, an area covering about one degree of the visual field. Effective lookout therefore means moving the eyes in short steps and pausing at each, so the fovea is brought onto successive small sectors of sky.
65KUF9GMeECAKlYjz4ty: Forecast upper winds, on significant weather charts, wind/temperature charts and in flight documentation, are always given relative to TRUE north and in knots. Only ATC-passed surface winds (for take-off and landing) are given relative to magnetic north, because they are being compared directly with a runway direction.
667Sj5AvltP4qDsHJVf1: VOR operates in the VHF band, 108.0 to 117.975 MHz, sharing the lower part of that range with the ILS localiser. VHF gives line-of-sight propagation, so VOR range depends on altitude and terrain, and the signal is free of the sky-wave errors that plague NDBs in the MF band.
66pJ36RZhohJhbmZ7Gyj: Downlink is from the aircraft down to the ground - position reports, ACARS messages, maintenance data. Uplink is the other way, from the ground station to the aircraft. The convention is the aircraft's point of view throughout.
68PNJoOD37e0V4cvYcWI: The eyewall, the ring of towering cumulonimbus immediately surrounding the eye, contains the strongest surface winds, the most violent updraughts and downdraughts, the heaviest precipitation and the lowest pressure gradient scale in the storm. The eye itself is comparatively calm with light winds and often broken cloud, and conditions moderate steadily with distance from the centre.
68etVjSiJOZ5HlX1LFw7: The flight warning system exists to tell the crew what is wrong and what to do about it, so it improves situational awareness (1), presents the required action (3) and prioritises alerts so that the most urgent is presented first (4). It certainly can annunciate aerodynamic limit exceedances, and it does not talk to ATC.
68sbNsAaWRyKaQgPHWSX: CVR regulations permit erasure of information that is more than 30 minutes old, provided there has been no accident or incident requiring preservation. The most recent 30 minutes must always be retained to capture any event that may have just occurred.
6AAbKm3AWI6cu7ju9iW2: Planned time for the first 75 NM at 115 kt is 39 minutes; being 1.5 minutes late makes the actual time about 40.6 minutes, so the actual groundspeed is 75 x 60 / 40.6 = about 111 kt. The remaining 175 NM then takes about 95 minutes, giving a total of about 2 h 15 min from 0900, so the revised ETA is 1115 UTC.
6AKhmNL2zzXzRdvTkRnO: The wind from 340 is 37 degrees off the port bow of the 017 course, giving a crosswind of 30 x sin37 = 18 kt from the left. The wind correction angle is therefore about 2 degrees to the left, which is written as negative. The headwind component is 30 x cos37 = 24 kt, so the groundspeed is about 396 kt.
6AX6IKNVLw5v3hUr7xBG: The vestibular system senses angular and linear accelerations; conflict arises where the eyes report one thing and the inner ear another. That covers false impressions of aircraft attitude (statement 1) and of rotation (statement 4), such as the leans and the graveyard spiral. The autokinetic illusion and misjudged size and distance are purely visual phenomena with no vestibular component.
6AXu84bz3qs5ZbDk8m24: There is no fixed protection time. The holdover a Type II fluid gives depends on its concentration (the fluid/water mix), on the outside air temperature and on the type and intensity of precipitation, and holdover tables are published for exactly those variables. Once holdover time is exceeded the aeroplane must be de-iced and treated again.
6AhVhaliyz79MSPTsU0w: Breathing 100% oxygen removes nitrogen from the alveolar gas, so alveolar oxygen partial pressure becomes ambient pressure minus water vapour and CO2. That keeps alveolar oxygen at the value normally found around 10,000 ft until roughly 40,000 ft, which is where hypoxia symptoms reappear. Above that, 100% oxygen alone is insufficient and positive-pressure breathing is required.
6BRsKEpZrbBd0lj2suJ0: GPWS Mode 4 warns of unsafe terrain clearance when the aircraft is not configured for landing - gear not down (4) or flaps not in the landing setting (3). Deviation from a selected altitude is the altitude alerting system, which is a separate function driven by the barometric altitude and the selected level.
6Bjz89XOICGQqFjhmDbP: Noise abatement procedures on landing exist, but ICAO is explicit that they must not deny the crew the deceleration devices that keep the landing safe - the use of reverse thrust is not prohibited. Noise relief on arrival comes from things like continuous descent, later flap and gear extension, and preferred routings.
6CWzlxYcRk4oKD7jKXxi: For carriage of a person in the custody of law enforcement, no more than one person considered to be in the maximum risk category may be carried on a flight, and the person must have at least two armed law enforcement escorts. This ensures adequate control of high-risk individuals.
6E1szbKMznV4XI3PXswS: Ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere, with peak density around 20-25 km. This matters operationally because long-range aircraft cruising in the lower stratosphere can ingest ozone; catalytic converters in the air-conditioning packs break it down, since ozone irritates the eyes and respiratory tract.
6EKjtbrUfuqUIpVTKVfZ: Item 19 endurance is the time the TOTAL USABLE fuel on board will keep the aircraft flying, reserve included. It is not the planned flight time and it is not reduced by the reserve, because its purpose is to tell search and rescue how long the aircraft could possibly stay airborne.
6EfYMjXzf6nuxLELIGBV: With nothing to focus on - clear sky, haze, night - the eye relaxes to its resting focus of roughly one to two metres, so distant traffic is imaged out of focus and is not seen. The cure is to give the eye something real to focus on: scan in short deliberate steps and periodically fix on a wingtip, a cloud edge or the horizon to reset accommodation.
6G3GM8dM2oMRKi7zYh8U: A thermocouple's output depends on the temperature difference between its junctions, and with the cold junction held at or compensated to a fixed reference the EMF becomes a linear function of the hot junction temperature alone - E = K x Th. That linearity is what lets the output drive a simple movement scaled in degrees.
6GtcnEzptQycd6Ti2He2: Displacement is the volume swept by all the pistons in one revolution: the area of one piston multiplied by the length of its stroke gives the swept volume of one cylinder, and multiplying by the number of cylinders gives the engine's total. Cylinder length and bore alone would give a volume including the combustion chamber, which is not swept.
6Hh3rO3tUezamKtRVoaR: Heavy rain and hail can quench the flame in a gas turbine, and at high ambient temperatures there is no icing risk to justify anti-ice. The precaution is therefore continuous ignition: the igniters are selected on so that any flameout is immediately relit.
6Hr702NbcGbA1O3jRAKP: Henry's Law states that the amount of a gas dissolved in a liquid is proportional to the partial pressure of that gas above the liquid. When cabin pressure falls, dissolved nitrogen comes out of solution and forms bubbles in blood and tissue, producing the bends, creeps, chokes and neurological symptoms of decompression sickness.
6IMDoAr9yL17tI6JTQ52: A shock wave is an abrupt compression: the flow decelerates violently and much of its kinetic energy is converted into heat, so the static temperature RISES sharply across the wave. The local speed of sound depends only on temperature (a is proportional to the square root of absolute temperature), so it increases. Static pressure and density also rise, while total pressure falls - the energy lost as wave drag.
6Ihh8LXVH0bwLwmzAo7k: Lower atmospheric pressure means lower air density. Less dense air reduces the thrust the engine can produce and reduces the lift generated at any given TAS, so the aeroplane must accelerate to a higher TAS before it will fly - the take-off distance lengthens. The same thrust loss cuts the excess thrust available for climbing, so the initial climb gradient degrades too. Both effects work against the aeroplane.
6KVfzn4XhX3Bwi47a3wl: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies a 3-minute wake turbulence separation when a Light aircraft takes off behind a Medium aircraft using the same runway. This accounts for the vortex generated by the Medium aircraft that lingers over the runway.
6L1L8maDQbVLqX7V0IUd: A locator is a low-powered NDB, typically 15 to 25 W with a range of 10 to 25 NM, installed at an ILS marker or as an approach aid. So it differs from an en-route NDB in operational use and in transmitter power. It uses the same LF/MF band and appears on the same ADF/RMI display, so items 3 and 4 are not differences.
6LVNOg7Oo4yxKTZmQoQ4: PANS-OPS refers MDA/MDH to aerodrome elevation, except where the threshold of the runway in use is more than 2 m (7 ft) BELOW the aerodrome elevation, in which case the threshold elevation is used instead. The exception exists so the obstacle clearance is not eroded on a runway that sits in a dip.
6LdJumwsIMtfKaMqChPL: Full acclimatisation to a hot climate takes roughly two weeks, during which sweating starts earlier, becomes more copious and loses less salt. 6M2czfiEF7MT5kdX8PxV: Hypoxia tolerance and the symptoms produced vary widely between individuals, and vary in the same individual from day to day with fitness, fatigue, smoking and alcohol. That is why each pilot's own symptom pattern, learned in a chamber, is only a rough guide. No tolerance is built up by repeated exposure, and carbon monoxide reduces oxygen carriage rather than protecting the brain.
6MgUrxiKMy68g3W3D7BT: Statement 1 holds because quick-donning masks are mandatory above 25 000 ft and FL260 is above it. Statement 2 is wrong - the cabin altitude warning is set at 10 000 ft, not 13 000 ft - and statement 4 is wrong because first-aid oxygen is sized on 2% of the passengers, which for 150 passengers is three, not two.
6NzVAkG2XF7T9ee7yXDq: A series of green flashes from the control tower to an aircraft on the ground means the aircraft is cleared to taxi. It does not constitute a take-off clearance. A steady green light would mean cleared for take-off.
6O1tsguDebb90gEJtQvY: The vertex of a great circle lies 90 degrees of longitude from where it crosses the equator, and its latitude is 90 minus the track angle at the equator: 90 - 35 = 55 degrees. The track is northeasterly, so the vertex is in the northern hemisphere and 90 degrees east of 030W, i.e. 55N 060E.
6O2PfN4eNt7VJqpCHWTQ: A rate gyro has a single gimbal - one degree of freedom - so it can only precess about that one axis, and the resulting precession is resisted by a spring, giving a deflection proportional to the applied rate. 6OGGABwBFXZypC3Eb656: A diesel has no throttle butterfly and no mixture control: air is always drawn in unrestricted and power is set purely by how much fuel is injected (2 and 3). 6OcROEY9ItW26r4dywLT: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all recognised decision biases: availability from personal experience distorts risk perception, confirmation bias makes us seek evidence supporting a decision already taken, and group norms shape individual choices. 6P0wnqUlwLo1W1qlSAOj: Outside designated ATS routes, significant points in Item 15 must not normally be more than 30 minutes flying time or 370 km (200 NM) apart, whichever gives the closer spacing. The purpose is to keep the filed route trackable by ATC when there are no route designators to follow.
6QNKKZGGg0vLIhR0Sw2U: ICAO Doc 8168 defines a straight departure as one where the initial departure track does not deviate from the extended runway centreline by more than 15 degrees. Beyond 15 degrees, specific turning departure procedures apply with additional obstacle clearance requirements.
6RoJukGWIgMFpTjQTltP: Above 25 000 ft the time of useful consciousness after a rapid decompression is measured in seconds, so the flight crew's masks must be of the quick-donning type - deployable and supplying oxygen with one hand in under 5 seconds without disturbing spectacles.
6RqIiQDE8wRoR68UxaXu: In ICAO flight plan format, the letter Z in box 8 indicates a flight that starts under VFR and changes to IFR en route. Y indicates the reverse (IFR then VFR). I is for pure IFR and V is for pure VFR.
6Rx9JaFBxx1BXD7rsFXX: The boundary layer next to the skin is slowed by friction, so a pitot head immersed in it would sense less than the true total pressure. Mounting it on a mast clear of the surface puts the opening in undisturbed flow, which is what makes the reading valid.
6S9uiJV9DFut9R0t1leW: Both are correct. Reversible controls can be moved by the wind on the ground, so gust locks are needed to prevent the surfaces being slammed against their stops. 6SFJOzonI3SqGKeSgL0P: Air is supplied to the cabin at a roughly constant rate, so the pressure is set by how fast it is allowed to leave. 6T0R90uOhkrlZNK4sr9C: As the aircraft climbs the air thins but a fixed mixture control keeps supplying the same fuel, so the mixture becomes progressively richer. 6T0Z41CbgStsUdHj67gI: At FL370 the time of useful consciousness after an explosive decompression is on the order of 15-20 seconds, so the mask goes on FIRST - before communication, transponder or any attention to the cabin. Nothing else can be achieved by a crew that has lost consciousness.
6U0pOI5hATlkC5shChqg: The two switches are wired in series and both must be made for the trim to run, so a single stuck or shorted switch cannot drive the trim by itself. Trim runaway loads the controls progressively and can become unrecoverable, so the split switch is a simple and effective guard.
6VYKVoxTdNFauQ6NJKpF: Item 15 describes the en-route portion only. The route is filed from the end of the SID to the start of the STAR, and the procedures themselves are assigned by ATC on the day, so neither the SID nor the STAR designator is entered. Filing them would conflict with whatever runway and procedure is actually in use.
6WSCCjjTQb8GsRkFSaBL: The sympathetic fight-or-flight response produces sweating, a dry mouth (salivation is suppressed), dilated pupils, rapid shallow breathing and a raised heart rate and blood pressure. Constricted pupils and a fall in blood pressure belong to the opposite, parasympathetic state, and chest pain is not a normal stress sign.
6XvGS7UqMSBFY8hzU2oD: Halon breaks the chemical chain reaction of combustion, is non-conductive, leaves no residue and needs only a small quantity, which is why it became the standard aircraft agent. Powder is unsuitable on a flight deck because it coats instruments and obscures displays, water is limited to class A material rather than to 'minor' fires, and cargo compartments are protected by halon systems rather than CO2.
6XzpFxF7a4BesubbfLb9: Fire extinguishers, portable oxygen bottles and the chemicals in first-aid kits are all dangerous goods by classification, but they are carried under the exemption for articles required aboard for airworthiness, operating or medical reasons. 6Y16cKx9X8pGs0NWJHIl: An Aeronautical Information Circular (AIC) is a notice containing information on flight safety, air navigation, technical, administrative, or legislative matters, originated by a State's AIS. It is distinct from a NOTAM (time-critical operational changes) and from the AIP (permanent reference information).
6YwHdT7VVND7niShzSqZ: Tolerance to acceleration depends on all four: how large the G is, how long it is sustained, how quickly it is applied (a rapid onset defeats the cardiovascular compensation that a gradual onset allows) and in which axis it acts, since tolerance to +Gz, -Gz and transverse G differ greatly.
6ZxCUUe8P4jMLQPGPKmL: In presbyopia the crystalline lens loses elasticity with age, so the ciliary muscle can no longer make it more convex. The result is a progressive loss of accommodation - the near point recedes - while distance vision is unaffected. The cornea and vitamin A status are not involved.
6a5nXpCNkuj1LuWMA8fq: Short-term (working) memory holds around seven items for roughly 10-20 seconds unless the material is actively rehearsed. This is why a clearance must be written down or read back promptly, and why long strings of numbers must be chunked to be retained at all.
6aEFgcVXIvzMPcw2JR1g: On-condition maintenance replaces a part when its measured condition says it needs replacing, rather than at a fixed interval: oil analysis, borescope inspection, vibration and performance trends are monitored and action is taken when a parameter passes its limit. Hard-time replacement by hours or cycles is the alternative philosophy.
6aEQtI8eZLC5ZC3TiSbw: A hung start is one in which the engine lights but then stabilises below idle, because there is not enough starter assistance for the fuel flow being supplied. Introducing fuel before the starter has brought the compressor to the required speed produces exactly that: combustion begins with too little airflow to accelerate the engine.
6b7RX3AY0jBCk0jvOq4d: Orientation uses all four sources: vision (dominant and the only reliable one in flight), the otolith organs of the utricle and saccule sensing linear acceleration and head tilt, the semicircular canals sensing angular acceleration, and the proprioceptive seat-of-the-pants sense from muscles, joints and pressure receptors. In IMC the last three become unreliable because they cannot distinguish acceleration from gravity.
6cDzUleLnO7LlDrNwv3c: Detonation is spontaneous ignition of the end gas, and anything that raises the temperature or pressure of the charge promotes it - a high cylinder head temperature above all, along with high manifold pressure, a weak mixture and advanced ignition. 6cgoWVAIFMOpgNjPje2f: Convert relative bearings to the TRACK, not the heading, because drift is what the aircraft actually follows: with 10 degrees of right drift the bearings become 45 degrees and then 90 degrees off the track, the classic doubling. True track is 165 - 25W + 10 drift = 150, so the feature bears 060 from the aircraft, and the aircraft bears 240 FROM the feature.
6d5yN7nCfrnfspBn76WO: ICAO Annex 15 requires that prohibited, restricted, and danger areas be identified by the nationality letters assigned to the State for location indicators, followed by the letter P, R, or D and a number. For example, EG D123 identifies a UK danger area.
6dTmxg00USGpHIqbQUjX: Entering W instead of E displaces the INS longitude by twice 139 46.3, which is 279 32.6, equivalent to 80 27.4 in the other direction. 6e4p2oTm9jT8xbPhOorA: HF data link is the slowest, being narrowband and subject to propagation, VHF data link is considerably faster but limited to line of sight, and satellite communication offers the highest data rate along with global coverage. The choice is normally made automatically by the communications management unit.
6ezGpg6gojWKcKN4siIK: Acceleration errors appear on east and west headings, where the pendulous magnet system is displaced by the fore-and-aft force. In the northern hemisphere acceleration produces an apparent turn to the north and deceleration one to the south - the mnemonic ANDS.
6f4quCu8eK90dA6PrB67: A diffuser is a diverging passage, so the air slows down and its kinetic energy is converted into static pressure. In a centrifugal compressor the impeller does the work by flinging the air outwards at high velocity, and the diffuser then turns that velocity into the pressure rise the engine actually needs.
6h0Cmyv5qJdxKDSZMH9P: Flutter is a coupling between the surface's bending and torsional modes driven by the aerodynamic load, and it is provoked when the surface's centre of gravity lies behind its hinge line. Mass balancing - adding weight ahead of the hinge - moves the centre of gravity forward and breaks the coupling.
6h8yiecTQeHbBEmpSTlb: GPS is a passive, one-way ranging system. The receiver measures how long a satellite's coded transmission took to arrive, multiplies by the speed of light and obtains a pseudo-range, which places the aircraft on a sphere centred on that satellite. Four such measurements resolve latitude, longitude, altitude and the receiver clock error. The aircraft never transmits.
6hwRZWmmKHAVBwGrRG2U: The most severe airframe icing occurs where supercooled water droplets are most abundant, in the band from 0 C to about -10 C or -15 C. Interpolating the sounding, 0 C lies near 10,600 ft and FL150 is around -8 C, squarely in that band. FL80 is above freezing so no icing occurs, and FL180 (-14 C) and FL220 (about -22 C) are increasingly glaciated, giving lighter rime rather than severe clear ice.
6iAl1WRM5lNWDnBT0fPl: Rated power is the maximum the engine is approved to deliver continuously at a specified RPM and manifold pressure - the figure the engine can sustain indefinitely without damage. Take-off power is higher but time-limited, and critical power is not a defined term.
6iU5k5PlocgXfObxHdii: Information about parachute jumping sites is published in the Airport/Facility Directory (now called the Chart Supplement in the US). NOTAMs cover temporary activity, but the permanent listing of designated sites is in the directory.
6j9p0NsNHsBZDpmzK0bx: Entry into NAT MNPS airspace requires a specific ATC clearance, containing the route, level and Mach number, and the aircraft and crew must hold MNPS approval. Nothing about the type of operation changes that requirement.
6jViUxNLKWCXwpXy2zO2: VLE is the maximum speed at which the aircraft may be flown with the gear already extended, limited by the loads on the doors and legs in the airflow. VLO, a separate and usually lower speed, is the limit for operating the gear - moving it up or down.
6jf01QlUxTP6Dp50M8oa: Automation offloads work to the machine, so the pilot's remaining actions become highly routine and are executed at the skill-based level with little conscious monitoring. Mistakes, by contrast, are failures of planning at the rule- or knowledge-based level.
6juTLMawlR78XPczVGk9: Altitude alerting works against the selected altitude: it gives an advance warning as the aircraft approaches the level (1) and an alert if the aircraft subsequently departs from it (5). Altitude loss after take-off and configuration warnings belong to the GPWS.
6kBW5obDK8hl4zL2SImz: IAC charts show obstacles, OCA/OCH values, DME frequencies, and other operationally critical data. 6krQZVHqRIsBa23lCWoE: An open-circuit voltage tells you little, because a nearly flat battery can show a normal voltage until current is drawn. Applying a known load and comparing the on-load with the off-load voltage reveals the internal resistance and therefore the true state of charge - a large drop under load means a discharged or failing battery.
6kw8wNrKaes0zREFSdNZ: An underspeed means the drive is failing to hold the generator at its rated speed, so the output frequency is out of tolerance and the machine must be taken off the bus. 6mRH0DyauhhaEYe3L4fp: Circling minima by category start at 1500 m visibility and an MDH of 400 ft for Category A. Category B is 1600 m, C is 2400 m and D is 3600 m.
6nOEVwtE5eVY2sdNCCFj: At altitude the reduced ambient pressure allows nitrogen that was dissolved in body tissues and fluids at ground level to come out of solution as bubbles, in accordance with Henry's Law. 6nOlNclAYbeyOqkfkB2R: In a strapdown system nothing is gimballed: the accelerometers and laser gyros are bolted to the airframe and therefore measure along the aircraft's own axes. 6o7wCbsXUBX2iNudyESM: JAR-FCL requires successful completion of multi-crew cooperation (MCC) training before a pilot can obtain the first type rating on a multi-pilot aeroplane. MCC training teaches crew resource management and coordination skills specific to multi-crew operations.
6pYW8rWnQMej85PJ1fnf: The level offset follows the vertical separation regime you are entering. 6qkaptJBkf7HMGJAGDbv: A big fan at full thrust with no forward speed is drawing far more air than the intake can capture cleanly, and a crosswind makes the flow round the intake lip separate on one side. 6rATg478cDarJwE4vtE3: V2 must give an adequate margin above the stall with an engine failed, and the required margin depends on how much the aeroplane can reduce its power-on stall speed.
