V2 must also be at least 1.1 VMCA.
6slUuH8FfNZl4b81twwK: All three describe the same function from different angles: running the stabiliser cancels the elevator hinge moment the autopilot is holding (1), which unloads the servo actuator (2), and it leaves the aeroplane in trim so that the pilot takes over a balanced aircraft at disconnect (3).
6tMudOGed3y1Ogja9DT9: Leading-edge ice reduces CLmax and, critically, lowers the angle of attack at which the wing stalls. The highest angle of attack of the whole take-off occurs at the END of rotation, just as the aircraft is unstuck at minimum speed - so that is where the reduced stalling angle bites first and hardest. In the subsequent climb the angle of attack is lower and the margin correspondingly greater.
6ugebKVo8bfObBBnnwvL: A ring laser gyro has no spinning mass, so there is virtually no spin-up time and it is insensitive to g loading, shock and vibration. It DOES suffer lock-in at very low input rates, which is precisely why dither is fitted, so any option claiming freedom from lock-in is wrong.
6upC5GmnhD11kwkXyptb: VY is the speed for the best RATE of climb - the greatest height gain per unit TIME, found where excess POWER is greatest. VX is the speed for the best ANGLE of climb, the greatest height gain per unit DISTANCE, found where excess THRUST is greatest, and is the speed used for obstacle clearance. V2 is the take-off safety speed.
6vZz6Dc0rVnNatRuDMEN: Bonding straps give static charge a low-resistance path between components so that it drains away steadily to the discharge wicks. Where the bonding is poor the charge builds and jumps across the joint, and each of those small sparks is a burst of radio noise heard as crackle on the receiver.
6vvBI46fEfZahoHHZC9Q: Minimum sink rate is flown at (CL^3/CD^2)max and best glide ANGLE at (CL/CD)max, and the minimum-sink condition always occurs at the lower speed of the two - typically around 76% of the best-glide speed. Fly slower to stay airborne longest; fly faster, at best glide, to travel furthest. Both are TAS relationships and the ordering never reverses between aeroplane types.
6vwExMrsi7G7rhEI1CUr: A gyro axis fixed in space defines a plane through the aircraft and the Earth's centre, and the track it traces on the surface is a great circle. Only apparent wander (earth rate) and drift disturb that; remove them and the constant gyro heading is a great circle path, which is why grid navigation uses gyro steering in polar regions.
6xXEFTv6kEbKYkOD4MGg: With runway edge lighting, centreline lighting and multiple RVR readings, the take-off minimum for Category A, B and C aeroplanes falls to 150 m RVR (200 m for Category D). Lesser facilities give 200 m, 250 m or 500 m, and low visibility procedures must be in force for the lowest values.
6xrvkp1hAh2YuQMvYTjo: A hydraulic fuse senses either an abnormal flow rate or an excessive volume passed and shuts off that branch, so a burst line downstream cannot empty the reservoir. The affected service is lost but the rest of the system, and the fluid, are preserved.
6yXXQ4FFM54vRpUrwiOd: At 60 degrees off the runway the headwind component is V x cos60 = 0.5V and the crosswind is V x sin60 = 0.87V. Needing at least 10 kt of headwind gives V of at least 20 kt; a 35 kt crosswind limit gives V no more than 35 / 0.87 = about 40 kt. So the wind speed must lie between 20 kt and 40 kt.
6yeTsZdbxe1tfxUZpkiL: Clear ice forms when large supercooled droplets freeze slowly on impact, so the water flows back over the surface before it freezes and builds a dense, transparent, tenacious layer. It is heavy, adds significant weight and drag, distorts the aerofoil section, spreads well aft of the protected leading edges, and is hard for de-icing boots to shed. Rime ice, by contrast, is opaque, brittle and light because it traps air.
6zPLDtcs8qsX31l4JnxE: The VOR pointer is servo-driven to the correct bearing ON the compass card, so with the card frozen the value read at the tail is still the valid radial: 135. What is lost is relative bearing, because that needs the true heading of the aircraft, and the frozen card no longer supplies it. Remember the head of the needle gives QDM and the tail gives the radial.
6zVmewykP3GPldcAIYr5: A technical landing is a stop made for refuelling, maintenance, or crew change without embarking or disembarking passengers or cargo commercially. This is the Second Freedom of the Air — the right to land in another state for non-traffic purposes.
70MpYgChfLuXNfLnRr0P: A thermocouple is two dissimilar metals joined at the point whose temperature is to be measured. The junction generates an EMF proportional to the temperature difference between it and the reference junction, and because it produces its own voltage it needs no power supply - which is why it suits turbine and cylinder head measurement.
71nJD5B35WOYBmFq9PXy: V1 is a decision speed, and a decision to continue is only meaningful if the aeroplane can actually be kept straight on the runway after the failure - which requires V1 to be at least VMCG, the minimum control speed on the ground. At the other end, V1 may not exceed VR. Together these bracket V1 between the speed at which control is assured and the speed at which rotation begins.
71sYFqepBi6DbOX00Aqc: Trace elements - iron, zinc, iodine, selenium and others - are needed in milligram or microgram quantities and are spread across many foods, so a varied, balanced diet supplies them naturally. Concentrating on one food group leaves gaps, and supplements risk excess, since several trace elements are toxic in overdose.
72OIEX3ZPFfNReq9wn1Q: In RVSM MNPS airspace the vertical minimum is 1000 ft between FL290 and FL410, and the standard lateral spacing between organised tracks is 60 NM. 500 ft is never a separation minimum - it appears only in the contingency offset procedure.
72v6CNwHUAaaLmID1K9R: The iris muscles change the diameter of the pupil, which controls how much light reaches the retina - constricting in bright light and dilating in the dark. The cornea and lens focus the image and the ciliary body alters lens shape for accommodation; none of them regulates light quantity.
73MYcmiqgpk6TFHChpWV: Track east from 100E to 140W passes the vertex at the mid-longitude 160E, where the track is 090T. Convergency from there to 180 is 20 x sin85 = about 20 degrees, and in the southern hemisphere an eastbound great circle track decreases, so the true track at 180 is about 070. Grid track on a south polar chart gridded on Greenwich is true track plus east longitude, so 070 + 180 = 250G.
73kTtHoMMj4gUMzcbXfx: The starting sequence is starter, then ignition, then fuel: the igniters must already be firing when fuel reaches the nozzles, or the fuel simply collects in the engine and produces a wet start. Note that none of the four options here states a correct proposition - the starter pressure affects EGT the opposite way, a hot start comes from fuel introduced at too LOW an rpm, and a seized starter prevents a start altogether - so this row is defective.
75eT8wUSAXudwSWVA82x: The certification scale runs minor, major, hazardous, catastrophic. A major failure produces a significant reduction in safety margins, physical discomfort to the occupants and a significant increase in crew workload - but the crew can still be relied upon to cope. Distress that impairs their ability defines the hazardous case.
764hMqfOJWeuVTw3kvrA: Category II is a precision approach with a decision height below 200 ft but not lower than 100 ft, and an RVR not less than 300 m. Category I stops at 200 ft, and anything below 100 ft DH - or with no DH at all - is Category III.
76CNT6BpibiGXdQ2Uhxd: Amber is the caution colour: it requires immediate crew awareness and subsequent corrective action, but not immediate action. Red is reserved for warnings needing immediate action, and green, white, cyan or magenta carry advisory and status information.
76Ic4pcwBjVotS85dyYg: A temperature-dewpoint spread of less than 1 C means the air is effectively saturated, so condensation is occurring or about to occur at the surface. That produces fog or very low cloud. Pilots use the spread as a quick indicator: 3 C or less with clear skies, light wind and a long night is the classic radiation fog set-up.
77TJsB3R86XVZEVtQCf6: Accident analysis repeatedly shows that the crew possessed the handling skills and the information needed but made a poor decision - continuing into deteriorating weather, pressing on with an unstable approach, mishandling a minor technical problem. Judgement, not stick-and-rudder skill or maintenance, is the dominant deficiency.
77YYA0IWw2NbgJtVg0XJ: Strapdown means exactly that - the sensors are fixed to the airframe, so accelerations are measured along the aircraft's own pitch, roll and yaw axes. The computer keeps a running attitude solution from the gyros and uses it to transform those accelerations into earth axes.
781XpeD588ZI5NQlQhYg: The stall is a matter of angle of attack, and the angle at which it occurs depends on the configuration - so the computer needs the measured angle of attack (2) and the flap or slat position (3). Mass, temperature and altitude are not needed, which is exactly why an angle-of-attack based warning is superior to a speed-based one.
78bA6tuzNltk3dbPH7d5: Moving the CG aft shortens the moment arm to the tailplane, so a given elevator deflection generates more pitching moment and less stick force is needed to produce a given g - manoeuvre stability, measured as stick force per g, falls. Beyond the aft limit that figure drops below the certified minimum, so the aeroplane becomes dangerously easy to over-stress and gives the pilot almost no force cue that it is happening.
79Tp5kHUdyADxHTinl7j: Both are correct. Thinner air at altitude means less mass flow and therefore less thrust available. It also means less drag for a given TAS and a more efficient operating point, so specific fuel consumption falls slightly - which is why jets cruise as high as their weight allows.
79lrwrSCUqWE4gCPRMGT: The earth distance along the 37N parallel between meridians 5 degrees apart is 5 x 60 x cos37 = 300 x 0.799 = 240 NM = 444 000 m = 44 400 000 cm. Scale = 9 / 44 400 000, which is about 1 : 4 900 000, so approximately 1 : 5 000 000. Forgetting the cosine of latitude is what produces the 1 : 6 000 000 distractor.
7AE1UmCFVRz3XB5nvYVu: Cumuliform cloud forms in unstable air where vigorous updraughts carry droplets upward, allowing them to grow large by collision and coalescence. Large droplets freeze slowly on impact and produce clear ice; the vertical motion gives turbulence; and precipitation falls as showers of limited horizontal extent. Stratiform cloud in stable air has the opposite set: small droplets, little turbulence, continuous widespread rain and rime ice.
7Aca5xhsemje0IQZxFKk: Acceleration and deceleration errors arise because the pendulous magnet system is displaced fore and aft, and that displacement only produces a turning moment when the magnet lies east-west. On a northerly heading the magnet is aligned with the acceleration, so there is no turning moment and no apparent turn.
7BdxtFCNPXAU3Qjkj1Ik: Cylinder head temperature is measured with a thermocouple - a washer or bayonet of two dissimilar metals fitted under a spark plug or into the head - because it generates its own EMF and needs no power, and because it copes with the temperature range involved.
7Biyzt3zvz4RqkughZpT: Polar charts use the polar stereographic projection: meridians are straight lines radiating from the pole, scale is very nearly constant over a wide area around it, and a straight line is close enough to a great circle to be flown as one. A Direct Mercator cannot even show the pole, and a gnomonic is not conformal.
7BzyGarICnZdLrPIIGHj: With altitude the falling density means a given indicated airspeed corresponds to an ever-higher true airspeed, and in TAS terms both VX and VY increase. In IAS terms they move toward each other - VX rising slightly and VY falling - until they meet at the absolute ceiling, where the only remaining climb speed produces zero rate of climb. The two framings are often confused, so note which the question is using.
7DPCPvIQzJJyg5lAyGaV: The primary area of an instrument approach segment is a defined area symmetrically disposed about the nominal flight track in which full obstacle clearance is provided. The secondary area flanks the primary area and provides reduced (tapering) obstacle clearance.
7DpvFCxvFoX6U8dSmECC: A constant-speed unit works by sensing rpm and adjusting blade angle to hold the selected value. Medium turbulence produces small, transient changes in the airflow through the disc and hence small rpm excursions, so the governor responds with correspondingly small blade angle changes. The whole point of the system is that the pitch changes are gentle and continuous, never large or abrupt.
7ELAwC6L8NZvLUAsacbt: Bonding ties every metallic part of the airframe together at a low resistance so that static charge, lightning current and equipment return currents all have a defined path. Without it charge builds at joints and discharges as sparks, which is both a radio interference problem and an ignition hazard near fuel.
7FkpxG2KxFNHdNGbipMK: The flight crew system uses gaseous oxygen from high pressure cylinders, because the supply must be available immediately, repeatedly and for as long as the descent takes. Chemical generators, which are used for passengers, run once for a fixed period and cannot be shut off.
7GLZQ9oGWERS77WZzk0n: Isogonals join points of equal magnetic variation. Isoclinals join points of equal dip, isogrives join points of equal grivation (the angle between grid north and magnetic north), and isotachs are lines of equal wind speed on a meteorological chart.
7HaEG7I8dLvwFjQS8abA: ISA at FL330 is 15 - (33 x 2) = -51C, so ISA+15 gives an actual temperature of -36C = 237 K. The local speed of sound is 38.94 x root(T) = 38.94 x 15.4 = about 600 kt, so the Mach number is 487 / 600 = 0.81. Note that the speed of sound depends only on temperature, not on altitude or pressure.
7IJmPNh2EkrfzPlzxxyY: ICAO Annex 18, 'The Safe Transport of Dangerous Goods by Air', is the governing document, with operational detail in the Technical Instructions (Doc 9284). The Washington Convention (CITES) concerns endangered species, not hazardous materials.
7Jb5H8CkYQNH2BHo20IG: An increase in surface wind strengthens mechanical turbulence, which mixes the saturated surface layer upward through a deeper column. If it lifts the fog clear of the ground it becomes low stratus; if the mixing is strong enough it dissipates the fog entirely. Surface cooling, increasing stability and a low-level inversion all reinforce fog rather than clear it.
7K0cWlWoWEkP8MGe3OxE: A lapse rate of 1 C per 100 m is exactly the dry adiabatic lapse rate (3 C per 1000 ft). An unsaturated parcel displaced vertically in that environment cools or warms at exactly the same rate as its surroundings, so it always has the same temperature and density as the ambient air and neither returns nor continues: neutral stability for dry air. For saturated air the same layer would be unstable, because a saturated parcel cools more slowly.
7KtryPmPtsuJNlAmlBA0: Radiation fog is shallow because it is produced by cooling from the ground upward through a light-wind, stable, inversion-capped layer. Typical depths are 100-1000 ft, averaging about 500 ft. That is why the sky is often visible vertically through it while horizontal visibility at the surface is close to zero, and why it lifts into low stratus so readily as the wind picks up.
7LANuZJUsydnf2YLFjFJ: In the SHELL model, Software means the non-physical part of the system - checklists, manuals, procedures, symbology and computer logic. A pilot working through a checklist is therefore a Liveware-Software interface. Hardware would be the switches and displays, Environment the surroundings, and Liveware-Liveware the interaction with other people.
7MGjSY6SXYx05K4sc2MK: Convergency = change of longitude x sine of the mean latitude = 7 x sin60 = about 6 degrees. The flight is westbound in the southern hemisphere, where the great circle track INCREASES as longitude decreases, so the track at B is about 6 degrees greater than at A.
7McKrUQhKhqcK17VABvz: Convert to true first: 120(M) with 17W variation gives 103(T), because west variation is subtracted from a magnetic heading. The island lies 15 degrees left of the nose, so its true bearing from the aircraft is 103 - 15 = 088.
7N64lFaDTtvS1ARmL0i3: The best lift-to-drag ratio occurs at a fixed angle of attack and therefore a fixed lift coefficient, whatever the mass. A heavier aeroplane needs more lift at that same CL, and since lift depends on 1/2 rho V2 S CL, the only way to get it is to fly FASTER. So the best-glide speed increases with mass. The glide ANGLE, however, is unchanged - the heavier aeroplane covers the same distance, just more quickly.
7OMwgjryedu90dAnEA1p: The information-processing chain starts with a physical stimulus acting on a sense organ - sensory stimulation - which is briefly held in sensory memory. Only then does selective attention pick out part of that input, after which perception interprets it and recognition matches it against stored knowledge.
7OZB2wsfHHjgdUtlWaRl: Hydraulic power gives the force needed to retract heavy legs against the airflow, with precise sequencing of doors, locks and legs and simple free-fall reversion. Electrical actuation appears on some smaller types and pneumatic operation is rare.
7Og5JP9xCAuG1MxTdppI: On a polar stereographic chart convergence equals the full change of longitude, so the angle between the local meridian at 100E and the 180 meridian the grid is aligned to is 80 degrees. Applying that 80 degrees to a grid course of 280 degrees gives a true course of 000 degrees - the aeroplane is tracking straight up the 100E meridian toward the equator.
7OsoYw3IA40LYyVVsjXv: A quick donning mask is designed to be fitted with one hand in five seconds and incorporates a microphone, so the pilot can continue to communicate on radio and interphone while wearing it. That is what allows a decompression drill to be flown as a crew.
7OyubsogE9FN0hkm7Im0: An INS flies the great circle, whose track changes by the convergency of 20 x sin45 = 14 degrees over the leg. The vertex lies at the mid-longitude 020W where the track is 270, so the track is about 263 leaving A and about 277 arriving at B. Westbound in the southern hemisphere the track increases as the flight proceeds.
7POxOrY0VSVMxzVr1whE: Gas temperature at the turbine entry is far too high to measure directly, so the probes are placed downstream - at the high pressure turbine outlet or in the jet pipe - and the reading is used as a representative indication of the internal temperatures. Hence exhaust gas temperature as the limiting parameter.
7PSqFVHGxuIXXlhQeN9O: A radio altimeter measures the actual distance from the aerial to whatever is below, and the calibration is corrected so that it reads the height of the lowest part of the aircraft - the wheels - above the surface, whatever that surface happens to be. It has nothing to do with sea level or with the runway specifically.
7Ptgmkw5Ig0cBsI4EZhH: A horizontal white dumbbell with a black bar across each circular portion, displayed in the signal area, means aircraft are required to land and take off on runways only, but other ground manoeuvres (taxiing) need not be confined to runways and taxiways — they may use other paved or suitable surfaces.
7Q18quEnrYezIlXCC9lL: Convert to true first: 355(M) with 15E variation gives 010(T). The island is 30 degrees right of the nose, so it bears 040(T) from the aircraft. The question asks for the bearing of the AIRCRAFT FROM the island, which is the reciprocal, 040 + 180 = 220 degrees.
7QAsar2fAY49VAHoI2xD: Above about 14,000 ft cabin altitude the passenger masks drop automatically throughout the cabin, for cabin crew and passengers alike. The flight crew masks are not presented automatically - they are stowed ready for quick donning and the pilots must reach for them, which is why the drill begins with masks on.
7QLhy7nxSK5wG2pjA8F6: Stalling speed varies with the square root of weight, so a heavier aeroplane stalls faster. The other effects of added mass are all adverse too: climb gradient and rate are reduced, and endurance and range are shortened because more thrust is needed to sustain flight.
7QaFIX2b1f9kveQ1OwAo: All four reduce the oxygen available to the retina, which is one of the most oxygen-hungry tissues in the body and one of the first to show impairment. Anaemia cuts the haemoglobin available, smoking and any source of carbon monoxide occupy haemoglobin that would otherwise carry oxygen, and altitude hypoxia reduces the supply directly - night vision degrades measurably from around 5,000 ft.
7QfcksPGncXhXilEWuGE: An isolated aerodrome is one for which no destination alternate exists, so the aeroplane must carry additional fuel in place of alternate fuel: for a turbine-engined aeroplane, two hours at normal cruise consumption, computed above the destination. The 30-minute figure belongs to the final reserve, and that is 30 minutes of HOLDING at 1500 ft, not 30 minutes of cruise consumption.
7RdQYyIvPIqwELW14eDp: In mid-summer the Azores high is at its strongest and extends north-east toward Europe, while the Icelandic low is at its weakest and displaced, leaving a shallow low over north-east Canada and Baffin Bay. The pattern reverses in winter, when the Icelandic low deepens sharply and the Azores high retreats south, steepening the gradient and driving the strong westerlies of the North Atlantic track.
7RtSjTIhxu03aiVWBn7h: Local mean time changes by 4 minutes for every degree of longitude, i.e. 1 hour per 15 degrees, and is earlier to the west. 120W is 30 degrees west of 90W, which is 2 hours earlier, so 1400 LMT at 90W is 1200 LMT at 120W.
7RyLEadyAxe9mkK2UgMN: In a stabilised platform the gyros and the accelerometers are mounted together on the same gimballed platform, the gyros holding it fixed in space so that the accelerometers measure in a known frame (1). Two accelerometers, one for each horizontal axis, are the minimum needed to navigate over the earth (4).
7SJ5rHjBC4ysKDnu0NFk: Exceeding VMO or MMO threatens the structure, so it demands immediate corrective action and is annunciated as a warning - red, with an aural alert. A caution, in amber, would imply that action could wait, which at an overspeed it cannot.
7TfP8swE9KC53h3KmAfR: Hydraulic power provides the force needed to retract heavy legs against the airflow, with precise sequencing of doors, locks and legs and simple free-fall reversion in an emergency. Electrical actuation appears on some smaller types and pneumatic operation is rare.
7UPUNT70uYc9fNDpxYVm: A directional gyro must be kept with its spin axis horizontal, so a levelling system senses any departure from the local vertical and drives an erection torque motor which precesses the gyro back. Without it the gyro would drift out of the horizontal and the heading indication would become meaningless.
7UTU5iPzURHOkcgCi7jg: The question asks specifically for physiological responses - bodily changes driven by the sympathetic nervous system. Sweating, a dry mouth and rapid or laboured breathing are all such changes. Anxiety, fear and apprehension are psychological or emotional responses, so any option containing them fails the physiological test.
7W8aDanj80EuKxb9Mrj8: The intensity scales hinge on one word. Moderate turbulence: definite strain against seat belts, unsecured objects dislodged, food service and walking DIFFICULT. Severe turbulence: abrupt large changes in altitude and attitude, occupants forced violently against belts, food service and walking IMPOSSIBLE, and the aircraft may be momentarily out of control. Light turbulence gives only slight, erratic changes.
7W8tap5AejMXlUFt3q4Z: Rate of climb is the climb gradient multiplied by the speed along the path. 100 kt is 100 x 6076 / 60 = about 10,130 ft/min, and 3.3% of that is roughly 330 ft/min. A useful rule of thumb follows: gradient in percent times groundspeed in knots, times about 1.013, gives the rate of climb in feet per minute - so roughly 'percent times knots' is close enough for a mental check.
7WXvco01iuLUsYCDT6eQ: Bonding straps drain static charge steadily to the discharge wicks. Where a bond is broken or high in resistance the charge builds until it jumps the joint, and each of those tiny sparks is heard as a burst of noise on the radio - which is the classic symptom of poor bonding.
7Wf9wxKLNHTRsgpdRSug: In a right turn the outside of the turn is to the LEFT, so a ball displaced left has swung to the outside - the classic SKID, meaning the rate of turn is too high for the bank angle. There are two coordinated fixes: reduce the rate of turn with less right rudder, or match the bank to the rate by rolling in MORE right bank. Of the options offered, more right bank is the coordinating input.
7XBrSKovvsnlHGWVt7hh: Wake vortices are a by-product of lift, so they begin when the wing starts carrying the weight - at rotation - and end when the weight returns to the wheels at touchdown. The take-off roll and the landing roll therefore produce jet blast but not wake turbulence.
7XFbQGRWQMNkxEdHHYL8: In a steady level turn the lift must support the weight and provide the turning force, so L = W / cos(bank), i.e. the load factor n = 1/cos(bank). At 45 degrees, cos 45 = 0.707, so n = 1.41 - a 41% increase in lift. Useful reference points: 30 degrees gives n = 1.15, 45 degrees n = 1.41, and 60 degrees n = 2.0.
7XorvdEuG6fRZub7qk3M: The same angle of attack means the same lift coefficient, and in level flight the lift must still equal the weight. Since L = CL x 1/2 rho V2 S, holding CL and L constant while density FALLS with altitude requires V - the true airspeed - to increase. The indicated airspeed, which is what the dynamic pressure determines, stays the same: this is the basis of flying by IAS at all altitudes.
7YFeb60f4IoB2Qn1fYbd: Above FL250 the time of useful consciousness after a decompression is short enough that a mask must be fitted within seconds, so the flight crew masks must be of the quick-donning type - one hand, five seconds, with the ability to communicate once fitted.
7YpRVSk1rxQf3hkAQwfG: At low rotor speeds the rear compressor stages choke and the front stages stall, because the compressor is far from its design point. Opening bleed valves between the spools dumps flow overboard, unloading the front stages and restoring the stall margin. At high speeds the compressor is near design and the valves are closed.
7avKGBZSCJpeGa9GPleh: Attention is not confined to the channel being consciously monitored: unattended channels are still processed at a low level and personally relevant material - one's own callsign in a stream of other traffic, the cocktail-party effect - breaks through into awareness. Sensation and perception describe the handling of information once it is taken in, not this selective filtering.
7bDU8Di0upeXR1Td6hSS: This is Newton's second law in its rotational form: an unbalanced moment produces an angular acceleration about that axis, just as an unbalanced force produces a linear acceleration. Steady flight - straight and level, or a steady turn or descent - therefore requires the sum of moments about ALL THREE axes to be zero, which is what trimming achieves.
7cDZnBZl4zSwfgS6ILzm: In normal law the longitudinal control is a load factor demand with a pitch rate term (1), the trim runs automatically to give neutral speed stability (2), and pitch and bank attitude are limited with the limits varying with speed and configuration (3). The laws do cover the whole envelope in normal law, degrading only when the required sensor data is lost.
7dCMoSI9SF0FNMVJAHMs: A decreasing headwind is a decreasing-performance shear: the aeroplane's inertia holds its groundspeed, so airspeed falls, lift falls with it and the aeroplane sinks BELOW the climb-out path. This is the dangerous direction of shear, and it is what the escape manoeuvre - full thrust and pitch to the stick shaker - exists for.
7dZYMgEqQgE1cZyjZ880: Radiation fog needs a light wind: enough gentle turbulence to mix the cooling upward through a shallow layer, but not enough to stir it out. Below about 5 kt is the classic requirement. In dead calm the cooling stays right at the surface and produces dew or frost instead of fog, and above roughly 10 kt the mixing lifts the layer into low stratus.
7eLIjF4L5Z6aiNmbqWvJ: Motion sickness arises from conflict between what the eyes report, what the vestibular system reports and what past experience predicts. The resulting symptoms are pallor, sweating, nausea, vomiting and apprehension. It is not an infection and has nothing to do with dissolved gases or reduced pressure.
7eLT8oMK2yJ33wxfXgX2: Assertiveness - stating a position, concern or proposed course of action clearly and backing it with reasons while remaining open to challenge - is what puts the crew's information on the table where it can be used. Without it the junior pilot's doubts stay unspoken. Competitiveness harms crew decision making, and friendliness and intelligence alone do not get information voiced.
7evt1podJBYjb3OAzbxm: Turning onto north in the northern hemisphere the compass lags, so the turn must be stopped before it reads north - undershoot north, overshoot south. Turning left the heading is decreasing towards 360, so the roll-out is at a heading still east of north, and at 50°N the lead is of the order of 30°.
7fhLBMAcAMYk0JlIdgO3: Crew performance is more than the sum of individual technical skill: it depends on the social competence of the members - communication, feedback, conflict handling and willingness to be challenged. Team membership also raises motivation, and a second pair of eyes detects errors that the individual will not detect alone, which is the whole basis of two-crew operation.
7fvvcLASGzYPjBvoW6yJ: On a free turbine engine the propeller and the gas generator are not mechanically connected, so they are controlled separately. The propeller lever sets propeller RPM through the governor (1), and the power lever sets the gas generator's output, indicated as torque (5) and limited by turbine temperature (6).
7gQr3Sb1EP7GaN3Av3C5: A four-channel CVR records each pilot's audio - which carries the radio transmissions made and received (2) - the third station or public address channel (4), the crew interphone (3) and the cockpit area microphone, which picks up conversation and every aural warning sounded on the flight deck (1). All four are therefore recorded.
7h4egbuB1lw6WY1l3xDy: Freezing rain needs a warm layer aloft above a sub-zero layer below, so rain falls as liquid, becomes supercooled while descending through the cold air, and freezes on impact. That structure exists ahead of a warm front in winter, where warm air is overrunning cold air trapped at the surface. It is among the most dangerous icing conditions because the droplets are very large and the ice accretes far aft of protected surfaces.
7hjxtMjfmyByd3pDdBG8: Slush adds two penalties: displacement drag as the wheels plough through it and spray impingement drag on the airframe, both of which slow the acceleration and lengthen the run. It also degrades braking if the take-off is rejected, which is why contaminated-runway take-off performance is separately certified. Headwind, lower mass and a downhill slope all SHORTEN the take-off distance.
7ht4lIgWffyqV0ENeRF1: On an attitude indicator, bank is read from the pointer against the graduated arc at the top of the instrument and pitch from the position of the aircraft symbol against the horizon bar and its pitch ladder. A 40° left bank puts the pointer at the fourth major graduation on the left, with the symbol 15° below the horizon.
7hwCxdWv6UyAo4Y9ge8z: The constant speed drive absorbs the variation in engine speed and turns the generator at a fixed speed, so the output frequency stays at 400 Hz whatever the engine is doing. Voltage is a separate matter, controlled by the regulator acting on the generator field.
7i0Toq1iyc8ZiF2tbDom: Conditioned air is bleed air processed by the packs to the required temperature and delivered at the pressure the pressurisation system schedules. Its oxygen content is not altered - it is ordinary air, simply supplied at a higher pressure than outside - and it is dry because the air taken in at altitude was dry to begin with.
7i3KrgP0JQKTJMLGdeNM: The autocratic or authoritarian leader decides alone and issues instructions without consultation. It contrasts with the democratic style, which involves the crew in decisions, and with laissez-faire, which leaves the crew to organise itself. Autocratic leadership can be appropriate in a time-critical emergency but suppresses the crew input that CRM depends on.
7iNP5SSXLSUAi7t1SzH3: The flux valve is a static magnetic detector, usually in a wingtip or fin well away from the aircraft's own magnetism, which senses the direction of the earth's field and passes it to the compass system. The directional gyro provides the short-term stability and the flux valve provides the long-term magnetic reference.
7jsw5K5i1ffoltMW26rU: Newton's second law states that force equals mass times acceleration, F = m a. Rearranged, a = F/m - which is why a heavier aeroplane accelerates more slowly for the same thrust, and why take-off mass has such a direct effect on the ground run. The SI unit of force follows from this: 1 newton is 1 kg m/s2.
7kib4a0O1OrgI85dX9j9: The torque link connects the fixed upper part of the oleo to the sliding lower part, so the strut can telescope freely but the wheels cannot castor about the strut axis. Without it the wheels would be free to rotate; on a steerable nose gear the steering actuator works through the same linkage.
7l8GDELrXQzfHZ8FIDKh: Fuel is 20,100 x 0.78 = 15,678 kg, leaving 15,428 kg at brakes release after taxi. The take-off limit gives 67,200 - 34,930 - 15,428 = 16,842 kg. Landing fuel is 15,428 - 9,250 = 6,178 kg, so the landing limit gives 54,200 - 34,930 - 6,178 = 13,092 kg. The landing mass binds, so the traffic load is about 13,090 kg.
7lkf6XGqdKH7oHF53ltC: Crossing the date line westbound you gain a day, so the date increases; eastbound you lose a day and the date decreases. This is the opposite of the time change on the same crossing, which is why the date line exists at all: without it, a circumnavigation would end on the wrong calendar day.
7mKiYJIEMFB6Jgk7h5au: Alignment works by sensing the earth's rotation rate against a platform held stationary, so any translation of the aircraft corrupts it. Full alignment is therefore possible only on the ground with the aircraft completely stopped. In flight only a partial or attitude-only realignment is available, which is why an INS lost airborne cannot be fully recovered.
7mONhyuE1RQgBnelhuPA: ICAO Doc 4444 states that speed adjustments requested by ATC on intermediate or final approach shall not exceed plus or minus 20 knots, and no speed adjustment shall be applied once the aircraft is inside 4 NM from the threshold. This protects the stabilised approach.
7nS99ASZDeXcurVVaWbE: An aircraft in the traffic pattern experiencing radio failure that needs to land without requiring immediate assistance signals this by repeatedly switching the landing lights on and off. This visual signal alerts the tower to the communication failure and the intent to land.
7nxWBLtXsiu9rpslTZck: Constant scale, correct shapes and accurate sheet fit are all genuine requirements of a topographical map. Having ALL bearings correct is not, and in fact no projection can deliver it: correct bearings everywhere would require both the great circle and the rhumb line to be straight on the same sheet.
7nxsD2uZbxoBrwXh54uW: Detonation is driven by cylinder pressure and temperature, so the immediate action is to reduce power - throttle back, and enrich the mixture, since the extra fuel cools the charge. Leaning would make it worse, and carburettor heat raises the induction temperature, which also makes it worse.
7p8ior5cbxuZ3nBcc5gy: Position error is caused by the local pressure field around the static port, and that field scales with dynamic pressure - so the faster the aeroplane, the larger the error. It is also why the correction is quoted as a function of speed and configuration in the flight manual.
7pW9BNLWR8lN0SSO6Nee: NAT MNPS airspace is the volume between FL285 and FL420, and the levels flown within it (FL290-FL410) are those to which the MNPS lateral and vertical accuracy requirements attach. Aircraft and crews must be MNPS-approved to fly within it.
7pze8JcALv6DV5jh0KvS: Declination is the celestial equivalent of latitude: the angular distance of a body north or south of the celestial equator. The sun's declination swings between 23.5N at the June solstice and 23.5S at the December solstice, passing through zero at the equinoxes, and that swing is what produces the seasons and the changing length of day.
7qV4xtg9VjRj6zFpqg2T: First get both ends onto the same datum. With QNH 1030, 2000 ft indicated is a pressure altitude of about 2000 - (1030 - 1013) x 27 = 1540 ft, so the descent is from 15 500 ft to about 1500 ft, i.e. 14 000 ft. At 500 ft/min that takes 28 minutes, and at 260 kt with no wind the aircraft covers 260 x 28/60 = about 120 NM.
7qnbtOoKLVdu4CfIsQWn: The low-range radio altimeter is a frequency-modulated continuous wave device (3) working around 4.3 GHz, and its accuracy near the ground is of the order of a couple of feet (5) - which is what allows it to be used for the flare in an automatic landing. Its range is about 2,500 ft, not 5,000, and it is not a pulsed system.
7qv59cS0AUHzjFTfRDN3: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies that longitudinal separation based on DME when both aircraft are on track and using DME is 20 kt speed difference at 10 NM. The leading aircraft must maintain a TAS at least 20 kt faster than the following aircraft for the 10 NM minimum to apply.
7rvKc04oZkxLrGRc2gch: Information is what reduces the receiver's uncertainty (statement 2) and it is measured in bits (statement 3). Statement 4 is wrong because one bit halves the uncertainty - it is the answer to one yes/no question - rather than reducing it by a quarter, and statement 1 misstates the definition. So only 2 and 3 apply.
7swc4ECxFHxFpztTbXPA: Close to the ground the surface interferes with the formation of the wing tip vortices, so the downwash behind the wing is reduced. Less downwash means a smaller induced angle of attack, which tilts the lift vector less far rearward and cuts induced drag - by as much as 40-50% at very low height. The aeroplane consequently floats, and the reduced downwash over the tailplane also produces a nose-down trim change.
7t4cWI65H1jPmLQFfY1I: A fully charged lead-acid cell is about 2.2 volts on open circuit, giving 13.2 V for a six-cell 12 V battery or 26.4 V for a twelve-cell 24 V one. Nickel-cadmium cells produce about 1.2-1.3 V, which is why more of them are needed for the same nominal voltage.
7tVRgo38wrbjrrsv2Czk: The centre of gravity is 12.53 - 9.63 = 2.90 m aft of the leading edge of the mean aerodynamic chord. Expressed as a fraction of the 8 m chord that is 2.90/8 = 0.363, so 36.3% MAC.
7toPWyXdEO9X2mQnPgxZ: A rate gyro has a single gimbal, so it has one degree of freedom and can precess about that one axis only. The precession is opposed by a calibrated spring, giving a deflection proportional to the rate applied - which is what makes it a rate-measuring rather than a position-measuring instrument.
7u6RrHpQ9C0jjNXxt8zx: ICAO Doc 8168 allows a zone of flexibility of 5 degrees on either side of the sector boundaries in a holding pattern. This means the pilot may use either of the adjacent entry procedures when approaching within 5 degrees of a sector boundary.
7wX9NgKn9RzSOemiMP6V: Maximum range for a jet means the most nautical miles per kilogram of fuel, and since fuel flow follows THRUST, that means minimising drag per unit of speed - i.e. minimising D/V, which is maximising V/D. Geometrically, the minimum of D/V is where a straight line from the origin just touches the total drag curve. That tangent point lies at a higher speed than VMD, which is why jet maximum-range speed is faster than minimum-drag speed.
7x163cjjED45FXyWUI8D: The Direct Mercator wraps a cylinder round the equator, so all meridians project as parallel vertical straight lines at equal spacing. It is the PARALLELS whose spacing expands towards the poles, and that expansion is what makes the projection conformal despite the meridians never converging.
7y8k98QsTeiggP3lzzEr: At speeds away from the design point the front and rear of the compressor are mismatched, and the front stages stall. Bleed valves opened between the spools dump some of the flow overboard, restoring the axial velocity through the early stages and so restoring the stall margin.
7yX9XaVeaJs8pYTSL3zw: In Rasmussen's model, rule-based behaviour applies a stored if-then rule to a recognised situation. When the situation does not match any stored rule - or the rule is tried and fails - the operator must fall back on knowledge-based behaviour, reasoning from first principles about the system. It is the unsuitability of the known rules, not of automated skills, that forces the transition.
7ybw83unWaCRGzFAea0H: In a reversible system the connection between the surface and the cockpit control works both ways, so the aerodynamic loads on the surface are felt at the control column. That natural feel is lost in an irreversible power system, which is why an artificial feel unit has to be added.
7zcyalgkt1L3tlaRWU8s: Tip vortices are the direct consequence of the pressure difference that produces lift: air spills round the tip from the high pressure below to the low pressure above and rolls up into a vortex. No lift, no vortex - which is why the wake begins at rotation and ends at touchdown.
80CknzaTgITnmZ6RvRcE: Cockpit noise and a windscreen that restricts the field of view are properties of the workplace and its design - the fit between the human and the machine - which is the domain of ergonomics. Social factors concern relationships within the crew, organisational factors concern company pressures and rostering, and psychobiological factors concern the individual's own state such as fatigue or illness.
813g1qOAhCBfqGwArDpc: Over-breathing washes out carbon dioxide, and the resulting alkalosis constricts cerebral blood vessels and disturbs nerve and muscle function. The picture is dizziness, tingling or pins and needles in the fingers, toes and around the mouth, nausea, blurred vision and eventually muscular spasm. Cyanosis belongs to hypoxia, and the heart rate rises rather than falls.
81JOPMiudtblE59CBVWk: The centre of pressure moving aft in the transonic region increases the distance between it and the CG, lengthening the restoring moment arm. A larger restoring moment for a given disturbance is by definition greater static longitudinal STABILITY - the aeroplane resists pitch changes more strongly. It also produces the nose-down Mach tuck, since the increased download aft pitches the nose down.
82Qx8YWBzrq2fsv2e58V: A safe forced landing is an unavoidable landing or ditching with a reasonable expectancy of no injuries to persons in the aircraft OR ON THE SURFACE. Two elements distinguish it: it is forced, not voluntary, and the expectation of no injury is reasonable rather than guaranteed - no landing can be guaranteed injury-free.
82Sj7aDrVqSuI1tb9b6u: Hyperventilation is driven by anything that makes breathing outrun metabolic need, and emotional arousal - fear, anxiety, stress, sudden startle - is by far the commonest trigger in flight. The low CO2 pressure and the reduced (not increased) cerebral blood flow are consequences of the over-breathing, not causes of it.
82bteCd8MmHX6M1qLQwV: No drift on a heading of 180 means the wind is blowing along the north/south line, so it is either from 360 or from 180. On a heading of 090 the drift is 5 degrees starboard, i.e. the aircraft is pushed south, so the wind must be from the north, 360. Speed follows from the drift: crosswind = TAS x sin5 = 200 x 0.087 = about 17 kt.
8389t4pVrbGpWEslf02e: Power brakes use the aircraft hydraulic system as the source of pressure, with the pedals working metering valves that admit a proportion of that pressure to the brakes. The pilot's foot force therefore controls the braking without having to generate it, which is essential on a large aeroplane.
83ViTaX68oBlHDUDlrEw: A generator fault requires the machine itself to be isolated and de-excited: the generator breaker opens to take it off the bus and the exciter control relay opens so it stops generating. The bus tie stays as it is, so the remaining generator can pick up both busses.
83kumOMhExGXwUErVUel: A sounding that crosses 0 C twice reveals a warm layer aloft over a sub-freezing layer beneath, the classic freezing-rain structure of a warm front in winter. Precipitation melts in the warm layer, becomes supercooled in the cold layer below and freezes instantly on the airframe. The resulting large-droplet clear ice runs back well beyond the protected leading edges and is graded severe.
84iKnCpRtINaB7akNiN7: At FL300 in standard conditions the temperature is 15 - 60 = -45°C, or 228 K, so the speed of sound is 38.94 x the square root of 228, about 588 kt. Mach number is 470/588 = 0.80.
85Qm0B2hrTV73DredAoz: Only about a quarter of the air entering a combustion chamber is burnt; the rest is secondary and tertiary air admitted progressively down the flame tube to cool the liner and the casing and to dilute the gas to a temperature the turbine can accept. Pressure falls slightly through the chamber and the peak temperature is in the primary zone, not at the outlet.
85oNjUFlNOAQRnlqQidg: Thrust from an underwing engine bends the wing forward inboard of the pylon, while drag on the outboard section bends it aft - so the front spar is compressed inboard of the engine and stretched outboard of it. That reversal along the span is one of the reasons the torsion box is heavier near the engine mounting.
86dVhKta5MHbR7jMUjZ0: The GPS navigation message is broadcast as 25 frames of 1500 bits, each frame taking 30 seconds, so the complete almanac for the whole constellation takes 25 x 30 = 750 seconds = 12.5 minutes. That is why a receiver that has been off for a long time, or moved a long way, takes so much longer to give a first fix than a warm start.
8739Ry58aP55V2039j0e: A sudden IAS increase with thrust and attitude unchanged is an increasing-performance shear, and its characteristic is that it reverses. The correct response is to hold the flight path, accept the positive speed excursion and monitor the trend, keeping thrust in hand for the decreasing-performance phase that usually follows. Pulling thrust off leaves the aircraft short of both speed and thrust exactly when the shear reverses.
87I2JgscoF7An2FdsPMS: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are genuine decision biases: the availability of personal experience distorts how likely a risk feels, confirmation bias makes us defend a decision against contrary evidence, and group membership pulls the individual towards the group's view. Statement 4 inverts the truth - people preferentially select the facts that support the option they already favour.
87k9bcR5Mj1hjVP9XMvB: A shuttle valve has two inlets and one outlet, and the piston inside is driven to whichever side has the lower pressure - so the actuator is automatically fed from whichever system is pressurised. That is how an emergency or alternate system takes over the same actuator with no crew selection.
87uSab1cY2D9FK9ypyZq: The speed of sound depends only on temperature, and at the standard sea level +15°C it is about 661 kt (340 m/s). It falls as the square root of absolute temperature, reaching about 573 kt at the tropopause.
88VIhFdwElrOnJjYms7T: Moving the centre of gravity aft reduces the download the tailplane must produce, so the wing has less lift to generate and less induced drag results. Less drag means less fuel for the same distance, so the range improves - which is why fuel is trimmed aft in cruise on many transport aircraft.
895MTBMl0bQH1kO1DDlU: Under the Tokyo Convention, the aircraft commander may deliver to the competent authorities of any Contracting State a person who the commander has reasonable grounds to believe has committed or is about to commit a serious offence against penal law on board. The commander may also restrain the person but the primary remedy is delivery to authorities.
8ANNmCfpaWoU10FWurgu: Statement B is the false one. The inverted-U shows that performance is poor at very low arousal as well as at very high arousal, so a complete absence of stress produces boredom, inattention and slow responses rather than efficiency. Moderate stress (eustress) is necessary. The other three statements are all true.
8Arvzkx44nIrCc1nA8ac: A centrifugal stage produces a large pressure rise - perhaps 4:1 or more - in a single stage, which makes it simple and robust, but it does so by flinging the air outwards, so the diameter is large. An axial compressor gives a small rise per stage but keeps a small frontal area, which is why big engines are axial.
8AzwQLlGhlY4GctAxUhV: Aircraft AC systems run at 400 Hz because the higher frequency allows transformers and motors to be made much smaller and lighter for the same power than at 50 or 60 Hz. The penalty is greater line reactance, which is acceptable over the short distances involved.
8BPczXJpCi7ScIC4ylMA: Anaemia is a shortage of functional haemoglobin, whether from too few red cells, too little haemoglobin in them or haemoglobin that cannot carry oxygen. Because oxygen is carried almost entirely on haemoglobin, an anaemic person has reduced oxygen-carrying capacity and a correspondingly reduced tolerance to altitude - this is anaemic (hypaemic) hypoxia.
8Boc8SqvpDcLFu1GMjcj: A cohesive crew shares goals, trusts one another and closes ranks under pressure, so information keeps flowing and workload is shared when things go wrong. Cohesion costs nothing when everything is going well; its value shows in difficulty, when a fragmented crew stops communicating exactly when communication matters most.
8CSUfiXWAKqApAPbeLjG: NDBs work in the LF and MF bands, roughly 190-1750 kHz, which corresponds to kilometric and hectometric wavelengths. Those long waves follow the surface as a ground wave, which is what gives the ADF its range beyond line of sight - and also its night effect and its vulnerability to thunderstorms.
8CieIEc4aMhPRZlpMsea: With both the ram inlet and the drain blocked, the total pressure in the system is trapped at whatever it was, while the static pressure continues to change with altitude. The indicated difference therefore varies with height alone, so the instrument behaves like a crude altimeter - over-reading in a climb and under-reading in a descent.
8CoxaODLjxHd9t0F64PR: The passenger system drops the masks automatically above about 14,000 ft cabin altitude, and the crew can also deploy it manually with the passenger oxygen switch. The diluter demand regulator belongs to the flight crew system and has nothing to do with the cabin.
8D66fZs6nddIM7uWjulV: Fuel tank boost pumps are centrifugal: they move a large volume at the modest pressure needed to feed the engine and to keep the line pressure above the fuel's vapour pressure, they cope with running dry briefly, and they cannot generate a damaging pressure if the outlet is closed.
8EAI73x8RUwh75niTe6P: An oleo-pneumatic strut uses compressed nitrogen as the spring and oil as the damper: on compression the oil is forced through a restrictor, and the work done against that resistance is what absorbs the energy of landing rather than returning it as a bounce.
8EiTVOvxcTgxmIs8fpta: Less flap means a lower CLmax, so the approach and touchdown speeds are higher and more energy has to be dissipated: the landing distance increases. But less flap also means much less drag, so if a go-around becomes necessary the climb gradient available is significantly better. This is exactly the trade a reduced-flap landing buys - runway length for go-around performance.
8FZLM6GkZ4WDeKCbDOMm: Turbulent mixing keeps the atmosphere homogeneous to about 80 km, so oxygen remains 21% by volume throughout the whole range of altitudes any aeroplane reaches. What falls with altitude is the total pressure, and with it the partial pressure of oxygen - which is the cause of altitude hypoxia, not any change in the percentage.
8FfK6MAW0mT7gQysAzTt: Weather radar on the ground is permitted but only with precautions. The beam carries enough microwave energy to injure eyes and tissue at close range and to trigger fuelling equipment or damage sensitive electronics, so it must not be radiated with people, buildings, fuel bowsers or other aircraft in the forward arc.
8GPzo5zHRLn5Sk4xedEZ: ICAO Annex 1 requires that an applicant for a Commercial Pilot Licence be at least 18 years of age. This applies to aeroplanes; the age requirement for gliders may vary by national regulation but the standard commercial minimum is 18.
8HMVjz6gWfU6KwyIrQql: The localiser aerial is at the STOP end of the runway, about 300 m beyond the runway end on the extended centreline, so its signal is aligned down the runway towards the approaching aircraft. The glide path aerial is the one offset to the side, about 300 m in from the threshold and 120 to 180 m from the centreline.
8HX7WxH6C2YAdzvTjGDg: Air cooling removes heat from the outside of the cylinders, but the inside of the engine - the pistons, bearings, camshaft and the cylinder walls - is cooled by the oil circulating over and through them. A significant proportion of the heat rejected by a piston engine leaves through the oil cooler.
8HZaQ5tqhSa8HDYwe4iZ: Motivation raises the general level of arousal and directs the attentional spotlight towards what matters to the individual, so a motivated pilot is more alert and attends more effectively. The other options understate this or contradict it by suggesting motivation produces low arousal.
8HqpsotTzFitY2pyGPLj: Rasmussen's three control modes each generate a characteristic error type. Routine errors belong to the automatic, skill-based mode; creative errors belong to the knowledge-based mode, where the operator has to reason out a new solution. The rule-based mode works by applying stored technical know-how to a recognised situation, so its errors are errors of technical knowledge - the wrong rule selected, or the right rule applied to the wrong situation.
8HxyAplQ8ke8NgEEvLfK: The flight crew system uses gaseous oxygen stored in high pressure cylinders, because the supply must be available immediately, must last as long as the descent takes and must be capable of being turned on and off. Chemical generators, used for passengers, run once for a fixed period and cannot be stopped.
8I8bbXo3yqtWH7WedqGY: On an opposite parallel track passing down your right-hand side, you are looking at the other aeroplane's starboard side, and the starboard navigation light is green. Its red port light faces away from you, and you would see red only if it were passing on your left.
8I93zQo6PMxf6GQZJyM9: With QNH 1013.2 there is no pressure error, so the whole 1000 ft discrepancy is thermal. Using true altitude = pressure altitude x (1 + 4 x deviation / 1000): 12,000 = 13,000 x (1 + 4d/1000), giving 4d/1000 = -0.077 and d = about -20 C. The aircraft being lower than its indicated level is the signature of colder-than-standard air.
8ICm9PbQhH5YZd8ZAWVZ: A decision exists only where there is more than one possible course of action: deciding is selecting one alternative from among several against some criterion. Applying an automatic procedure involves no choice, originality belongs to creative problem-solving rather than to decision-making as such, and imposing a view is a matter of leadership style.
8IEFdXnZGjeig4eELqCC: For an aeroplane certificated to JAR-25 or equivalent, the survival equipment for areas where search and rescue would be especially difficult need not be carried if it stays within 90 minutes at cruising speed of an area suitable for making an emergency landing. The 120-minute and 30-minute figures belong to the separate life-raft rule for extended overwater flight.
8IWuFdedPdM1L8gCMkYB: Pressure altitude is by definition the altitude indicated with 1013.25 set, so if the subscale is at 1013.25 and the needle shows 10,000 ft, the pressure altitude is 10,000 ft. Temperature affects true altitude and density altitude, not pressure altitude.
8IeeK3OuQ0cNzvHxdU5F: Bulk transport around the body is done by the circulation - oxygen carried on haemoglobin from lungs to tissues, carbon dioxide carried back mostly as bicarbonate in plasma. Diffusion only moves the gases the last short distance across the alveolar and capillary membranes; metabolism and oxidation are the chemical use of the oxygen, not its transport.
8J4Q88EKk1YlmTskrFHu: The command bars are attitude guidance, so they belong on the attitude display - the ADI, or the attitude portion of an EFIS primary flight display. The HSI shows the horizontal situation, EICAS shows engine and system data and the CDU is the FMS interface.
8KCKF4PPvWOugEM5n2Fu: The tropopause is simply the boundary surface between the troposphere, where temperature falls with height, and the stratosphere, where it is first isothermal and then rises. It is not itself an inversion or an isothermal layer by definition - it is the level at which the lapse rate changes - and the strong lapse rate belongs to the troposphere below it.
8KKVWovV5dnMDbGlNm8q: One US gallon is 3.78 litres. Keep it distinct from the Imperial gallon of 4.55 litres, which is the value the other options are built around. Mixing the two on a refuelling calculation produces a 20 percent error in the fuel uplift, which is the practical reason the exam keeps testing it.
8KNElZzMlb4twnEap09D: Under JAR-FCL, an instrument rating is valid for one year. It must be revalidated by passing a proficiency check within the three months immediately preceding the expiry date of the rating.
8KVNaJdkZHaJGGn4v5Kg: TCAS symbology escalates with threat: a hollow white or cyan diamond for other traffic, a filled diamond for proximate traffic, a filled amber circle for a traffic advisory and a filled red square for the intruder that has caused a resolution advisory.
8Kk7Bw1kYNPiegiuWTer: Parallax error is a reading error, not an instrument error: it arises when the observer's eye is off the axis of the pointer so the needle appears against the wrong part of the scale. It is why instruments are read from directly in front and why some have anti-parallax mirrors.
8L4JQnKBiJCYyViXS8nr: Both climb performance figures depend on excess power or excess thrust, and both shrink as altitude increases: thrust falls with density while drag at a given IAS does not, so the excess available for climbing steadily disappears. The best angle and the best rate therefore both decrease, reaching zero rate of climb at the absolute ceiling.
8L4TpJVJsmUBK57GHcVU: Standard time is the legally adopted time of a country or part of a country, chosen by its government and usually, but not always, a whole number of hours from UTC. It is not the same as local mean time, which varies continuously with longitude, and it is not UTC itself.
8LCO1lW9qcEjtbeWKz2Y: Wavelength is the speed of light divided by frequency: 300,000,000 m/s divided by 300,000 Hz gives 1,000 metres. A useful shortcut is that 300 divided by the frequency in MHz gives the wavelength in metres, and 300 kHz is 0.3 MHz.
8LylYDewrjo44j2hVG7b: Fail-passive means that a failure causes no significant deviation of flight path or attitude - the system simply disconnects in a controlled way (2) - but it is then no longer capable of landing the aeroplane, so the landing is not completed automatically (3). Fail-operational systems, by contrast, complete the landing after a single failure.
8MbQ1yjlVTfZjjlVqDkl: Runway width is a powerful height cue. A narrower-than-normal runway subtends a smaller angle, so it looks farther away and the pilot judges himself too high. Correcting for a height error that does not exist, he flattens the approach and descends below the correct path, arriving low and short - the classic undershoot on a narrow strip.
8Nfl56bmhuPN8MMaTVJ7: Power depends on the mass of oxygen in the charge, so the best conditions are the densest air: cold and at high pressure. Humidity is the third factor - water vapour is less dense than air and displaces oxygen - so dry air is better than humid, which is why hot, high and humid is the worst combination.
8NpMlGB19Z61YRwHgPQc: Parallels on a Direct Mercator are horizontal straight lines, but their spacing increases towards the poles as the secant of latitude. That expansion is what keeps the projection conformal once the meridians have been forced parallel, and it is why areas at high latitude look grossly enlarged.
8ODBVcKJU1edwWO6rU9X: In level flight the lift must equal the weight regardless of speed, so in L = CL x 1/2 rho V2 S the product CL x V2 is fixed. Doubling the indicated airspeed multiplies V2 by four, so CL must fall to a QUARTER of its original value - achieved by lowering the angle of attack. This inverse-square relationship is why the angle of attack falls away so rapidly as an aeroplane accelerates.
8OVrZoXpqf7qgo0MTMx4: An INS is highly accurate in the short term but its error grows steadily with time, typically about 2 NM per hour. GNSS has no drift but can suffer short outages and integrity problems. Coupling them lets GNSS continuously reset the INS drift while the INS carries the position smoothly through any GNSS gap, which is far more than simple redundancy.
8OzLsk7Rsu0osTH7wgn6: The passenger mask is a continuous flow type with a rebreather bag: oxygen flows into the bag at a fixed rate and the wearer draws it in mixed with cabin air through the ports round the edge of the mask. It is not a sealed mask and there is no pressure demand function.
8PNsUyuDV6rT6Uv80WY3: The change is 10 minutes of arc per year for 3 years, i.e. 30 minutes = 0.5 degrees. An INCREASE applied to 6W makes the westerly value larger, so the variation in 2005 is 6.5W. Note that increase means numerically greater in the same sense, not a move towards east.
8PjTufWJcOvBFfCH3L4x: The inner ear contains both the vestibular apparatus and the cochlea. The semicircular canals sense angular acceleration, the otolith organs (utricle and saccule) sense linear acceleration and head tilt, and the cochlea converts sound into nerve impulses. All three functions listed therefore belong to the inner ear.
8Qay0qhHMCUmAYpI7vH3: The high-range radio altimeter used for cruise levels works at a few hundred megahertz, giving wavelengths of the order of a metre or less - decimetric. The low-range altimeter used for approach and flare works much higher, around 4.3 GHz, for the precision the flare requires.
8QejTNY0pj5K2Z09TZZj: A fusible plug in the wheel rim melts at a set temperature and lets the tyre deflate in a controlled way, so an overheated brake cannot burst the tyre. It is why an aircraft with hot brakes is left alone after a rejected take-off rather than approached from the side.
8Qom2JFvXT82YHPLwdKn: Separation minima near an airport may be reduced when the commander of the following aircraft has the preceding aircraft in sight and is able to maintain own separation. This is commonly applied during visual approaches in VMC.
8R0mbMHnB1iwJjrUZfjf: Useful load is take-off mass less dry operating mass. The dry operating mass is the empty mass plus operational items: 61,300 + 2,300 = 63,600 kg. So the useful load - traffic load plus usable fuel - is 132,000 - 63,600 = 68,400 kg.
8RAjPAIzm8JkR0LhnLtG: Approaching a warm front, the gently sloping frontal surface (about 1:150) means cloud is met in a predictable descending sequence: cirrus and cirrostratus roughly 800 km ahead, then altostratus, then nimbostratus with continuous precipitation from about 300 km out to the surface front. Cumulonimbus and squall lines belong to the cold front, which has a much steeper slope of about 1:50.
8SCaFuWT7xuRRwLuzsNh: If the oceanic clearance has not arrived by the boundary, the aircraft continues in accordance with the CURRENT flight plan while the crew keeps trying to obtain it - it does not hold, offset or turn back. 8T9hrC4Ya0xysmeorjvg: A loose root fit lets the blade rock slightly, and that movement absorbs and damps the vibratory energy that would otherwise be transmitted into the blade. Damping the vibration is what prevents fatigue cracking at the root - which is why compressor blades rattle audibly when the engine is stopped.
8TC8rmz1nfpoAl0TbdVe: Hypoxia is insidious: the earliest effects are euphoria, over-confidence and impaired judgement, so the affected pilot is the person least able to notice them and is often pleased with his own performance. In a crew another pilot may spot the change; flying solo there is nobody to detect it, which is what makes it especially dangerous.
8TikIxc04orKLJjFX3EA: JAR-OPS 1.515 requires a turbo-propeller aeroplane to be able to make a full stop from 50 ft within 70% of the landing distance available, and the same factor applies at the destination and at any alternate - there is no relaxation for being an alternate.
