8U65xqVOVLRlubdmph0G: ICAO Doc 4444 requires that during independent parallel approaches, the vector to the localizer shall establish the aircraft in level flight for at least 1.5 NM prior to intercepting the glide path. This stabilisation distance ensures proper localizer tracking before descent begins.
8UNh1Lss2K3W3i4Pyvbt: An air data computer takes the raw pitot and static pressures and total air temperature, applies the corrections for position error and compressibility, and outputs altitude, airspeed, Mach number, vertical speed and static air temperature as electrical signals that drive the instruments and feed the other aircraft systems.
8UPqcJ56i94cIJTOEDjm: Both statements are wrong as they stand. The take-off configuration warning monitors the items that would make the take-off unsafe - flaps and slats, stabiliser trim, speedbrake and parking brake - and it is triggered by advancing the thrust levers. Elevator position as such is not monitored, and low brake pressure is not a take-off configuration item.
8UeFOkf05lKH7HrtoDy2: Local mean time is measured from the MEAN sun's transit of the observer's anti-meridian, which defines 0000 LMT, i.e. midnight. The mean sun crosses the observer's own meridian at 1200 LMT. The apparent sun is not used because its transit interval varies through the year.
8WRtWgDBCxdL1uu9II2F: As ambient pressure falls, nitrogen dissolved in the body's tissues and fluids at ground-level pressure comes out of solution and forms bubbles - Henry's Law. Those bubbles cause the bends, creeps, chokes and neurological symptoms. Low inspired oxygen pressure causes hypoxia, a completely separate problem.
8WZbyBlF7EfsiXkNGZ4N: The movement area of an aerodrome together with adjacent terrain and buildings with controlled access is termed the aeronautical part (or airside). The manoeuvring area covers only runways and taxiways, a terminal is just a building, and a security programme is an operational plan, not a physical area.
8WakWomLlfXw5VEkO6y3: A gaseous system carries as much oxygen as the cylinders hold, so its duration is set by the bottle size rather than by a fixed burn time (1); it can be turned on and off and used again (3); and the flow can be regulated to the altitude and the demand (5). Chemical generators are simpler to store but run once, for a fixed period, and cannot be stopped.
8WpZ1nWScRTBVzdEojTC: An engine fire is a red warning: it lights the fire warning light and the master warning and sounds the fire bell, so it cannot be missed whatever the crew are looking at. Visual alone or aural alone would each be capable of going unnoticed.
8XvioNrZr2s0uM49ElMw: The wind from 160 lies 52 degrees off the port bow of the 212 course, so the crosswind is 50 x sin52 = about 39 kt and the headwind component is 50 x cos52 = about 31 kt. Allowing about 10 degrees of drift correction, the groundspeed is about 220 x cos10 - 31 = about 186 kt. Both the course and the wind are magnetic, so no conversion is needed.
8YVgi9tlo1jBzWh1QO8J: Time = distance / groundspeed = 103 / 105 hours = 0.981 h, which is 58.9 minutes, so 59 minutes. A quick check: at 105 kt the aircraft is 2 NM short of a full hour's run, and 2 NM takes just over a minute.
8Yd9tjdFmXVLcZxveVWh: The primary flight controls are the surfaces that control the aircraft about its three axes - ailerons for roll, elevators for pitch and rudder for yaw. Flaps and speed brakes change the lift and drag characteristics rather than the attitude, and the cockpit controls are the inceptors rather than the controls themselves.
8YqHfNmHBw2QQ4L5I7I7: ICAO Doc 4444 prohibits the radar controller from requesting speed adjustments after the aircraft has passed a point 4 NM from the threshold on final approach. Beyond that point the crew must be free to configure the aircraft for landing without ATC speed constraints.
8Z56fYPpauXkJYy7V4sw: VA is defined as the speed at which the aeroplane will stall at exactly the limit manoeuvring load factor - so at or below VA a full elevator deflection produces a stall before it produces structural damage. Where a single fixed value is published rather than a weight-dependent one, it is computed at maximum take-off mass. Note that VA protects only against a single full deflection in ONE direction from 1g, not against rapid reversals.
8ZKxwyJ0soSEJikW4sck: Certified performance data assume a fully serviceable anti-skid system, because braking is used both in the accelerate-stop distance (take-off) and in the landing distance. Anti-skid may therefore be credited for BOTH. The corollary matters operationally: with anti-skid inoperative the AFM penalties must be applied to both take-off and landing figures, and reduced-thrust take-offs are prohibited.
8Zt6muzdHqr3pgfxYaBT: The wind from 320 is on the port bow of the 355 heading, so expect right drift and a headwind component. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 005 and a groundspeed of about 102 kt, i.e. 10 degrees of starboard drift and 23 kt off the TAS.
8bH8dIllvEgJ73lF5DG9: RVR appears only in METAR and SPECI, as an RDD/VVVV group following the visibility. It is an instrumented, aerodrome-specific, near-real-time measurement, so it has no place in a TAF (a forecast) or a SIGMET (an en-route hazard warning). RVR is included whenever the visibility or the RVR itself is below 1500 m.
8bJ4YMqZ9RnzuVdPmfrh: A shuttle valve has two inlets and one outlet with a free piston between them, which is pushed across by whichever supply is pressurised. The actuator is therefore fed automatically from the normal system, or from the alternate one if the normal fails, with no crew action required.
8bUeZcfipfxgWpKkXL7e: Work outwards in order. True heading = true course minus right drift = 300 - 8 = 292. Magnetic heading = true heading plus west variation = 292 + 10 = 302. Compass heading = magnetic heading minus deviation = 302 - (-4) = 306.
8bhp3et0Jix1jqRiWk3Q: Clamshell doors swing into the exhaust stream and turn it forwards and outwards through cascades, so the thrust acts against the direction of travel. The gas is redirected rather than stopped - the engine goes on running normally and the flow is simply pointed the other way.
8bnUmdUK7khxfPqw6NX6: To obtain pressure altitude below 18,000 ft, set the altimeter to 29.92 inches Hg (1013.25 hPa). The reading shown is pressure altitude. There is no need to use a flight computer or contact a station — simply dialling in the standard pressure setting gives pressure altitude directly.
8bzBUMjMBS0nXyxjiDA4: The CS-23 positive manoeuvring limit load factors are 3.8 for the Normal category, 4.4 for Utility, and 6.0 for Aerobatic. The Utility category permits limited aerobatics such as spins and steep turns, so it carries a structure stronger than Normal but lighter than a full aerobatic aeroplane. The 2.5 figure is the large-aeroplane (CS-25) minimum.
8c3U6jzrIEmIDScDhymt: Flying efficiency starts to degrade as soon as the cabin altitude climbs much above 8000 ft - which is why 8000 ft is the maximum normal cabin altitude of a transport aeroplane, why crew oxygen becomes mandatory above 10 000 ft, and why 100% of the passengers must be supplied above 13 000 ft. At 14 000 ft without oxygen, night vision, judgement and useful work are all measurably impaired.
8cnIWjNgGjhVqfRRVKlB: Real load - the useful kW - depends on how much torque each engine puts into its generator, so real load sharing is achieved by trimming the constant speed drives so that each machine takes an equal share of the mechanical input. Reactive load, the kVAR, is shared by adjusting the field excitation instead.
8cwHmUh92ulyJnb4CkpC: The ITCZ is where the two trade wind systems converge, forcing deep ascent in warm, very moist air, so frequent and widespread thunderstorms with tops often above FL500 are its defining feature. It migrates seasonally, following the sun with a lag, and it is not associated with a jet stream (the equatorial easterly jet is a separate, seasonal feature).
8cxdDE2GEPhSKLpPDWUF: Human reliability studies put the error rate on a simple, repetitive task at roughly one in a hundred operations. Methodical training improves this by about an order of magnitude, to around one in a thousand, and only very well designed, highly practised tasks approach one in ten thousand. These figures are why single-pilot checking is not relied upon and why cross-checking and checklists exist.
8d6pcO9cXO9qtLyFT9CD: A relief valve set above the normal regulated pressure sits in the system as the last line of defence: if the pump's own pressure control or the unloading valve fails, the relief valve opens and dumps fluid back to the reservoir before the pressure can burst a line or a component.
8d8mD6sUor2yUUcNcHlv: Maslow's hierarchy rises from physiological needs at the base - air, water, food, sleep, warmth - through safety and security, belonging and affection, and esteem, to self-actualisation at the top. The lower needs must be reasonably satisfied before the higher ones motivate behaviour, which is why a fatigued or dehydrated crew member's performance suffers before anything else does.
8dDvVaYRk436B1j8JLng: For required cabin crew in a pressurised aeroplane: the entire flight time above a cabin altitude of 13 000 ft but never less than 30 minutes, plus the flight time above 10 000 ft up to 13 000 ft after the first 30 minutes at those altitudes. Note that statements 3 and 4 in this question express the same rule in two different ways, so more than one combination reads as correct.
8dHXgEjNnD2qRWCR3RTV: A visual approach clearance may be given when the pilot reports the field in sight. The controller continues to provide separation from other controlled traffic — this is the key distinction from a contact approach, where the pilot requests it and accepts reduced separation responsibility.
8dmD0yPDPKDpoBBgjOHE: In sleep the body's activity is reduced across the board: metabolic rate falls by roughly 10-20%, arterial blood pressure falls and the pulse slows, along with body temperature and respiratory rate. Sensory thresholds rise rather than fall - the sleeper is harder, not easier, to rouse - so statement 4 is false.
8dnISMTRQXP8vUqcEckM: Time of Useful Consciousness is the interval between the onset of an inadequate oxygen supply and the loss of the ability to take corrective action. It shortens sharply with altitude - a few minutes at 25,000 ft, well under a minute above 35,000 ft, and less again after a rapid decompression - and it also varies between individuals and with fitness, smoking, workload and physical activity.
8e3Melk8ZNq1bqCGZcS8: Inertia acting head-to-feet is positive Gz: the blood tends to pool in the lower body and the column of blood above the heart is harder to lift. Pressure at head level therefore falls, producing greyout, tunnel vision, blackout and finally G-induced loss of consciousness as G increases.
8e4ub5tL0Oz8pamUefTu: Psychosomatic means literally mind-body: mental or emotional stressors produce genuine physical illness such as ulcers, hypertension, headaches or skin conditions, which is statement 1. Statement 2 reverses the direction and adds an absolute - a physical problem is not always followed by psychological stress - so only statement 1 is correct.
8eC0ixH1NhTOCh7wvQgP: A nozzle or tailpipe fire on the ground is residual fuel burning in the jet pipe, not a fire in the engine zone, so the fire bottles would put the agent in the wrong place. The remedy is a dry crank - motor the engine with the starter, fuel and ignition off, so the airflow blows the burning fuel out of the tailpipe.
8eiGz5Nzg8X1zBjNvj0u: Short-term memory holds only about seven items (statement 3), loses them within roughly 20 seconds unless they are rehearsed or transferred to long-term memory (statement 4), and is easily wiped by an interruption or by competing information (statement 1). What it is not is difficult to access - retrieval from short-term memory is immediate, unlike from long-term memory - so statement 2 is false.
8eqcS3I88CVI6vl6LbLh: The regulator controls the generator by controlling how much current reaches the shunt field, so it is placed in the field circuit and senses the output voltage across the machine. Increasing the field current raises the output and reducing it lowers the output, which is how a constant voltage is held as load and speed vary.
8f393DoBwM7o09QDEPDr: Decompression sickness usually appears during or shortly after exposure to reduced pressure, but delayed onset is well recognised: symptoms can develop hours after landing, and exertion after the flight can precipitate them. That is why any suspected case must be reported and treated rather than dismissed because the flight is over.
8fG4qZpBRBVFj7VImzey: Contaminated means more than 25% of the required surface covered by water or slush or loose snow equivalent to more than 3 mm of water, by compacted snow, or by ice including wet ice. A film thin enough merely to make the surface shiny defines a WET runway, and moist grass appears nowhere in the definition.
8fgAHiCIo0dR4cPk9I9Y: A computer beats the human comfortably on speed, on working-memory capacity and on tireless repetition. What the human retains is flexibility: the ability to recognise an unfamiliar pattern, work from incomplete or contradictory data and improvise a solution to a situation nobody anticipated. That is why the pilot remains in the loop.
8fzOnAhunBmM3ldWuUYw: A plain flap simply hinges the rear portion of the aerofoil downward, which increases the effective CAMBER of the section. More camber raises CLmax and shifts the whole lift curve up and to the left, so the wing generates the same lift at a lower speed. It also lowers the stalling ANGLE of attack and increases drag markedly - unlike a slat, which raises the stalling angle.
8hIBIXrwa8ozu5gRXyc1: The automatic controller schedules the cabin altitude against the aircraft altitude (1), limits the rate at which the cabin altitude changes so that ears can cope (2), and holds the differential pressure below the structural limit (3). Ventilation flow is a separate function of the packs, and the differential is not constant - it varies with altitude.
8hlblGkbK7gZu2NNuWAa: ICAO Doc 4444 states that when vectoring to the ILS localizer course, the intercept angle is normally 30 degrees but shall not be greater than 45 degrees. The 45-degree maximum prevents excessive overshoot of the localizer beam while still allowing operational flexibility.
8i5klJCVjPE2xJRYN9f6: CS-25.113(b) defines the take-off run for the all-engines case as the horizontal distance from the start of the take-off to a point equidistant between the point at which VLOF is reached and the point at which the aeroplane is 35 ft above the surface - in effect, half the airborne segment is counted. It is not the same as the accelerate-stop distance, nor a distance measured to V2, nor the take-off DISTANCE (which measures the full run to 35 ft).
8iQwwWLJSrMANOeykfyH: This question depends on a plotted diagram that this text-only version cannot show, so learn the principle instead. Three VOR radials rarely meet at a point; they enclose a small triangle known as a cocked hat. After correcting for known systematic errors the remaining scatter is random, so the most probable position is inside the cocked hat, not at any vertex and not outside it. If the triangle is large, distrust the fix and check for a mis-identified station.
8id1V194Qw0ntHaP3zSr: ICAO Annex 2 requires a controlled flight to notify ATC when the TAS varies or is expected to vary by plus or minus 5% of the value in the flight plan. This ensures ATC can maintain accurate traffic spacing based on current speeds.
8ipRbLrCGJksJBeJ0R2c: Air spills round the tip from the high-pressure region under the wing to the low-pressure region above it, so each vortex circulates from the underside up over the tip and inboard across the top. Seen from behind, the left vortex turns clockwise and the right one anticlockwise, which is why the flow between them is downward and outside them is upward.
8jk03M160VrGvjgQuKZU: A thermal circuit breaker uses a bimetallic element heated by the current, so it trips on the heating effect of an overload after a delay that depends on how large the overload is. That delay lets it ride out harmless surges while still protecting the wiring from a sustained overcurrent.
8jm1xIjzBDTd4TjSfraa: On a light twin the blue radial line marks the best rate of climb speed with one engine inoperative, Vyse - the speed to fly to get the best out of the aeroplane after an engine failure. The red radial line marks VMCA, the minimum control speed.
8k7fECYQrq2XtPaSpe1V: Cigarette smoke contains carbon monoxide, which binds to haemoglobin with over 200 times the affinity of oxygen. A smoker therefore carries several percent of his haemoglobin as carboxyhaemoglobin and is already, in effect, at altitude before take-off, so his tolerance to hypoxia is reduced. The gas is carbon monoxide, not carbon dioxide, and the effect is a loss of tolerance, never a gain.
8kL2ImuTu88jzTvL1h31: JAR-OPS 1.670 requires airborne weather radar for night or IMC operation in areas where thunderstorms may be expected on all pressurised aeroplanes, and on unpressurised aeroplanes with a maximum take-off mass above 5700 kg or a maximum approved seating configuration of more than nine. Being engaged in public transport is not by itself the trigger.
8lNwclbyk0EJmfuJz4L2: The three-phase tachogenerator on the engine feeds a synchronous motor in the instrument, which therefore turns at a speed locked to the supply frequency and hence to engine speed. That motor then drives a magnetic drag-cup element which converts its rotation into a pointer deflection.
8lo8n4g03GCPnCzNa0dz: The passenger mask is a continuous flow type with a rebreather bag: oxygen flows into the bag at a fixed rate and the wearer draws it in mixed with cabin air through the ports round the mask. It is not a sealed mask and there is no pressure demand function.
8lvTVuVoVYMvMtL4lEmj: The remedies are to restore the oxygen supply and reduce demand: descend below 10,000 ft (statement 1), breathe 100% oxygen (statement 2) and cut physical activity, since exercise raises oxygen consumption and shortens the time of useful consciousness (statement 4). Climbing to or above 10,000 ft would make the hypoxia worse.
8mBoWCMWFxKCApIeZP53: The Alert phase (ALERFA) is declared when apprehension exists as to the safety of an aircraft and its occupants. The Distress phase (DETRESFA) is when the aircraft is considered to be in a state of emergency. The Uncertainty phase (INCERFA) is the initial stage when communication is overdue.
8mKudwAjlCgr90Uekc3I: A rhumb line crosses every meridian at the same angle. On a Direct Mercator the meridians are parallel vertical lines, so a line of constant angle to them is a straight line. That is the defining property of the projection and the reason it is used for plotting charts. Great circles, by contrast, appear as curves concave to the equator.
8mn0D0Bii1vXYkli7IQd: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that runway threshold lights and wing bar lights shall be fixed unidirectional lights showing green in the direction of approach. Green marks the beginning of the usable runway for landing.
8nxsjQLbM1BdEBenMqjZ: With no ground lights, no horizon and no texture between the aircraft and the runway, the only cue left is the aerodrome lighting itself, which the pilot tends to read as being nearer and lower than it is - so he feels too high and too far out. Correcting for that false impression he descends below the proper path and lands short, often into terrain short of the threshold.
8pAmNtSDh0nsHovNtOk3: A self-centred cockpit is one where each crew member works in isolation, without telling the others what he is doing and assuming without checking that they know. Cross-monitoring collapses and errors go undetected. Synergy is the opposite condition and requires deliberate, explicit communication, so the other options describe outcomes that cannot follow from egocentric behaviour.
8ppNTYPArb6ExX87cWlA: In the event of radio communication failure, the pilot shall set transponder code 7600 on Mode A regardless of the previously assigned code. Code 7600 is the internationally recognised squawk for communication failure, alerting ATC to the situation.
8qHueGKn5cWomehqEVZw: At low rotor speeds the low pressure compressor delivers more air than the high pressure compressor can swallow, so the LP stages stall. The bypass valve opens to spill that surplus, restoring the axial velocity through the LP compressor and keeping it clear of stall until the engine has accelerated.
8rMqoJJJJn1y4EkNkxTa: A resting adult breathes about 12-16 times a minute, moving roughly 500 ml per breath. Rates well above this at rest indicate hyperventilation, and the depth as well as the rate matters, since it is total ventilation relative to CO2 production that determines whether the blood CO2 level is maintained.
8rTSO5HqVYmDluYVHKwV: Airside is defined as the movement area of an aerodrome, the adjacent terrain and buildings or portions thereof, access to which is controlled. This is distinct from the manoeuvring area (runways and taxiways only, excluding aprons) and broader than a terminal building.
8rbRWFIonHoxG79pmbTl: For a short stop the body clock should be left on home time, because it will not have adapted before the return sector. Once the layover exceeds about a day it is worth adapting: adopt local time immediately for sleeping, eating and daylight exposure, since those are the cues that shift the circadian rhythm.
8ryfw0DoI89mn8E4cBI3: A clearway is a defined rectangular area at the end of the take-off run available, selected or prepared as a suitable area over which an aeroplane may make a portion of its initial climb to a specified height. It extends the effective take-off distance but cannot be used for stopping.
8sP8IGShUUJrG5GbvWuX: A bus-bar is simply a heavy conductor to which sources and loads are connected - the point from which power is distributed. Splitting the system into several bus-bars, connected through tie breakers, is what allows a fault or a generator failure to be isolated without losing everything.
8subayLVaRIVZKGmaW6R: On the ground the aeroplane yaws without banking, so the needle shows the yaw to the right while the ball, thrown outwards by the turn, moves to the left. The result is a fully deflected needle with the ball out - the classic skidding indication, which on the ground is entirely normal.
8tibwYM5YvzsDWFhtNWw: On the ground the altimeter shows the height of the aircraft above the datum set on the subscale. Setting 1013 when the actual QNH is 1008 is 5 hPa too high, and at about 27 ft per hPa that adds roughly 135 ft. Airfield elevation 1240 ft plus 135 ft gives 1375 ft, which is the pressure altitude of the airfield.
8uurTEKXbXD5lPJtzlTg: A Control Area (CTA) is a controlled airspace extending upwards from a specified limit above the earth. The lower limit is not fixed at 1000 ft — it varies and is established by the relevant authority. A Control Zone (CTR), by contrast, extends upwards from the surface.
8wATAXuXdoCUXh1PSyOm: A stabiliser jammed at the cruise setting leaves the aeroplane trimmed nose-down relative to what a normal flap-down approach needs, so the elevator has to hold a large out-of-trim pull force. Landing faster reduces the elevator deflection required, and selecting less flap reduces the nose-up trim change that has to be countered in the first place. Both measures reduce the residual out-of-trim force to something manageable in the flare.
8wb3N8WGfsfjhbhZj0rV: TCAS needs its own aircraft's pressure altitude, which it takes from the Mode S transponder (1), radio height to inhibit advisories near the ground (2), and configuration inputs such as gear position so that it can suppress advisories during take-off and landing (3). Inertial data plays no part in it.
8wumd3jxMIJptLXgbnSV: The autothrottle controls thrust, so its modes are a thrust setting expressed as N1 (1) or a speed to be held with thrust (3). N2 is not a thrust-rating parameter, and the autothrottle is a separate system which can be engaged or disengaged independently of the autopilot - a manual approach with the autothrottle in speed mode is normal practice.
8wvRxHElCpDdlgghJG7W: Spatial disorientation arises from conflict between sensory channels - typically the vestibular organs and seat-of-the-pants sense reporting one attitude while the instruments report another. The correct response is to believe the instruments; disorientation is most dangerous when the pilot resolves the conflict in favour of his bodily sensations, so the risk grows precisely when that contradiction exists.
8xnFoDvLY7JEYFJZAvEO: Drift down is the procedure used when an engine fails at a cruise level above the one-engine-inoperative maximum altitude, so the aeroplane can no longer hold height. It descends at the speed for the best gradient, at maximum continuous thrust on the remaining engine or engines, until it reaches the level-off altitude - and the requirement it must satisfy is obstacle clearance along the net flight path during that descent.
8xzpDDigGMHzSupz2WDZ: Life jackets are required for every occupant once the aeroplane operates over water beyond gliding distance from land or more than 50 NM from the shore, so they are needed here. Life rafts become mandatory only beyond 120 minutes at cruising speed or 400 NM, whichever is less: at 180 kt, 120 minutes is 360 NM, and the aeroplane is 340 NM out, just inside the threshold.
8zA8eyenkfkcymS25FPL: Decode the abbreviations: MOD TO SEV CAT is moderate to severe clear air turbulence, FCST means forecast rather than observed, BTN FL260 AND FL380 gives the vertical extent of the hazard, STNR means the area is stationary, and INTSF means the intensity is increasing. The validity 030700/031100 runs from 0700 to 1100 UTC on the 3rd. Note that STNR rules out any answer describing the zone as moving.
8zCj8Zan7lFnLH0Q2kcS: Moments in a loading manifest are always taken about the datum, not about the current centre of gravity. The arm is therefore 16 m, and the moment is 500 kg x 10 m/s2 x 16 m = 80,000 Nm. The 10 m to the present centre of gravity is what would be used to calculate the shift the load produces, which is a different calculation.
90XKVymQWxEqwPT64ubl: Deep stall - a stable, unrecoverable stall - needs two things together. A swept wing tends to stall at the tips first, which moves the centre of pressure forward and pitches the nose UP, driving the angle of attack higher still. A T-tail then sits directly in the low-energy turbulent wake shed by the stalled wing, so the elevator loses effectiveness exactly when it is needed to push the nose down. Aircraft with this combination are fitted with stick pushers.
917rzllpSyowPuLMVHxy: The APU drives a generator for electrical power (1) and supplies bleed air, which is used both to start the main engines (2) and to run the air conditioning packs on the ground (4). It has no hydraulic pump of its own - hydraulic power on the ground comes from electric pumps driven by the APU generator.
91Cx6FXD6Y4VkTDbGFKh: A thermal low is maintained by surface heating, which drives convergence into the low at the surface. That converging air must rise, and the ascent can only continue if it is removed aloft by upper-level divergence. Widespread ascent cools the air adiabatically to saturation, producing extensive cloud and precipitation. The reverse pattern - surface divergence with upper convergence - describes an anticyclone.
924eDXECBQOdR4Elz0I7: With both aircraft TCAS II equipped the two units exchange their intentions over the Mode S data link before issuing advisories, so the manoeuvres are coordinated - one climbs and the other descends. TCAS does not know what ATC has instructed and cannot coordinate with it, which is why an RA takes priority over an ATC clearance.
92QrqAiXZh5TwLGf2PAn: A piston engine converts only about 30% of the energy in its fuel into useful shaft power. Roughly a third goes out with the exhaust and another third into the cooling air and oil, with the remainder lost to friction - which is why an engine needs so much cooling for the power it produces.
92ZpShEoOZFvMeWRb27B: Diving loads the tissues with extra dissolved nitrogen at pressures above one atmosphere. Climbing to a cabin altitude soon afterwards lowers the ambient pressure further, so bubbles form and decompression sickness results without any decompression event in the aircraft. The recommended wait is 12 hours after a no-stop dive and 24 hours or more after dives requiring decompression stops.
93u0Q4FCZrbSuahdawtn: Bypass ratio is the cold flow divided by the core flow. With 500 kg/s entering and 250 kg/s through the core, the other 250 kg/s bypasses it, giving 250/250 = 1:1 - a low bypass engine typical of early turbofans.
93v8aq8GoSz73mpVaOUL: An under-inflated tyre bulges so that the shoulders take the load while the centre of the tread lifts clear, so wear appears at the edges. Over-inflation does the opposite, wearing the crown. Under-inflation also builds heat in the sidewalls and lowers the aquaplaning speed, which varies with the square root of pressure.
942ZrkeA4ylnmKTZrQbu: Carbon monoxide binds to the same site on haemoglobin as oxygen but with an affinity around 200-250 times greater, so it occupies carriage capacity and will not release it. It also shifts the dissociation curve so that the oxygen still carried is released less readily to the tissues. The lungs and the diffusion membrane themselves are unaffected.
94iNoHCgbPh6YnpIC6JU: Bernoulli's theorem gives total (pitot) pressure = static pressure + dynamic pressure, where dynamic pressure is 1/2 rho V2. Total pressure is what a pitot tube facing the airflow senses; static pressure is what a flush port parallel to the flow senses. The ASI works by measuring the difference between the two, which is the dynamic pressure and hence the indicated airspeed.
9577z1bvzcHmgjx70Imi: On a Lambert the chart convergence is correct only at the parallel of origin, so a great circle drawn on the sheet bows slightly towards that parallel: it is a curve CONCAVE to the parallel of origin. 957v24v1DphMo7h4L2qQ: A clearance issued as 'via flight planned route' accepts the route exactly as filed, including any deviation from the ATS route structure that was written into Item 15. 95cAfdKNVBGN4pEGJoO7: A capacitance probe is a pair of concentric tubes forming a capacitor with the fuel and the air above it as the dielectric. 97atGVIikeB0RH6KuTl2: A shock stall is separation caused by the steep adverse pressure gradient behind a shock wave, and shock waves appear once the LOCAL flow goes supersonic - which at high cruise Mach numbers happens at quite a low angle of attack. This is the essence of the coffin corner: at high altitude the aeroplane can be close to both boundaries at once.
97szYddUTdBKB5dmfhmt: Hypoxia results from any failure to restore the oxygen supply after a loss of cabin pressure at altitude, and the time of useful consciousness after a rapid decompression at high level is measured in seconds. 97zQ0rym2OJprOXu7WtC: Temporary information of long duration (3 months or more), or short-term information containing extensive text or graphics, is published as AIP Supplements. 9ABMYTMt0mczEbnprGnv: A full alignment takes several minutes because gyrocompassing has to detect the earth's rotation rate, which is a very small signal, and average out the noise. 9AT5KhJqRp7ak507zauE: Lambert chart convergence is a constant, dlong x sin(parallel of origin), whereas earth convergency is dlong x sin(latitude) and therefore varies. 9AlnPRa0IbsTizQQupED: The saturated adiabatic lapse rate is lower than the dry rate only because condensation releases latent heat, and the amount of latent heat available depends on how much water vapour the air holds. Cirrus forms at very low temperatures where the air can hold almost no moisture, so almost no latent heat is released and the SALR approaches the DALR of 3 C/1000 ft. In warm cumulus near the surface the SALR can be as low as 1.2 C/1000 ft.
9BHnE6exXVf391tNPz6P: The cone constant, also called the constant of the cone or n, is the sine of the parallel of origin, which lies midway between the two standard parallels. The mean of 10 40 N and 41 20 N is 26 degrees, and sin26 = 0.44. The same number is the factor used to convert change of longitude into chart convergence.
9CeFH6hGuMxVfNX038hV: During an approach, the altimeter should be set to the reported aerodrome QNH within the transition layer — that is, between the transition level and the transition altitude. This is where the changeover from standard pressure to local QNH occurs.
9DJ88Hovjl5bSunKtTbi: Apparent drift is 15 x sine of the latitude degrees per hour, so at 30° it is 15 x 0.5 = 7.5°/hr. In the southern hemisphere the apparent rotation is the opposite way round to the northern, so the drift appears to the left.
9DWaw48BUlgnnI3dkzhp: All four are recognised forms. Statement 1 is hypoxic hypoxia (low inspired oxygen partial pressure), statement 2 is anaemic or hypaemic hypoxia (carriage capacity lost to carbon monoxide), statement 3 is stagnant hypoxia (blood does not reach the tissue) and statement 4 is histotoxic hypoxia (the cell cannot use the oxygen delivered, as with alcohol).
9DuFSrWPgtVy9TAHIPr9: Alerting Service and Flight Information Service are often provided by the same ATS unit, typically a Flight Information Centre or Area Control Centre. This is operationally efficient because both services require the same situational awareness of traffic in the FIR.
9DvDBbEWKnceo7RC1vS8: The tropical tropopause is both the highest (16-18 km) and the coldest, at around -75 C to -80 C, because deep convection lifts air a long way and it cools all the way up. The mid-latitude tropopause is near -56.5 C at 11 km and the polar tropopause is the warmest, near -45 C at 8 km. Height and temperature therefore vary inversely with latitude.
9ENu4pHE0QgV3hit1OPv: A unit flowmeter works on the pressure drop the flow produces across a known restriction, with a temperature input so that the density can be allowed for and the reading converted into mass flow. Measuring pressure and temperature is therefore what the instrument physically does; flow is what it computes from them.
9EYTv6hhlniRF4X77Kan: Both are correct. On a free turbine engine the propeller is not mechanically tied to the gas generator, so reducing the power setting reduces the fuel flow, the gas generator slows down and less gas is produced - so both the HP spool speed and the turbine gas temperature fall. The propeller speed stays where the governor holds it.
9EjN4OsUeMVfTuBE6KDs: The ITCZ follows the overhead sun with a lag, so it crosses the equator twice a year, near the equinoxes. Equatorial Africa therefore has two rainy seasons, around March-May and October-November, separated by two relatively drier periods. Away from the equator the two passes merge into a single wet season.
9F1uRl22rgIx7AKTDdmV: A pack a day typically produces a carboxyhaemoglobin level of around 5-8%, so that fraction of the haemoglobin is unavailable for oxygen carriage. The practical consequence is a physiological altitude several thousand feet above the actual cabin altitude and a measurable loss of night vision on the ground.
9GBvVk3eabuzpxAy9zuK: Below VMD the aeroplane is in the region of reversed command, where induced drag dominates and rises as speed falls. Slowing down therefore INCREASES the total drag and so requires MORE thrust - the reverse of normal intuition. This is why an approach flown behind the drag curve is unstable: any speed loss increases the drag, which loses more speed unless thrust is added promptly.
9GlEKJGUmmZttDfVjY7D: Both points are on the 70S parallel and the flight runs west from 065E to 025W, so the vertex is at the mid-longitude 020E, where the westbound track is 270. Convergency from A to the vertex is 45 x sin70 = about 42 degrees, and a westbound great circle track in the southern hemisphere increases along the route, so the departure track from A is about 270 - 42 = 228, closest to 225.
9Gqm4CovmapKTq8KcyYS: For turboprops the required landing distance at the destination and at any alternate must not exceed 70% of the landing distance available - equivalently the landing distance is factored by 1/0.7, about 1.43. Turbojets use the more demanding 60% (a factor of 1.67), and a further 15% is added to either figure if the runway is forecast to be wet.
9GuuG2UiF5fD9RXrN6Ig: Water extinguishes by cooling the fuel below its ignition temperature, which suits class A solids - paper, fabric, carpet, wood. It is dangerous on flammable liquids, which it spreads, on live electrical equipment, which it conducts through, and on burning metals, which react with it.
9GwWHhcLqt2Z1zn7ZZ2f: ICAO Annex 10 requires that when an aircraft carries a serviceable transponder, the pilot shall operate it at all times during flight, regardless of whether the aircraft is within airspace where SSR is used for ATS purposes. This ensures the aircraft is always visible to any available radar.
9J24iThmTVKYDfp55VFx: The Direct Mercator is a cylindrical projection: a cylinder is wrapped round the earth touching at the equator, and the graticule is projected onto it, which is why the meridians end up parallel. Lambert charts are conical and polar charts are azimuthal (plane).
9JTe3cRWR89e425N1G8r: At high indicated airspeed a full rudder deflection would generate loads beyond the fin's design case, so the limiter progressively reduces the available travel as speed increases. It is a structural protection, and it is why full rudder authority is available at low speed where it is needed for engine failure control.
9K2YBGj5kL4EIWQ8aW0I: Two effects combine to produce Mach tuck. First, the shock wave forming on the upper surface moves the centre of pressure AFT, lengthening the nose-down moment arm about the CG. Second, the shock-induced separation reduces the downwash reaching the tailplane, which DECREASES the tailplane's effective angle of attack and hence its download, removing some of the nose-up moment it was providing. Both act nose-down.
9K3RiTX8jISWPwVe6kCs: Standard procedures already cover the procedural actions, so the value of a briefing lies elsewhere: it builds a shared mental model of what this crew will do in this situation - the non-procedural decisions and contingencies - so that when the moment comes each pilot knows what the other expects. That shared schema is what makes coordinated action possible without discussion at the critical time.
9KIw941m6Nqqx5OsTm9C: In a reaction turbine the pressure falls across both rows: the nozzle guide vanes accelerate the gas and drop its pressure, and the rotor blades, being aerofoils forming convergent passages, drop it further as the gas accelerates through them. 9KgVRwxbPX8E27D8SgOA: The passenger system is continuous flow: a chemical generator or a metered supply feeds oxygen into a rebreather bag at a fixed rate, and the passenger draws it in mixed with cabin air. 9LKZGKIeryp87V9SolIM: Dewpoint can never exceed the air temperature, because as soon as air is cooled to its dewpoint it saturates and further cooling condenses out the excess. It can, however, equal the air temperature: that is precisely the saturated state, with relative humidity 100%, which is the condition inside cloud and fog.
9MXSLXn7ZrALJKHE5kQ7: Stress management works on both ends of the problem: preventing stress where it can be prevented, by good rostering, preparation, fitness, sleep and workload management, and removing or reducing it once present, through relaxation techniques, exercise, delegation and talking the problem through. Neither half alone is a complete programme, and psychoactive drugs are not part of it.
9NRcokmCDrZlqsT5GWCe: Low pressure fuel readings are taken with a capsule or bellows referenced to a second pressure, so that a small pressure is measured accurately and the reading is unaffected by ambient changes. 9NW4GHJpkQuZwmahdXsJ: Take-off fuel is 17,000 + 5,000 = 22,000 kg. The traffic load is then 130,500 - 82,000 - 22,000 = 26,500 kg.
9Nc5VGODlDWDcJ6TMJrP: Deviation is the angle between magnetic north and compass north, caused by the aircraft's own magnetism. Variation is the angle between true north and magnetic north, a property of the earth. Dip is the angle between the horizontal and the total field, and is not an azimuth error at all.
9NhpxGPhtweq8TqCQtWG: Air accelerating through the venturi throat falls in pressure, and it is the difference between that reduced pressure and the atmospheric pressure in the float chamber which drives fuel out of the main jet. The stronger the airflow the greater the depression, so fuel flow follows air flow automatically.
9Np6IJ0hSkG0HoWCozC9: Stick POSITION stability - the relationship between elevator position and airspeed - is set by the CG position and the configuration, not by the trim setting. Moving the trim tab changes the speed at which the stick force is zero, and hence the whole stick FORCE curve, but the elevator still has to sit in the same place to hold a given speed. So stick position stability is unaffected.
9Nwwo9vVkD5B9g8mJu6C: Pre-ignition is ignition of the charge by a hot spot in the cylinder - a glowing carbon deposit, an overheated valve or plug electrode - before the spark occurs. The charge burns while the piston is still rising, so peak pressure arrives too early and the piston fights it, producing very high temperatures and rapid damage.
9OEtfKka0trQ0OG6uOtJ: Dutch roll is a coupled oscillation in which yaw and roll feed one another, common on swept-wing aircraft where strong dihedral effect combines with relatively weak directional stability. A yaw damper senses yaw rate with a rate gyro and applies rudder to oppose it, breaking the coupling at source. Roll spoilers and rudder limiters serve quite different purposes.
9OfOHNEIcdtjBqhxBHFd: The ICAO Technical Instructions require dangerous goods markings and labels to be in English, in addition to any language demanded by the State of Origin. English is the common language of the transport chain, so a handler anywhere along the route can read the hazard.
9OponICftZGu1W6LrphL: The number of oxygen dispensing units is driven by the number of SEATS fitted, not by the passengers actually booked, and it must exceed that number by at least 10%: 200 seats gives 220 units. 9P93oMkFtWpzrRytlJ1S: An inversion is a layer in which temperature increases with height, reversing the normal profile. 9QAk0dmdVyYRdYAM92rX: The worst case combines a heavy generator, an aeroplane just rotating (heavy, clean and slow), and a LIGHT crosswind - light enough to carry the vortex sideways onto the adjacent runway but too weak to break it up or clear it away. 9QQ5G2X94Ao3fB3Lwa4x: Statement I is correct: the acrylic or glass laminate is much more brittle when cold, so with the window heat inoperative a lower speed limit applies below a given altitude to keep bird strike energy within what the cold window can absorb. 9R1KeYjNP2Uar8eYUcGB: A symmetrical aerofoil has no camber, so at zero lift the pressure distributions on the upper and lower surfaces are mirror images and there is no residual couple: Cm0 = 0. 9RDUUANFMVrP8kDMREwd: All four help. 9RG5Hda1sAjDqZjy5B5q: With the pitot blocked the total pressure is trapped, while the static pressure continues to fall in a climb and rise in a descent. 9SCBdwnqU2MojYTO8UwZ: Mass and balance documentation must be retained for three months, in common with the operational flight plan and the journey log, so the flight can be reconstructed if it is later investigated.
9SXjMCZ6zdpT0729iK3K: A stopway is a defined rectangular area at the end of the take-off run available, prepared so that an aircraft can be stopped in the case of an abandoned take-off. It is included in the accelerate-stop distance available (ASDA) but not in the take-off distance available (TODA).
9SZqC7btlxwfVu8UlOLX: Entry into a holding pattern should be determined based on the aircraft's course (the intended path of flight), not heading (which is affected by wind), bearing, or track. The three entry sectors are defined relative to the inbound course to the holding fix.
9SddSp6uNpiDpRTyl4ZN: Fifteen degrees of drift at 240 kt TAS means a crosswind of 240 x sin15 = about 62 kt, so the along-track air component is 240 x cos15 = about 232 kt. 9ShPWigveuyGEYO5Dtlv: A non-MNPS approved aircraft may be cleared to climb or descend through MNPS levels where it is under radar surveillance and in direct VHF contact with the controller, because the controller can then provide the separation the aircraft cannot guarantee by its own navigation performance. 9T5wRN7iaopbpOG3T3oA: The gust envelope in CS-25 is built on three reference gust velocities in the clean configuration: 66 ft/s at VB (the rough air / design gust speed), 50 ft/s at VC (design cruising speed) and 25 ft/s at VD (design dive speed). 9TNmIWLGFZsuqG3RqI8N: Outboard ailerons give a long moment arm and hence powerful roll control, which is wanted at low speed with the flaps out. 9Tn7SY9OgqAXde0YY9Jf: Dispatch with items inoperative is permitted only as allowed by the Minimum Equipment List, the operator's Authority-approved document derived from the manufacturer's MMEL. 9UIugWDAZcNcDWTIF9Q2: Nickel-cadmium cells accept and deliver very high currents (3), work over a wide temperature range (4), hold their charge well in storage (5) and are built into a robust metal case (6). 9UMUSvFrjCwp3B6fOgBL: Compression raises the pressure of every constituent gas equally, so the proportions are unchanged - the air remains 21% oxygen. What pressurisation does is raise the partial pressure of that 21%, which is exactly what makes the cabin habitable at altitude.
9UNpNYAhAwYIkV4LR5aD: Sustained exposure above about 90 dB damages the hair cells of the cochlea, producing a permanent sensorineural loss that typically shows first as a notch around 4 kHz. 9UO1zC6Ram2grX58HiWL: The stoichiometric or chemically correct ratio is about one part fuel to fifteen parts air by mass - the proportion at which all the fuel and all the oxygen are consumed. 9UgZ5j9BtkI6v5MZTjSV: AIRAC (Aeronautical Information Regulation and Control) is a system of advance notification based on common effective dates for changes that require significant operating procedure amendments. It is not a publication itself but a scheduling mechanism using 28-day cycles.
9UzO977MtQMig9iBHdBs: Air is supplied to the cabin at a roughly constant rate, so cabin pressure is set by how fast it is allowed to escape. The controller drives the outflow valve to follow the scheduled cabin altitude; the inward and duct relief valves are protective devices which only operate at their limits.
9VaavzNUNyUR2u8vCEcB: A radio altimeter that detects an internal failure or loses lock removes the height indication altogether and displays a failure flag, so the crew cannot act on a reading that may be wrong. Silently displaying an erroneous height near the ground would be far more dangerous than showing nothing.
9W8UdJTRbXp7zA5Kik9f: The primary area of an instrument approach segment is a defined area symmetrically disposed about the nominal flight track in which the full Minimum Obstacle Clearance (MOC) is provided. 9WWX3tcbJTSX5W5LGiyB: Moving the head out of the plane of a turn stimulates a second pair of semicircular canals while the first pair is already responding, and the brain interprets the combination as tumbling in a completely different axis. 9WZN8fa7fBuuZAy0Qn2J: The polar front jet is driven by the horizontal temperature contrast across the polar front. 9WmgyUP7OEyPTtUMwjNt: A fail-operational system has enough redundancy to complete the landing automatically after a single failure, but once that failure has occurred the remaining capability is only fail-passive: a second failure will cause a disconnect without a significant deviation, and the landing must then be completed manually or a go-around flown.
9XBJtsfe66CD9vrGdwnF: A helicopter has very little natural stability, and the stability augmentation system supplies what the airframe lacks - restoring the tendency to return towards the trimmed condition after a disturbance. It has limited authority and works through series actuators, so it augments rather than controls.
9XBuECLFkCZB3v0wHwSj: Stall speed rises whenever more lift is demanded or less CLmax is available. 9XQ5vzbAW2PPKY7zEPLQ: The operator is responsible for ensuring that the performance claimed in the operations manual can actually be achieved, including any allowance for the state of the aircraft and the conditions of the day. The manufacturer supplies certified data and the commander applies it, but demonstrating the performance is achievable in service is the operator's duty.
9XV1Gc4pNe0XJIU7G0i5: Alignment uses the only two references available without any outside aid: gravity, which the accelerometers sense to establish the local vertical during levelling, and the earth's rotation, which the gyros sense to find true north during gyrocompassing. 9XZAqj4dofXyXuXPXJ0N: All four appear in an overstressed pilot. 9YKfHkgRUXdxU4oALd38: Wet snow reduces the friction coefficient available to the wheel brakes and, on a contaminated surface, raises the risk of reverted-rubber or viscous aquaplaning. 9ZbDlwjyXaparC5oC1dj: Aircraft on the same track at the same Mach number are separated longitudinally by 10 minutes in MNPS airspace. 9ZllLJrJHB8XVzZLAtp7: The Kenya Civil Aviation Authority sets 35 hours as the minimum flying experience for the grant of a CPL(H) — Commercial Pilot Licence (Helicopter). National requirements vary and may differ from ICAO minimum standards.
9ZmyIL0mhBWQMgBkvPQD: Carboxyhaemoglobin is cleared slowly - the half-life breathing air is several hours, and complete recovery from a significant exposure takes days, which is why an affected crew member cannot simply return to duty once the symptoms ease. 9aHJXpY7BikZPDeBeiUV: Two features crossed at right angles at a known distance apart give a measured time over a known ground distance, which is groundspeed. 9aJiZhLP94DDJ2x7ccHR: On east-west NAT tracks south of 70N, position reports are made at each 10 degrees of longitude between 5W and 65W. North of 70N the interval opens to 20 degrees, because the meridians converge and 10 degrees would be an impractically short leg.
9bCwnyrn19gLqkRuQRjF: Human reliability figures quoted in this context run from about one error in a hundred on a simple repetitive task, to about one in a thousand once the task has been methodically trained, with one in ten thousand attainable only for very well designed and highly practised operations. One in a thousand is therefore the realistic post-training figure.
9bqQMP4k94aYMvDaYFdQ: As the core temperature falls the brain is affected early: the person becomes apathetic and withdrawn, loses interest in his own situation and stops taking sensible protective action, before shivering ceases and consciousness is lost. That indifference is the dangerous feature, because the victim will not help himself and may not be recognised as being in trouble.
9bz83kchIdN3V1Tu1Cvr: As keyed, the fuel requirement for a VFR flight to an offshore platform is the same as for VFR over land. 9c0304oCVPswOdAjnel8: Centre of gravity position is quoted as a distance along the longitudinal axis from the datum, or as a percentage of the mean aerodynamic chord, because it is fore-and-aft position that governs longitudinal stability and control. 9c1c9PKOc2TbfezPs0Bp: Carbon monoxide is colourless, odourless and tasteless, so there is no sensory warning at all - contamination from a cracked exhaust heat exchanger is detected only by the symptoms or by a detector. No amount is harmless in flight, altitude makes the effects worse rather than better because both reduce oxygen delivery, and it lowers rather than raises blood oxygen saturation.
9c4urqjkiT74vDtKu2N3: The command bar shows what to do next, not where the aeroplane is. Above the glideslope it will initially command a pitch down, but once the pilot has established an appropriate rate of descent the bar centres to say 'hold this' - so a centred bar with the aircraft still displaced simply means the correction in hand is the right one.
9e75UH7EJYW0NarbzwKv: An air-cooled piston engine is cooled by ram air ducted through baffles round the cylinders, its flow controlled by cowl flaps. That is why cooling is poorest at low airspeed and high power - the climb - and why cowl flaps are opened for the climb and closed in the cruise.
9eWN9SDVR1HWXYfg4JSe: GPS satellites orbit at about 20 200 km above the WGS-84 ellipsoid, which gives the 12 hour period. Do not confuse this with the 35 800 km of a geostationary satellite, used for communications and for SBAS augmentation, or with the much lower orbits used by earth observation satellites.
9fTjXeKkwUD4sWjgPggD: 3000 ft is above the friction layer, so the wind there is the gradient wind, blowing parallel to the contours (isohypses). Backed, not veered, is the key point.
9fTmci6ay9zx0NiQV9OP: The turbine extracts energy from the gas stream, so as the gas expands through it the pressure and the temperature both fall while its velocity rises through the nozzle guide vanes. That pressure drop is the energy being converted into shaft work to drive the compressor.
9fb73yYAFvgCDRJNFnof: Emotional arousal - fright, anxiety, stress or pain - is the usual trigger for hyperventilation in flight, because it drives breathing beyond what metabolism requires. 9fekrHmbsd8JioB874Kz: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies that ATIS broadcasts should include cloud information when the clouds are below 2000 m (approximately 6000 ft) or below the highest minimum sector altitude, whichever is greater. This threshold captures operationally significant cloud cover.
9gAG7RopefdVibl9dDJI: A subsonic intake is a divergent duct: it slows the air down before it reaches the compressor, and in doing so converts velocity into static pressure - the ram effect. 9gYuXKQuHpK0vf1GCT78: Cold air is denser, so the pressure levels lie closer together and the aeroplane is lower than the altimeter suggests. The indication is therefore higher than the true altitude - the origin of the warning that flying from high to low, or hot to cold, means look out below.
