MEnuUP4PtOFqssNCbiqr: Bandwidth is conventionally measured between the points where the response has fallen 3 dB below its maximum - the half-power points. Defining it that way makes the figure comparable between amplifiers and reflects the range over which the gain is effectively flat.
MF5XE0IkjopDvHGyBvv8: The cochlea is the spiral, fluid-filled organ of the inner ear in which sound vibrations are converted into nerve impulses by hair cells on the basilar membrane, arranged so that different positions respond to different frequencies. The semicircular canals and the otolith organs are the vestibular part of the same inner ear.
MFGo2FISGuCo7TwUZSwC: An open-circuit voltage tells you little, since a nearly flat battery shows a normal voltage until current is drawn. Applying a known load reveals the internal resistance, and a large voltage drop under that load is what identifies a discharged or failing battery.
MFR8yfUahNuEDmGrXISa: The flight director recomputes continuously, so the command bars always show the best thing to do from where the aircraft is at this instant - not a fixed path laid down when the mode was selected. That is why following the bars smoothly produces a capture without overshoot whatever the starting geometry.
MFb95bOYOGi4XeQJJ4Eh: Hyperventilation means breathing beyond metabolic need, and in flight the trigger is almost always emotional: fear, anxiety, stress, pain or startle. The result - a falling CO2 level - produces symptoms that mimic hypoxia and can feed the anxiety that started it.
MG9X9PNxu3Xj6dzxYFTq: The white arc is the flap operating range: its lower end is VS0, the stalling speed in the landing configuration, and its upper end is VFE, the maximum speed with flaps extended. The green arc above it covers the clean configuration from VS1 to VNO.
MGSxD1g35Ea9cKrHUbUH: Zero fuel mass is 34 000 + 13 000 = 47 000 kg, inside the 51 250 limit. MGfcau5pxd8nAeJrur7h: Quadrantal error is caused by the incoming wave being re-radiated and bent by the aircraft's own metal structure, so it is worst at relative bearings around 045, 135, 225 and 315 and zero on the cardinal relative bearings. It is a property of the airframe, so it is measured and compensated for during installation.
MHJLTwS3VWvj6A5F48GX: The passenger mask is a continuous flow type with a rebreather bag: oxygen flows into the bag at a fixed rate and the wearer draws it in mixed with cabin air through the ports round the mask. It is not a sealed mask and there is no pressure function.
MHwgWrkFwkBWhHSB8El1: A DC tachogenerator produces a voltage proportional to speed, which is easy to transmit to a simple voltmeter (1) and needs no aircraft supply, since the generator makes its own signal (2). Its weakness is the commutator, which produces brush noise - so statement 3 is exactly what it does not offer.
MIRO8VbwnYvHAsM2PUBs: Cold air is denser, so the pressure levels lie closer together and the aeroplane is lower than the altimeter suggests. The indication is therefore higher than the true altitude - the basis of the cold weather altitude correction and of the warning that flying from hot to cold means look out below.
MIjG0A33MBkYJsbcSKpu: A flight deck fire almost always involves live electrical equipment, so the agent must be non-conductive and must not obscure the instruments: halon or CO2. Water conducts, and powder coats the panels and displays, which is why neither is used there.
MJAVRCAB42On1M95lAZw: The air data computer takes pitot, static and total air temperature and computes everything that follows from them: pressure altitude (1), Mach number (2), calibrated airspeed (3), true airspeed (4) and static air temperature (5), along with vertical speed. All five are outputs.
MJe4eUaEaGuAzeqSqe8m: The Q-group in a METAR gives QNH in whole hectopascals, rounded DOWN to the next lower whole hPa. Rounding down is deliberate: a slightly low subscale setting makes the altimeter read slightly low, which places the aircraft slightly higher than indicated - the safe direction of error. QFE is never given in the METAR pressure group.
MK6AHoxouR6kCw2YIgNK: Endurance is time aloft, so maximum endurance means minimum fuel flow - and that is achieved in steady, unaccelerated LEVEL flight at the speed of least fuel consumption: minimum power for a propeller aeroplane, minimum drag for a jet. MKewOJ6plTqaDSZPYoUz: Above FL250 the dispensing units must exceed the number of seats by at least 10%, so the requirement is 110% of the seating capacity. The surplus covers cabin crew moving about and passengers not in their own seat when the masks drop.
MKuXSsIu2rSVe1JZxJL5: A deep stall is reached by continuing past the normal stall to a very high angle of attack - often 30-40 degrees - at which the stalled wing's wake completely blankets a T-tail, so the elevator loses effectiveness and cannot lower the nose. Because it is stable in that condition it is unrecoverable by normal means, which is why affected designs carry stick pushers. A shock stall, by contrast, occurs at LOW angle of attack.
MLSmuTa4SDjStIUaqYE1: Maximum range corresponds to a particular aerodynamic condition - a fixed point on the drag polar - and that point is defined by a lift coefficient, which is therefore the same at every altitude. What changes with altitude is the true airspeed at which that CL is achieved: it increases as density falls, which is exactly why cruising higher gives more miles per kilogram until thrust or buffet limits intervene.
MMCwmJLEMvPZLDcjULDE: All three describe the same function from different angles: running the stabiliser cancels the elevator hinge moment the autopilot is holding (1), which unloads the servo actuator (2), and it leaves the aeroplane in trim so the pilot takes over a balanced aircraft at disconnect (3).
MMKnKaaYOOB23GvpiyZH: An error is a mismatch between what the person intended and what actually resulted - the definition covers slips of execution as well as mistakes of intention. A violation, by contrast, is deliberate: a rule knowingly not followed. And no amount of training eliminates error, which is why systems are designed to tolerate and trap it.
MN0gWfOzwMY3zW1knTpq: Bonding ties every metallic part together at a low resistance, so lightning current has a defined path through the airframe (1), the whole structure sits at one potential (4), and static charge cannot build at joints and discharge as sparks, which would be heard as radio noise (3). It is a connection, not a reset to zero volts.
MN2ZPRLMwQDImogc7l2C: Halon is the agent of choice for a flight deck fire because it works on the electrical and material fires likely there, needs only a small quantity and leaves no residue on the instruments and controls. At least one halon extinguisher must be within reach of the crew.
MNqT65xAPggOs6wgkMw4: Apparent drift is 15 x sine of the latitude degrees per hour, so it is zero at the equator and reverses sign across it. On a due north track from 5°S to 5°N the magnitude never exceeds about 1.3°/hour and the effect on one side of the equator is cancelled by the other, so the net error is nil.
MOHaGYJK4x0Py5Y2rVMW: Wake turbulence is purely aerodynamic - the tip vortices that are the by-product of producing lift. Engine thrust produces jet blast, which is a separate and much shorter-lived hazard, and flap position changes the vortex pattern without being its cause.
MPYcSFpA5pL9jqgFC0pG: Power changes are made RPM first up and throttle first down, so that manifold pressure is never high while the crankshaft is turning slowly. Increasing RPM before manifold pressure keeps the engine out of the over-square condition that produces high peak cylinder pressures and detonation.
MPdx6MoyW4Y50QOKp3Wm: Autopilot functions divide into stabilisation, which controls the aircraft's rotation about its centre of gravity, and guidance, which controls where that centre of gravity goes - the flight path in three dimensions. Selecting a heading, a level or a localiser is guidance; holding wings level is stabilisation.
MRB1bMFFDQOWNNpRwYUv: Absolute instability means a parcel keeps rising whether it is saturated or not, which requires the environmental lapse rate to exceed even the dry adiabatic rate of 1 C per 100 m. Such superadiabatic layers are shallow and short-lived, typically just above a strongly heated surface on a hot afternoon, because the resulting convection quickly overturns and stabilises the layer.
MRfoF0TjklZgbLzB0bY6: Zero fuel mass is 33 510 + 7600 = 41 110 kg. On arrival at the alternate the fuel remaining is the final reserve plus the contingency fuel, which the plan assumes was not needed: 983 + 102 = 1085 kg. So the estimated landing mass at the alternate is 41 110 + 1085 = 42 195 kg. The alternate fuel is burned on the diversion and the trip fuel long before that.
MRmPuTsrZFW7EyjUXslD: A cross-track disagreement shows only that the two systems differ. INS 1 is coupled to the autopilot, so it reads zero by definition and that proves nothing about its accuracy; the 8 NM on INS 2 could be its error or INS 1's. All that follows is that at least one of them is drifting.
MRskgstC0OX2qin8fkOL: IAC charts include OCA/OCH values, DME frequencies, and obstacles in the final approach sector. However, visibility minima for alternate aerodrome use are typically published separately in the AIP text.
MRwQHJDStSeqMD3QMhjY: The fire handle isolates the engine, and that includes taking its generator off the bus and stopping it generating: the generator breaker opens and the exciter control relay opens. The bus tie is left alone so that the remaining generator can pick up the load.
MS3HJurETvDkCAABBvcm: Light flickering at a few cycles per second - sunlight chopped by a propeller or rotor - can produce disorientation, nausea, headache and, in susceptible individuals, a seizure. The remedy is to break the flicker: change heading or rotor speed, or block the light. Switching on strobes would add a second flickering source rather than remove one.
MSBuf9RjVVhTqFdZhYTW: TCAS works entirely by interrogating other aircraft's transponders, so an intruder whose transponder is off or unserviceable returns nothing and does not appear at all. It is the fundamental limitation of the system and the reason a visual lookout is still required.
MSgLUbKy9ztm6UQen8LF: Carbon dioxide dissolved in blood forms carbonic acid, so ventilating it off lowers the carbonic acid level and the blood becomes more alkaline - a respiratory alkalosis. The disturbance affects nerve and muscle function and produces the tingling, spasm and dizziness of hyperventilation. Oxygen is not the gas being lost; its saturation stays high throughout.
MStzG1GATYfQYUPVgyKY: Item 15 takes the planned TRUE airspeed, prefixed N when expressed in knots (K is used for kilometres per hour and M for Mach). So TAS 180 kt is filed as N0180. Groundspeed and calibrated airspeed never appear in the box.
MT8h3nGQSfAe9MsjTBjk: Put both ends on the same datum. QNH 1023 is 10 hPa above 1013, so at 30 ft per hPa the aerodrome's PRESSURE altitude is 1500 - 300 = 1200 ft. FL75 is a pressure altitude of 7500 ft, so the height to climb is 7500 - 1200 = 6300 ft.
MTfU5HiGsMKD0dC8MaL8: ICAO Doc 4444: a specific flight level is considered occupied when the aircraft is within plus or minus 300 ft of that level. This criterion may be reduced by appropriate ATS authorities.
MU8m4tzNopd3T7by14Db: Secondary controls change the aircraft's configuration or trim rather than controlling it about an axis: the trimmable stabiliser (1) and the speed brake (3). The rudder and the ailerons control yaw and roll directly, so both are primary flight controls.
MVN8Q8QWajV5b6c5Aq2g: Dry operating mass is the basic empty mass plus the operating items - crew and their baggage, catering, and any rescue or fly-away equipment carried: 30,000 + 300 + 365 = 30,665 kg. Take-off fuel and the traffic load are excluded by definition, and unusable fuel is already inside the basic empty mass, so adding it again would double count.
MVvSJpAH92lOmBzEyTCA: JAR-OPS requires life jackets when the aeroplane is flown over water more than 50 NM from the shore, and when the take-off or approach path is so disposed over water that a ditching would be likely. The 40 NM figure is not a JAR-OPS threshold.
MW0CXtGyt2wO7sCp1yAz: As fuel burns the aeroplane needs less lift, flies at less drag for the same speed, and burns less fuel per mile - so specific range INCREASES steadily through the cruise. The altitude at which that best specific range occurs also rises, because a lighter aeroplane can achieve its optimum lift coefficient in thinner air. This continuous rise in optimum altitude is why step climbs are flown.
MWVm0XAPWGq5x5zWjx9c: A runway wider than the pilot is used to subtends a larger angle, so it looks nearer and the aircraft feels lower than it is. The pilot compensates by holding off, and the round-out is started too early and too high - with the risk of a heavy landing or a stall onto the runway. A narrower-than-usual runway produces the opposite error and an undershoot.
MWYO49klkZ3crcT1vsCp: Each slide carries its own cylinder of compressed gas, so inflation is immediate and independent of every aircraft system - which matters because the aircraft may have no power at all when the doors are opened. Deployment is automatic once the door is armed and opened.
MWiJpcs2hswIQBrpiENz: Only the power stroke delivers work; the other three consume it, which is why a single cylinder engine needs a flywheel to carry it round. Multi-cylinder engines overlap their cycles so that at least one cylinder is always on its power stroke.
MWo9OExELVK3Kft9DdO6: On a 3 degree path the height is about 300 ft per nautical mile, so 2500 ft corresponds to 2500 / 300 = about 8.3 NM from the threshold. The same relationship in reverse gives the familiar rate of descent of about five times the groundspeed.
MWrsb3C9lhEb9Vf7WSJP: A single pole system runs only the live conductor to each component and returns the current through the metal airframe, which halves the wiring weight. It depends absolutely on good bonding, and it is unusable on a non-metallic airframe, which needs a two-wire, double pole system.
MXykUTUGGUnsbX0g06J6: At FL80 the pressure is about 753 hPa and the air at +20C is far warmer than the ISA value of -1C, so the density ratio is about 0.73 and TAS = CAS / root(sigma) = 120 / 0.855 = about 141 kt. Altitude alone would give about 139 kt; the warm air adds the rest.
MYBFaPya6Ga7wr54unPs: In a steady glide tan(glide angle) = CD/CL, so the descent angle is fixed entirely by the lift-to-drag ratio - and that ratio is determined by the angle of attack together with the configuration (flaps, gear, spoilers) that defines the drag polar. Mass and altitude change the SPEED at which a given angle of attack is flown, but not the glide angle achieved.
MYRN0G4hG8inJRKnDhsH: Pressing TO/GA sets go-around thrust automatically (1) and the autopilot flies the rotation and the climb-out (2), but changing the configuration remains the crew's business - the pilot calls for and the other pilot selects gear up and the flap reduction (5). Automation flies the aeroplane; it does not reconfigure it.
MYgs912xScTdqQQoZxlV: A magneto is entirely self-contained: rotating permanent magnets induce the primary current in its own coil, so the ignition works with the battery off and the electrical system dead. That independence is why a piston engine keeps running after an electrical failure.
MYoMkoNduq0yYDmuiRka: Communication is the first thing to go: under stress attention narrows onto the perceived problem, messages become shorter, more abrupt or stop altogether, and listening suffers most of all. Because everything else the crew does depends on it - cross-checking, monitoring, decision making - its loss is what turns an individual's stress into a crew failure.
MYw3GSpqJuVq9ShVoYvO: The wind from 130 is 40 degrees off the 090 track, giving about 13 kt of crosswind and 15 kt of headwind, so the groundspeed out is about 84 kt and back about 114 kt. Setting d/84 + d/114 = 2 hours gives d = about 97 NM. This is a radius of action problem: the answer is always less than half the still-air distance.
MZ5oXyjDXi1bkZqfNusQ: Above a certain Mach number the aft shift of the centre of pressure makes a swept-wing aeroplane tuck nose-down, so the stick force gradient flattens or reverses - apparent speed stability is lost. The Mach trimmer senses Mach number and applies an automatic nose-up input to restore a positive gradient. Straight-wing aeroplanes generally do not operate high enough into the transonic region to need one.
MZl85l71vLuhP6Sqbimp: Descending into the friction layer, the wind slows because of surface friction, and the weakened Coriolis force lets the pressure gradient force turn the flow toward low pressure - which in the northern hemisphere is a BACKING. So the surface wind is backed and weaker relative to the 2000 ft wind, by about 30 degrees and half the speed over land, or 10 degrees and a smaller reduction over the sea. Climbing out, the reverse: veers and increases.
Ma6KGrIGYhD3oao0dcCJ: Both are correct. Bypass ratio is the cold stream mass flow divided by the core mass flow, and since the inlet flow is the sum of the two, knowing the inlet and the core flows gives the bypass flow by subtraction and hence the ratio.
MaO1eqYpJL4g35fvDnTm: A small droplet contains little latent heat, so on striking a cold surface it freezes essentially instantaneously where it lands, trapping air between the frozen droplets. The result is rime: white, opaque, brittle and comparatively light, building forward from the leading edge. Only large droplets carry enough latent heat to stay partly liquid, run back, and build clear ice.
McJJUWvi7dWk7iNbRXBI: The Aerodrome Reference Code uses numbers 1-4 and letters A-F. Code 2B is valid (number 2 for field length 800-1200 m, letter B for wingspan 15-24 m). 5E and 6D are invalid as numbers exceed 4.
Mcze4HxiB5Gfr0sssQUU: RVR is used for non-precision approaches too - the idea that it applies only to precision approaches is simply wrong. The controlling value is the TOUCHDOWN ZONE (threshold) RVR, which must be at or above the minimum before the final approach is commenced; mid-point and stop-end values become controlling only in the lower categories where they are relevant.
MdExK5vszoEMSx3MCpPa: On initial power-up the CDU shows the IDENT page, which lets the crew confirm the model, engine rating and, critically, that the navigation database is the current AIRAC cycle. The normal sequence then runs IDENT, POS INIT, ROUTE, PERF INIT, TAKEOFF.
MdePOnefJwd5yo1Ihp1v: A compass swing is required after any large and PERMANENT change of magnetic latitude, because the aircraft's hard iron magnetism and the deviation it produces are latitude-dependent. A change of longitude does not matter, and the storage case that matters is standing on ONE heading for a long period, not being moved frequently.
MeYaTuGsz6TOapGrVKoV: The seat-of-the-pants sense is proprioception: receptors in the muscles, tendons and joints reporting the position and movement of body parts, together with pressure receptors in the skin. Because it senses the resultant of gravity and acceleration and cannot separate the two, it is unreliable in IMC. The utricle, saccule and semicircular canals are the separate vestibular system.
Mef88niOSwfnIc2b3huS: Statements 1, 2 and 3 form the standard drill: maintain a systematic instrument scan, believe the instruments rather than the sensations, and consciously disregard the illusions however convincing they are. Statement 4 would make it far worse - head movement during rotation is what produces the Coriolis illusion in the first place.
Menylot36NIwOxRMcRxk: During a prolonged turn the fluid in the semicircular canals catches up with the canal and the sensation of turning dies away. Rolling out then makes the fluid overshoot and deflect the cupula the other way, so the pilot feels he is turning in the opposite direction and is tempted to re-enter the original turn - the somatogyral illusion behind the graveyard spiral.
MfBrzDEyqaLLqpOQj4KF: The CVR is a microphone and pick-up system feeding a recorder built to survive impact, fire and immersion, with an underwater locator beacon. The flight data recorder is a separate unit recording parameters rather than audio, and the CVR is powered from the aircraft rather than from its own battery.
MfVLsSbAB8kZcCNUEOWy: Cigarette smoke contains carbon monoxide, which binds to haemoglobin with over 200 times the affinity of oxygen and will not readily let go. The haemoglobin so occupied is unavailable for oxygen carriage, so the smoker is effectively at altitude before take-off. Tar is a carcinogen but does not affect oxygen transport.
MfXVRk0vuuZMkGW1VdMh: Dalton's Law states that in a mixture each gas exerts a partial pressure proportional to its share of the mixture. Oxygen stays at 21% of the air all the way up, so as total pressure falls its partial pressure falls with it - and it is that falling partial pressure, not any change in composition, that produces hypoxic hypoxia.
Mfm6WMegx1oohjhVXGcv: The current ICAO AIP structure consists of three parts: GEN (General), ENR (En-route), and AD (Aerodromes). The older structure with separate AGA, COM, MET, FAL, MAP, RAC, and SAR sections has been superseded.
MfoZC3FdfGBVgMTr2fQn: The ICAO Standard Atmosphere is defined by pressure (1013.25 hPa at mean sea level), temperature (+15°C, lapsing at 1.98°C per 1,000 ft to the tropopause) and the density that follows from them. It assumes dry air, so humidity forms no part of the definition.
MgcvSts9KcvqP6Ch7JIW: Drag = CD x 1/2 rho V2 x S: it depends on the shape (through CD), the frontal area, the air density and, above all, the SQUARE of the airstream velocity. The body's mass, weight and centre of gravity have no bearing on the aerodynamic force at all - they matter for the accelerations that force produces, not for its magnitude.
Mgi43WFR00vYUIdqT5yJ: Heading is measured about the vertical, so the gyro's spin axis must lie in the horizontal plane and it needs two degrees of freedom to hold that axis fixed in space while the aircraft manoeuvres around it. A single degree of freedom would give a rate gyro instead.
Mhh6ojAENLhx88wHF41V: The constant speed drive holds the generator's input speed constant, which fixes the output FREQUENCY at 400 Hz. Voltage is a separate matter: it falls as load increases, so a voltage regulator is still required, controlling the field excitation to hold 115 V whatever the load.
Mi3VkWKGD01mxRqOnTMx: Geometric pitch is the theoretical distance a blade element would advance in one revolution if it moved through the air like a screw through a solid nut - determined purely by the blade angle and the radius. The difference between that theoretical distance and the actual distance advanced is SLIP. Note the other definitions: blade angle is measured from the PLANE OF ROTATION, and blade angle of attack from the relative airflow.
Mi6dQ8NTlFyTBnYhSb9I: Alignment needs the system's true starting position, entered as latitude and longitude, because the IRS senses the earth's rotation rate and must know the latitude to interpret it. Everything else the system needs it works out for itself; heading in particular is DERIVED by gyro-compassing, not supplied by the crew.
MiAUNCWX1KTC61Fw91zG: Transport (travel) wander is caused by carrying the gyro across meridians, so it equals the change of longitude multiplied by the sine of the mean latitude: g x sin Lm. 15 degrees per hour times sin(latitude) is EARTH rate - a function of time, not distance - corrected separately.
MiSQGJZEqGXEkdjrYaVq: The usable indications are a change in the environmental sound as outflow changes, and the cabin altimeter showing an unexplained rise. Differential pressure becoming EQUAL - that is, zero - is not a symptom of a malfunctioning system but the end state of a complete loss of pressurisation.
MiqXfCUTf0cWLUGqP39h: Amber or yellow marks cautions and abnormal sources on an EFIS, red is reserved for warnings and system limits, green for present-status dynamic data, magenta for selected data and white for present status and scales. The convention mirrors the traffic-light logic used on every other flight deck annunciator.
Mk1aif6bdfvOcQlxI6oh: A low flap setting gives less drag and therefore a better sustained climb GRADIENT, at the cost of a longer ground run. So it suits a long runway (the extra distance is affordable) with DISTANT obstacles (the sustained gradient is what matters), and it is especially valuable when high elevation and high temperature have already eroded the climb performance. CLOSE-IN obstacles argue the other way - more flap, to get airborne sooner.
MkI7kHvybSBkJjIKwjym: Showers, of rain or snow, come from convective cloud - cumulus and cumulonimbus - because the strong updraughts allow particles to grow large and the cloud has limited horizontal extent, so the precipitation starts and stops abruptly. Snow showers are typical of cold unstable air behind a cold front. Stratiform cloud such as nimbostratus or altostratus gives continuous, widespread snow instead.
Mkg1ApnTzLYeVWaqVeu0: Induced drag coefficient is proportional to CL squared divided by aspect ratio, so a HIGH aspect ratio wing produces LESS induced drag - its tips are a smaller proportion of the span, so the tip vortices influence less of the wing and the downwash is reduced. The trade-offs are greater structural weight and bending loads, and MORE gust sensitivity, since a high aspect ratio gives a steeper lift curve slope.
MkmpJuZccC0HvS4dONKj: V2 must be at least 1.1 VMCA - a 10% margin over the minimum control speed in the air - so that directional control remains assured throughout the second segment climb with the critical engine inoperative. V2 must simultaneously meet the stall margin requirement (1.2 VS, or 1.13 VSR), and whichever floor is higher governs.
Mkpd7SIgsBMp2etC2z9e: The standard upper-air charts sit at approximately 850 hPa near FL50, 700 hPa near FL100, 500 hPa near FL180, 300 hPa near FL300 and 200 hPa near FL390. FL170 is therefore closest to the 500 hPa chart, which is also the standard chart for the mid-tropospheric flow pattern and for locating cold pools.
MkzrKBlleC5NUM2eKCIk: The stages of hypoxia run from the indifferent stage to about 10,000 ft, the compensatory stage to about 15,000 ft and the disturbance stage to about 20,000 ft, beyond which lies the critical stage - where compensation fails, judgement and consciousness go quickly and recovery may not follow even if oxygen is restored. Passing about 20,000 ft without oxygen is therefore crossing into the critical zone.
MoLSO3cJWsOhoc1Y4UEG: Holding the angle of attack fixed means holding CL fixed, so a heavier aeroplane must fly FASTER to generate the extra lift. Drag also rises, since CD is fixed and both the weight being supported and the speed have increased - and power required is drag multiplied by speed, so it rises on both counts. More speed AND more power are needed; the power setting certainly cannot stay unchanged.
Mq9FujS4wJJY2EiOnHbC: The aeroplane technical log is retained for 24 months after the date of the last entry - much longer than the three months that applies to the operational flight plan, mass and balance documentation and journey log, because the technical log is the record of the aeroplane's continuing airworthiness.
Mqa7OK1CH4FTklXmyJF9: Flutter is a self-exciting oscillation in which aerodynamic, inertial and elastic forces couple: bending and torsional distortions of the structure feed energy into each other at a resonant frequency, so the amplitude grows rapidly and can destroy the structure within seconds. It appears only above a critical airspeed, so the immediate action is to reduce IAS; it is designed out by structural stiffness and mass balancing of control surfaces.
MqaO2C0JJ6z4L3x2nCKS: A cross-track difference between the two systems proves only that they disagree. INS 1 is driving the autopilot so it reads zero by definition, which tells you nothing about its accuracy, and INS 2's 8 NM could be its own error or INS 1's. All that can be deduced is that AT LEAST ONE of them is drifting.
MqdJVOwDZCS4szmzMl9Q: Life jackets for every occupant become mandatory once the aeroplane operates over water more than 50 NM from the shore, or beyond gliding distance from land. The 100 NM and 400 NM figures belong to the separate life-raft requirement.
Mqj1qMQX0lB0zZyhXv84: Compressing a gas does work on it, so its temperature rises along with its pressure - by several hundred degrees across a modern compressor. The axial velocity is deliberately held roughly constant, and the whole point of the compressor is that the pressure is far higher than at inlet.
MqnQ2xh9cDDiY6dUoAB7: The purpose of CRM is to get the information in each crew member's head into the decision. A doubt must therefore be stated and kept on the table until it has actually been resolved by evidence, not dropped because the other pilot sounds confident. Unquestioning obedience, conflict avoidance and staying silent to avoid being awkward are the failures CRM exists to prevent.
MrDeTCXgf2dsAldPS7nx: The navigation database holds the fixed data needed to fly a route: airports (1), navaids (3), runways (5), waypoints, airways and procedures. Take-off speeds are computed from the aircraft's performance database for the day's conditions, and terrain data belongs to the EGPWS.
MrSQPDOg7hhh7pjR1VJc: At FL140 the density is about 67% of sea level, so 260 kt CAS corresponds to roughly 317 kt true. The temperature is 15 - 28 = -13°C, or 260 K, giving a speed of sound of 38.94 x the square root of 260, about 628 kt. Mach number is therefore 317/628, about 0.51.
MsA7qGmAVG239GfUfAuP: The angle between the wind and the runway is 100 - 063 = 37 degrees, so the crosswind is V x sin37 = 0.60V. Setting that equal to the 20 kt limit gives V = 20 / 0.60 = about 33 kt. Note the runway QDM and the wind are both magnetic, so no conversion is needed.
MsIO776PEe4fnlocOnvZ: The flux valve is a static magnetic detector, mounted in a wingtip or fin well away from the aircraft's own magnetism, which senses the direction of the earth's field. Its signal slaves the directional gyro, giving the instrument gyro steadiness with magnetic accuracy.
MsnuH3IHnxuxk6zADez2: Barotrauma occurs wherever gas is trapped in a rigid cavity that cannot equalise: the paranasal sinuses, the middle ear behind a blocked Eustachian tube, and gas under a filling or in a decayed tooth. The outer ear is open to the atmosphere and the stomach can vent, so those are not the classic sites.
MtArMjmZf8IUlNeruIcP: A leak lets the total pressure bleed away towards cabin pressure, which in an unpressurised aeroplane is close to static. The difference the instrument sees is therefore smaller than it should be, so the airspeed indicator under-reads - which is why the alternate static source drill has its own airspeed correction.
MtIdqI7XKb9zINzzk7eL: The platform must be held perpendicular to the local vertical as the earth turns beneath it and as the aircraft moves over the curved earth. So the computer torques the gyros for earth rate, for transport wander as latitude and longitude change, for coriolis, and for the accelerations of the aircraft's own manoeuvres.
MvnpZyBoeLpDSDRJQPHY: Cross-feed opens a manifold between the tank feed lines so that any engine can be supplied from any tank. Its uses are correcting a lateral imbalance and keeping an engine running when its own tank or pump has failed - it is not restricted to opposite wings or to ground use.
MwDNcSSZuImRokRkSQo9: Cross-feed connects the engine feed lines through a common manifold, so any engine can be fed from any tank. Transferring fuel between tanks is a different system, and cross-feed is used in flight to correct imbalance or to cope with a pump or tank failure.
MwnGeqT6PdCo8q3GHyhV: The centre of gravity shift is the mass moved multiplied by the distance moved, divided by the total mass: 1,600 x (23 - 16) / 36,000 = 11,200 / 36,000 = 0.31 m. The load has moved aft, so the centre of gravity moves aft by that amount.
MyslciTN1uF8kylWMaRZ: The datum is a reference plane chosen by the manufacturer purely for convenience of calculation, and its position is published in the flight or loading manual. It is not derived from any weighing, and the pilot has no freedom to choose it - every arm in the manual is measured from it.
MzFLsA7JN2Fg9jWiSwPX: Convert to true first: 020(M) with 25W variation gives 355(T). The island is 30 degrees left of the nose, so it bears 325(T) from the aircraft, and the bearing of the AIRCRAFT FROM the island is the reciprocal, 325 - 180 = 145.
MzHr45xP0pxBDJzBz8ks: Renewed protection means starting again: the surface must be de-iced to remove the spent fluid and any contamination it holds, and only then is fresh anti-icing fluid applied. Spraying a new layer over a lapsed film does not restore holdover, and waiting for the protection time to expire before acting is the opposite of what is needed.
MzvuffmCJ7YgYS3pNvuf: A blocking anticyclone is a WARM-cored high extending through the depth of the troposphere, quasi-stationary and sited unusually far north, typically between 50 N and 70 N over Scandinavia, Greenland or the north Atlantic. Because it is warm-cored it persists at altitude and diverts the polar front jet and its depressions around it, north or south - hence 'blocking'. Cold anticyclones, such as the Siberian high, are shallow and confined to low levels.
Mzxr7k2IRiNKyof2nfuN: For powered aircraft on VFR night flights, an electric landing light is required if the flight is for hire. This ensures the pilot can see the landing area during night operations.
N15i9TG9oY4vjwuGZWue: The high-level outflow from a tropical revolving storm spreads out as a vast shield of dense cirrus, which is thrown out ahead of the system and can be seen 300-500 NM before the storm itself arrives. Long-period swell and a falling barometer are the other classic early indicators. The cumulonimbus of the eyewall is not visible at that range.
N2ugyOQJ0ccmIa3G5yB7: The definition has two parts: more than 25% of the required surface covered, by water or slush or loose snow equivalent to more than 3 mm, by compacted snow, or by ice. Only the compacted-snow option here states both the correct percentage and a contaminant that actually counts.
N3MSs5Ln6FDk3j6YMP7v: Taxiway centreline lights (except exit taxiway lights) are fixed green. This distinguishes them from taxiway edge lights (blue) and helps pilots track the centreline.
N40RdM9YOnmSinvjSSse: In Class B above 10,000 ft AMSL, VMC minima are 8 km visibility with 1500 m horizontal and 1000 ft vertical distance from clouds. The 'clear of clouds' provision for Class B applies only below 10,000 ft.
N5ijpB0g0bp4m9MAdofk: Noise at this level does nothing useful. It masks speech and warnings, interferes with concentration, adds to fatigue and stress, and above about 90 dB causes cumulative and permanent damage to the hair cells of the cochlea. Whatever arousing effect noise may have at low levels, at this intensity the balance is entirely negative.
N5jOMub7tDthiOZhzzvV: Once a hypothesis is formed it becomes the framework through which subsequent data are read: confirming evidence is accepted, contradicting evidence is discounted or explained away, and the alternative interpretation is not generated at all. This mental set is why a second pilot's independent look matters, and why a deliberate 'what if we are wrong' question is worth asking.
N5xj3FqG0GArdY07dOpm: Use the 1-in-60 rule twice. Track error = 4 NM in the 60 NM run = 4 degrees. Closing angle = 4 NM in the 30 NM remaining = 8 degrees. Total alteration to reach B = 4 + 8 = 12 degrees left. The later the fix, the smaller the track error and the larger the closing angle.
N6fwpnBkQ2kXwfejBohG: The laissez-faire captain abdicates: he offers few suggestions, takes few decisions and allocates nothing, leaving the crew to work out for themselves what should be done and by whom. The result is not freedom but a vacuum, in which tasks are duplicated or dropped and nobody has the overall picture.
N6ijCRgV1lYmlPEvwZjy: A series of red flashes from the tower to an aircraft in the circuit means the airport is not available for landing. The aircraft should not land and should proceed as instructed or to an alternate.
N79q6NHd6LEM4ai1dbPk: The speed of sound depends only on temperature, and at the standard sea level +15°C it is about 661 kt, or 340 m/s. It falls as the square root of absolute temperature, reaching about 573 kt at the tropopause.
N7cQtY1E8Zh1N4ryDyLl: Runway lead-in lighting consists of groups of at least three white lights flashing in sequence towards the runway. This guides pilots from the approach area to the threshold.
N7geUfp9D2guQLbnaUKu: Barodontalgia is pain produced when pressure change acts on gas trapped in or under a tooth. A healthy, sound tooth has nowhere for gas to be trapped, so the pain occurs where there is disease or recent work - a leaking filling, a decayed cavity, or inflamed pulp and periapical tissue around the root. It can arise on climb as trapped gas expands and on descent as the outside pressure rises against it.
N9e0SVaeO410C9rCHPL3: ICAO Doc 4444: for independent parallel approaches, a No Transgression Zone (NTZ) of at least 610 m wide is established equidistant between the extended runway centrelines.
N9yB8BeabpYibwDePUG5: The atmosphere remains well mixed to about 80 km, so at 18,000 ft the air is still 21% oxygen. What has changed is the total pressure - roughly half its sea-level value at 18,000 ft - so the partial pressure of oxygen is halved, which is why hypoxia occurs even though the percentage is unchanged.
NBev9CD45WDiV3Itj9gR: The blade's rotational speed increases with radius, so without twist the angle of attack would vary greatly along the span - large at the root and small at the tip. Twisting the blade coarser at the root and finer at the tip keeps the angle of attack roughly constant and the thrust distribution even.
NBnQdSIy1mAJspZn9G4J: A radio altimeter measures the actual distance from the aircraft to whatever is below, calibrated to read the height of the lowest part of the aircraft above the surface. It is used by the GPWS, the autoland flare and TCAS as well as by its own indicator, and it has nothing to do with barometric altitude hold.
NCUebcAL0XIOyohDgxgE: Position error is a property of the airframe: the pressure at the ports is not quite free-stream because the airflow around the fuselage disturbs it, and the discrepancy varies with speed and configuration. The machmeter, being fed from the same pitot and static system, inherits it.
NCl7yCkbnu8IozamjSwo: An open circuit is a break in the path, so no current can flow and the component simply does not work. Nothing is drawn, so no fuse or breaker operates and the ammeter shows less load rather than more - which is why an open circuit is found by continuity testing.
NDMzKU4qardw5jjXIybf: The dispensing units must exceed the number of SEATS by at least 10%, so 180 seats requires 198 units. The surplus covers cabin crew moving about the cabin and anyone away from their own seat when the masks drop.
NDZVX52SOY9232bPG5sr: Descending at constant CAS the true airspeed falls, because the same dynamic pressure needs a lower true speed in denser air. The speed of sound rises as the air warms, so the Mach number - a falling TAS over a rising speed of sound - falls faster still. Both decrease.
NEOwpSKEvnBSMA38blwF: Without ETOPS approval, a two-engined Class A aeroplane with 20 or more seats is limited to 60 minutes from an adequate aerodrome at the one-engine-inoperative cruise speed. That threshold is what ETOPS approval exists to extend.
NFhY1w2v5JO5qi8pEnBz: Stress is the body's normal, non-specific adaptive response to demand - the mechanism by which an individual mobilises to meet a situation. It becomes harmful only when it is excessive or prolonged. It is not confined to fragile personalities, and eliminating it entirely would leave a person under-aroused and performing badly.
NG48WtluhPsqMBYVxgGq: Cruise cabin humidity falls to roughly 5-15%, drier than most deserts, because the air drawn in at altitude holds almost no water. The steady fluid loss that follows produces dehydration, with headache, fatigue and reduced concentration, so crews must drink before they feel thirsty.
NGTHLnY0JT5NpTeLLOCQ: VHF direction finding is done by the ground station, which measures the bearing of the aircraft's transmission. The aircraft therefore needs nothing special at all - just a normal VHF transceiver on which it can be asked to transmit for the bearing to be taken.
NGUJxzh7bRr3CoHifAU5: Planned time for the first 150 NM at 240 kt is 37.5 minutes; being 2 minutes late makes it 39.5 minutes, so the actual groundspeed is 150 x 60 / 39.5 = about 228 kt. The remaining 330 NM then takes about 87 minutes, giving a total of about 2 h 06 from 1000, so the revised ETA is 1206.
NGkgzFSia4hiH4XKO23p: The respiratory centre is driven principally by the carbon dioxide level in arterial blood, detected as a change in pH. A rise increases the rate and depth of breathing; a fall shuts it down. Oxygen acts only as a weak secondary stimulus at low levels, which is why hypoxia gives no sensation of breathlessness and therefore no warning.
NHErZraVNmdncEMC5S8p: A pulse radar cannot receive while it transmits, which is what creates a minimum measurable range. A continuous wave set transmits and receives at the same time on separate aerials, so that limitation disappears entirely, which is why CW is used for radio altimeters and Doppler. The price is that plain CW gives no range at all without modulation.
NHby8s109MtIfA9mRRCD: Error cannot be designed out of a human operator, so the design objective is not perfection but consequence management: make the errors that matter less likely to occur and, where they do occur, make them visible before they cause harm. Effort is therefore concentrated on the errors with serious consequences rather than spread evenly over every possible slip.
NIDrn9VRGkOfsugvDMzF: Work in stages. Radial 210 INBOUND is a magnetic track of 030, and with 75W variation that is a true track of 030 - 75 = 315. On a north polar chart gridded on Greenwich, grid = true + west longitude, so 315 + 68.25 = 383, i.e. 023 grid. Convert to true, then to grid, and never the other way round.
NIXBJ3QfocnNmVHiTqfF: The vestibular apparatus comprises the three semicircular canals, which sense angular acceleration, and the two otolith organs - the utricle and the saccule - whose weighted membranes sense linear acceleration and the direction of gravity. The cochlea and auditory nerve belong to hearing, and the Eustachian tube is not sensory at all.
NIdNer0qCidMb83Ng3NT: A speaker adjusts to his audience. Judging the listener competent, he strips out redundancy and says less (1); judging him less competent, he simplifies the content and says it more plainly (3). Statement 2 has it backwards, since a non-native listener is helped by simpler words rather than more complicated ones, and statement 4 attributes checklist shortcuts to conflict when they actually come from familiarity and complacency.
NJ5JZAoKL5i7BpPCjcXP: Alcohol is broken down by the liver at a roughly fixed rate of about 15 mg per 100 ml of blood per hour, and nothing accelerates it - not coffee, not oxygen, not exercise, not habituation. Only time works, which is why the regulations specify a minimum interval between drinking and duty rather than a remedy.
NJPwsqNcVpxCk1wxF8cZ: All four must be demonstrated: no fire hazard from the system or its operation, fuel discharging clear of every part of the aeroplane, no fumes entering the aeroplane, and no adverse effect on controllability. Jettison puts a large quantity of fuel into the airflow immediately beside the airframe, so each of those is a real failure mode.
NJfTcraHpx9CFesrox56: In the transonic region the dominant physics is compressibility: shock wave formation, the aft movement of the centre of pressure, shock-induced separation and buffet all depend on how close the LOCAL flow is to the speed of sound. Since Mach number is the ratio of TAS to the local speed of sound, it is the parameter that captures all of this - which is why high-level cruise is flown to a Mach number rather than an airspeed.
NJu1ivzwxrhUefn31ZWF: Sleep follows the circadian temperature rhythm closely: sleep comes easily as core temperature falls towards its low point in the early hours and is hard to obtain on the rising limb during the day. That is why a night-flying crew trying to sleep in the afternoon sleep badly, and why body temperature is used as the marker of circadian phase.
NKDADFngO9vZSIlir9j8: The rods are the more oxygen-hungry of the photoreceptors and are affected first, so night vision degrades measurably from around 5,000 ft while daylight acuity holds up much longer. This is why supplemental oxygen is recommended for night flying well below the altitude at which it would otherwise be needed.
NKUqCVFqQCzeQgZx5Faw: The requirement is capability: the aeroplane must be certificated and equipped with approved ice protection before being flown into expected or actual icing conditions. Ground treatment deals with contamination already present and does nothing about the ice the aeroplane will meet in flight, and no meteorologist can authorise flight into icing without the equipment.
NKvITFQcI1cuUuQ2bz4T: A physiological stressor is any stimulus that disturbs the body's homeostatic mechanisms - heat, cold, noise, vibration, acceleration, hypoxia, hunger, illness, fatigue. The body's non-specific response to such demands is the stress reaction itself, and coping is what the individual does about it; the stressor is the disturbing stimulus.
NMDZu67lUbpzuEDZCEiV: For three- and four-engined aeroplanes the take-off alternate must be within two hours at the one-engine-inoperative cruising speed in still air; the equivalent figure for a twin is one hour. The speed is always the engine-out speed, because that is the condition in which the diversion would be flown.
NMGWq0DhAeCMS3ugaiyI: Optimum altitude is the altitude at which specific air range is greatest for the current mass, so the economical plan flies at or about it. As fuel burns off the mass falls and the optimum rises, which is why the plan is a series of step climbs following that rising optimum rather than a single level held for the whole cruise.
NMGtBo6O1F7paOa79nij: The central nervous system is the brain and the spinal cord, everything else being peripheral. Visual signals leave the retina by the optic nerve and are processed in the visual cortex at the back of the brain - the retina transduces and pre-processes but does not perceive, which is why perception can be wrong even when the eye is working perfectly.
NN8dmPlzhixTfZRIkvBp: ICAO Annex 7: registration marks shall not use four-letter combinations beginning with Q, as Q-codes are reserved for international telecommunications signals. Five-letter combinations from the international code of signals are also avoided.
NNMPDKRLyIrXcWePjA8X: A relief valve that fails to seat allows oil to escape back to the return side continuously, so the pump cannot build the pressure it should. The gauge shows low pressure - and the same symptom, with a full oil quantity, is what distinguishes a valve problem from a leak.
NNP1RTy0M0muOERosBOH: In a level turn the lift must both support the weight and provide the turning force, so the load factor n = 1/cos(bank) is always GREATER than 1. Stall speed rises with the square root of the load factor, so it is correspondingly HIGHER than in straight and level flight - by 19% at 45 degrees of bank and 41% at 60 degrees.
NNVNLuqdRR8nnNbJQFU6: Primary radar relies on a REFLECTED echo, attenuated on the way out and again on the way back, so range varies with the fourth root of power and power varies with the fourth power of range. Doubling the range therefore needs 2 to the fourth = 16 times the power. A one-way beacon would need only 4 times.
NNib65JEGqUCbL3zPXW8: Differential pressure is the difference between the pressure inside the cabin and the ambient pressure outside at whatever altitude the aircraft is flying. It is the quantity the structure must withstand, which is why it is limited and why the relief valves are set against it.
NNwHz2M6t98gLdJf06Xz: The raw accelerometer signal is small and contains vibration from every source at once, so it is amplified and then passed through filters tuned to the shaft frequencies. Only the filtered amplitude at the N1 and N2 frequencies is displayed, which is what makes the indication interpretable.
NOK38ylEWKWFZiqnCQ46: Using the structure as the return conductor halves the wiring, which saves considerable weight (1), and a fault to earth is easy to find because there is only one wire to trace (2). It also reduces the chance of a short between two live conductors, since there is only one (4) - though it demands excellent bonding.
NOMXs6Hs155Zl2uTb7cA: First the DR run: with about 11 kt of tailwind component the planned groundspeed is about 130 kt, so in 15 minutes the DR position is about 32.5 NM along track. Being 2.5 NM ahead puts the aircraft 35 NM along and 3 NM off, leaving 15 NM to run. Track error = 3/35 x 60 = 5 degrees, closing angle = 3/15 x 60 = 12 degrees, so the alteration is 17 degrees.
NPMIrS6cPOmEnDJiyK33: As the aeroplane accelerates, the airflow meets the blades at a flatter helix angle, which would reduce their angle of attack and let the rpm rise. The governor detects the rpm change and COARSENS the blade angle to restore the selected rpm - so blade angle increases with speed. That is the essence of constant-speed operation: rpm is held while blade angle varies.
NPm7HsIWothhwiQYy1ND: Rate of turn depends on both bank angle and speed: for a given bank the turn is tighter at low speed and wider at high speed. The needle therefore reads a smaller rate as the true airspeed increases - which is why a rate one turn needs more bank the faster you fly.
NPuR6st72orWPWPb6ZZt: The transducer output contains vibration from every source in the engine, so it is filtered to the frequencies corresponding to the spools of interest before being displayed. Without that filtering the indication would be dominated by noise and would say nothing about which rotor was out of balance.
NQp309qycO9HKX8TjvjA: Magenta marks SELECTED data on an EFIS, and the active route or flight plan leg is selected data, so it is drawn in magenta while inactive route segments appear in white or cyan. The same logic makes the heading bug and the selected altitude magenta.
NT9HMT15LNeEFdLVUy7d: A spin is rotation about all three axes at once, so what the body is subjected to is angular acceleration - and it is the semicircular canals responding to it, and then adapting to it, that produce the disorienting sensations of the spin and of the recovery from it.
NTPyHaHc85kP2evbT37V: The healthy young ear responds from about 20 Hz to about 20,000 Hz. Below 20 Hz the vibration is felt rather than heard, and the upper limit falls with age and with noise exposure. Speech occupies roughly 500 Hz to 4 kHz within that range, which is why high-frequency loss shows up as difficulty understanding words.
NU2moMAjPZZTfUyWBNus: Statement I is correct: fail safe design provides more than one load path, so that if one member fails the others carry the load until the damage is found. Statement II overstates safe life - the part is retired at a life established by test with a large scatter factor, which makes failure very unlikely rather than impossible.
NU5GOoXrqWRjZ5BXhxbF: Take-off mass is everything on board at brakes release: the dry operating mass, the traffic load and the fuel remaining after taxi. Adding the take-off fuel to the actual landing mass would omit the taxi fuel and, more importantly, would be circular - the landing mass is derived from the take-off mass.
NUC75cDAaLwjKEuhUV1a: Underslung engines put the thrust line BELOW the centre of gravity, so a thrust increase produces a nose-UP couple about the CG. To keep the net pitching moment at zero the tailplane must generate a nose-down moment, which requires DOWN elevator. This is why a go-around from a low-speed configuration demands prompt forward pressure, and why the effect is most pronounced on large-diameter engines slung well below the wing.
NVp5NntAwYaWcFf9l4WA: The 10% passenger case applies in the band above 10 000 ft up to 13 000 ft, for the entire flight time after the first 30 minutes at those altitudes. Above 13 000 ft the requirement becomes 100% of passengers with no grace period.
NW3QcDBoA0d0d2ft9duX: A warning is the top of the alerting hierarchy: it signals an emergency requiring immediate recognition and immediate corrective action, and it is presented in red with an aural alert. A caution requires awareness and later action, and an advisory only awareness.
NWIQg23Na7JJFEYFBV4G: The accelerate-stop case is built on an engine failure recognised at V1, followed by an allowance of 2 seconds of pilot reaction time at V1 speed before the first retarding action takes effect, and the aeroplane must then stop within the ACCELERATE-STOP DISTANCE AVAILABLE (runway plus stopway). That 2-second allowance is precisely why V1 is a decision speed rather than the failure speed VEF, which occurs earlier.
NWLRmCiiyu1pw3mjpDZz: Coordinated cooperation means the crew members perform different but interlocking actions, so the result exceeds the sum of the parts (1), with communication serving to synchronise those actions and share out responsibility (3). Statement 2 describes duplication rather than coordination, and statement 4 points the communication outward when the whole point of coordination is that it is directed within the crew.
NX3JtqZthCoKOu6Vz3Vn: V2 must give an adequate stall margin with an engine failed, and for a jet without provisions to significantly reduce the one-engine-inoperative stall speed the floor is 1.2 VS (modern rules express this as 1.13 VSR). V2 must simultaneously exceed 1.1 VMCA, and whichever floor is higher governs - at high flap settings that is often VMCA.
NXTIuG42iz5zSwKFRWNT: Fail-operational means the system has enough redundancy to carry on after a single failure: the approach, flare and landing are still completed automatically. A fail-passive system merely disconnects safely, leaving the crew to land manually or go around.
NYQJZMrc9yWosfK0LR0G: Loosely fitted blade roots let the blades rattle when the engine is stopped, which is normal and audible. Once running, centrifugal force pulls each blade hard against its root fixing and the aerodynamic load holds it in the correct plane, so the assembly becomes rigid at operating speed.
NYVFk68sDbEaguwLEvLb: GPWS needs to know how high it is above the ground, from the radio altimeter (3), and whether the aircraft is configured for landing, from the gear and flap position (1) - because unsafe terrain clearance means something different when the aeroplane is configured to land. Engine and TCAS data play no part.
NYcOHEY3AxT3MxYb7cEv: ICAO Doc 8168: the obstacle clearance in the primary area of the intermediate approach segment is 150 m (492 ft). This is less than the initial segment (300 m) and more than the final approach segment.
NZ5u5IrsCQK78HmlovVv: Bypass ratio is the mass flow of the cold stream that goes round the core divided by the mass flow of the hot stream that goes through it. A high bypass ratio means most of the air is moved slowly around the core, which is what makes a modern turbofan efficient.
NZmEzs5niIHF2ur528Q8: TCAS resolves conflicts vertically only - climb, descend, or maintain a vertical speed limit. Bearing derived from its directional antenna is not accurate enough to base a turn on, so horizontal resolution is not attempted and speed control plays no part.
NZpojMFy8Jwaz5xJNsNb: The CDU accepts a five-character identifier for anything held in the database with one: named waypoints, navaid identifiers, airport ICAO identifiers and runway designators such as RW27L. Frequencies, positions and plain-language airport names are attributes of those entries, not identifiers you can type in their place.
NbIuP0URUczl8jj4nhjk: On 28 November the sun's declination is about 21 SOUTH, so northern days are short and get shorter the further north you go. Moving from 54N to 44N on the same meridian therefore lengthens the day, which means an EARLIER sunrise. Same meridian only guarantees the same LMT-to-UTC conversion, not the same sunrise time.
NbIyHMYA2T5FAqqB3Bkc: The maximum zero fuel mass is a certificated structural limit (1), derived from the bending moment the wing root can take when there is no fuel in the wings to relieve it (3), and established at the design load factor (2). Fuel in the wings reduces that bending, which is why the limit applies to the fuel-less case.
Nbdt3guBVyaxJrMYdbw9: In a two-step treatment the holdover clock starts at the BEGINNING of the second step, when the anti-icing fluid starts going on. It is deliberately conservative: by the time the last surface is treated, part of the protection has already been used.
NbumkVCiL6a30lvglpFJ: Acceleration along the long axis of the body is Gz, and its dominant physiological effect is hydrostatic: blood is displaced towards the feet under +Gz and towards the head under -Gz, so blood pressure at head level and the distribution of blood volume change markedly. This is what produces greyout, blackout and G-LOC, and it is also sensed by the saccule.
NcSKwheZNLCsDGITHTl0: This question depends on a diagram this text-only version cannot show, so learn the distinction instead. GEOCENTRIC latitude is the angle at the earth's CENTRE between the equatorial plane and the line to the position. GEODETIC (geographic) latitude is the angle between the equatorial plane and the NORMAL to the ellipsoid surface at that position, and that normal does not pass through the centre except at the equator and the poles. The two differ by up to about 11.5 minutes of arc, greatest near 45 degrees, and it is geodetic latitude that is charted.
NcgOs7GSL0fp1lXNBxT0: Frost, ice or snow found on the surfaces after treatment means the fluid has failed, and the aeroplane is contaminated regardless of what the holdover table says. The whole de-icing and anti-icing process must be repeated - holdover time cannot be used to justify departing with visible contamination.
NcqchGaUsgPrnePqb3eT: Specific fuel consumption normalises fuel flow against what the engine is producing - fuel mass per unit of power (or thrust) per unit time. That makes engines of different sizes directly comparable and shows how efficiency varies with altitude, speed and power setting.
NcukoNE5ofFzvmy4YWZi: The neutral point is by definition the CG position at which static longitudinal stability is exactly zero. Ahead of it the aeroplane is stable; behind it, unstable. The distance between the CG and the neutral point is the static margin, and certification requires a minimum value of it - which is precisely what sets the aft CG limit.
NdToKRQUZKFvSh98J3u8: Working memory is the temporary store that holds material for the few seconds it is being used - about seven items for 10-20 seconds - which is exactly what is needed to retain a clearance from the last word to the pen. Remembering one's own name is long-term memory, the very brief visual store is sensory memory, and filtering out other aircraft's calls is selective attention.
NdWNuVVVRcMq68tgSjrV: The MEL is the operator's document, produced from the manufacturer's MMEL and approved by the Authority. The Authority approves it and the manufacturer supplies the master list, but neither writes the operator's MEL.
Nda9mHc1D8gyf5BrtFPI: An attitude is a learned disposition to respond consistently, favourably or unfavourably, towards something - and because it is learned from experience, it can be changed by experience, training and persuasion. That is what makes attitudes the target of CRM training, whereas personality, being stable, is not.
NfPdpY42I9KxNmDcZ0fW: The earth's field dips steeply from the horizontal outside the magnetic equator, and a freely suspended magnet would follow it. Hanging the assembly below its pivot makes it pendulous, so gravity holds the card nearly horizontal and only the horizontal component of the field is used for direction - though it also creates the turning and acceleration errors.
NfSAuoGXyjTfvAF3k7J5: 70 m/sec is 70 x 3600 = 252 000 m per hour = 252 km/h, and dividing by 1.852 gives about 136 kt. A useful approximation to carry: 1 m/sec is very nearly 2 kt.
NgDrkTU3gQxD6tMBerUu: A decision is a selection between alternatives directed at a goal. The other options each add a claim that does not hold: decisions are not always based on the commander's experience, they are never wholly objective since the weighing of options involves judgement, and the goal is not necessarily one the commander alone has set.
NhKC7tc4C54yGci9fxXF: Advection fog forms when warm, moist air is carried horizontally over a surface colder than its dewpoint and is chilled from below to saturation. It needs a wind of roughly 10-15 kt: enough turbulence to deepen the fog, but not so much that it lifts into stratus. Unlike radiation fog it forms over the sea or over cold or snow-covered land, and it can persist by day and night.
Nhda54Dlrz5OigROdjR1: A straight line on a Lambert changes its true direction by the chart convergence, dlong x n = 6 x 0.5 = 3 degrees. The track is easterly in the northern hemisphere, where the direction INCREASES along the route, so the track at B is 088.5 + 3 = 091.5.
NiKHgt0lLM10tCnlaFbL: Contaminated runway performance data is derived largely by CALCULATION, using models of displacement drag, spray impingement and degraded braking friction, with only limited flight test validation - the conditions are too variable and too hazardous to demonstrate exhaustively. That is why contaminated data carries more uncertainty than dry or wet data, and why reduced thrust is prohibited on contaminated runways.
NiOywCSO8avjggv4dNK8: Local hour angle is measured westwards from the observer's meridian to the body. At 1200 LMT the mean sun is on the observer's meridian, i.e. in transit, so the LHA is 000. At 0000 LMT it is on the anti-meridian and the LHA is 180.
NiYldEnsKyZ2kISehsVk: Hypoxia follows from any failure to restore the oxygen supply after a decompression at altitude, and the time of useful consciousness at cruise levels is measured in seconds. Getting the mask on immediately is what prevents it: 100% oxygen at 30,000 ft, or even at 15,000 ft unpressurised, provides ample alveolar oxygen, and rate of climb by itself causes no hypoxia.
NjRB4BCbLxMR4Ly8g9NC: Convergency = change of longitude x sine of the mean latitude = 6 x sin60 = about 5 degrees. The flight is westbound in the southern hemisphere, where the great circle track INCREASES as the flight proceeds, so the true track increases by about 5 degrees. The TAS plays no part.
Nk0cRJ3zgoUfpZpmyPHK: The second segment begins the moment the landing gear is FULLY RETRACTED and runs to the acceleration altitude (at least 400 ft). It is flown at V2 with take-off flap and take-off thrust, and it is the most demanding segment for climb gradient - 2.4% for a twin - which is why the climb-limited take-off mass is usually set here.
Nk8DoBV7JtzxN3txP84u: The height interval corresponding to 1 hPa grows with altitude because the air becomes less dense: about 8 m (27 ft) near sea level, about 15 m (50 ft) at 5500 m (the 500 hPa level), and around 32 m (105 ft) near 10 km. This is why the 27 ft per hPa rule is only valid for low-level altimetry problems and must not be applied at cruise levels.
NkEVJ0v7oAYqzfB5xkHo: Planned time for 325 NM at 315 kt is 61.9 minutes, giving a planned ETA of about 1232. At 1205 the aircraft has 160 NM to run and about 27 minutes left, so the groundspeed needed is 160 x 60 / 27 = about 355 kt. Work from the time REMAINING to the planned ETA.
NkvXNXbA1BKwIGlW43mu: The angle on the bow doubles from 45 degrees (relative bearing 315) to 90 degrees (relative bearing 270), so the range at the second bearing equals the distance run: 3 minutes at 180 kt = 9 NM. Abeam is also the point of closest approach, so 9 NM is the minimum distance.
Nl3lKLwZ6pHE9URDpUp9: Above FL 290 in non-RVSM airspace, VSM is 2000 ft. In RVSM airspace (FL 290-FL 410), it reduces to 1000 ft. The 2000 ft standard applies where RVSM is not implemented.
NlQoVaXEM55x6Q1i2E1U: Cells release energy by oxidising carbohydrates and fats, and the waste products are carbon dioxide and water. The CO2 diffuses into the blood, is carried mostly as bicarbonate to the lungs and is exhaled - and its concentration in the blood is also the main driver of the breathing rate.
NlhjTJCnhqRUtKgWLdqx: The flight comes first: say that there is a problem so it is not hidden, then get on with the job and deal with it properly on the ground, where there is time to discuss it without a cockpit to fly. Threatening consequences escalates it in the air, and withdrawing or shutting down communication damages exactly the crew coordination the flight depends on.
NlkNY6t6hIBxwUGgqeYB: The full chain is IAS corrected for instrument error, then for position error to give CAS, then for compressibility to give EAS, then for density to give TAS. All four corrections apply; at low speed and low level the last two are small, which is why they are often ignored in light aircraft work.
Nmp3PYV4MCQSBVhwTKay: CO2 displaces oxygen and leaves no conductive residue, so it can be used on paper and plastic (class A), hydrocarbons (class B) and live electrical equipment - all four here. Its weakness on class A is the absence of cooling, which lets a deep-seated fire re-ignite; burning metal is the absolute exclusion.
NmqaGMKXZD4YEQfjxtHi: The low-range radio altimeter used for approach and flare works around 4.3 GHz, a wavelength of about 7 cm - centimetric. That short wavelength allows a small aerial and the accuracy of a couple of feet the flare requires.
NnAAs9hgTcs1DmKVw7mV: The flux detector goes in a wingtip or the fin because that is the position furthest from the engines, generators, wiring looms and ferrous structure that cause deviation. Being remote from the cockpit also removes the old compromise between magnetic cleanliness and readability, which is the whole point of a remote indicating system.
NndPtlKlq9AzjFBPdLnS: The standard outbound timing in a holding pattern at 14,000 ft or below is 1 minute in still air conditions. Above 14,000 ft it increases to 1.5 minutes.
Nndn9IhRqu1dTMuXiJJ5: In Class E below 10,000 ft AMSL, IFR flights are subject to the standard 250 kt IAS speed limitation. This reduces closing speeds in terminal airspace.
Noz4d8wImatQDHlDWncc: ATIS broadcasts should be updated immediately when a significant change occurs — such as a runway change, significant weather change, or change in approach type. Regular updates without changes are also required.
NpXirdKxotMDXoCtYRNT: QNH is derived from the measured aerodrome pressure precisely so that an altimeter set to it reads the aerodrome elevation on the ground. That is exact at the aerodrome by construction, regardless of temperature - the ISA assumption only introduces error at heights ABOVE the reference level. Setting QFE, by contrast, makes the altimeter read zero on landing.
NqM8MfmkuX6ccim6B091: Phase matching matters only when two machines are to be connected to the same bus. Operating unparalleled, each generator feeds its own bus in isolation, so their relative phase is of no consequence - which is why split-bus systems avoid the complexity of synchronising altogether.
NqeKzLzzpRE9vpXhjZHH: As angle of attack increases, the oncoming flow meets the aerofoil from further below, so the stagnation point migrates DOWN and aft along the lower surface. Simultaneously the suction peak on the upper surface sharpens and moves FORWARD toward the leading edge - which is why the centre of pressure of a cambered section moves forward with increasing alpha.
NrKOd4KFOEpsYsGlZbfX: ICAO Annex 9: documents for entry and departure of aircraft are accepted at the contracting State's discretion regarding format. They may be handwritten or produced electronically.
Nrk0mg9hJox21yDhNpm5: ICAO Doc 4444: the radar separation minimum may be reduced by the appropriate ATS authority but shall not be reduced below 3.0 NM. This is the absolute minimum radar separation.
NsMLjcOi4QhOelQKU1SO: ICAO Annex 15: each State shall provide an Integrated Aeronautical Information Package comprising AIP, AIP Amendments, AIP Supplements, NOTAMs, PIBs, and AICs.
NsUI43jRQLT8ftVJGsKo: Each IRS holds a magnetic variation model in its own memory and applies it to the true heading it has computed, producing the magnetic heading the FMS and displays use. The flux valve only slaves the IRS heading at low latitudes and on the ground, and the FMS does not derive variation from position on its own.
Nt3OcDHaY220wlgURhPk: Behaviour is the product of all three: biological make-up sets the capacities and the temperament, the immediate social environment shapes what is expected and rewarded, and cultural background shapes attitudes to authority, to rules and to the expression of disagreement. NtRpXUeaLgIyxgiA3Bip: The autoland sequence is scheduled against radio height: the flare begins at about 50 ft, the thrust is retarded at about 30 ft, and de-crab and roll-out follow at touchdown. NuAobGUmlcXnHwyJWTAk: Static wicks are fitted at the trailing edges and extremities (2 and 4), where the field is most concentrated, so that the charge built up in flight leaks away continuously and quietly instead of discharging in bursts that interfere with the radios (5).
