Nuo9hqu1kphloAdfo6NS: The cone cuts the sphere at the two standard parallels, so the quoted scale is exact along those two lines only. Between them the chart lies inside the sphere and the scale is slightly small, reaching its minimum at the parallel of origin; outside them it is slightly large.
Nv5Rurz3evfBHwSYqcPc: At a constant flight level the pressure is fixed, so colder air is denser and the same dynamic pressure - the same CAS - is produced by a lower true airspeed. Mach number is essentially unchanged, because the speed of sound falls with temperature in the same proportion as the TAS does.
NvVZcAcRmf26zCNBPfLd: For pilots in a pressurised aeroplane, oxygen must be available for the entire flight time at cabin pressure altitudes above 13 000 ft, plus the flight time less 30 minutes in the 10 000-13 000 ft band. 25 000 ft is the certification threshold that fixes the minimum QUANTITY, not the altitude at which supply is needed.
NwO8F0nZOwu5q3WXfd9L: The local speed of sound depends only on temperature: LSS = 38.94 x root(258) = about 626 kt, so Mach = 250 / 626 = 0.40. The flight level enters only through the temperature that goes with it, and here the temperature is given directly.
NwOnkCwAAnwVIFFFrmoK: The FMS manages the flight plan laterally and vertically (1) and computes the aircraft's position by blending its radio, inertial and satellite inputs (3). Terrain awareness is the EGPWS's function and de-icing is not automated by the FMS at all.
Nwn6C7AYVcJyoOPQYEwo: A wing stalls at a fixed ANGLE OF ATTACK, not at a fixed speed - so as long as alpha remains below the critical angle the wing cannot stall, whatever the airspeed, attitude, weight or load factor. This is why an aeroplane can be stalled at high speed in a steep turn, or in a nose-down attitude during a recovery, and why stall protection systems sense angle of attack rather than airspeed.
NwvCtTQcSoNJnMKRyZ78: The circulation is the body's transport system for everything: oxygen from the lungs to the cells (1), carbon dioxide and other waste products away from the cells (2), and nutrients absorbed from the gut, along with hormones, heat and the cells of the immune system (3).
NwzCJBD89LaaRfjfz6t2: Advection is horizontal transport - the movement of air, and with it heat and moisture, from one place to another. Convection is vertical transport driven by buoyancy, and subsidence is slow widespread descent. Advection is what brings warm or cold air masses over a region, and advection fog is named for exactly this mechanism.
Nx7SMambsGJljallob2I: The generation system is protected against every condition that would damage the machine or the loads it feeds: over- and under-voltage (1 and 2), over-current (3), over-speed (4) and under-frequency (5), each of which trips the generator off the bus. Vibration is not an electrical protection.
NxF3Tqky5QoQz8iJjHRT: Halving the range scale doubles the distance each inch of screen represents in reverse: a target at 50 NM that sat halfway up the 100 NM display now sits at the very top of the 50 NM display, and because the picture is magnified the return also covers more screen area. Nothing about the weather has changed, only the presentation.
NxM8g0eXPEokIDvn3zh4: An increasing headwind is an increasing-performance shear: airspeed rises, lift rises with it and the aeroplane goes ABOVE the glide path. The hazard is not the excursion itself but the reversal that usually follows, so the technique is to hold the path and monitor the trend rather than pull thrust off.
NxV6o6X2zdyck5tMgtrO: Above 200 seats the extinguisher requirement rises once per 100 seats: four for 201-300, five for 301-400, six for 401-500, seven for 501-600 and eight beyond that.
NzZcIGxWnwmKAWXKQQIf: The magneto builds a magnetic field with a low voltage primary current, and it is the abrupt opening of the contact breaker points that collapses that field. The rapid rate of change induces the very high voltage in the secondary winding - which is why the points and their gap are so critical to a good spark.
NzgnLrrDZMQN8Qwm0Rrv: Take the drift out first, then the variation. Left drift means the track lies to the LEFT of the heading, so the true heading = 192 + 5 = 197. Then magnetic heading = true heading minus east variation = 197 - 7 = 190.
O0NM2cL8dZULc65vL3Kq: Total temperature is the static temperature plus the kinetic heating of bringing the air to rest, and for air that ram rise is a factor of (1 + 0.2 M squared). Recovering the static temperature therefore means dividing the measured total temperature by that factor.
O0hfdFGPoyNoo1y83z1l: CAS is a measure of dynamic pressure, so descending into denser air the same dynamic pressure is produced by a lower true airspeed - TAS falls. That is true whatever the temperature profile; an isothermal layer only means the speed of sound is unchanged, so the Mach number falls with the TAS.
O0xZg5gdezKbJzLHYa9a: Personality is the product of inherited temperament and everything that has happened since: upbringing, childhood and accumulated experience all shape it. It is essentially formed and stable by adulthood, which is why selection tests for personality but training targets attitudes and behaviour instead.
O17e01tnrd7OvCXhj5wI: Gyroscopic precession appears only when the plane of the spinning disc is TILTED, which happens when the aeroplane pitches or yaws - rolling turns the aeroplane about the propeller's own axis and produces no precession at all. The applied force then takes effect 90 degrees onward in the direction of rotation, which is why raising the tail on take-off produces a yaw.
O1GLMF19UiXAcC1NfclI: Output voltage falls as load increases, because of the internal resistance of the machine. The regulator senses that fall and increases the field excitation current, which restores the output - and it does the reverse when the load is reduced.
O1QI0uUGAc9kGEepaGZN: Two degrees of freedom allow the gyro to hold its axis fixed in space while the aircraft manoeuvres around it, and a horizontal spin axis makes that fixed direction a heading reference - the directional gyro. A vertical spin axis would give an attitude reference, and one degree of freedom a rate gyro.
O27tjMZmywk16vhfnESJ: Personality is the set of relatively enduring psychological characteristics that make one individual distinguishable from another. It is stable in adulthood and is not altered by mood or by a training course. The tendency to evaluate things favourably or unfavourably describes an attitude, which is learned and can be changed.
O2MAfnI9pZw6VClnA2mf: ICAO Annex 1: CPL applicants need at least 20 hours cross-country as PIC including a flight of at least 540 km (300 NM) with full-stop landings at two different aerodromes.
O2bepZz1jxeEUT1piKdY: A flight deck fire almost always involves live electrical equipment, so the agent must be non-conductive and must leave the instruments readable: halon or CO2. Water conducts, and powder coats the panels and displays, which is why neither belongs there.
O2zu5Wc2VabrSVLP1MpU: Two plugs light the charge from two points, so the flame fronts meet in the middle and the charge burns in roughly half the time. Faster, more complete combustion means more of the fuel's energy appears as work - which is why the magneto check shows an rpm drop when one system is switched off.
O31Di32GTZUffc7jQbNa: Braking action is reported in descriptive terms - good, medium (or medium to good / medium to poor) and poor, with unreliable as a further category - because the figure a friction measuring device produces cannot be translated directly into aeroplane stopping performance. Those terms are what the crew relates to the landing distance data.
O3KmwJ1itsl1xK2YUG5h: Lambert chart convergence is a constant, dlong x sin(parallel of origin), while earth convergency is dlong x sin(latitude) and therefore varies. The two agree exactly only at the parallel of origin: the chart over-reads south of it and under-reads north of it.
O4TlCApFY7OrPp00A8TB: An isothermal layer has the same temperature throughout its depth, so its environmental lapse rate is zero. It is very stable: a parcel displaced upward cools at its adiabatic rate while the surroundings do not cool at all, so it becomes colder and denser and sinks back. A layer in which temperature actually INCREASES with height is an inversion, which is more stable still.
O4vUfhq5hWWFtliKarZX: The wind at 275 is only 15 degrees off the nose for a track of 260, so it is almost a pure headwind. The crosswind of 30 x sin15 = 8 kt gives less than 2 degrees of drift, so the heading is about 262, and the headwind of 30 x cos15 = 29 kt brings the groundspeed to about 241 kt.
O77HX5GSIUBiHKgzp51A: In a right turn the outside of the turn is to the LEFT, so a ball displaced left has swung to the outside - a SKID, meaning the rate of turn is too high for the bank angle. Two coordinated fixes exist: reduce the rate of turn with less rudder, or match the bank to the rate by rolling in MORE right bank. Of the options offered, more right bank is the coordinating input.
O7D5MlY6sd00TSmFN9qx: ICAO Doc 7030: the transition altitude should not normally be less than 3000 ft above aerodrome elevation. This ensures adequate separation between QNH-based and standard pressure-based operations.
O7nIwonldmprAwBXeEaT: Fail-operational means the system has enough redundancy to carry on after a single failure, completing the approach, flare and landing automatically. A fail-passive system merely disconnects safely, leaving the landing to be flown by hand or a go-around to be made.
O7vUzk3j0f8k39CKWBqK: An INS computes track and groundspeed from its own accelerometers with no air data at all, so it needs no TAS to navigate. Supplying TAS lets it subtract the air vector from the ground vector and display the wind velocity, which is a by-product rather than a requirement.
OAjm0OzrkYB62GEWMO7R: VHF direction finding works entirely from the aircraft's ordinary transmissions: the ground station measures the bearing of the incoming signal, so ATC can obtain a bearing, and with two stations a fix, without any radar and without any special airborne equipment. It follows that it is useless if the aircraft cannot transmit, and it is not a precision approach aid.
OAvjELlFzhnPyJsTNk3A: An inertial reference system integrates accelerations, so it produces position (1), attitude (3) and ground speed (4), along with track, drift and true heading. True airspeed requires air data - the air's own motion is invisible to an inertial system.
OBczYzu8L3XFTgLenecC: A LIGHT following a MEDIUM on approach takes 3 minutes, the longest of the approach wake minima, because the light aeroplane has the least roll authority to resist a vortex. A MEDIUM or LIGHT following a HEAVY is separated by 2 minutes.
OC5mOUO61GcsHkPeTXRg: In Class E airspace, VFR flights do not require ATC clearance or two-way radio communication. VFR aircraft operate freely with traffic information provided as far as practical.
OCTQtekqlwHQydzCMSHn: ICAO Annex 12 colour codes for droppable SAR containers: red for medical supplies and first aid equipment. Blue is food/water, yellow is blankets/clothing, black is miscellaneous.
OChNlELpPSWug7uLHci2: In a climb the propeller disc is inclined to the airflow, so the DOWN-going blade meets the air at a greater angle of attack and higher relative velocity than the up-going blade, and therefore produces more thrust. With a right-turning propeller the down-going blade is on the RIGHT, so the extra thrust is on the right side of the disc and the aeroplane yaws LEFT. This P-factor adds to torque and slipstream effects in the climb.
OChbmWJZHuu2G7IqEr6l: Single-pilot IFR or night operation carries its own recency on top of the normal three take-offs and landings: five IFR flights including three INSTRUMENT APPROACHES in the preceding 90 days, flown in the single-pilot role on the type or class. The extra requirement is about instrument currency without another pilot to monitor, which is why it is counted in approaches rather than in landings.
OE3rfpMGHJB53SilzwDj: Reactive load - the kVAR associated with the phase difference between voltage and current - is controlled by the excitation. Trimming the field current of each paralleled machine therefore equalises the reactive load, while real load is shared by trimming the constant speed drives.
OEfengp93vNU1SwJ1Clo: The SELCAL check is completed at or before entry into the NAT region, so the crew know the alarm will actually alert them before they stop listening continuously on HF. Discovering a failed SELCAL an hour out means either a continuous listening watch or a communications failure.
OEx736UOD7jPtDgY7HIo: The General Adaptation Syndrome is triggered by the brain's appraisal of a threat, not by the threat's reality: an imagined or anticipated danger produces the same adrenaline release, the same rise in heart rate and blood pressure and the same mobilisation as a real one. That is why worry is as physiologically costly as the event itself.
OF8cxpsrXMzEHcmrqRsq: The flux valve's magnetic heading goes to the error detector, which compares it with the heading the gyro is showing. Any difference is amplified and drives the torque motor, which precesses the gyro slowly onto the magnetic heading - the slaving loop.
OFh9gJaCib9rOt5719wi: Two corrections. QNH 993.2 is about 20 hPa below 1013, so the indicated altitude is 25 000 - (20 x 27) = about 24 460 ft. ISA at 25 000 ft is -35C, so -45C is ISA-10 and the aircraft is LOWER than indicated: 4 ft per 1000 ft per degree gives about 980 ft, so the true altitude is about 23 480 ft.
OG5Vb0FJ9Wot3G3z0zwr: IAS 200 at FL120 with OAT -5C gives a TAS of about 242 kt, so with a 30 kt tailwind the groundspeed is about 272 kt and 100 NM takes about 22 minutes. Five minutes more is 27 minutes, needing about 222 kt groundspeed, hence about 192 kt TAS; converting back at the same density ratio gives an IAS of about 159 kt.
OH70R8Kcbjon2dkKQDEN: The remedies for overload are to use one's own reserves intelligently (1), to share the work out across the crew (2), and - critically - to shed the tasks that do not matter and hold to the top priorities (4). Statement 3 is nonsense: long-term memory is not a substitute for working memory, and the answer to overload is to reduce the load, not to reorganise where it is stored.
OHBvhNBDv4evZYmtCOPo: Active errors are made by the person at the sharp end, at the human-machine interface (3), and their consequences show up immediately in the action being performed (2) - which is what makes them visible and what makes them the errors that get investigated. Errors that lie dormant and are hard to detect are latent errors, the conditions built into the system beforehand.
OHGEmHnlJDFULTXYE9FQ: The fovea is the small central pit of the retina, packed with cones and containing no rods at all. It gives the best daylight acuity and all the colour vision, and it is useless in the dark - which is why a faint object at night disappears when looked at directly and must be viewed off-centre.
OI3FJFeYbajD7oL33zDe: A microburst is a concentrated downdraught that strikes the surface and spreads out radially, giving a strong headwind, then a downdraught, then an equally strong tailwind in seconds - severe wind shear in both the vertical and horizontal planes.
OInVMTh3ewBWwZ5zyVFf: From E008 to W008 is 16 degrees of longitude, which at 60N is 16 x 60 x cos60 = 480 NM = 888 960 m. At 1:5 000 000 that is 888 960 / 5 000 000 = 0.178 m = 17.8 cm. The scale quoted is the one AT 60N, so no further secant correction is needed.
OItWPil9Nc4gtw9bJ6MR: Mode 3 monitors barometric altitude after take-off or a go-around and announces 'DON'T SINK' if the aircraft begins to lose height while still low. 'SINK RATE' belongs to Mode 1, 'TERRAIN' to Mode 2 and 'TOO LOW TERRAIN' to Mode 4.
OJm6JWRCCixPyeI5ctXM: A precision approach uses both azimuth (bearing) and elevation guidance to direct the aircraft to the runway. The most complete definition includes bearing, elevation, and distance information with specific equipment requirements.
OKDtTIDnS6ePd8m6EG4r: Taxiway directional signs indicate the designation and direction of taxiways leading out of an intersection. They help pilots navigate the taxiway system.
OKL6H3d68iNbXImfCqXK: Surface synoptic charts plot mean sea level pressure computed using the ACTUAL temperature profile, which is QFF - the value that makes pressure patterns from stations at different elevations directly comparable. QNH uses the ISA profile and is an altimetry setting, not an analysis quantity; QFE is aerodrome-level pressure; QNE is the pressure altitude reading with 1013 set.
OKyL1QKMg9lgILWm6Kdr: A four-stroke cycle takes two crankshaft revolutions, so each cylinder fires once every second revolution. The spark occurs before top dead centre so that the charge has time to burn and peak pressure arrives just after it, with the advance increasing as engine speed rises.
OM9XLw2hoM7huXOgyVh2: The number is scheduled against the approved passenger seating capacity, in bands - one for 7 to 30 seats, two for 31 to 60, three for 61 to 200, and so on. It depends on the seats installed rather than on the passengers actually carried on the day.
OMXudvQsiqfB4xeEXEKG: In the ICAO Standard Atmosphere the temperature falls at 1.98°C - conventionally 2°C - per 1,000 ft from +15°C at mean sea level up to the tropopause at 36,090 ft, above which it is taken as constant at -56.5°C. The lapse rate is constant only within the troposphere, which is why the qualification matters.
OMrWrYGq2gRdbpcoRAmK: In subsonic flow a diverging passage slows the air down, and the kinetic energy it loses reappears as static pressure and as temperature. That is what a diffuser does - in a compressor, in a jet engine intake and in the venturi of a carburettor after the throat.
OOPo3I2Et6FDSaebaDVw: On a clear, calm night the ground radiates its heat away and cools rapidly, chilling the air in contact with it far more than the air a few hundred feet up. The result is a surface-based inversion, typically a few hundred feet deep, which is very stable, traps moisture and pollution, and gives rise to radiation fog, mist and marked low-level wind shear at its top.
OPFN9d14UTRMCUdY1lNi: The behaviour follows from the pendulous construction of the compass: the magnet system hangs below its pivot, so the dip component of the earth's field drags it round in a turn (3). The oscillations it produces are also different on north and south headings for the same reason (2). It is not a fault and it is not hemisphere-dependent in the sense of one being less reliable than the other.
OPfrBOfTZD8wRBvsW0cM: The fuel-oil heat exchanger does two jobs at once: the fuel takes heat out of the oil, and the oil warms the fuel enough to stop water in it freezing into crystals that would block the filter. One unit therefore serves both the oil cooling and the fuel de-icing requirement.
OPgOyMfV4xomt3yNb8op: Non-precision and precision approach runways (CAT I, II, III) are all classified as instrument runways. Non-instrument runways are those intended for visual approaches only.
OPtbisD5ZufTS9knY9tr: The alerting hierarchy is warning, caution, advisory. A warning signals an emergency requiring immediate action, so it takes precedence over everything else - if a caution and a warning coincide the warning is presented first, and it is never inhibited by a lesser alert.
OQFCYlGYSdloJZ54FhSy: VHF direction finding uses the ordinary VHF communications band, 118 to 137 MHz, which corresponds to wavelengths of about 2 to 2.5 metres - the metric band. That is why no special airborne equipment is needed beyond the normal transceiver.
OQLIkQy0NrkR27QKdWz5: During a sustained spin the fluid in the semicircular canals catches up and the sensation of rotation fades. Stopping the rotation then makes the fluid overshoot and deflect the cupula the other way, so the pilot feels he is spinning in the opposite direction - and the instinctive 'correction' would re-enter the original spin. This is the graveyard spin.
OQvlHfQCdG0OmOCUM3m0: Pilot's vertigo is prevented by not provoking the vestibular system and by having a reliable reference when it misbehaves: avoid steep turns, abrupt manoeuvres and unnecessary head movements, and maintain a systematic instrument cross-check so that the aircraft is flown by the panel rather than by sensation. Relying on the balance organs or on fleeting outside cues is what produces the problem.
ORATcdkarQbYUP7ggle3: Radio altimeters operate in the band 4200 to 4400 MHz, a wavelength of about 7 cm, which gives a small aerial and the precision of a couple of feet needed for the flare. Weather radar works around 9 GHz and primary surveillance radar lower still.
ORLf0fW3DK3iKSGc8IBq: ANDS: Accelerate North, Decelerate South on east/west headings in the northern hemisphere. Accelerating on a westerly heading gives an apparent turn towards the NORTH, so the indicated heading moves from 270 up towards 360, i.e. it increases, and an increasing indication means the card is turning anti-clockwise.
OSFqBcDnQGVNW81EArZz: A layer in which temperature increases with height is an inversion, and it is absolutely stable. A parcel lifted into it cools at its adiabatic rate while the surroundings get warmer, so the parcel becomes very much colder and denser than its environment and is forced straight back down. Inversions therefore act as lids, capping convection and trapping haze, smoke and moisture below them.
OSdtptV6se97lBfz5QZM: The carburettor meters fuel against the volume of air passing rather than its mass, so as the air thins with altitude the mixture becomes progressively richer. Leaning reduces the fuel flow to match the smaller mass of air, keeping the ratio near the intended value.
OSoXkEcIrNr6aQk3Crf4: Proficiency shows as spare capacity. When the routine handling and procedural work have become automatic, they consume almost no conscious attention, leaving the pilot's limited cognitive resources free for monitoring, anticipation and decision making. The pilot who must think about every action has nothing left over when something unexpected happens.
OT80vfwWGm6cRaV50lZp: FADEC has full authority over the engine, so it runs the start sequence automatically - motoring, ignition, fuel and monitoring for a hot or hung start (1) - and controls the thrust reverser deployment and the reverse thrust setting (4). Aircraft speed and yaw are the business of the autoflight system, not the engine control.
OTPcps0KNhp9X5DAq35Q: A swept wing's natural failing is that it stalls at the TIPS first, producing a nose-up pitching moment and a loss of aileron authority. Slats give the largest increase in stalling ANGLE of any device, so they are fitted where that margin is most needed - the tips. Leading-edge (Krueger) flaps, which add camber rather than raising the stalling angle as much, go at the roots, where an early stall is actually desirable.
OTbvov184dxrq4R7EwZ4: Angle of attack is measured by an airflow sensor mounted where the local flow is representative: either a vane which weathercocks into the flow and drives a synchro (2), or a slotted conical probe which rotates until the pressures at its slots are equal (3). A pitot probe measures pressure, not direction.
OUBTKugBpYfYvgUmDxr1: The wind from 130 is 40 degrees off the 090 track, giving about 13 kt of crosswind and 15 kt of headwind, so the groundspeed out is about 84 kt and back about 114 kt. Setting d/84 + d/114 = 2 hours gives d = about 97 NM. A radius of action is always less than half the still-air distance.
OULietOYn1X0at8VICOo: Both statements are correct. Sleep runs in roughly 90-minute cycles, and the proportion of REM in each successive cycle increases through the night, so REM is concentrated in the last hours. That is why a shortened or repeatedly interrupted sleep costs disproportionately much REM, and REM deprivation shows as irritability, poor concentration and impaired memory consolidation.
OUkDHKt8ZHyVpMYgGNa8: The dangerous goods transport document is the SHIPPER's document: the shipper classifies, packs, marks, labels and declares the consignment and signs to certify it. The operator checks it on acceptance and the commander is notified of what is aboard, but neither draws it up.
OVYbnWDmf4Y0Slz3DL7L: Special VFR without a radio receiver is only permitted in Class E airspace. Classes C and D always require two-way radio communication.
OVg3XW6PtTqfomAkNiwQ: Basic empty mass includes the full oil and hydraulic fluid, so those are left in place; what must be removed is everything the definition excludes - usable fuel, toilet fluid and removable service equipment. Draining the oil would give a figure that does not correspond to the definition being measured.
OWVTQ9loexT7cXv4zZkE: Two corrections. QNH 1003 is 10 hPa below 1013, so the indicated altitude is 15 000 - 270 = 14 730 ft. ISA at 15 000 ft is -15C, so -5C is ISA+10, warmer and less dense, and the aircraft is HIGHER than indicated: about 590 ft more, giving a true altitude of about 15 300 ft.
OYFbwoHQ4hfXON9fDr8E: For timed approach wake turbulence separation: Medium behind Heavy = 2 minutes. This is the time-based equivalent of the distance-based separation used with radar.
OYKgbiKoxX9IjyfsyR4n: The wind from 015 is almost on the port beam of the 110 track, so nearly all 40 kt is crosswind: the drift correction is about 11 degrees left, giving a heading of about 099. Only a few knots is left as an along-track component, so the groundspeed stays close to the TAS at about 199 kt.
OZCviLn36zCtBXOdwvK2: Before the autopilot engages, its computers are driven to match the aircraft's existing attitude and the servo outputs are nulled, so that engagement produces no control movement at all. Without that synchronisation the aeroplane would jerk to whatever the computer happened to be commanding.
OZWVS1nsQWZNfJgou7t0: The constant of the cone is the sine of the parallel of origin, which lies midway between the standard parallels. The mean of 50N and 70N is 60N, and sin60 = 0.866. That constant converts change of longitude into chart convergence anywhere on the sheet.
OZb3ecA1Z3YIYYsbhnof: Thrust depends on mass flow, and warmer air at the same pressure is less dense, so the same EPR corresponds to less thrust as the temperature rises. That is why take-off thrust is scheduled against temperature and why a flat rated engine loses thrust above its corner point.
OaUGPrCaIMbSBGgovfKF: Work in stages. Radial 238 INBOUND is a magnetic track of 058, and with 50W variation that is a true track of 058 - 50 = 008. On a north polar chart gridded on Greenwich, grid = true + west longitude, so 008 + 94 = 102, i.e. about 103 grid.
OadbSrYjxd2iFEgsp7D2: The datum is an arbitrary reference plane on the longitudinal axis chosen by the manufacturer for convenience, and it is frequently placed ahead of the nose so that every arm comes out positive and no sign errors creep in. It need not lie between the nose and the tail at all.
ObJeWXqOLk5aVPwIc2LI: The angle of INCIDENCE is the fixed rigging angle built into the airframe between the wing chord line and the fuselage longitudinal axis - it does not change in flight. Angle of ATTACK, by contrast, is measured between the chord line and the RELATIVE AIRFLOW and varies continuously. Confusing the two is a common trap, since only one of them is a variable.
OcGbsvFhze9mczc5YcFz: This question needs an Air Almanac extract that this text-only version cannot show, so learn the method instead. Duration of morning civil twilight is the LMT of sunrise minus the LMT at which the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon, both taken from the almanac for the date and latitude. Note how strongly it depends on latitude: a few minutes at the equator, an hour or more near the Arctic Circle in winter, which is why the answer here is of the order of an hour rather than minutes.
OcKUNU6ZDP5B4cZuQVJW: Divided attention is not genuine simultaneous processing - the limited attentional resource cannot be split that way. What actually happens is rapid switching: several items are handled one after another, each getting the attention for a moment. That is why each task suffers, and why adding a task under high workload means something gets dropped altogether.
OcRAmaQQkhRriDgeyUsU: An elliptical planform produces an elliptical spanwise lift distribution, which gives uniform downwash across the entire span - the theoretical minimum induced drag for a given lift and span. Rectangular and tapered wings depart from that ideal and pay a small penalty, expressed as a span efficiency factor below 1. In practice taper and washout are used to approximate the ellipse at far lower manufacturing cost.
OcZZjtoOLDmRJ1tOOSV5: Work through it in steps. Doubling the speed at constant lift requires CL to fall to a quarter, since lift depends on CL x V2. Induced drag COEFFICIENT is proportional to CL squared, so it falls to (1/4)2 = 1/16. Induced DRAG then equals that coefficient multiplied by the dynamic pressure, which has quadrupled: 1/16 x 4 = 1/4. So the coefficient falls by 1/16 and the force by 1/4.
OdvVsDNCMfs5Cmp8WoOY: In a level turn the vertical component of lift must equal the weight, so L cos(bank) = W, giving n = 1/cos(bank). Nothing else appears - not speed, not radius, not weight. This is why a 60 degree bank always means 2 g whatever the aeroplane or the airspeed, and why bank angle alone determines how close a level turn takes you to the structural limit.

PTslTys2Rx000yqZoUv9: Cultural differences on a flight deck show up as communication difficulty (2), as differing expectations about authority, delegation and how a crew should be run (3), and as interpersonal friction arising from both (4). Statement 1 is about technical training and skill, which is not what the question asks - the differences here are explicitly non-technical.
PTz4l1taYOWSZQnk9VFO: Boots work by inflating to crack and shed ice that has already formed, so they are a de-icing rather than an anti-icing device and must not be operated before an accretion has built up. They are laid along the leading edge, and they are used on turboprops precisely because such aircraft lack the bleed air for thermal anti-icing.
PV0h6w6cHK1UR2hO33M6: The dry adiabatic lapse rate is 3 C per 1000 ft, equivalently 1 C per 100 m. It is a fixed constant set by the thermodynamics of an expanding parcel, not by the state of the surrounding atmosphere. Compare 2 C per 1000 ft, which is the ISA environmental rate, and the saturated adiabatic rate, which is variable and always less than 3 C per 1000 ft.
PV1qpZ5plUNR7hUMZB3b: The FMS manages the lateral flight plan (4) and predicts and monitors fuel, giving the crew fuel remaining at each waypoint and at destination (3). Traffic and resolution advisories are TCAS functions and have nothing to do with the FMS.
PVHUdrj5RM5yjfoYfBLL: Holdover assumes still conditions. A strong wind, or the jet efflux of another aircraft, physically shears the thickened fluid film off the wing, so the protection can be gone long before the table's time has elapsed - which is why crews avoid sitting in another aeroplane's blast after treatment.
PW0sQ81Xi0KVhisiLPiP: A compass swing measures and then compensates DEVIATION, the error caused by the aircraft's own magnetism. Variation is a property of the earth and cannot be adjusted out; acceleration and parallax errors come from the instrument's design and installation, not from calibration.
PWNvMZBfgeCQh1zNaJqi: Both statements are wrong. Gust locks are for use on the ground only and must be removed before flight - using one in the air would remove control of the aeroplane. And reversible controls are precisely the ones that need a gust lock, because the wind can slam the surfaces against their stops.
PWltopsWOhLE8NxJVLKw: The airspeed indicator measures dynamic pressure, and dynamic pressure is what remains when static pressure is subtracted from the total pressure sensed at the pitot head. The capsule sees total inside and static outside, so its deflection is a measure of the difference.
PWn20DOgqWGB4LVAulhQ: Bypass ratio is cold flow divided by core flow: 888 divided by 111 is 8:1, a high bypass ratio typical of a modern large turbofan.
PWqwFm1OphbB2gaQKfVU: The pilot-in-command is responsible for ensuring appropriate aeronautical charts are aboard the aircraft. This is part of the PIC's pre-flight planning responsibilities.
PWtsH5OKpkZuN0OpWmpc: Take the legs in order. 2950 NM north is 49 degrees 10 minutes of latitude, taking the aircraft from 04 10 S through the equator to 45 00 N. Then 382 NM west along the 45N parallel is 382 / cos45 = 540 minutes = 9 degrees of longitude, and from 178 22 W that crosses the 180 meridian to 172 38 E.
PX8Z57ZeUaILlzPuRWPV: The indicated altitude of 19 300 ft is already on the local QNH, so only the temperature correction remains. ISA at that level is about -25C, so 0C is roughly ISA+25: the air is warmer and less dense, and the aircraft is HIGHER than indicated. At 4 ft per 1000 ft per degree that is about 1900 ft, giving a true altitude of about 21 200 ft.
PXOyOw2a8bHETzA026b3: An autopilot system comprises the computer which works out what to do (4), the actuators which move the controls (1), the mode control panel through which the crew selects what it should do (2) and the mode annunciator which tells them what it is actually doing (3).
PXceLf1u261c8M6R1s6p: The flight data recorder must retain at least the last 25 hours of operation. The recorder measured in minutes is the CVR - 30 minutes for aeroplanes certificated before 1 April 1998 and two hours after.
PY9pFFpcFYBVr3QhMWbP: Galactic cosmic radiation is attenuated by the atmosphere above the aircraft, so the dose rate rises steeply with altitude - and also with latitude, since the earth's magnetic field deflects less of it near the poles. This is why long-range crews on polar routes receive the highest occupational doses and why exposure is monitored.
PYONl9hHrirBXOzJNjFH: A hung start is one in which the engine lights but then stabilises below idle, because there is not enough starter assistance for the fuel being supplied. Low starter air pressure is the classic cause, and it is why starter pressure is checked before an engine start on a hot day or at altitude.
PZLJsF0fFinkQ3Uud2cz: Oil does far more than lubricate: it carries heat away from the pistons, bearings and cylinder walls to the oil cooler, and a significant proportion of the heat rejected by a piston engine leaves that way. It also cleans, seals the rings and inhibits corrosion.
PZn9K6EAI0lEoqpEVyzM: JAR-FCL: an ATPL(A) applicant must demonstrate ability to perform as PIC in an aircraft certificated for a minimum crew of two pilots under IFR. This reflects the multi-crew nature of ATPL operations.
PaRoGtpNNIgWHlWmwPMw: VA is the speed at which the aeroplane stalls at exactly the limit manoeuvring load factor, and since stall speed rises with the square root of load factor, VA = VS x sqrt(n). For a large transport aeroplane the positive limit load factor is 2.5, giving VA = VS x sqrt(2.5), about 1.58 VS. Below VA a single full elevator deflection stalls the wing before it overstresses the structure.
Papchs2xC027U4kBe5uf: A central processing unit is built from an arithmetic and logic unit which performs the operations (1), a control and timing section which sequences them (2), and registers which hold the operands and results while it works (3). Memory and input-output are outside the CPU itself.
PcR4N1fzifCK4egLuHsq: Flying into a microburst you meet the outflow head-on first, so the initial indications are an INCREASING headwind and apparently better climb performance. That is the trap: the encouraging phase lasts a few seconds before the downdraught and then the tailwind arrive, and the performance loss that follows is the reverse of the gain.
PcS8x3whODRzRoW9v27r: Two corrections. QNH 1033 is 20 hPa above 1013, so the indicated altitude is 25 000 + 540 = 25 540 ft. ISA at that level is -35C, so -45C is ISA-10 and the aircraft is lower than indicated by about 900 ft over the height above the station, giving a true altitude of about 24 600 ft. Clearance above the 20 410 ft ridge is therefore about 4200 ft.
PcZP22wkjUdeeJB16SWe: The governor holds RPM constant, so as forward speed rises the blade must be coarsened to keep the same angle of attack and absorb the same power. Blade angle therefore increases with true airspeed, which is why the propeller is fine for take-off and coarse in the cruise.
PdauclI6g33cQXBmZY70: The glide angle relative to the AIR is fixed by L/D and is unaffected by mass or wind - a heavier aeroplane simply flies the same angle faster. What extends the ground distance is a TAILWIND, which carries the aeroplane along while it descends and so flattens the path traced over the ground. A headwind does the reverse.
PdteRaokHkgDacYcgZLV: The parallel of origin of a 37N/65N Lambert is 51N, and both points lie SOUTH of it. A great circle on a Lambert is concave towards the parallel of origin, so from south of it the great circle bows away from the straight line towards the equator, and the rhumb line lies further equatorward still. Both are therefore south of the straight line.
PepUnHZbI1Mwarw84nDn: Active clearance control sprays cooling air onto the turbine casing to shrink it in the cruise, closing the gap between the blade tips and the shroud when the engine is running steadily, and relaxing it during transients when the disc grows fastest. Managing the clearance actively is worth a measurable improvement in fuel consumption.
Pg8UL8rv3z9CDs5DI6B1: Both are correct. Sleep loss and disrupted sleep patterns produce drowsiness, irritability and poor concentration, and the resulting slowing of reactions, impaired memory and narrowed attention translate directly into a higher error rate. Fatigue is a flight-safety issue for exactly this reason, and it is why flight and duty time limitations exist.
PgGynN02MzbqL54e2rTO: The pilot-in-command is responsible for terrain clearance when following an ATC clearance. ATC provides separation from traffic but terrain clearance is always the PIC's responsibility.
PgSc97hM6N2ehoJBeRFd: The capsule is fed total pressure from the pitot head and the case is fed static pressure, so the capsule expands by an amount that depends on the difference between them - the dynamic pressure. That is why a blocked pitot or a blocked static each produce their own characteristic error.
PhHJb1AM5mVNCVkxxJKB: A turbocharger uses the energy still left in the exhaust gas to drive a turbine, which drives a compressor on the same shaft to boost the induction pressure. Because it recovers waste energy it costs little in power, unlike a supercharger driven mechanically from the crankshaft.
PiGBKbAi7quWe80XcGgd: Runway width is a height cue. A runway wider than the pilot is used to subtends a larger angle, so it appears nearer and lower, and the aircraft feels lower than it is. Correcting for a height error that does not exist, the pilot flies higher than the correct profile and arrives high and fast, with a long landing or an overshoot.
PiNDxktDPrm2WxPaqNyT: First-aid oxygen is undiluted oxygen for a passenger who needs it for physiological reasons after a decompression - treatment given once the aeroplane is at a safe level. Supplemental oxygen protects everyone during the descent, and protective breathing equipment protects the crew against smoke and fumes.
PiR9sTBrVOK4b9PyRCUs: The gyro provides a stable directional reference, so it has two degrees of freedom and its spin axis is kept horizontal by an erection system. Slaving to the flux valve then supplies the long-term magnetic accuracy that the gyro alone cannot provide.
PiwRfa6fPNqX84iIJkyy: The question asks specifically for physical stimuli - stressors acting on the body from the physical environment or from bodily state - so noise (1), temperature (3) and hunger (5) qualify. Conflict and administrative problems are real stressors but psychological and social in origin, not physical.
Pk9XBUcvJ1Mz2uFELBqz: The cones give daylight acuity and colour vision, are concentrated in the central retina and are highly sensitive to any shortage of oxygen - along with the rods, which is why colour discrimination and night vision fail early in hypoxia. Retinal blood flow is not maintained under high G, which is what produces greyout and blackout, and neither photoreceptor is located in the lens.
PkKM8wkVmA0M0dMQ1P7I: Same latitude means the same LMT of sunrise, so convert. At 040E, LMT is UTC + 2 h 40 min, so sunrise at 0243 UTC is 0523 LMT. At 035W, LMT is UTC - 2 h 20 min, so the same 0523 LMT is 0743 UTC. Sunrise happens 5 hours later in clock terms simply because the second position is 75 degrees further west.
Pktjmt9x0ZD45IByYzy8: ISA at FL330 is 15 - 66 = -51C, so ISA+15 gives -36C = 237 K. The local speed of sound is 38.94 x root(237) = about 600 kt, so the Mach number is 487 / 600 = 0.81. The speed of sound depends only on temperature, never on altitude or pressure directly.
Pl1THi8GSf6ama8PM46G: Negative habit transfer is a well-learned action from a previous aircraft reasserting itself on a new type where it is now wrong - the fuel lever moved to the position that used to mean ON. It is favoured by stress, distraction and relaxed attention. Confusing left and right is an action slip, and missing a checklist item is a lapse.
Pl1pbXb7SSSeSQMmugUS: The ICAO Standard Atmosphere specifies a temperature decrease of 0.65 C per 100 m (6.5 C per km, or 1.98 C per 1000 ft) from 15 C at sea level up to 11 km, where it reaches -56.5 C and then stays constant to 20 km. The 1 C per 100 m alternative is the dry adiabatic lapse rate, which describes a rising parcel rather than the standard environment.
PmT6WprmNb7ZQ1oKSWVY: A bimetallic switch closes on a rapid rise in temperature, and vibration or a momentary hot gas puff could close it briefly. The built-in delay means the contacts must stay closed for a defined period before the warning is raised, so genuine fires are annunciated but transients are not.
Pn15d8xuRCWX0A8l5Eu5: The IRS mode selector runs OFF - ALIGN - NAV - ATT. NAV is selected once alignment is complete, or directly, in which case alignment runs first. ATT sits at the end because it is the reversionary attitude-only mode, entered when navigation has been lost.
Podjn2C5aySutE6NxY8w: With one port blocked the instruments read only the other. In symmetric flight both ports see the same pressure, so nothing is wrong. In a sideslip the two differ, and using only the remaining port introduces an error whose sign depends on which way the aeroplane is slipping.
Poz5RKPkPMA8yJ1Qpx8p: The take-off sequence runs VMCG (the lowest speed at which the aeroplane can be kept straight after a failure, and hence the floor on V1), then V1 (the decision speed), then VR (rotation), then V2 (the take-off safety speed achieved by 35 ft). VMU and VLOF fall between VR and V2. Each speed bounds the next, which is why the ordering is fixed.
PpByUxRV9qVlSf3R0Jb0: Category I is a precision approach with a decision height not lower than 200 ft and an RVR of not less than 550 m. A DH of 100 ft is Category II; below 100 ft, or with no DH at all, the approach is Category III.
PpG74U3Ma0blaThiJSbN: Interference drag arises where the airflows around two adjoining components - wing and fuselage, nacelle and pylon, fin and tailplane - meet and interact, producing separation and turbulence that neither component would generate alone. It is a component of parasite drag and is minimised by fairings and fillets at the junctions. It is quite distinct from induced drag, which comes from the tip vortices.
PqDOHZTXkRVcdEUqXyZw: Habit offers the familiar solution first and makes it feel right, which is efficient most of the time and is why experienced pilots are fast. The cost is that the familiar option is taken without the alternatives being generated, so in the case where it is not the best answer the better one is never considered.
PqGyslNje1L2S8h0lkFA: The packs control the temperature of the air delivered to the cabin, mixing cold air from the cold air unit with hot bleed air to whatever the crew has selected. The oxygen content is not altered at all - the air is ordinary atmospheric air, simply supplied at a higher pressure than outside.
PrWhN18fBwwhFjMjuvQN: For a short layover there is no time to adapt - the body clock takes roughly a day per time zone - so shifting it would leave the crew desynchronised for the return sector as well. The strategy is to stay on home time for eating and sleeping and to treat the stop as a period of the home day. Adaptation is worth attempting only for stays beyond about 24 hours.
PtdGq4JvoFSsMwV9cDv4: A combined DC starter-generator saves the weight and complexity of two machines: it motors the engine for the start and then, once running, is switched to act as the generator. It suits helicopters and small turbine aircraft, where the electrical load is modest.
PtuauNPYfs0QP6gNDNf8: A float senses the height of the liquid surface, so any pitch, roll or acceleration moves the surface relative to the float (2 and 3), and temperature changes the fuel's density so that the same level represents a different mass (4). Simplicity is the float gauge's principal virtue, and it runs on the DC system.
PuSFf5zMNat5O8NFoWhl: ICAO Doc 4444: for independent parallel approaches, missed approach tracks must diverge by at least 30 degrees from each other.
PuXJAa9NHC82RHeTzOEm: Machines beat people comfortably on speed, memory capacity, precision and tireless repetition. What the human retains is creativity and flexibility: the ability to recognise an unfamiliar pattern, reason from incomplete or contradictory information and improvise a response to a situation nobody programmed for. That is why the pilot remains in the loop.
PumlMoCEUhcknIkl7d0g: The command bar is a command, not a raw-data display: it shows the bank change needed to capture and then hold the localiser. Where the aeroplane actually is relative to the beam is shown by the localiser pointer, and the roll attitude by the aircraft symbol against the sky pointer.
PwE1kFycEwW8Cxeg8IZX: Build the fuel up in order: trip 5350, contingency at 5 percent of trip = 268, the 4380 kg needed for the go-around and diversion, and final reserve of 30 minutes at the HOLDING flow = 0.5 x 6000 = 3000 kg. That totals about 13 000 kg. Contingency is a regulatory requirement, so it must be included even when the stem does not spell it out.
Px0K84gb21HqkMmyPxB6: Hot air anti-icing keeps the leading edge clean, so the wing's aerodynamics are unaffected - that is the point of it. What it costs is bleed air taken from the compressor, which reduces the thrust available and increases fuel consumption, and is why anti-ice selection is accounted for in the performance figures.
PxpIM3A5ig9yuKZdgAKe: During a visual approach in Class C, ATC applies separation with all traffic. Class C provides separation service to all participating flights, both IFR and VFR.
PyLLnnlINul0bBEVuaxs: Hypoxia is prevented by keeping the alveolar oxygen pressure up, which means supplemental oxygen above about 10,000 ft cabin altitude. The body provides no reliable warning - euphoria and impaired judgement come first - so waiting for symptoms is precisely the wrong strategy, and swallowing and the Valsalva manoeuvre address ear pressure, not oxygen.
PyVQ0GfCZW5zvxLqSjsG: A HEAVY following another HEAVY on approach to the same runway requires 4 NM (7.4 km). The larger figures apply where the following aircraft is lighter than the leader: 5 NM for a MEDIUM behind a HEAVY and 6 NM for a LIGHT behind a HEAVY.
PyskE6vTzxOSJgVLbJsn: Glaucoma is a rise in intra-ocular pressure (4) which damages the optic nerve fibres from the periphery inwards, so the visual field narrows progressively (2), and it does so painlessly and unnoticed until a great deal has been lost (3) - which is why the pressure is measured routinely rather than waiting for symptoms.
Pz2aHcW75gMythO4I4mD: Above roughly 2,000 metres - about 6,000-7,000 ft - the falling partial pressure of oxygen begins to produce measurable compensation: breathing deepens and quickens and the heart rate and cardiac output rise to maintain oxygen delivery. Below that the body is in the indifferent stage and no significant compensation is needed; above about 15,000 ft compensation can no longer keep pace.
PziowbdvQGtiUaMjBXe8: On a straight-in VOR approach, descent below OCA may continue when it seems possible to land — meaning the pilot has sufficient visual reference and confidence that a safe landing can be made.
PzqgpJLt8IWLtXVWpeRo: The navigation database holds the fixed data needed to fly a route: airports (1), navaids (3), runways (5), waypoints, airways and procedures. Take-off speeds are computed from the performance database for the day's conditions, and terrain data belongs to the EGPWS.
Q0IaqjPUcDPxa8fCjxZP: Carbon monoxide binds haemoglobin with over 200 times the affinity of oxygen, so even a brief exposure to a high concentration - a cracked exhaust heat exchanger feeding the cabin heater - can occupy enough carriage capacity to cause headache, poor judgement and impaired vision within minutes. The gas is odourless, tasteless and colourless, and no tolerance to it develops.
Q1bIiKBpxkvyNUl9Swj0: An inversion is any layer in which temperature increases with height, reversing the normal profile - no minimum rate of increase is required. Inversions are extremely stable, so they cap convection and trap moisture, smoke and dust beneath them, giving haze and poor visibility. Common types are radiation (nocturnal, surface-based), subsidence (aloft, in an anticyclone), frontal and turbulence inversions.
Q1nUQ18SR5EGvJ8G54WA: Hypoxic hypoxia, the aviation form, is caused by a fall in the partial pressure of oxygen in the alveoli, which follows directly from the fall in total pressure with altitude. Nitrogen partial pressure has no bearing on oxygenation, and a greater haemoglobin affinity or more red cells would improve oxygen carriage rather than impair it.
Q1ten2gdZtF9MXVb6ogW: Both statements hold. The tanks add wetted area and frontal area, so PARASITE drag rises. But sitting at the tips they act as endplates, obstructing the flow that would otherwise spill around the tip from the high-pressure lower surface to the low-pressure upper surface - so the tip vortices weaken and INDUCED drag falls. This is the same principle that winglets exploit.
Q3XkpJX067uFwPbhLvUa: Fog, snow and haze reduce contrast, and the brain reads low contrast as distance, so objects appear farther away than they are - and, being apparently farther away at the same angular size, larger and slower. The visual approach picture is therefore unreliable in reduced visibility and the instruments or the glidepath guidance must be used instead.
Q5G5CGHYmBBGx6ug5XqE: An input peripheral supplies data to the computer, which is what a keyboard does. A printer is an output device, and disk drives both read and write, so they are storage rather than purely input or output.
Q5jI21in4VcEyRmJrL1A: The erection system uses a pendulous device to find the vertical, and a deceleration displaces that pendulum exactly as a pitch change would. The erector therefore drives the gyro towards a false vertical and the horizon shows a nose-down attitude which is not there - the acceleration error of the attitude indicator, in reverse.
Q60v5pDewonNpior3UaN: The alternate fuel must not be touched, so the fuel available for the rest of the trip is 60 - 12 = 48 US gallons, and it must last the 1 h 35 min still to run, i.e. 1.583 hours. The maximum rate is therefore 48 / 1.583 = about 30.3 US gallons per hour. Any higher rate eats into the diversion fuel.
Q6Au696iQkFBPKfwTyVO: The MEL is prepared by the OPERATOR from the manufacturer's MMEL, approved by the Authority, and inserted in the Operations Manual as a crew document. The Flight Manual is an aircraft document approved for the type and is not where operator dispatch relief lives.
Q6bXlnVbb67tmsPjBsF2: Circling visibility runs 1500 m for Category A, 1600 m for B, 2400 m for C and 3600 m for D. Category A is the slowest group, so its visual manoeuvre stays closest to the runway and needs the least visibility.
Q6uUR9snC7Dj2JxggUHG: The vertical bar is a roll command: how far it is displaced tells the pilot how much bank to apply as well as in which direction. It is not a repeat of any raw deviation - the localiser and glideslope displacements are displayed separately by their own pointers.
Q70YbHv8YrSS6P18V2ob: The flux valve is excited by an alternating current in its primary and senses the horizontal component of the earth's field through the distortion that field produces in the core's flux. Its output can drive a flux gate compass or slave a directional gyro, and being fixed in a wingtip or fin it is accurate to a small fraction of a degree.
Q7Wu55bNqjOmDpMmbR21: A tubeless tyre has no inner tube to chafe against the casing, so it runs cooler and a puncture deflates it slowly instead of bursting (3). Its weakness is the valve, which is mounted in the rim and can be sheared off by a heavy landing or by careless handling (2).
Q8Jzme1Yw05OWIrk8vkg: A motor programme is a learned sequence run automatically, and its two characteristic failures are the action slip - the right intention executed with the wrong action - and environmental capture, in which a familiar setting triggers the habitual programme even though a different one is now required. Both are skill-based failures rather than errors of intention.
Q8ixAIO5nD9H9bnmthkY: Stressors add together, so several small ones can exceed a limit none of them would reach alone (1). Errors chain, each one creating the conditions for the next (2). Carboxyhaemoglobin builds up because it is cleared far more slowly than it is acquired (3). And conflict escalates once started (4). Colour blindness is a fixed condition and does not accumulate.
Q9PMpk5FL7xzaezQuaay: When weather conditions at destination and alternate are marginal, the PIC should list at least one additional alternate airport to ensure safe diversion options.
Q9QfMyWJPEmtDKERD6De: A copy of the OPERATIONAL flight plan - the operator's own document, with the fuel plan, the route detail and the calculations behind them - must be retained on the ground for the duration of the flight. The ATC flight plan is a message to air traffic services and carries none of that detail.
Q9WqLTn5XMAVuPc4WETI: JAR-FCL 3 specifies that licence holders must inform the Authority of illness causing incapacity for 21 days or more. This differs from the ICAO standard of one calendar month.
Q9Yo4x0DuUkl5PD4QKdO: If a transponder is unserviceable before departure, the aircraft may depart to the nearest suitable airport where repair can be effected. The flight is not completely prohibited.
Q9vpZu61kdADeP3vLcss: ICAO Annex 13: the State of Design and State of Manufacture must inform the State of Occurrence of their investigation representative when the aircraft has a maximum mass exceeding 2,250 kg.
Q9wtatD4rMKBpg0gugOk: At a constant power setting the heat being put into the oil is constant, so a rising oil temperature means the heat is not being removed - a blocked or bypassing fuel-oil or air-oil heat exchanger. Ambient temperature has little effect, since the cooling medium is fuel or engine air rather than outside air.
Q9xPjAYXaO3KXRM5UXQy: Synergy means the crew achieves more than the individuals could separately: two pilots working together catch errors neither would catch alone and produce better decisions, so 1 + 1 is greater than 2. A crew that works badly together can fall below the sum of its parts, which is the case the other expressions describe.
QAFJCsgrwVe4OCl7qmP3: 2000 ft AGL is above the friction layer, so the wind there is the gradient wind. Reversing the over-land friction rule - surface wind backed about 30 degrees and roughly half the speed - means going up you VEER about 30 degrees and DOUBLE the speed. 160 becomes about 190 and 20 kt becomes about 40 kt, giving 19040KT. Over the sea the change would be only about 10 degrees with a smaller speed increase.
QANscr6MeKtFBuQgg8UN: In Rasmussen's model, holding a coordinated turn is skill-based behaviour: for a trained pilot the control inputs are an automatic, continuously adjusted motor programme requiring almost no conscious attention. Rule-based behaviour applies a stored if-then procedure, and knowledge-based behaviour is reasoning out a novel problem from first principles.
QBL5hQBRVsDnpAouIq23: A demand regulator delivers gas only when the wearer inhales, which is what makes the supply last: the pressure drop as he breathes in opens the demand valve, and it closes again on exhalation. The dilution setting determines what is delivered, not whether it is delivered.
QBWGiQqqvznglQsZoEkC: The second segment is a ONE-ENGINE-INOPERATIVE case, so with three engines only two remain: thrust = 2 x 50,000 = 100,000 N. Then sin(gamma) = (T - D)/W gives 0.027 = (100,000 - 72,569)/W, so W = 27,431 / 0.027 = 1,015,963 N. Dividing by g = 10 gives a mass of 101,596 kg. The trap is using all three engines' thrust.
QD7ZB24O6sGFdbhw0Rse: The first response to cold is shivering and increased muscle tone, which generates heat but sharply raises oxygen consumption - so the demand for oxygen goes up initially and hypoxia tolerance falls at exactly the altitude where cabin heating has been lost. Only much later, as the core temperature falls and metabolism slows, does demand drop.
QDQcuU8QGxqsfzHZGeYA: Supplemental oxygen is the reserve carried to supply the occupants after a loss of cabin pressurisation. Oxygen for an individual passenger with a breathing difficulty is first-aid or therapeutic oxygen, and crew fighting a fire use protective breathing equipment.
QDrOfDktKeKPS9lkBJRJ: A pressure cabin is simply one that can be held at a pressure higher than the ambient outside, so the cabin altitude stays low while the aircraft climbs. It cannot hold sea level indefinitely - the differential limit prevents it - and the differential is not constant, since it grows during the climb.
QETnXijPa80TxON4J4x6: A professional language works by restricting itself: a limited, agreed vocabulary in which each term has one meaning (1), and a shared operational context that supplies the rest and so removes ambiguity (4). Richness and complexity are exactly what standard phraseology is designed to eliminate, since they are what produce misunderstanding.
QEqDhZQ96oLz3OlHQMli: The system compares the measured angle of attack (2) against the stalling angle for the current configuration, so it needs the flap and slat position (4). Airspeed is not used, because a wing stalls at an angle rather than at a speed - which is exactly why an angle-of-attack based warning is superior.
QG1YDBXQGugcx04qS8eO: ICAO Doc 4444: for dependent parallel approaches, missed approach tracks must diverge by at least 30 degrees from the adjacent approach's missed approach track.
QH14EcWgOr2U5OKyOCTi: Recency for a commander is three take-offs and three landings as pilot flying within the preceding 90 days, in an aeroplane of the same type or class or in an approved simulator of the type to be used. Neither generic experience on any aeroplane nor a shorter window satisfies it.
QH4jgZuMrw55ldHkmpS5: Rate of turn depends on the bank angle, which sets the horizontal component of lift, and on the speed, which determines how long the aircraft takes to be turned through a given angle. Weight does not appear: a heavy and a light aeroplane at the same bank and speed turn at the same rate.
QHIXb0GOiETCZfET8sob: ICAO Doc 8168: the minimum obstacle clearance in the intermediate phase of a missed approach is 50 m (164 ft). This is between the initial phase MOC and the final phase MOC.
QHp4LKDi6qwQ9bNicO42: The centre of gravity must move 15% of a 1 m chord, or 0.15 m. Transferring mass m over the 3 m between the holds moves the centre of gravity by m x 3 / 2,200, so m = 0.15 x 2,200 / 3 = 110 kg.
QI6Udx1juqIg4zXpOyjB: Alcohol interferes with the brain cells' ability to use the oxygen delivered to them - histotoxic hypoxia - so its effects add to those of altitude and the combination is worse than either alone. One drink is commonly quoted as adding a couple of thousand feet to the physiological altitude, and the accompanying loss of judgement makes the state harder to recognise.
QK2Fze1e8F1SHrx7L4RS: The escape from a shear is flown on thrust and attitude alone: hold the configuration you are in and raise the pitch progressively to the stick shaker. Retracting gear and flaps mid-manoeuvre loses lift while the aeroplane is already short of it, and limiting the pitch change surrenders the only performance left once thrust is at the stop.
QKT50f5XBZBmF8JZRf9m: ICAO Annex 9: unaccompanied baggage carried by air should be cleared under the procedure for accompanied baggage or another simplified customs procedure distinct from cargo.
QKZDxOwJDdKzj7JwT5cU: The behavioural signs of stress are aggression and irritability (1) and withdrawal from the task and from the other crew member (4), along with restless purposeless movement. Better communication and greater group cohesion are the opposite of what stress produces - communication is the first thing to degrade and the crew fragments rather than closing ranks.
QKbsyR3Rm2VqLkhaAlm2: All four apply to the flight crew supply. They must have oxygen for the whole time above 13,000 ft cabin altitude (1) and for the excess over 30 minutes between 10,000 and 13,000 ft (2), and in no case less than 30 minutes on an aeroplane certificated below 25,000 ft (3) or 2 hours on one certificated above it (4).
QKm4mwrkMtOtAXobJYY6: Climbing at constant IAS on maximum climb thrust, the thrust available falls steadily with density while the drag at a given IAS does not - so the excess thrust, and with it the climb ANGLE, reduces continuously. Pitch attitude is the climb angle plus the angle of attack, and at constant IAS the angle of attack is essentially unchanged, so the pitch attitude falls with the climb angle.
QKp9Tx6QLZVncdxNVpsw: Where a flight crew compartment door is fitted it must have a locking system preventing unauthorised access, operated from within the compartment. It is a security requirement - the door is not a pressure boundary and is not designed to hold cabin pressure.
QLHgbZtJqn2KpH55Sm8x: As printed this row has lost everything except the words 'Identify the latitude', so there is no data from which any answer can be derived. Learn the two standard routes to a latitude instead: a change of latitude is distance in NM divided by 60, since one minute of latitude is one nautical mile everywhere; and where a departure along a parallel is given, latitude comes from cos(latitude) = departure / change of longitude in minutes.
QM2GeavfARAYfhxxPdLI: Isogonals are lines of equal variation, and variation is the angle between true and magnetic north. Both references become indeterminate at their own poles, so the isogonals crowd together and converge at all four: the north and south GEOGRAPHIC poles and the north and south MAGNETIC poles.
QMBr5aRxZJH5vmyrqmrR: At very low rotation rates the two counter-rotating beams of a ring laser gyro pull into synchronism and the output disappears - lock-in. The cure is dither: a piezo-electric motor vibrates the whole block back and forth at a few hundred hertz, so the instantaneous rate is almost never near zero, and the dither is subtracted from the output.
QN9Qp5udZuMiHW9gg5k0: Air is supplied to the cabin at a roughly constant rate, so cabin pressure is set by how fast it is allowed to escape. The outflow valve modulates that escape and the controller drives it to follow the scheduled cabin altitude; everything else affects the supply rather than the regulation.
QNP8EvwQKIu7MXUmowA0: An unexplained disagreement between GPS and the conventional aids means one of them is wrong and you do not yet know which. The required action is to find out why and either correct the error or shut down the system identified as faulty; carrying on with an unresolved discrepancy, on either source, is not acceptable under IFR.
QNWDksFaZQMZZv4ZQZ9W: Time pressure removes the opportunity to analyse, so the response is to decide in advance what matters. Prioritising tasks ensures the important ones survive when something has to be dropped, and applying established procedures substitutes ready-made, already-validated sequences for decisions there is no time to make - which is exactly what a standard drill is for.
QNhgugQC9uePhb8UtFSE: A blocked static traps the pressure in the instrument cases, so the altimeter freezes and the vertical speed indicator falls to zero. The airspeed indicator still sees the rising pitot pressure of the descent against that trapped static, so it over-reads and the indication creeps up.
QOiAevGvebeXvEUCksyj: With irreversible controls the surface loads never reach the pedals, so a trim tab has nothing to balance and the feel comes from an artificial feel unit. Trimming therefore means shifting the zero-force datum of that unit so the pedals sit at a new position with no force on them.
QOkzsdgBtStyQAhpRdlC: OIS stands for Obstacle Identification Surface. It identifies obstacles that penetrate the approach surface and may affect obstacle clearance calculations.
QOydrgf5Ech5DNjkjJEn: A 2 degree change in angle of attack raises CL by 2 x 0.079 = 0.158, so the new lift coefficient is 0.35 + 0.158 = 0.508. Since the speed has not changed in that instant, lift is directly proportional to CL, so the load factor is the ratio of the new coefficient to the old: 0.508 / 0.35 = 1.45.
QPUJR3YeFBJ4BVdwsdOG: Long-term memory has effectively unlimited capacity and holds material permanently, but retrieval is neither immediate nor certain - it takes time and depends on the right cues. That is why knowledge which will be needed is deliberately pre-activated: the approach briefing, the review of the drill before descent, the mental rehearsal of the go-around.
QQ0DQ018rbWGjdP1Zyg7: Oxygen does not burn, but it makes everything else burn fiercely, so the precautions are about ignition and about pressure: no smoking, no sparks, and shut-off valves operated slowly to avoid the adiabatic heating that a sudden surge of high-pressure oxygen can produce. Radio equipment is not an ignition source and is not restricted.
QQgaOAAbSghblQlgIDxN: In ground effect the reduced downwash means more lift and much less induced drag, so the aeroplane floats: it is reluctant to stop flying and decelerates slowly in the flare. That extends the airborne portion of the landing and INCREASES the landing distance. The same effect can produce a premature lift-off on take-off, with the aeroplane sinking back as it climbs out of ground effect.
QRHU3di9sviewfQ2WLJZ: The blade's angle of attack is the difference between its fixed blade angle and the helix angle of its path, and that helix angle is set by the ratio of forward speed to rotational speed. Increasing TAS at constant RPM steepens the helix, so the angle of attack - and with it the thrust and the torque - falls.
QSW4SapnWDj2miayoeuJ: Airport information signs (other than location signs) have black inscriptions on a yellow background. Location signs use yellow on black. This colour distinction aids quick recognition.
QSm2IRazgIARpMThmayv: Moving the head while the aircraft is banking - that is, while a rotation is in progress - brings a second pair of semicircular canals into the plane of rotation while the first is still responding. The brain reads the combination as tumbling in a different axis, and this Coriolis illusion is the most powerful vertigo-producing manoeuvre in flight.
QSyRYPE2DlLWAqFZY9hn: Longitude in time is 95 20 x 4 minutes per degree = 6 h 21 min 20 s, and west longitude is subtracted from UTC. 0000 UTC minus that gives 1738:40 on the PREVIOUS day; subtracting past midnight always moves the date back one day.
QUJ2z17J8Yq9hoZ1Zh2U: A cold swells the lining of the Eustachian tube so it can no longer let air into the middle ear. On descent the rising outside pressure then forces the eardrum inwards, causing severe pain, temporary hearing loss and possibly rupture - and the faster the descent, the worse it is. The problem is mechanical and usually reversible, not a permanent hearing loss.
QV0UtkUL89w4oaHU3HQB: The MEL is a crew operating document and lives in the Operations Manual. The Flight Manual is an aircraft document approved for the type and carries limitations and performance, not the operator's dispatch relief.
QVCB2Ltpgp6xSvSSG0aw: METAR temperatures are given in whole degrees with M prefixed for negative values, and 0.5 is rounded up. A temperature of -0.5 C rounds to zero but is still below freezing, so it is coded M00 - the special 'minus zero' form that preserves that information. The dewpoint of -1.5 C rounds up to -1 and is coded M01, giving M00/M01.
QW0sDtlipIuI7fWUM6iT: The warning must track a limit that is a fixed airspeed low down and a fixed Mach number higher up, so it needs both an aneroid capsule sensing static pressure, to know the altitude, and an airspeed capsule sensing dynamic pressure, to know the speed. The two together define the barber's pole.
QWGX6ZhIdPJxPWnqH9dW: Cruise cabin humidity falls to roughly 5-15%, since the air drawn in at altitude holds almost no water. The steady fluid loss produces dehydration with headache, fatigue and poor concentration, so the effects are far from negligible and crews must drink before thirst appears.
QYVvbsmqEor429iTEVgj: The Mach trim system senses Mach number and, as it rises toward Mcrit, automatically repositions the trimmable stabiliser nose-up to counter the tuck-under produced by the aft movement of the centre of pressure. It restores a positive stick force gradient so the aeroplane retains apparent speed stability. It does not hold the Mach number constant - that is the autothrottle's job.
QYYaqheTCaMSL4kXfnWj: Circling visibility runs 1500 m for Category A, 1600 m for B, 2400 m for C and 3600 m for D. A Category B aeroplane - VAT 91 to 120 kt - therefore needs at least 1600 m.
QZdZmVTEqvwAecVWBkOe: MLS works around 5 GHz, a wavelength of about 6 cm - centimetric. That short wavelength allows the narrow scanning beams on which the system's angular precision depends, and permits curved and segmented approach paths that ILS cannot provide.
QZoJRvew806aO0kl3rxz: All three are correct. At 6,000 ft the density ratio gives a TAS about 10% above the indicated speed (1); at 100 kt compressibility is negligible so EAS and CAS are effectively the same (2); and with instrument and position errors removed the indication is by definition calibrated airspeed (3).
QZrOjFcZ4zH9npD135RS: Equivalent airspeed is calibrated airspeed with the compressibility correction applied, allowing for the fact that the air is compressed at the pitot head rather than merely brought to rest. Density is the remaining correction, converting EAS to true airspeed.
QbBNed2gPXpr4c3muL5J: Adaptation - the progressive decline in response to a constant stimulus - is a general property of the senses. The eye adapts to light and dark, the ear to steady noise, the nose to a smell within minutes, the skin to a constant pressure or temperature. Operationally it means a continuous warning, whether visual, aural or a persistent smell, stops being noticed.
QcOW3ABs3HFzfG7CxtSR: In Class C below 10,000 ft AMSL, VFR flights are subject to the 250 kt IAS speed limitation. This standard limit applies across most airspace classes below 10,000 ft.
QdMmR5Ma7KDrC3NtJrNq: A reflex is an involuntary, stereotyped response to a stimulus, wired at spinal or brainstem level without conscious processing. Being automatic it is fast, but it is also fixed - the same input always produces the same output - which makes it useful for protection but useless for anything requiring judgement.
Qdf5U8IqlyrmIVTLERFm: Approach Control Service provides ATC service for arriving and departing controlled flights. It covers both IFR and VFR traffic receiving ATC service in the terminal area.
QfJnY8nzJGFvosaneI2B: Changing from IFR to VFR is initiated by the aircraft commander. ATC cannot unilaterally change the flight rules; the pilot must request cancellation of the IFR flight plan.
QfZJrnVgIQktx4wIVFyY: Rain repellent works by making the water bead and blow off, and it must be applied only to a wet screen - sprayed onto dry or lightly wetted glass it smears and badly degrades the view. That is why it is reserved for heavy rain and why the wipers are used first.
QfmNH6nC2IaW9ywRcBy0: Turning onto north in the northern hemisphere the compass lags, so the turn must be stopped before it reads north - undershoot north, overshoot south. Turning right the heading is increasing towards 360, so the roll-out is at a heading still west of north, and at 40°N the lead is of the order of 30°.
Qga2WukjXpUsqRO2c7Hs: A rate one turn is 3 degrees per second, so after 30 seconds the actual heading is 135 + 90 = 225. Turning right from 135 the aircraft passes through SOUTH, and in the northern hemisphere a turn through south makes the compass LEAD, so it reads more than 225. Through north it lags; through south it leads.
QhDA3UmI0t1F8PSs7CRB: A tornado is a very small but extremely intense vortex: the funnel is typically only 100-150 m across, with a track a few kilometres long, yet wind speeds inside can exceed 200 kt. Its small size is precisely why it is so destructive locally and so hard to forecast. Larger diameters of several kilometres belong to the parent mesocyclone, not the tornado itself.
QhDODNbqaup0gJTI6G6I: Simplicity of construction is the float gauge's one real advantage - it is cheap, robust and easy to install. Everything else in the list is a weakness: the reading is affected by attitude, by acceleration, by temperature through the fuel's density, and by vibration.
QhVyLBPqJrdmX6cZTeTB: FL370 is below FL410, where levels are 1000 ft apart under RVSM, so the contingency offset is 500 ft - it puts the aeroplane midway between the levels other traffic is using. Above FL410 the vertical minimum is 2000 ft and the offset becomes 1000 ft.
Qhyk3uit61CG8jPMYnxB: Useful feedback is specific: it refers to an observed behaviour in a particular situation, so the recipient knows exactly what is being discussed and can do something about it. Generalised comments about the person invite defensiveness and change nothing. Feedback also need not be requested, and demanding an immediate justification turns it into an accusation.
Qi05Wa3ioUjjbP5VipYv: A white dumbbell with black perpendicular bar indicates taxiing need not be confined to the taxiways. Aircraft must use runways for takeoff/landing but may taxi on other surfaces.
Qi0OyUdkKTBECx3Go34v: Time = distance / groundspeed = 433 / 135 = 3.21 hours, and the decimal 0.21 of an hour is about 12 minutes, so 3 HR 12 MIN. Converting the decimal part of the hour is what the near-miss options test.
Qiob6Ic4jPcVJGtX04Qr: Compression ratio compares the volume above the piston at bottom dead centre - swept plus clearance - with the volume at top dead centre, which is the clearance volume alone. A higher ratio gives better thermal efficiency but brings the charge closer to detonation.
QjUn98J4ljXApOpacbeD: A slat moves forward and down, opening a slot that ducts high-energy air from beneath the wing onto the upper surface. Two things follow: the boundary layer is re-energised so it resists separation, and the suction peak transfers from the fixed wing's leading edge onto the SLAT itself, so the main wing's own adverse pressure gradient is much gentler. Together these postpone the stall by 5-10 degrees of angle of attack.
QjXsFEihhdaMWiKMc9LT: The capsule is fed total pressure from the pitot head while the case is fed static pressure, so its deflection depends on the difference between them. That difference is the dynamic pressure, which is what the airspeed indicator actually measures.
QjkCqxYNEw5ffmiWYe3m: SRA termination distance varies by authority. Common values include 2 NM from touchdown, though some authorities specify different distances based on local radar capability.
QjwlZOel6ybyW1TgGXgm: At -25 C most of a layer cloud has glaciated into ice crystals, leaving very little supercooled liquid water, and crystals bounce off a cold airframe rather than adhering. Severe icing is therefore unlikely at this temperature. The serious risk lies between 0 C and about -15 C, where large supercooled droplets are abundant - which is why -5 C in dense cloud would be a real concern.
QkFUVszFyDtevZbjTm6F: Advection fog forms when warm, moist air is carried horizontally over a surface colder than its dewpoint and is cooled from below to saturation. It needs a wind of roughly 10-15 kt: enough turbulence to deepen the fog without lifting it into stratus. Cold air over a warmer surface does the opposite - it is heated from below, becomes unstable, and gives convection or steaming fog.
QkdyJwdmBm5E2dtuqTn0: A frequency wild generator is driven directly by the engine with no constant speed drive, so its output frequency rises and falls with engine speed. That is acceptable for loads that do not care about frequency - resistive heating and rectified supplies - which is exactly what such systems feed.
QkmmIEUU5yEIHN4tEBuY: The dividing line is drawn at about one second. Accelerations lasting less than that are short-duration and their effect is mechanical - the impact loads of a crash or an ejection, where the body's structural tolerance is what matters. Longer accelerations are long-duration, and their effects are physiological, acting through the displacement of blood and organs.
Qkss4IFko6kDMf7PQbu4: Controlled flight into terrain was the largest single category of hull loss until the ground proximity warning system was mandated, after which CFIT accidents fell sharply through the 1980s. TCAS addressed a different and rarer risk and arrived later; SSR and DME are not warning systems at all.
QlIF0yiZs81d2nPxtRmN: The descent is 35 000 - 11 000 = 24 000 ft, and 100 NM at 335 kt takes 100/335 x 60 = about 17.9 minutes, so the minimum rate of descent is 24 000 / 17.9 = about 1340 ft/min. Work out the time available from the groundspeed before touching the height.
QlV6aZueHBajw5OArkvy: Category IIIA is flown with a decision height below 100 ft, or none at all, and an RVR of not less than 200 m. IIIB takes the RVR down to 75 m and IIIC removes the limitation altogether.
QlaFS1hfOSg3sjqF1aum: The oxygen dissociation curve is flat at the top, so saturation holds near 97% up to about 10,000 ft and then falls away increasingly steeply as the alveolar oxygen partial pressure drops - roughly 87% at 10,000 ft, 80% at 15,000 ft and below 65% at 20,000 ft. It is that steep part of the curve which makes altitude above 10,000 ft so much more dangerous than the figures suggest.
QlnbktrnCpLUa7Jqc9bL: The altimeter is a static instrument: an evacuated capsule expands as the pressure around it falls, and that movement drives the pointers. Pitot pressure is needed only by the airspeed indicator, which is why a blocked pitot leaves the altimeter working normally.
QmRuNP1TUunsDeVVLphK: Longitude in time is 95 20 x 4 minutes per degree = 6 h 21 min 20 s, and west longitude is SUBTRACTED from UTC to get LMT. 0000 UTC minus 6 h 21 min 20 s gives 1738:40 on the PREVIOUS day. Watch the date: subtracting past midnight always moves the date back.
