QnXHAQDY0gSPike2GcgP: Anything that impairs the circulation's ability to keep blood at head level lowers G tolerance: obesity through poor cardiovascular fitness, alcohol through dehydration and vasodilatation, and sleep deprivation through reduced cardiovascular and cerebral reserve. A reclined seating position and short stature actually improve tolerance by shortening the heart-to-brain column.
QnYGtYEzCNm8sTBBI4uR: Holding the greatest possible altitude on one engine means minimising the thrust required, and thrust required is least where DRAG is least - at the angle of attack giving the greatest lift-to-drag ratio. Any other speed needs more thrust than the remaining engine can supply for level flight, so the aeroplane will drift down further. Long-range cruise speed is faster than this and would cost height.
QoZRh3EmgkZzOrcPcn9S: Needle left means the aircraft is turning left. Ball left means it has slipped to the inside of the turn, which happens when the bank is greater than the rate of turn requires - too much bank for the turn being flown. The remedy is to reduce bank or increase the rate.
QokKpdTeaNnlPXMwaewa: Gastrointestinal upset is the commonest cause of in-flight incapacitation, so the response before departure is to assess honestly whether one is fit to fly, taking medical advice if needed (2), and to stay on the ground if there is any doubt (3). Self-medicating and flying anyway is exactly what the rules exclude, since the drug and the illness both impair.
QoyMfLijy37i9ZkP6Hmy: The requirement applies to turbine-powered aeroplanes - turboprop and jet - above defined mass and seating thresholds, because those are the aircraft flying the instrument approaches in which controlled flight into terrain occurs. Piston-engined aeroplanes are outside the scope.
QpQZqadtu9jzeixxDHll: Variation is the angle between true and magnetic north at a place, and it is read from the isogonals printed on the chart. Deviation, from the compass card, is the further correction between magnetic and compass heading; isoclinals show dip, which is not used for this.
QqhzU1bkt76RuQ3fJKgy: Only statement 2 is right: a message must be pitched so the receiver can decode it, in his language, his vocabulary and his level of experience. The others invert good practice - the verbal and non-verbal channels should agree rather than be desynchronised, the relational content matters as well as the informational, and using more channels adds redundancy and makes a message more robust, not less.
QqiQfjWV2PcYQYDOQpEC: From W002 to E008 is 10 degrees of longitude, which at 60N is 10 x 60 x cos60 = 300 NM = 555 600 m = 55 560 000 cm. Scale = 20 / 55 560 000, which is about 1 : 2 780 000. Omitting the cosine of latitude would double the earth distance and give 1 : 5 560 000, which is the trap.
QrWUdtY6GaHDH87sFR28: Static stability guarantees only the INITIAL tendency to return; what happens afterwards is a separate question. A statically stable aeroplane may converge smoothly (dynamically stable), oscillate at constant amplitude (dynamically neutral), or oscillate with growing amplitude (dynamically unstable). Static stability is a necessary but not sufficient condition for dynamic stability.
Qrc2mIVfhJk8Oz0FT8UA: Aviate before anything else, and here that means securing your own oxygen: an unconscious pilot cannot help his colleague, start a descent or call anyone. Mask on and flow confirmed first, then the emergency descent, and only then attention to the other pilot and to assistance from the cabin crew.
QriuoZjknj9qjLax7Aq9: Team spirit rests on mutual respect and a shared objective - each pilot valuing what the other brings and both working towards the same outcome. Airline rosters rarely allow crews to fly together regularly, which is precisely why standard procedures and CRM exist; shared politics and a common uniform contribute nothing.
QrkFqh7kdeZtTJwhDQN4: Dry powder is the agent for a wheel fire. CO2 and water both cool a red-hot wheel abruptly and the thermal shock can burst it; foam has the same drawback. The same logic explains why a hot wheel is approached from the front or rear and never from abeam.
QroQg2uwlaTmJjpWVtCb: A turbocharger is a turbine and a compressor on a single shaft: exhaust gas spins the turbine, and the compressor on the other end of the same shaft boosts the induction air. There is no gearing, which is why the assembly runs at very high speed and needs its own oil feed.
QtRlb7WFWnNKJtKW2wuh: The jet core sits at the tropopause break, on the warm-air side of the polar front and just beneath the higher warm-air tropopause - that is, within the WARM air mass, immediately above the sloping frontal surface. The strongest CAT is generally found on the cold (polar) side of the core and just below it, where the vertical and horizontal shear are greatest.
QtriIPYIi0ESta6PX0b6: Hysteresis is the capsule's reluctance to return exactly to its previous shape, and the longer it has been held at a given pressure the more it sets. The error therefore depends on how long the aircraft has been at that altitude, and it is largest after a long cruise followed by a change of level.
QtsFxtt1Ik24TQpjy27Y: A labyrinth seal works by making the leakage path long and tortuous rather than by contact, so a little air always passes - which is deliberate, since that flow keeps oil in the bearing chamber. Not touching means no wear and tolerance of the thermal growth and shaft movement of a running engine.
QucDWALORogoNgY2YaqH: With the static source blocked the pressure in the case is trapped at whatever it was, so the capsule stops responding and the pointers stay where they were. The altimeter therefore freezes at the reading it showed when the blockage occurred, whatever the aircraft subsequently does.
QucllHeHu0FD71T2PAt7: The decision point procedure lets an operator carry contingency fuel for only the sector from a nominated en-route DECISION POINT to the destination, rather than for the whole trip, because the decision to continue or divert is taken there. It reduces the contingency element and nothing else; holding and reserve fuel are unaffected.
Qvqn3bh10sGhpip6cNmy: The requirement is capability: the aeroplane must be certificated and fitted with approved ice protection before being planned into expected or actual icing conditions. Ground treatment removes contamination already present and does nothing for the ice met in flight, and no forecast can substitute for the equipment.
QwkTOXlXicGWEiZGwvL4: Clear ice is the most dangerous form. It comes from large supercooled drops that only partly freeze on impact and run back over the surface before solidifying, so it is dense and heavy, adheres tenaciously, distorts the aerofoil section and spreads well AFT of the protected leading edges where boots and hot air cannot reach it. Rime is lighter and brittle, and hoar frost is a thin surface deposit.
QxDEMbuJp45mxO35cAbD: A ventral fin is keel area added BELOW the fuselage and behind the CG. Behind the CG it adds directional stability, so the effect on that axis is POSITIVE. Below the CG, however, the sideforce it generates in a sideslip acts beneath the roll axis and therefore rolls the aeroplane INTO the slip - a NEGATIVE contribution to lateral stability. It is exactly this combination that makes it useful for taming Dutch roll. Pitch is unaffected.
Qxjea5SDDjTvHLawasAe: The final approach segment is where alignment and descent for landing are made. It extends from the FAF/FAP to the runway or missed approach point.
Qy3VaII4ZI3BTBD8EV0S: Distance is the integral of speed with respect to time, so with the speed already available a single integration gives the distance covered. The initial position is needed only to convert that distance into a position, and the initial speed only if you are starting from acceleration.
Qz1EeTT2FH5ecL9aTFA6: Error is combated by designing out the mechanisms that produce it (1), by training crews to recognise and manage it rather than pretending it will not happen (2), and by improving detection and recovery so that an error that does occur is caught before it causes damage (4). Sanctions are counterproductive: they suppress reporting, which removes the information the system needs to improve.
QzszIhIiAzM5gOmDCwxB: The latitude difference is 3 degrees = 180 NM, but that is only the north/south COMPONENT of the leg. On a track of 120 the meridian component is distance x cos60 = half the distance, so the distance is 180 / 0.5 = 360 NM. At 1:1 000 000 that is 360 x 1852 = 666 720 m = 66.7 cm on the chart.
R055mqnGZZZcLZw62JvD: Boots work by cracking ice off, so they need an accretion to crack - operating them too early simply forms a shell of ice over the deflated boot which subsequent cycles cannot remove. The usual guidance is to wait until roughly half an inch has built up before the first cycle.
R0yD0uo3YAPTARnLsWN2: Transport aircraft systems run at about 3,000 psi, a compromise between component weight, which falls as pressure rises, and the sealing and fatigue problems that very high pressures bring. Some recent designs use 5,000 psi for the weight saving it allows.
R1XoevP978KLa3AKt7Ud: Transport wander is a geometric effect - the gyro axis stays fixed in space while the aircraft is carried across the Earth and the local meridian turns beneath it - so it is measured against TRUE north, as a function of change of longitude and latitude. The magnetic field plays no part in gyroscopic apparent wander.
R2HgpjNFRHGnfvz2U9dn: PET distance from Q = D x H / (O + H) = 1760 x 385 / 820 = about 826 NM, and the TIME to reach it is that distance at the OUTBOUND groundspeed: 826 / 435 = 1.90 hours = about 114 minutes. The question asks for time, so do not stop at the distance.
R4YPenm79nKs7EAwugKy: Instrument runways include both non-precision approach runways and precision approach runways (CAT I, II, III). Non-instrument runways are for visual approaches only.
R4w5MBeKoyOuQ9UxwQnc: The torsion link, or scissor, connects the fixed upper part of the oleo to the sliding lower part, so the strut can telescope freely but the wheels cannot castor about the strut axis. On a steerable nose gear the steering actuator works through the same linkage.
R5KG9zCd3CvnTrajV5Wr: Holding, approach, and departure procedures are published in the ENR (En-route) section of the AIP, not in AD (Aerodromes).
R5Xb03mYR6bIyEk8EDrC: A compensated capacitance system measures mass, not volume: warming the fuel expands it but also lowers its density and its permittivity in step, so the computed mass is unchanged. That is the whole point of compensation - the same fuel weighs the same whatever its temperature.
R5a01wl4CF3S6Iph9NUy: The wind from 359 is almost exactly behind the 180 heading, so it is a near pure tailwind: the track stays at about 180 and the groundspeed rises from 198 to about 223 kt. Any option with a groundspeed at or below the TAS can be discarded at once.
R6iL7UxcyydXexIXX82T: Planned time for the first 150 NM at 240 kt is 37.5 minutes; being 2 minutes late makes it 39.5 minutes, so the actual groundspeed is 150 x 60 / 39.5 = about 228 kt. The remaining 330 NM then takes about 87 minutes, a total of about 2 h 06 from 1000, so the revised ETA is 1206.
R72pSSjqbVW2VBClvdDO: Short-term memory holds material for roughly 10-20 seconds unless it is rehearsed or transferred into long-term memory. This is why a clearance not written down or read back immediately is simply lost, and why an interruption during a checklist destroys whatever was being held at the time.
R79WKtL9ANQzP0PldwrF: Entrained by daylight, meals and social routine, the human circadian rhythm runs on the 24-hour day, governing the cycle of body temperature, hormone release, alertness and sleep. Left free-running without those cues it drifts slightly longer, which is why a westward phase delay is easier to adapt to than an eastward advance.
R7D03ju45Cpkmu1UTwtT: A diesel has no throttle butterfly (2) - air is always drawn in unrestricted and power is set purely by how much fuel is injected (3). Diesel fuel is far less volatile than petrol and correspondingly less of a fire hazard (5). Its thermal efficiency is higher, not lower, thanks to the high compression ratio.
R7gpnEGXLV7TfcOnAwud: Decompression sickness arises because tissues that were saturated with nitrogen at ground-level pressure become supersaturated when the ambient pressure falls, and the excess comes out of solution as bubbles - Henry's Law. The joint pain is the bends and affects the large joints; the chokes are chest symptoms; and the condition is serious and requires treatment, not observation.
R7ldqDyob4vy33H0msQ7: A cold front passage in the northern hemisphere always produces a VEER in the surface wind - typically from south-westerly to north-westerly - together with a sharp temperature drop, a pressure rise, and a burst of showers. The two go together: the marked temperature change and the veer identify the frontal passage. In the southern hemisphere the wind backs instead.
RC6WAkYOkwDlTLq06OTp: The pulmonary artery is the one artery carrying deoxygenated blood: it takes blood from the right ventricle to the lungs, so it is low in oxygen and rich in carbon dioxide. The pulmonary veins return the oxygenated blood to the left atrium - the mirror image of the usual arrangement.
RCy7yNSAJNAOYBgtnG0x: With nothing to focus on - clear sky, haze, darkness - the eye relaxes to its resting focus of a metre or two, so distant traffic is imaged out of focus and is not seen even though it is in the field of view. The remedy is to give the eye something real to focus on: a wingtip, a cloud edge or the horizon, at intervals through the scan.
RDBEK5xiVBMjtOZRWDKt: A tubeless tyre has no inner tube to chafe against the casing, so it runs cooler and a puncture deflates it slowly rather than bursting (3), and it seals directly against the rim, which makes the fit between tyre and wheel a closer one (4). The rim must be flawless for that seal to work.
RDUDYh7q71KjZzPcO33L: The minimum lateral separation in MNPS airspace is 60 NM, which is also the spacing of the organised tracks and the reason the navigation accuracy standard exists. 30 NM appears only as the contingency offset distance in the lost-communications procedure.
RDpyNunDclRzFW5iEjgP: Category IIIB has a decision height below 50 ft, or none at all, with an RVR below 200 m but not less than 75 m. Below 75 m only Category IIIC remains, which has no RVR limitation and requires the taxi route to be usable in the same conditions.
RDxmoFKZUY7p5PHD44U5: Climbing at constant IAS, the falling density raises the TAS for that IAS while the falling temperature lowers the local speed of sound - both effects drive the MACH NUMBER up. Checking the others: at constant IAS the TAS increases, at constant TAS the Mach number also increases, and at constant Mach the IAS decreases. This is why a climb schedule runs at constant IAS to a crossover altitude and then at constant Mach.
REofBafMjH8JvuYprl8H: Guidance functions control where the aeroplane goes: holding a selected speed or Mach number (3), holding a level (4) and tracking a VOR radial (5). Holding a pitch attitude, keeping the wings level and damping yaw are stabilisation - they control how the aeroplane sits rather than where it goes.
RFugPn0amxWjdnhDeYTV: The wind is 350 - 322 = 28 degrees off the runway centreline, from the right, so the crosswind is 20 x sin28 = about 9 kt. The drift correction is arcsin(9/95) = about 6 degrees into wind, so the heading must be about 322 + 6 = 328. Both the runway and the tower wind are magnetic, so no conversion is needed.
RG0Xbp0YJJHGPTiE2u0w: A lapse rate steeper than 1 C per 100 m exceeds even the dry adiabatic rate, so a parcel displaced upward - saturated or not - is always warmer and less dense than its surroundings and keeps accelerating. That is absolute instability. Such superadiabatic layers are shallow and short-lived, typically just above a strongly heated surface, because the convection they trigger quickly overturns and stabilises the layer.
RH8nNcXoDcX89kt7g9jr: A capacitance probe is a pair of concentric tubes forming a capacitor with the fuel and the air above it as the dielectric. Fuel has a much higher dielectric constant than air, so the capacitance rises as the tank fills - and because it responds to the fuel's dielectric properties it can be compensated to read mass.
RHIBMGNCoO6HmO21hJca: Viscosity is a fluid's internal resistance to shearing - its reluctance to flow. It falls sharply as oil warms and rises as it cools, which is why multigrade oils, oil coolers and cold weather warm-up procedures all exist.
RHPiMViOGqOTXM4HqWrX: A clogged filter would starve the bearings, which would destroy the engine within seconds, so a bypass valve opens when the differential pressure across the filter reaches a set figure. Unfiltered oil is far better than no oil, and a bypass warning tells the crew what has happened.
RHteyLypEdMV7fX07tja: Changing the subscale from QNH 1023 to the standard 1013 is a reduction of 10 hPa, and winding the subscale down winds the indication down with it - by about 10 x 27 = 270 ft. The reading therefore DECREASES. The general rule: with QNH above 1013 the flight level reads lower than the QNH altitude, and with QNH below 1013 it reads higher.
RI9C3wYYlHt02BqajM9V: With generators paralleled, a persistent imbalance is a fault in the sharing between machines rather than in one machine alone, so the protection splits the system by opening the bus tie breakers. Each generator then supplies its own bus and the healthy side is unaffected.
RIGcRcHBHx80Xo5LoVZp: Slack towline is removed by adding a little drag without changing the glider's position relative to the towplane. Yawing the nose to one side with rudder while holding the wings level with aileron produces exactly that - a controlled increase in drag that takes the slack up gradually. Pitching up or turning would change the geometry and risk a sudden snatch load when the rope comes taut.
RIbVk5f7xFa73MHLmHId: A demand regulator delivers gas only when the wearer inhales, which is what makes the supply last. The dilution function determines what is delivered - air mixed with oxygen on an altitude schedule, or pure oxygen when selected - but the flow is always demand-driven.
RIrPf7FwQ8vwIjZ6cJjk: Mach number is true airspeed divided by the local speed of sound, and the speed of sound rises as the air warms. Descending below the tropopause at a constant Mach number therefore means the true airspeed must rise with it, in proportion to the square root of the absolute temperature.
RIs7gIP7eWvzTnPmUS5u: The buffer area extends 5 NM beyond the holding area boundary. This provides protection for aircraft that may exceed the holding pattern limits.
RJLG9oLket7ejUgyoRbW: For an aeroplane certificated to operate above 25 000 ft, the crew oxygen supply must in no case be less than two hours - the time assumed for a descent and diversion after a decompression at high level. Aeroplanes certificated to 25 000 ft or below need a minimum of 30 minutes.
RJNYot350BZBfY6PevZB: ICAO Doc 4444: the MNT distance-based separation in lieu of 10 minutes longitudinal is 80 NM when the preceding aircraft maintains equal or greater Mach number.
RJWd8pGsG0vSysBEOxPT: Both are correct. A fuse works by melting a link and must be replaced once it has operated; a circuit breaker uses a thermal or magnetic trip and can be reset by hand. That is why breakers, not fuses, are used where a reset may be needed in flight.
RK8NZJJ7BJ7CRCRRwSDm: The gas and fluid sides of an accumulator are separated by a piston or diaphragm which transmits pressure but not fluid, so once the system is pressurised above the pre-charge both sides read the same. The gauge therefore shows 3,000 psi; the pre-charge appears only when the system is depressurised.
RKZCxr39nzDsq75GWd4A: Magnetic north at a place is simply the direction the HORIZONTAL component of the earth's field points there. It is not the great circle to the magnetic pole, because the field is not a neat dipole and the field lines curve, which is exactly why variation must be surveyed and charted rather than calculated.
RLe5Bwd1BZXpic9kG0wZ: Descending at a constant Mach number, the density rises rapidly, so the dynamic pressure increases and the lift coefficient needed to support the weight FALLS. A lower CL means the aeroplane is further from the angle of attack at which low-speed buffet occurs, so that margin INCREASES. The high-speed buffet margin improves too, which is why descending is the standard escape from coffin corner.
RM4S86psV6LUuH0dhTvz: The climb is flown at an indicated airspeed, and wind has no effect on the aeroplane's performance relative to the AIR - so the rate of climb, the time to height and the fuel burnt are all unchanged. What a tailwind changes is the GROUND distance covered during the climb, which increases. Wind affects the ground track, never the air-mass performance.
RM9pNTtKa6xmIZ6kx2OU: VREF is defined as 1.3 times the stalling speed in the landing configuration (1.23 VSR0 under modern rules), so the margin is 30%. That margin gives protection against gusts, turbulence and handling errors in the flare. Increments are then added for wind and gusts, typically half the steady headwind plus the full gust factor, up to a capped maximum.
RMilrnQqg2ng6YIO4pp3: A hot or direct bus is wired straight to the battery, upstream of the master switch, so it is live whenever the battery is connected. It feeds the few loads that must be available with everything else off - the clock, the entry lighting, the fire bottles.
RNsUdEUc2rwvBOsNMk8W: V1 is the take-off DECISION speed - the maximum speed at which the first stopping action must be taken to reject, and the minimum speed at which the take-off may be continued after a failure. It is deliberately distinct from VEF, the speed at which the engine actually fails, which occurs one reaction time earlier.
RPHzaosD2NPZulg2s6hd: The Operations Manual is the operator's document. The operator provides the relevant parts to its operations personnel and issues the amendments that keep them current. The Authority approves or accepts it, and the manufacturer and owner have no role.
RPYJzzAHHLxKC8FpHkGe: The induced drag coefficient is proportional to CL SQUARED divided by ASPECT RATIO (with a span efficiency factor and pi as the constants). Two consequences follow: induced drag rises very steeply as speed falls and CL climbs, and a long slender wing suffers far less of it than a short stubby one - which is why aspect ratio is the primary design lever for efficiency.
RPhZl2N8r3gDjf7X964o: An active warm front brings extensive nimbostratus with a low, ragged base and continuous rain, and the rain falling into the cold air ahead raises its humidity to saturation, giving mist, drizzle and often frontal fog. The result at low level is a low cloud base with poor visibility - the classic marginal-VFR trap. Thunderstorms and severe turbulence belong to the cold front, whose slope is far steeper.
RQJyEOqo24FMQB2gOrk2: The pulse must travel out 50 km and back, i.e. 100 km, at 300 000 km/s, which takes 333 microseconds. The next pulse cannot go until then, so the PRF is 1 / 0.000333 = about 3000 pulses per second. A higher PRF would fold distant returns back into the display as second-trace echoes.
RQjNfZoTm2x9p8xZJque: In the SHELL model S is Software: the non-physical parts of the system - checklists, manuals, standard operating procedures, symbology and computer logic. H is Hardware, E is Environment and L is Liveware, the human at the centre and the other people around him.
RQyEPwTVZzpelq3x7euh: Murphy's Law, in its human-factors form, says that if equipment can be operated wrongly then sooner or later it will be. It is the argument for designing errors out - incompatible connectors, controls that cannot be confused, defaults that fail safe - rather than relying on training and care to prevent them.
RRFr5wzNL7nDXt3R8dIJ: FIS collision hazard information is provided in airspace classes C through G. In Classes A and B, ATC provides full separation service so FIS collision info is implicit.
RSIojMrNCnA3LNIPHBXF: Both are correct. The laminate is much more brittle when cold, so with the window heat inoperative a lower speed limit applies to keep bird strike energy within what the cold window can absorb. And side windows are usually only demisted, with full anti-icing confined to the windscreens.
RStQvodvqTKmspotjqi2: A forward CG requires a larger tailplane DOWNLOAD, so the wing must generate the weight plus that download. More lift means a higher stalling speed, and it also means more induced drag - so for a given power setting the cruising speed FALLS. This is why an aft CG (within limits) gives the best cruise performance and the lowest stall speed, and a forward CG the most stability.
RTYyO4fPvqEUYAwUjMZY: Both conditions must be met. The water must be deep enough to flood the tread - at least the groove depth, since half-filled grooves still drain - and the speed must exceed 9 times the square root of the tyre pressure in psi. 10 bar is about 145 psi, and 9 x 12 gives roughly 108 kt, so the 104 kt figure is the one in range.
RUSYG3BCW9tSxxoxJvy7: A tubeless tyre seals against the rim itself, so the wheel must be of the solid or split type with a flawless sealing surface (1). Its advantages are that a puncture deflates it slowly instead of bursting (5) and that there is no tube to chafe against the casing, so it runs cooler (6).
RUxEGHwGnmQlQfANaLxH: A chemical generator is light and compact for the oxygen it yields (1), needs no pressure vessel so there is nothing to explode (4), and sits in its stowage for years needing nothing done to it until its replacement date (2 and 6). Its drawbacks are that once fired it runs for a fixed period at a fixed rate and cannot be stopped.
RVimcPkWqqu174xuiTbl: Maximum drift occurs with the wind at 90 degrees to the HEADING, not to the track, and its size is arcsin(wind/TAS) = arcsin(30/120) = about 14.5 degrees. With a course of 040 and the wind from the right, the heading is 040 + 14.5 = 054.5, so the wind must come from 054.5 + 90 = about 145 degrees.
RVtuu18gGx3lXPXrommI: ICAO Annex 17: after an unlawful interference landing, notification goes to: State of registry, State of operator, States of citizens who were fatalities/injured/hostages/on board, and ICAO.
RWwCjozDtTlHNdynSKFV: The CVR runs from before the aeroplane moves under its own power until it can no longer do so - the whole of taxi out, flight and taxi in. Starting it at thrust application or stopping it at brakes set would omit exactly the periods in which taxiway and ramp events occur.
RX8jcxg23xXVV7CEUB7n: On the 240 radial the aircraft is 240 degrees FROM the station, so the station bears 060(M) from the aircraft. Relative bearing = magnetic bearing to the station minus magnetic heading = 060 - 360 = 060. The ADF needle therefore points 060 degrees to the right of the nose.
RY9wWQSLYtppraT8RnBF: The stall is a matter of angle of attack, and the angle at which it occurs depends on the configuration - so the computer needs the measured angle of attack together with the flap and slat positions. Thrust parameters and spoiler position are not inputs.
RYy1BdRtX2OgP88RpRza: The two groups have different needs, so they have separate systems: gaseous oxygen with demand regulators for the crew, who must be able to don masks instantly, use them repeatedly and talk through them, and a simple continuous-flow system, often chemical, for the passengers.
RZjmmr36Q7FFJLOtrHcm: The flight management computer blends the position sources available to it: GPS (1), the inertial reference systems as the smooth continuous reference (2), and radio fixing from DME and VOR (3). ACARS is a communications link and contributes nothing to navigation.
RaEZULrNkCTywMsAb1hd: An inverter converts DC into AC, which is what a DC-primary aeroplane needs to run AC instruments such as gyros and synchros. A transformer rectifier unit does the opposite, producing DC from AC on an AC-primary aeroplane.
RasKCb9MPyAkfolGolT1: ATS must be informed when average TAS varies by plus or minus 5% from the flight plan value. Track deviations and time errors have separate notification triggers.
Rau0HHIh1zaMFgFDahLT: JAR-FCL: IR(A) applicants need 50 hours cross-country time as PIC in aeroplanes or helicopters, of which at least 10 hours in aeroplanes.
RbD62mtEk7qdPShH437E: Physical stress is a disturbance of the body's homeostatic mechanisms by external conditions - heat, cold, noise, vibration, acceleration, hypoxia. It is distinguished from psychological stress, which arises when the perceived demand exceeds the perceived ability to meet it, and from mental overload, which is a limit on information processing.
Rblv92eKLZQZAmMYAscI: The geostrophic wind is defined as the balance of exactly two forces: the pressure gradient force and the Coriolis force. That balance is only possible with straight isobars and no friction, and it gives a wind blowing parallel to the isobars. Adding the centrifugal force, for curved isobars, gives the gradient wind; adding friction gives the surface wind.
RbuSlEN4Z8G5jR0FpCp5: Time of useful consciousness at 30,000 ft is of the order of a minute or two breathing air, and a rapid decompression roughly halves it because gas is driven out of the lungs and alveolar oxygen pressure collapses immediately. A minute or less leaves time for one action only: mask on, then the emergency descent.
Rcd8hdNmJCGlSsxTNHAo: ECAM presents a failure three ways at once: an aural attention-getter (1), the affected system's controls lit on the overhead panel (2), and the relevant synoptic with the drill on the system display (3). What it does not do is act on the failure - the crew carry out the actions.
RdeKyRPzpOtCiHHb23Ja: Safe life design uses a single load path (2) and retires the part at a life established by test with a large scatter factor, whether or not anything has been found wrong with it (3). Redundancy and multiple load paths are the fail-safe philosophy, which is the alternative approach.
Re6AA8tHLgDAFWoZ7un1: Anxiety affects all four. Attention narrows and becomes selective, concentration cannot be held, retrieval from memory becomes unreliable, and prudence goes - risks are either not seen or accepted too readily. This broad cognitive impact is why an uneasy crew member is a flight-safety matter and not merely uncomfortable.
ReXhqIK6Rcq6kKGFnaNg: Confirmation bias is the tendency to look for evidence that supports the hypothesis already held. The only reliable defence is to invert the search deliberately: ask what would prove the hypothesis wrong and go looking for that. Simply gathering more supporting evidence, however carefully, reinforces the bias rather than testing it.
RfnVU6rdKUi7opv9ra4N: The north and south legs cancel exactly, but the east and west legs do not. Going 600 NM east at 06S needs 600 / cos6 = 603 minutes of longitude, while coming 600 NM west at 04N needs 600 / cos4 = 602 minutes. The two differ by about 2 minutes of longitude, so the aircraft finishes about 2 minutes EAST of where it started, at 029 58 W.
Rg9zkL1Tj4aueOiQ2mtV: The computer compares the speed of the braked wheel with a reference free-rolling speed (1 and 2) and modulates brake pressure to hold the difference at the slip ratio that gives maximum friction (4). Brake temperature and tyre pressure play no part in the control loop.
RgfS6bxPWBZyswp0AvmE: Retrieval from long-term memory takes time and depends on the right cues, so knowledge which will shortly be needed is deliberately brought forward in advance - the approach briefing, the mental review of the go-around, the run-through of the drill before descent. Pre-activated material is then available immediately when there is no time to search for it.
RgyQNW1OgI9wMYUDIfDv: A brushless machine has no slip rings, so the initial field must come from somewhere self-contained: a small permanent magnet generator on the same shaft supplies the exciter, which feeds the rotating rectifier and hence the main field. That is why a brushless generator can build up its own output from nothing.
RhxwexSzqoWGn1LPTsb6: Aircraft AC systems run at 400 Hz because the higher frequency allows transformers and motors to be made much smaller and lighter for the same power than at 50 or 60 Hz. The penalty is greater line reactance, acceptable over the short distances involved.
RhzOhd6dbwGHD3pOgtYb: The heart muscle cannot take oxygen from the blood passing through its chambers; it is fed by the coronary arteries, which leave the aorta immediately above the aortic valve. Narrowing of those arteries produces angina on exertion, and complete blockage of a branch produces a myocardial infarction.
RipsbUUQL8KGC7QOP7ZI: An isolated aerodrome has no alternate, so additional fuel replaces alternate fuel: for a turbine-engined aeroplane, two hours at normal cruise consumption computed after arrival overhead the destination, and that quantity includes the final reserve. The 30-minute figure is the final reserve alone, and it is 30 minutes of HOLDING at 1500 ft, not of cruise consumption.
Riy3sb5TyMdqdTAXXErP: The slide inflates automatically when the armed door is opened, but if that fails the manual inflation handle fires the gas cylinder directly. It is the backup for the automatic system, and its location is part of the door drill.
Rjqc1n5PwD6EbKcVem32: Drift down is the procedure for exactly this case: an engine failure at a cruise level above the one-engine-inoperative maximum altitude, where the aeroplane can no longer hold height. It descends at the speed for the best gradient on maximum continuous thrust until it reaches the level-off altitude, and the net flight path during that descent must clear the terrain.
Rk3NreGyiFpQzUMcc4gL: For a jet, thrust available is roughly constant with speed, so the maximum EXCESS thrust - and hence the best climb angle VX - occurs at VMD, which is also the maximum endurance speed. Maximum range lies higher, at about 1.32 x VMD, and long range cruise is faster still. So Vs, then VX, then maximum range speed is the correct ascending order.
RkZmg8WzRAAyYJJcL5iq: A swept wing generates a spanwise flow toward the tips, which thickens the outboard boundary layer and makes the tips stall first - producing a pitch-up and a loss of aileron authority. A boundary layer fence is a chordwise plate that physically blocks that spanwise drift. It is therefore a LOW-SPEED fix, addressing stall behaviour rather than compressibility, and it does not change Mcrit.
Rkjrd0kf6187gDRXg8Ut: The transition level is not published on charts but is calculated based on current QNH and passed to aircraft by ATS units. It varies with atmospheric pressure.
Rl5PcTXMZihLFhEuqxkj: Equivalent airspeed is calibrated airspeed with the compressibility correction applied, allowing for the fact that the air is compressed at the pitot head rather than merely brought to rest. Density is the remaining correction, converting EAS to true airspeed.
RlLPK8ri20wGOZURcxTA: Torque direction depends on the relative direction of the field and the armature current, so reversing BOTH would leave the rotation unchanged. Reversing one of them - the field connections or the armature connections, but not both - is what reverses the direction of rotation.
Rls3d3EqFy7JwwxY3Jl0: Frequency equals the number of pole pairs multiplied by the speed in revolutions per second, so it is fixed by the machine's construction and its rotational speed. That is why holding 400 Hz means holding the generator's speed constant, which is the constant speed drive's job.
Rmp3LMCJStflAiynuhab: Once a chemical generator is fired it runs at a fixed rate for a fixed period and cannot be turned down (1) or turned off (3), and that fixed duration is short - typically 12 to 22 minutes, enough only for an emergency descent (5). Its compensating advantages are low weight and negligible maintenance.
RmxKNSiU4lK4nQtB9Am8: Stress arises from appraisal: the individual weighs what he believes the situation demands against what he believes he can do about it, and it is that subjective judgement, not any objective property of the event, which determines whether stress occurs. The same approach in the same weather stresses one pilot and not another.
RnXJEzSthSAqA5cC4DnI: Relative bearing is measured from the aircraft's nose, so it is the difference between the bearing the pointer indicates and the heading the card is showing: 225 - 090 = 135°. A frozen card does not prevent the reading, it merely means the indication must be interpreted rather than read directly.
Rou0iD5QevLdWFkX7XPz: Moving the head - particularly out of the plane of rotation - while the aircraft is turning stimulates a second set of semicircular canals and produces the powerful Coriolis illusion. The defence is to keep the head still during turns and while the fluid in the canals is still settling. Breathing technique addresses hyperventilation, not vertigo.
RpUXrR9MSQcRiODh8tPr: The Rescue Coordination Centre (RCC) is responsible for promoting efficient organisation of SAR service within each SAR region. ACCs and FICs initiate alert phases but the RCC coordinates the actual SAR operation.
RpYNxgMBDcaTQAMHXLg2: Stress is the pressure or demand acting on the individual's physical or mental systems together with the response it produces - both halves matter, since the same demand affects two people differently. Defining it as invariably harmful or as invariably pleasant misses the inverted-U: moderate stress improves performance and only excess degrades it.
RpnF63SY8XdESugB7KkF: In the braking or reverse range the blade angle is taken below fine, so the propeller pushes air forward and produces negative thrust - and it takes engine power to drive it in that condition. Feathering is the opposite: no thrust and no power absorbed, the blades edge-on to the flow.
Rq778zvkbzb2xBxcssXI: The complete CAT I (Calvert) approach light system has 5 crossbars with centreline light units of 3, 2, and 1 lamp per unit progressing towards the runway threshold.
RqIVWV0QYDpoMFy53MLl: Stress does not require a present danger. Imagining or anticipating a situation produces the same physiological response as the situation itself (3), and a new situation resembling a previous stressful one triggers the reaction learned from the earlier event (4). This is why anticipatory worry is as costly as the event and why a bad experience colours later ones.
RqPJYAML9BeW7wmXV6nS: A small error in the gyros tilts the accelerometer frame, so a component of gravity is integrated as if it were acceleration, and the resulting position error grows steadily with time. That is why unaided inertial accuracy is quoted as an error per hour, and why radio or GPS updating is used.
RqQEmJo4MeMDyn3uYKC7: For a non-precision approach with no outer marker there is still a definite commit point: the approach may not be continued below 1000 ft above the aerodrome on the final approach segment when the reported RVR or visibility is below minima. It is the same principle as the ILS rule, expressed as a height rather than a fix.
Rqg5Mdyjdi9h132CBHrb: Decode carefully. 25020G38KT is a mean wind of 20 kt from 250 with gusts to 38 - the 38 is a gust, not the top of a mean range. +TSGR is a thunderstorm with HEAVY hail, not moderate. 23/18 is temperature 23 C and dewpoint 18 C. So the only fully correct reading is gusts to 38 kt, thunderstorm with heavy hail, dewpoint 18 C.
RrfokvZOVWahEV5G0arz: Vapour lock is fuel boiling in the line: heat, low pressure or a volatile fuel produces a bubble that the pump cannot shift, and the flow to the engine is interrupted. It is a hot-day, high-altitude problem, which is why boost pumps are run for take-off, climb and in hot conditions.
RsA3VGsEbhacC0Db4yaq: On the ground the aeroplane yaws without banking, so the needle shows the yaw to the left while the ball, thrown outwards by the turn, moves to the right. The result is a fully deflected needle with the ball out - normal on the ground.
RsRQbP3p8ra2F1E9fRla: With 250 selected and the aircraft on the 240 radial, the difference is only 10 degrees, so the flag reads FROM. Being on the 240 radial puts the aircraft LEFT of the 250 course, which means the course line lies in the 340 direction from the aircraft - and with the aircraft heading 160, that is directly BEHIND it. So the deviation bar sits behind the aeroplane symbol with the FROM flag showing.
RsifGVtfWgF7panH9052: Pressure altitude is by definition the altitude indicated with 1013.25 set, so if the subscale is at 1013.25 and the needle reads 15,000 ft, the pressure altitude is 15,000 ft. Temperature affects the true altitude and the density altitude, not the pressure altitude.
RtqRLgxyjwyDKIDCsSox: A VFR flight constitutes essential traffic to other VFR flights in Class B airspace only. In Classes C and D, VFR flights receive traffic information rather than essential traffic status.
RtuYOLNGZ0mT6Mfx2SSv: Losing 15 000 ft at 3000 ft/min takes 5 minutes, and with no wind the aircraft covers 320 x 5/60 = about 26.7 NM in that time. Find the time from the height and the rate, then the distance from the groundspeed.
Ru1oP1gFL1p6jRYtTSRj: Carburettor ice forms where the pressure and temperature drop most sharply: at the venturi throat, where the air accelerates, and at the partly closed throttle butterfly, where it accelerates again and where the fuel is evaporating. The combined cooling can be 20°C or more, which is why ice forms in air well above freezing.
RuJyIhCxiY4s7PZxTBKt: The simple model has two inputs, both perceived rather than objective: the demand the task appears to make, and the ability the individual believes he has to meet it. Stress arises when the first exceeds the second. It follows that stress is reduced either by reducing the demand or by increasing competence and confidence.
RuWBStjEmjJDjMCTRG9K: The APU drives its own generator, so it replaces the ground power unit, and it supplies bleed air, which replaces both the air start cart and the ground air conditioning unit. That self-sufficiency is what allows an aircraft to turn round at an airfield with no equipment at all.
RvJ95NqnnYUDwD6UNWbE: RVSM in the NAT applies between FL290 and FL410 inclusive, where approved aircraft are separated by 1000 ft instead of 2000 ft. Above FL410 the 2000 ft minimum returns, which is why the contingency offset changes at that boundary.
RvRBLyVInKuXKoBKCAGm: The retina, and the rods in particular, are among the most oxygen-hungry tissues in the body, so night vision is the first function to degrade - measurably from about 5,000 ft, well below the altitude at which anything else is affected. This is why supplemental oxygen is recommended for night flying at altitudes that would otherwise not require it.
RvY98676VpjbfkYOTDyh: The dangerous goods transport document is the shipper's: the shipper classifies, packs, marks, labels and declares the consignment and signs to certify it. The operator checks it on acceptance and the commander is notified of what is aboard, but neither draws it up.
Rw1O08YrTzJM9qcYPrTE: Spanwise flow toward the tips thickens the outboard boundary layer on a swept-back wing, so the TIPS stall first. Because the tips sit well aft of the CG on a swept planform, losing their lift moves the centre of pressure FORWARD, producing a nose-up pitching moment that drives the angle of attack higher still - a self-worsening divergence. Fences, vortex generators and washout are the remedies.
Rwl5kjh8aVRQMXiloNkO: Aphelion, the furthest point at about 152 million km, falls in early July, and perihelion at about 147 million km in early January. It is worth fixing because it runs counter to northern hemisphere intuition: the earth is furthest from the sun during the northern summer.
RxZuh0xqSiNy068AYwEX: Deploying trailing-edge flap adds lift at the REAR of the section, so the centre of pressure moves AFT. Note what does not change: in steady level flight at constant IAS the lift must still equal the weight and the dynamic pressure is fixed, so the lift COEFFICIENT is unchanged - only CLmax and the drag increase. And the stall speed FALLS, since CLmax has risen.
RxyTObvtRx9UMRO0ZkUx: The radio altimeter transmits a continuously frequency-modulated signal and compares the frequency of the returning echo with the frequency being transmitted at that instant. The difference is proportional to the round-trip time and therefore to height, which gives the precision the flare requires.
Ry4NEheIE7eaAThzE3JB: The noise abatement take-off procedure specified for any one aeroplane TYPE must be the same at every aerodrome. Standardising by type keeps the departure a memorised drill; varying it by aerodrome would make a routine departure a source of error.
RyM0eW9tQBoIONuyE9Lf: 7500 signals unlawful interference, i.e. hijack. Learn the trio together: 7500 unlawful interference, 7600 radio communication failure, 7700 general emergency. 7000 is the European VFR conspicuity code.
RyXQ0Ncdi4ev9ANIvxLb: The green light means the leg is down and the downlock is engaged - that and nothing more. Door position is indicated separately where it matters, and a light showing merely that the gear is in the selected position would be useless, since it is the lock that carries the landing loads.
RyelyxmVqzEdbK6fGW3q: Track 207 against heading 206 is just 1 degree of right drift, and the groundspeed is 5 kt below the TAS, so the wind is a light headwind almost straight down the nose. Resolving the vectors gives a wind from about 180 degrees at 5 kt.
RzTihk7pCFq2aNpFsaFb: ICAO Doc 8168: a 5-degree flexibility zone exists on each side of holding entry sector boundaries. The pilot may use either adjacent entry procedure within this zone.
S0Z2d8bCtpYhAQwIH3qP: Moment is force multiplied by arm, so rearranging gives arm equals moment divided by force. In mass and balance the same relationship is used with mass in place of force: the centre of gravity position is the total moment divided by the total mass.
S0o5eI935UubeKlEnE7i: At a positive angle of attack the flow must travel further and faster over the more curved UPPER surface, so that is where the highest velocities - and therefore, by Bernoulli, the lowest static pressures - occur. The resulting suction over the upper surface accounts for most of the lift, typically around two thirds of it. At the stagnation point the velocity is zero, the exact opposite.
S1LVEMJrJSrXO6c9aCCd: Homing means continually turning to keep the needle on the nose, so the aircraft is dragged downwind and must keep turning INTO the wind to stay pointed at the beacon. A steadily DECREASING heading therefore means the aircraft is being blown to the right, i.e. it is experiencing right drift. Homing always produces this curved track, which is why tracking is preferred.
S1zqsr0uo2t0sokL5v3a: Ice pellets (PL) are frozen raindrops. They form where snow melts in a warm layer aloft and the resulting raindrops then freeze completely while falling through a deep sub-zero layer beneath. That is exactly the profile that gives FREEZING RAIN where the cold layer is shallower - so ice pellets at the surface are a direct warning that supercooled rain, and severe icing, exist at a higher level.
S2CkZWSRQZiZ4zBXZwSD: VNO is the maximum structural cruising speed - the top of the green arc. Above it, in the yellow caution range, the aeroplane may be flown only in smooth air and with care, because a gust could impose a load beyond the design case. VNE, the red line, must never be exceeded.
S3fzckxcT5fv97TSaSnc: The Valsalva manoeuvre - mouth closed, nose pinched, gentle blowing - raises the pressure in the nasopharynx and forces the Eustachian tube open, letting air into the middle ear to equalise it. Swallowing, yawning and jaw movement do the same more gently. Increasing the descent rate makes matters worse, and the real answer for a heavy cold is not to fly.
S3ns6OqMLQn7fjuIECLu: The system compares the measured angle of attack (1) against the stalling angle for the current configuration, so it needs the flap and slat position (5), and a computer (2) to make the comparison and drive the stick shaker. Airspeed is not used, because a wing stalls at an angle rather than at a speed.
S4MrGc3czHy1GetuvlSQ: Induced drag coefficient is proportional to CL SQUARED, so it climbs steeply as lift coefficient rises - which is why induced drag dominates at low speed and high angle of attack. It also varies inversely with aspect ratio, so a HIGHER aspect ratio reduces it, and it grows with stronger tip vortices rather than weaker ones.
S4jYqxDtbJSJWYSEZwpo: Resolving letters and numbers demands the fine sampling that only the densely packed cones of the fovea provide, over about one degree of the visual field. Outside it the retina is far too coarsely sampled to resolve characters, which is why the eye must be pointed directly at text and why peripheral vision detects movement but cannot read.
S4ydCg2EEVGMvZ1H88O4: The erection system uses a pendulous device to find the vertical, and an acceleration displaces that pendulum exactly as a pitch change would. The erector therefore drives the gyro towards a false vertical and the horizon shows a nose-up attitude which is not there - which is why the attitude indicator is treated with caution during the take-off run.
S5kpETwtFIHVohqFzBAy: Above a cabin pressure altitude of 13 000 ft in an unpressurised aeroplane, everyone on board - crew and 100% of passengers - must be supplied for the entire flight time. Below that, in the 10 000-13 000 ft band, only the flight deck occupants and 10% of the passengers (after 30 minutes) are covered.
S5uU8bJj7IJ4MOmmz3wv: The strainer must catch debris before it can reach anything that can be blocked or damaged, so it sits at the carburettor inlet, upstream of the needle valve that admits fuel to the float chamber. Downstream of that point the passages are small and a particle would already have done its harm.
S6MMdxllgFNqB3yTKaBX: Deviation is the error caused by the aircraft's own magnetism, and what remains after a compass swing is recorded on the deviation card for each heading. Applying it to magnetic heading gives compass heading; variation, from the chart's isogonals, converts between true and magnetic.
S6sRkd8h6k7s6Y0DOc90: CAS has already had the instrument and position errors removed, so the only correction left before EAS is compressibility - which allows for the air being compressed at the pitot head. Density is the further correction that converts EAS to true airspeed.
S7CpdNqlXIX2CUFNbcHL: ASHTAM is a special NOTAM series for volcanic activity, eruptions, or ash clouds. It uses a specific format to notify significant operational changes due to volcanic hazards.
S7GbJnjFkAU3OLe4SUeK: Earth distance = chart length x scale denominator = 4.2 cm x 1 600 000 = 6 720 000 cm = 67 200 m, which is 67 200 / 1852 = about 36.3 NM. The 67.20 option is that same figure in kilometres, mislabelled as nautical miles.
S8gSuvaPHf4vh8vCsNJn: Apply the 1-in-60 rule: 1 degree subtends 1 NM at 60 NM, so at 200 NM it subtends 200/60 = 3.3 NM, and exactly 200 x tan1 = 3.5 NM. The DME's own error is far smaller, so at long range the bearing is the weak part of a VOR/DME fix - which is why DME/DME is preferred where the geometry allows.
S90upLhNcoRcgKtVlkId: Reduced thrust may be used only when the aeroplane has performance to spare, which means a light aircraft (2) in dense air - a low temperature (4) and a high pressure (5). Under those conditions the actual take-off mass is well below the limiting mass and the surplus can be traded for engine life.
S9OcOcOegJryVMcLHLwL: Item 15 speed is written as a letter for the units followed by four digits: N for knots, K for kilometres per hour and M for Mach. So 470 kt is N0470, with the leading zero that keeps the field four digits wide.
S9vJYYYeCTZtgxVJLIjT: Proprioception reports the resultant of gravity and acceleration and cannot distinguish one from the other, so with no outside visual reference to resolve the ambiguity it produces confidently wrong information about attitude. No training makes it reliable in IMC; it is useful for motor coordination, but for orientation it must be disregarded in favour of the instruments.
SAJwHNOOXEtU7lCKHqHm: Descend to the lowest safe level - reducing the pressure difference stops the bubbles growing - and land as soon as possible so the casualty can be assessed and, if necessary, recompressed. Oxygen helps by washing nitrogen out, but the symptoms may not resolve and can recur or worsen after landing, so continuing the flight is not an option.
SAOIRhKSBzGf1g28YFSh: Barotrauma of the middle ear is mechanical damage caused by a pressure difference across the eardrum when the Eustachian tube cannot equalise - typically on descent, and much more likely with a cold. There is no infection involved initially, although a damaged, fluid-filled middle ear may become infected afterwards.
SBB0zXsxuus0nABjBZlG: Directly over the station the VOR signal is unusable and the deviation swings wildly, so the roll channel drops the radial and holds the heading it had until the aircraft emerges on the far side and the signal is valid again. Without that the autopilot would chase the noise.
SBtmhPWgqg3XcXSGakUj: Where the sill of a passenger emergency exit is more than 1.83 m - six feet - above the ground with the gear collapsed, a slide or equivalent means of descent must be provided, because an unassisted jump from that height would injure a significant proportion of the occupants.
SBxEZH7ppOUWKgnMAoE7: Dynamic hydroplaning needs enough water for the tyre to build a wedge of fluid pressure under the contact patch, so the depth of standing water decides whether it can occur at all. Tyre pressure then fixes the speed at which it starts; aircraft mass and wind have essentially no effect.
SCD5DVvP7ZyUz9VJaMxp: Static stability describes the INITIAL tendency after a disturbance; dynamic stability describes what happens over time. If the aeroplane does not even begin to return toward its original condition, there is nothing for the subsequent motion to converge upon - so a statically unstable aeroplane can NEVER be dynamically stable. Static stability is a necessary, though not sufficient, condition for dynamic stability.
SCfFvXCZ84gyWp9rxfNx: Noise abatement procedures for landing exist, but ICAO is explicit that they must not deny the crew the deceleration devices that keep the landing safe - the use of reverse thrust is not prohibited. Arrival noise relief comes from continuous descent, later configuration changes and preferred routings.
SDTr3rgrrjPgmRR3ty2k: Vapour lock is fuel boiling in the line: heat, low pressure or a volatile fuel produces bubbles that the pump cannot shift, and the flow to the engine is interrupted. It has nothing to do with water, exhaust gas or carburettor heat.
SEPQF6cCIXb9U9BMrh6g: On a polar stereographic chart the convergence between the local meridian and the grid datum meridian is the full change of longitude. The starting point is 10E and the grid is aligned with Greenwich, so the correction is 10 degrees: a true course of 305 becomes a grid course of 295.
SEeiF4vgXZKWHH5eyUOf: Breathing 100% oxygen removes nitrogen from the alveolar gas, so alveolar oxygen pressure is ambient less water vapour and carbon dioxide. That holds oxygenation adequate to roughly 38-40,000 ft, where hypoxia symptoms reappear; above it, positive-pressure breathing is required.
SFB8z3ZgY2iE9a2t96Go: Body mass index is mass in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. Below about 18.5 is underweight, 18.5 to 25 normal, above 25 overweight and above 30 obese. Obesity matters aeromedically because it carries cardiovascular risk, reduces G tolerance and complicates escape from an aircraft.
SFc8VpmKxCrmX3EwjPuO: Halon interrupts the chemical chain reaction, so it works on solids, flammable liquids and gases, and is safe on live electrical equipment because it does not conduct. Burning metals are the exception - they sustain their own oxidation and need a class D agent.
SGdTNOiirFGLKe2EsKKm: ICAO Annex 2: VFR flights in a CTR require clearance when ceiling is less than 1500 ft or visibility less than 5 km. Special VFR may be obtained under these conditions.
SHN9oWy8kdFCHozkZHne: Moderate turbulence gives definite changes in altitude and attitude, and occupants feel a positive strain against their seat belts, but the aircraft remains under positive control throughout and indicated airspeed varies. Severe turbulence brings large abrupt changes with the aircraft momentarily out of control, and extreme turbulence can cause structural damage. Light turbulence is the rhythmic bumpiness with no appreciable attitude change.
SHcd8mnJta6ZBSQXasCt: Dry air is about 21% oxygen and 78% nitrogen by volume, with the remaining 1% made up of argon and traces of other gases including carbon dioxide. The proportions stay constant to about 80 km, so it is the falling total pressure, not any change in composition, that causes altitude hypoxia.
SHnuqSqPShBUwXLG7PnR: Noise-induced hearing loss is destruction of the hair cells on the basilar membrane inside the cochlea; those cells do not regenerate, so the loss is permanent, painless and cumulative, typically notched around 4 kHz. Eardrum pressure differences, a blocked Eustachian tube and stiffened ossicles produce conductive loss, which is a different and often reversible mechanism.
SIg64zZd9V1tFTUS8dTQ: Acceleration errors appear on east and west headings, where the pendulous magnet system is displaced by the fore-and-aft force. In the northern hemisphere acceleration produces an apparent turn to the north and deceleration one to the south - the mnemonic ANDS.
SJb3tDouwM4et7rqpAnp: ILS glide path interception typically occurs at heights between 300 m (984 ft) and 900 m (2955 ft) above runway elevation, at the final approach point.
SK09581kSyTQMspXNXB6: The significant weather chart (SIGWX) is the flight-planning chart for en-route hazards: it depicts areas of moderate or severe icing and turbulence, CB and thunderstorm areas, jet stream cores, tropopause heights, fronts, and the height of the 0 C isotherm (freezing level). Constant-pressure charts give wind and temperature at a single level, and the surface chart gives the pressure pattern and fronts.
SKRFm8v3jaAe2dtdySKf: Central vision is cone vision: it resolves fine detail, colour and movement (2), and the fovea packs roughly 150,000 cones per square millimetre to achieve that resolution (4). Statement 1 is wrong because the rods lie outside the fovea and serve peripheral and night vision, and statement 3 is wrong because central vision fails in the dark - which is why a faint object at night must be viewed off-centre.
SKtLbqT3Ei4QP4h3tqjn: DME is UHF and therefore line of sight. At FL210 the theoretical range is 1.23 x root(21 000) = about 178 NM, so a station 220 NM away is simply over the horizon. Circling near a station causes a brief unlock overhead, not a loss at 220 NM, and DME range is not capped at 200 NM: from higher levels it exceeds that.
SLhTr4fCeYBq53K65PX5: Work outward from grid to compass. At 180W on a chart gridded to Greenwich the convergence is 180 degrees, so a grid heading of 045 is a true heading of 225. Variation 10E gives a magnetic heading of 215. The compass reads 220, and deviation is magnetic minus compass: 215 - 220 = -5 degrees.
SM3kxGNEfGo0T1bxVlXX: Glide distance through the AIR is set entirely by the lift-to-drag ratio, which is a function of angle of attack and configuration. Converting that to distance over the GROUND then requires the wind. Mass does not enter at all - a heavier aeroplane flies the same glide angle, just faster - and CLmax governs the stall, not the glide.
SMGpnyn8yqUAyYi48msj: Bypass ratio is cold flow divided by core flow. With 220 kg/s entering and 20 kg/s through the core, 200 kg/s bypasses it, giving 200/20 = 10:1.
SNk5JAP6pozRkYNYFnRE: Each inertial system navigates on its own accelerometers and gyros, so each accumulates its own independent error and drifts at its own rate. Three positions from three sets of sensors will always differ slightly, with no malfunction and no input error required.
SNrdeNnvgFwEo5LHCmpv: The pump is where the energy goes in, so it is where a fault first shows as heat - a failing pump, or one running against a blocked or closed system, will overheat long before anything else does. Overheat detectors are therefore fitted at the pumps and their outlets.
SNwgTGcgyzLTFMc84Sny: A cold swells the linings of the Eustachian tube and the sinus openings, so neither the middle ear nor the sinuses can equalise. The result is severe ear pain on descent (2), sinus pain (4) and, if one ear clears and the other does not, alternobaric vertigo (3). Flatulence is caused by expanding gut gas and has nothing to do with the cold.
SOD9sztpPltcgX2vULIC: VASIS (Visual Approach Slope Indicator System) has 4 light units per wing bar. The system typically uses two wing bars.
SPWdMDY5NvPGQLlbgHmt: The distributor takes the single high voltage output of the magneto's secondary winding and routes it, in firing order, to each plug in turn through the rotor arm and the segments in the cap. The primary circuit stays inside the magneto and never reaches the plugs.
SQ5v7Vrb7qDxUjdFJkNT: ICAO Doc 4444: minimum radar separation between aircraft on the same localizer course is 3 NM, plus additional separation for wake turbulence as required.
SQxj0DtvbVJ6mkZkIEok: For aeroplanes certificated before 1 April 1998 the CVR must retain the last 30 minutes. Aeroplanes certificated on or after that date require two hours, and 25 hours is the flight data recorder figure.
SS9b7hPMVSGA7LgVDQmX: A long checklist is broken into logical sections so each can be completed without interruption (1); the order follows the panel scan so the eye and hand move naturally and nothing is skipped (4); and critical items are given redundancy - a challenge and response, or a later confirmation (5). Critical items go at the beginning, where attention is highest, not the middle, and a checklist must never be lumped in with other tasks.
SSOW7ZXVWVN8jNW8NJVj: The low-range radio altimeter works around 4.3 GHz, which lies in the super high frequency band, 3 to 30 GHz. That frequency gives a small aerial and the resolution needed to measure a few feet of height in the flare.
SScvfhMQC5KuzOnXqehH: VHF range is line of sight: range in NM = 1.23 x (root of aircraft height + root of station height) in feet. With the station at sea level that is 1.23 x root(23 000) = 1.23 x 152 = about 187 NM, so about 190. Note the 151 NM option is the square root left un-multiplied by 1.23.
ST5v71RgG1NhmTBZHGMP: Tiredness is a subjective sensation - what the individual feels rather than a measurable quantity - and its operational significance is that it leads to hypovigilance, the drop in alertness and monitoring that precedes error. It arises from physical as well as mental load, or from sheer monotony, and its effects vary widely between individuals of the same age.
ST9Es7f51hz3paKIZUV6: Range over the GROUND depends on ground miles per kilogram, so in a headwind the optimum shifts to a HIGHER airspeed - the aeroplane spends less time exposed to the wind. The speed for maximum climb ANGLE, however, is an air-mass quantity determined by where excess thrust peaks, and wind cannot change that: it stays constant, even though the gradient achieved over the ground improves.
STPGh7B7ya7kIUmAgvqa: VMCG must be a figure the crew can rely on in the WORST case, and on a wet or contaminated runway the nosewheel has little grip - steering and differential braking may be useless. Determining VMCG with primary aerodynamic control (essentially rudder) alone therefore makes the number valid on any surface. This conservatism is why VMCG is comparatively high and why it sets the lower bound on V1.
STkI8Dm2LX25g0iaDscl: Alcohol and drugs interact, usually by potentiating each other: the sedative effect of an antihistamine or a tranquilliser taken with alcohol is far greater than either alone, and often greater than the sum of the two. Nothing about alcohol speeds its own elimination, and the interaction is present by day as much as by night.
SVVNCtR4G4T0OBYkJAoO: Without SSR, primary radar identification requires the pilot to execute one or more heading changes of 30 degrees or more. The controller observes the corresponding radar return change.
SWK0asfCXo66iHHuYgmM: The malleus, incus and stapes lie in the air-filled middle ear, where they transmit the eardrum's movement to the oval window, amplifying it to overcome the impedance of the fluid beyond. Because the middle ear is an air space with only the Eustachian tube for equalisation, it is also the classic site of barotrauma.
SWmQDUZcMoEL6P9AealS: Calibrated airspeed is indicated airspeed with the two airframe and instrument errors removed: instrument error, from the mechanism itself, and position error, from the imperfect siting of the static source. Compressibility and density corrections come later.
SXB2bz7ZaJrlkF7wdKLO: Drag = CD x 1/2 rho V2 x S, so at constant angle of attack (fixed CD) and constant TAS, the drag is directly proportional to DENSITY. Raising the pressure while holding the temperature constant raises the density, so the drag increases. The same reasoning explains why the drag at a given IAS is independent of altitude: IAS is itself a measure of 1/2 rho V2.
SXJhcfERITGzBaoUuPby: ICAO groups aircraft for wake turbulence by maximum certificated take-off mass: HEAVY at 136 000 kg or more, MEDIUM from 7000 kg up to but not including 136 000 kg, and LIGHT at 7000 kg or less.
SY8n5LbzLWD6MKWEw2FY: A ring laser gyro sends two beams round the same closed path in opposite directions. Rotation lengthens the path for one and shortens it for the other, so their resonant frequencies differ, and the beat frequency between them is directly proportional to the rate of turn. Nothing spins and nothing wears out.
SZPQhaeacUCegWvGSLR4: At either magnetic pole the earth's field is entirely vertical, so a freely suspended needle stands vertical and the dip is 90 degrees. Dip is zero along the magnetic equator and increases towards both poles, which is also why the horizontal component that drives a compass vanishes there.
SZVPpU7YLEvJzyi7vsNp: The datum is a fixed reference plane chosen by the manufacturer, and all arms are measured from it. It may be anywhere on the longitudinal axis or on its extension - frequently ahead of the nose, so that every arm comes out positive - and it does not move as the aircraft is loaded.
SZqseDzjNLu6FpZsjXZR: A non-synergistic cockpit is one where the crew has stopped functioning as a crew: members withdraw into their own tasks and communication becomes vague or stops. It is dangerous precisely because nobody is monitoring anyone else, and each assumes the other has checked. It can arise from an over-authoritarian atmosphere as readily as from an over-relaxed one.
SafvkKYCvyPYADlM5qM2: In the cruise ram air is forced through the pack heat exchangers by forward speed alone. On the ground and at low speed there is no ram effect, so electrically driven fans draw cooling air through both the primary and secondary exchangers instead.
Sb96q6Lhwt3iXpLojB19: Work it in stages. Compass 051 plus 2E deviation is 053 magnetic, and less 16W variation is 037 true, so the landmark bears 037 + 060 = 097(T) from the aircraft, and the aircraft bears 277(T) from the landmark. To plot FROM the landmark, apply chart convergency: the parallel of origin of a 37N/65N Lambert is 51N, so n = sin51 = 0.78, and 1 15 of longitude gives about 1 degree. The landmark is east of the aircraft, so the direction to plot is 277 + 1 = 278.
SctIofBlojGdbf84lLQ5: The heating is left on throughout the flight, because keeping the laminate at a steady temperature avoids the thermal cycling that delaminates it and, incidentally, keeps it above the temperature at which it becomes brittle. That is why a heat failure brings a speed restriction against bird strike.
SeKA2BD1DbYw3hBQC3yv: VMCA is defined with the CRITICAL ENGINE INOPERATIVE: below it, the rudder can no longer generate enough yawing moment to balance the asymmetric thrust, so straight flight cannot be maintained. Note the qualifier - with all engines running the aeroplane is perfectly controllable well below VMCA, so a blanket statement that it is 'uncontrollable' is wrong. VMCA applies to any multi-engine aeroplane, not just four-engine types.
SeMOPqNuyCNwqrJ3ypuf: The autothrottle moves the thrust levers to hold whatever the selected mode demands: a fixed thrust setting such as N1 or EPR for the climb, or a speed or Mach number to be maintained with thrust. It is an independent system and does not disable the manual levers.
SfBSgsCJJbYzYn0SnyFw: A windshield wiper or equivalent means of maintaining a clear portion of windshield is required at each pilot station on aeroplanes with a maximum certificated take-off mass above 5700 kg. The same 5700 kg threshold appears in several equipment rules, including the flight data recorder.
SfcYSnBRwoT8gTNMl56L: Density is mass per unit volume, so kg/m3 - ISA sea-level density is 1.225 kg/m3. Force follows from F = ma and is measured in newtons. The distractors confuse mass with force: a kilogram is a mass, not a force, and N/m3 would be a weight density rather than a mass density.
SgWsGFr6DEf8y8BjobOg: ICAO Annex 1: ATPL applicants need 250 hours as PIC or a combination of 100 hours PIC plus additional time as co-pilot performing PIC duties under supervision.
Sgpc8tJXgqT2PUjEppcg: A Bourdon tube is a flattened, curved tube which straightens as the pressure inside rises, and that movement drives the pointer. It suits the higher pressures of hydraulic and fuel systems; temperature is measured with thermocouples or resistance bulbs.
SheRHcJLNJM3vXiC7nNO: The green arc is the normal operating range: its lower end is VS1, the stalling speed in the clean configuration, and its upper end is VNO, the maximum structural cruising speed. Above VNO the yellow caution range runs up to VNE.
Sj2JrvrIQb6dld97qyi9: Automation complacency is the erosion of monitoring that follows from trusting the automatics: because the system has always worked, the crew stops checking that it is doing what they intended. The failure it produces is not detecting the mis-set altitude or the wrong mode until the aircraft has done something unexpected.
Sj31gDkSfXa0RHRjh24G: JAR-FCL integrated CPL course requires 150 hours of flight time. The 200-hour figure applies to non-integrated training.
SkMfYNZNP8NJqdooxoBa: A tropical downpour produces a density of large raindrops far beyond anything in temperate rain, and the water film streaming over the windscreen degrades the view further. Flight visibility from the cockpit can collapse to a few hundred metres - of the order of 500 m or worse - within seconds, with no warning, which is why a go-around decision must be made before entering the shaft rather than during it.
Sl3WYpA52fi7OaCw6DNf: From 010E to 030W is 40 degrees of longitude, which along the 60N parallel is 40 x 60 x cos60 = 1200 NM. At 480 kt that takes 1200 / 480 = 2.5 hours, i.e. 2 HR 30 MIN. Forgetting the cosine would give 2400 NM and 5 hours, which is the trap.
SlEVXAovPbAj3QnUD0Fz: The retina is highly sensitive to oxygen lack, so hypoxia degrades visual performance early: acuity falls, vision becomes blurred and the visual field narrows towards tunnel vision, with night vision affected first of all - measurably from around 5,000 ft. Hypoxia does not produce true colour blindness, and the effects begin well below the altitudes quoted in the other options.
SlM99UCLs2lmm9qieinl: Air distance is what the aircraft flies through the air and ground distance what it makes good over the earth, so the two are in the same ratio as groundspeed to TAS: GD = AD x GS / TAS. With a tailwind the groundspeed exceeds the TAS and the ground distance is the greater.
SnhbBDfCWUCIHDKdrG2w: Gyro-compassing detects the tiny false acceleration a misaligned platform produces. In flight the aircraft's own accelerations swamp that signal and the system cannot tell one from the other, so alignment is possible only on the ground with the aircraft stationary.
SnyQJFeDKzIvkK1CEMm4: Bypass ratio is cold flow divided by core flow. Of the 500 kg/s entering, 250 kg/s bypasses the core, so the other 250 kg/s goes through it - giving 250/250 = 1:1, a low bypass engine typical of early turbofans.
Spzm2ML1TuE5i0xjCQ8Z: Descending through the friction layer in the northern hemisphere, the wind BACKS and decreases - about 30 degrees and half the speed over land. A southerly (180) at 2500 ft AGL therefore becomes about 150 at the surface, which is south-south-easterly. Backing means turning anticlockwise, so 180 goes toward 150, not toward 210.
Spzp9mTfzgssZQ0i8mfA: EPR compares the pressure at the jet pipe with the pressure at the compressor inlet, so it measures the overall pressure rise the engine is producing and is therefore a direct measure of thrust. It is used as the thrust-setting parameter on engines that are not fan-speed rated.
SqEIyIMZjZLRUnERFwcI: A Performance Class A twin above 45 360 kg or with 20 or more seats, without ETOPS approval, must stay within 60 minutes of an adequate aerodrome at the one-engine-inoperative cruising speed. Extending beyond that is exactly what an ETOPS approval provides.
SrOYex6hTOixIVFUReYq: Calibrated airspeed is a measure of dynamic pressure, and dynamic pressure is total pressure minus the static pressure existing at the aircraft's own level. Sea level static does not enter into it - that only appears in the definition of equivalent airspeed, through the reference density.

T4XBBv93h1KvWs7c5ial: Shimmy is a self-excited torsional oscillation of the nose wheel about the leg, which builds rapidly at certain ground speeds and can be violent enough to damage the structure. It is prevented by a shimmy damper - a hydraulic snubber acting on the torque link.

T8w2XDO85uAG5Qwl5ZGb: Setting aside Mode S, the civil transponder has two modes, A for identity and C for pressure altitude, and the code is set as four octal digits, giving 8 x 8 x 8 x 8 = 4096 possible codes. That is why 7500, 7600 and 7700 all use digits in the range 0 to 7.
