XpZOJ1eOY7ynVjxpGJH0: The defence against automation complacency is to treat the automatics as another crew member: told what to do, and then monitored to confirm it is actually doing it. Xpe5Z4a2nLa5pu7KY7pH: Bootstrap describes the arrangement of the cold air unit, where the compressor and the turbine are mounted on a common shaft: the turbine's extracted work drives the compressor, so the machine raises the pressure of the air it then expands, pulling itself up by its own bootstraps.
XqNibvHvLg80LNUIBZ6d: A nose-heavy (forward CG) aeroplane needs a larger nose-up balancing moment, which means a greater tailplane DOWNLOAD - and to generate a download the stabiliser must sit at a negative incidence, with its LEADING EDGE LOWER. XrGn5kXZTCGm1nXcM6mK: The regulator controls the generator by varying its field excitation, holding the output voltage constant as the load changes and as the drive speed varies. Batteries have no regulator of their own - their voltage is whatever their state of charge and the bus give them.

XtfKpp024RL4qyBEx4sD: VLE is the limit speed with the gear already down and locked, set by the loads on the doors and legs in the airflow. VLO, the operating speed, is normally lower, because the doors and the moving gear are more vulnerable while in transit.

XwHsGua8LHHQT6CPc6YY: Zero fuel mass is 1 764 + 35 + 300 + 350 = 2 449 lbs. All 60 gallons are on board at take-off, which at 6 lbs a gallon is 360 lbs, so the take-off mass is 2 449 + 360 = 2 809 lbs. The trip fuel figure is only needed for the landing mass and has no part in this calculation.
XwJf8eFjrKrIL6aWpnw6: Generators operating independently feed separate isolated busbars, so their outputs never meet and their relative phase is of no consequence. Phase only matters when they are to be paralleled, which is precisely why paralleling requires a synchronising process first.

Xzmoi3Ddy7pMZUFtbfrq: The pilot-in-command is responsible for terrain clearance when following an ATC clearance. ATC provides separation, PIC ensures terrain safety.
Y05p3et8pF0b0ytO3Snf: ATC prevents terrain collisions when an IFR flight is being vectored by radar. During vectoring, ATC is responsible for keeping the aircraft above minimum safe altitudes.
Y0oXplVyNHqDz2I8fK3u: A control zone (CTR) extends upwards from the surface to a specified upper limit. A control area (CTA) starts above the surface.
Y13zZV6dDSUFTFbnO1Ds: A magnetic plug or chip detector attracts and holds ferrous particles carried in the scavenge oil, so that a rapidly wearing bearing or gear is revealed at inspection - or, with an electrical detector, annunciated in flight. It filters nothing; it is a diagnostic device.
Y1Gm7x6btZqPZc32qa3w: An attitude is a learned tendency to respond consistently, favourably or unfavourably, towards people, objects, institutions or events. Being learned it can be changed by experience, training and persuasion - which is what makes attitudes, rather than personality, the target of CRM training. Behaviour is the outward result, not the attitude itself.
Y1a5A0K52Wegy26ZbqNs: With about 11 kt of tailwind component the planned groundspeed is about 130 kt, so the DR position after 15 minutes is about 32.5 NM along track; being 2.5 NM ahead puts the aircraft 35 NM along and 3 NM off. Track angle error uses the distance RUN: 3/35 x 60 = about 5 degrees. On an easterly track, south of track means RIGHT of track, so it is 5R.
Y1h6XJOjheQRVOrp176X: ATS must be informed when TAS varies by plus or minus 5% from the flight plan value.
Y1rV48P6BMgg0iCqUTKq: Two sensing principles are used: a vane that weathercocks into the local airflow and drives a synchro (1), and a slotted or conical probe in which the pressure difference between slots varies with the flow direction (3). Neither has anything to do with the inertial system's computed flight path.
Y2zWpfVyD0wOMM6vZz8e: Quick donning masks must be put on with one hand within five seconds and must permit normal communication once fitted, so the microphone is built into the mask and its selection is automatic. A crew member on oxygen can transmit and receive exactly as before.
Y37JTxtGwHRQAw6xpkXB: PROB followed by 30 or 40 gives the percentage probability of the conditions in the associated group occurring. Only 30 and 40 are used: a probability below 30% is not considered significant enough to include, and 50% or more would be forecast outright with BECMG or TEMPO instead. PROB30 TEMPO combines the two - a 30% chance of temporary conditions.
Y3GG2IWsw91xIIaLShT6: A pressure cabin is simply one in which the pressure can be held above the ambient pressure outside. It does not follow that the cabin altitude is constant - it climbs and descends on its own schedule - nor that the differential is fixed.
Y4Popy07hj4Z35ktgjdk: Type ratings should be established for any aircraft type whenever the authority considers it necessary. Not limited to multi-pilot or helicopter types.
Y5G4veVwi73hJHQWiBKt: The fire warning and the illuminated shut-off handle are driven by the detection loops, so the handle goes out when fire is no longer DETECTED. Pulling the handle or discharging a bottle does not clear the warning by itself.
Y5NVnhLn71mtPcEFUnhM: The zero fuel limit gives 48 000 kg, to which the take-off fuel is added: trip 18 000 + contingency 900 + alternate 700 + final reserve 2 000 = 21 600 kg, so the take-off mass is 69 600 kg. That is within the 72 000 kg structural limit, and the landing mass of 51 600 kg is within the 56 000 kg limit, so nothing else restricts it. Taxi fuel belongs to the ramp mass, not the take-off mass.
Y5UkwxSj6Sa82RFnbgtB: Parallel runways: 2 parallels use L and R, 3 parallels use L, C, and R.
Y7BgBs2rdKKIoDSfCROJ: Transport aircraft are pressurised to a cabin altitude of about 6,000-8,000 ft in the cruise, with 8,000 ft the regulatory maximum in normal operation. That keeps occupants within the indifferent stage of hypoxia while limiting the pressure differential the fuselage has to carry - a structural compromise rather than a physiological ideal.
Y7sG4kYu6605qmFk12F9: A free gyro holds its axis fixed in space, so the earth turning underneath it produces apparent wander (1), and moving the aircraft over the earth changes the local meridian and produces transport wander (3). Both are predictable and are compensated for by a latitude nut or a computed correction; the magnetic field plays no part, as the instrument is not magnetic.
Y8T0VZYuW8On7QCRvcwx: A ring laser gyro measures rotation about its own axis, by the frequency difference between two beams travelling in opposite directions round the ring. It is entirely insensitive to linear motion - the accelerometers are separate devices.
Y8iJd6oKa8qidlb563Ia: A runway narrower than the pilot is used to subtends a smaller angle, so it looks farther away and he judges himself too high. Correcting for a height error that does not exist, he flattens the approach and descends below the correct path - a low approach ending short of the threshold.
Y8j45X1u0DEMO0fHxD6b: A frangible disc, with a green blow-out indicator on the fuselage skin, ruptures above the design pressure and vents the bottle overboard, so that the excess pressure cannot burst the container. A missing green disc on the walkround shows the system has discharged.
Y92GmDeMKm7pB1Br6yWr: The probe recovers only 85% of the ram rise, so the indicated temperature relates to the outside air temperature by Tm = OAT (1 + 0.2 Kr M squared). That factor is 1 + 0.2 x 0.85 x 0.49 = 1.083, and 225 K divided by 1.083 gives 208 K, which is -65°C.
Y9hlDDORO7xFRM0yOG4J: Equivalent airspeed is calibrated airspeed corrected for compressibility, and the size of that correction depends on how far the air has been compressed - which is a function of speed and of the pressure, hence the pressure altitude. Density and temperature only enter when going on from EAS to TAS.
Y9oOTuztVez3WcuVYd0v: The cumulus, or building, stage is defined by updraughts throughout the cell, drawing in warm moist air while the cloud grows vertically and all precipitation is still held aloft. Downdraughts appear only when precipitation begins to fall, which marks the start of the mature stage; by the dissipating stage downdraughts dominate throughout and the cell decays.
Y9tY7pLjYks79PI0GRCR: A free gyro suffers earth rate and transport wander together. Earth rate at a mean latitude of 61N is 15 x sin 61 = 13.1 deg/h, or about 19.7 degrees in 1 h 30 min; transport wander is the 20 degree change of longitude times sin 61, about 17.5 degrees - roughly 37 degrees in total. The gyro read 90 degrees less than true heading at P, so the unwandered reading at Q would be 005, and applying the 37 degrees gives about 328 degrees.
YAaVfXM2cFX5RKjdQE2f: Implicit communication leaves the sender room to retreat: nothing definite was said, so if the outcome is bad he can claim to have been misunderstood, and if it is good he can claim to have meant it. It transfers the risk of the message onto the receiver, which is exactly why standard phraseology and explicit statements are required on a flight deck.
YAoM3BztzkwXpJ5bHK11: The vestibular apparatus senses motion and orientation: the semicircular canals respond to angular acceleration and the otolith organs of the utricle and saccule respond to linear acceleration and to gravity. Hearing is the cochlea's function, and middle-ear pressure is not something the vestibular system senses.
YBRUDpsdyvkGGozN483f: D-ATIS is the ATIS delivered over datalink and displayed or printed in the cockpit rather than read from a voice broadcast, which removes transcription errors and the need to copy while flying. The content is the same as the voice version.
YBj6nPdpguvEX05j6sZX: Spoilers are panels on the upper surface which destroy lift when raised. Raised together they act as speed brakes in flight and as lift dumpers on landing; raised on one wing only they assist the ailerons in roll, so their deflection may be symmetric or asymmetric.
YDjipUvodSRMDhuWZ3Pw: DAMP means the surface is not dry but the moisture does not make it look shiny - a colour change only. Once the film is thick enough to appear reflective the runway is WET, and once more than 25% is covered by more than 3 mm of water, snow or ice it is CONTAMINATED.
YDm7Lew0C9RhEfGSyr8e: The oxygen briefing and demonstration are part of the pre-departure passenger briefing and must be complete before take-off, whenever the flight is planned above FL 250. Waiting until a level is reached would leave the passengers uninformed during the climb, when a decompression is entirely possible.
YDprsKcdYVWaDXi1o0aS: On climb the expanding middle-ear air vents itself through the Eustachian tube almost passively, but on descent the tube tends to act as a one-way valve and has to be forced open. A rapid descent gives it no time, so the rising outside pressure drives the eardrum inwards - which is why barotrauma is a descent problem.
YDylSypFGqJoPpOcvH4G: Left alone, a simple jet delivers fuel in proportion to the square root of the pressure drop, so the mixture progressively richens as airflow increases. The diffuser, or air bleed, admits air into the discharge tube to break up the fuel and weaken the effect, keeping fuel flow proportional to air mass flow across the range.
YEGrvrNZyBdWRKmlA4es: Vertical wind shear is quoted in knots per 100 ft, since it expresses the change in the horizontal wind over a vertical interval. The usual severity bands are light below 4 kt/100 ft, moderate 5-8, strong 9-12 and severe above 12. Values around and above the strong band on final approach are what make a go-around the correct decision.
YEHJu9PtL8O4Erq8K6py: Simple interpolation between two charts 200 hPa apart is unreliable because the wind does not vary linearly with height - a jet core between the two levels would be missed entirely, and FL250 lies squarely in the band where polar front jets are found. So interpolate, but cross-check against the maximum wind and jet core data on the significant weather chart before using the figure.
YFkbihHycDMV3ZuTLVUx: Bleed air is air the engine has already compressed and then does not expand through the turbine and nozzle, so every kilogram taken costs thrust and fuel. Turning packs and wing anti-ice on is why take-off performance calculations carry bleed penalties.
YG5ks1a0ijPmgxxp8N8v: A cold front is driven by dense cold air actively undercutting lighter warm air, so it moves fastest - typically 20-30 kt, often overtaking the warm front ahead of it and forming an occlusion. A warm front is slower, around 15-20 kt, because the warm air can only ride gently up over the cold air. An occlusion, having lost the warm sector that drove it, is slower still and decays.
YG8sb7AmRx17eyPMJ5zH: The radio altimeter transmits a carrier whose frequency is swept continuously up and down. The echo returns after a delay, when the transmitter is on a different frequency, and the beat between transmitted and received frequency is directly proportional to the height.
YGJ7OVrR3eEXRe1xMCkR: Feedback is the return message that tells the sender what was actually received, which is what closes the communication loop and turns transmission into communication. The readback is its formal aviation version, and its value lies in revealing the difference between what was meant and what was understood.
YH8MvqWjfVxw5FD5MzM8: Colour vision belongs to the cones, which are concentrated in the central retina and densest in the fovea. They need good illumination, so colour perception fails as light levels fall and the rods take over - which is why colours cannot be distinguished at night and colour-coded information degrades first in low light.
YHJarn7MuAOVeFiGzKQe: The computer works out the attitude the aeroplane ought to have in order to capture and hold the selected path, compares it with the attitude the aeroplane actually has, and drives the command bars with the difference. Flying the bars to the centre reduces that difference to zero.
YHK0BtiRbQmFilCafOiX: Oxygen crosses the alveolar membrane by passive diffusion down its partial-pressure gradient, from about 100 mmHg in the alveolus to about 40 mmHg in the arriving venous blood. Nothing pumps it. Dalton's Law explains why the alveolar pressure falls with altitude, but the transfer itself is diffusion.
YHKBb0K1xTOpXbWthLmE: To conduct flight instruction for PPL issue, a theoretical CPL examination plus flight instructor rating is sufficient under some JAR-FCL interpretations.
YHz9FY9veUuomWZTNtuD: Eastward flight shortens the day and requires the body clock to be advanced, which it resists because its natural free-running period is slightly longer than 24 hours. Westward flight lengthens the day and needs only a delay, which is easier and faster. North-south routes cross few time zones and need no resynchronisation at all.
YIaCKxMMbBzwE4ymP4gk: One degree of latitude is 60 minutes of arc, and one minute of arc along a meridian is one nautical mile, so one degree is 60 NM anywhere on earth. Longitude is the one that shrinks: one degree of longitude is 60 x cos(latitude).
YIcRIJgZ1TtNESsHOP4G: Cabin crew members must be at least 18 years of age. The rest of the requirement is about training, medical fitness and competence checks rather than about age.
YIk4vvGTQr3fvTGDoVWp: Diving loads the tissues with nitrogen dissolved at above atmospheric pressure. Flying before it has washed out lowers the ambient pressure further, so bubbles form and decompression sickness results at cabin altitudes far below the 18,000 ft normally needed - the body is starting from a supersaturated condition rather than from equilibrium.
YIrbwIhmEgVahUiNHcoQ: Two effects stack up. A fully forward CG demands the largest nose-up moment from the tail, and full flap increases the downwash at the tailplane while producing a nose-down pitching moment of its own. Both call for maximum tailplane download, which means maximum UP elevator - which is precisely why the forward CG limit is set by elevator authority in the landing flare.
YJOOA6bmciiD2p4Ohuwl: In a bootstrap system the air is compressed by the cold air unit's compressor, cooled again in the secondary heat exchanger, and only then expanded through the turbine, where it does work and cools sharply. The route is therefore from the secondary heat exchanger outlet to the turbine inlet.
YL5pND8NTtJRKwxAGWwe: Class B: IFR and VFR permitted, all flights subject to ATC, all separated from each other.
YLIRCMjwusNoRusxrS3m: The eutectic salt core of a continuous loop becomes conductive as it heats, so its resistance drops and the current leaking between the centre conductor and the outer tube rises. The control unit senses that rise and gives the warning - which is why a loop detects an overheat anywhere along its length rather than at discrete points.
YMFOgU8vqrV4yoFLLLTH: The two spools are mechanically independent and each runs at the speed its own turbine and load dictate: the large, heavy low pressure spool turns much more slowly than the high pressure spool. That freedom to run at different speeds is exactly what keeps both compressors near their best match and resists surge.
YMm6S8vBcM2NGsMnGi78: Both fixes are 40 NM from the station, so the aircraft has flown the chord of a 40 NM circle across the 90 degrees between radials 310 and 040. That chord is 2 x 40 x sin45 = about 57 NM, covered in 15 minutes, giving about 226 kt. Plotting the two points shows the chord runs on about 085, and with zero variation that is also the true track.
YPboAQT2Kyyg3mJW5dcM: Convergency = change of longitude x sine of latitude, so it varies as the sine: zero at the equator, where meridians are parallel, and equal to the full change of longitude at the poles, where they all meet.
YPlae8OrTkyxEynNFg1R: A supercharger compresses the induction air, restoring the charge density that the falling ambient pressure would otherwise take away. Power is therefore maintained as the aeroplane climbs, up to the engine's critical altitude, rather than falling away with the air.
YPv8yEEYS0l3OF9nukfx: On a north polar chart gridded on Greenwich, grid = true + west longitude, so true = grid - west longitude = 344 - 115 = 229. Establish which conversion applies before doing the arithmetic; getting the sign wrong gives 099, which is also offered.
YQkPcUW3o6DYdYi5jXCE: The two systems divide the work: the autopilot uses the elevator to fly the vertical path and capture the level, and the autothrottle moves the thrust levers to hold the target indicated airspeed. Any pitch change alters the drag, and the autothrottle absorbs it.
YRzMUnkofyydNUlepdH1: Survival at altitude requires all three: enough oxygen at a high enough partial pressure, enough total pressure to keep body fluids liquid and the gas in the lungs usable, and enough warmth. Above about 63,000 ft body fluids boil at body temperature whatever oxygen is supplied, which is why a pressure suit or a pressurised cabin is unavoidable.
YRzcp9ZpqwU0b1ELJn2J: General information, instructions and procedures for carrying dangerous goods live in the operator's Operations Manual, which is where crew and ground staff find what to do. The Technical Instructions are the regulatory source behind it, and the AOC records that the operator is approved to carry them.
YSEw9xbYEJK4NQElY0OQ: At or above the transition level with 1013.2 hPa set, vertical position is reported as Flight Level.
YSiRAhuJGLtXgTrwBovT: Age, obesity and recent SCUBA diving all increase susceptibility - fat holds several times more dissolved nitrogen than lean tissue and releases it slowly, the circulation becomes less efficient with age, and diving starts the body supersaturated. Physical activity after a decompression makes symptoms more likely, not less, and sex is not the prime factor.
YTTG1QMWw5VW1VRhbV47: Section 2 of an Air-Report (AIREP) contains the estimated time of arrival (ETA) and endurance.
YTVTEI501PcPVh6G7B2U: Adding blades increases the total blade area, so the propeller can absorb more shaft power without having to grow in diameter - which matters because tip speed limits diameter. The trade-offs are a small loss of efficiency (each blade works in the wake of the one ahead) and extra weight and cost, though noise generally REDUCES because the same power is spread over more, less heavily loaded blades.
YUEF3AyoA0EpvbLlfCzj: Flying into a tailwind gust the aeroplane's airspeed momentarily FALLS: its inertia keeps its groundspeed while the air mass now moves with it. Less airspeed means less lift, so the aeroplane sinks until it accelerates back to its trimmed speed.
YUuvjzXEFUVkDZU9Dv3h: Hydroplaning speed is about 9 times the square root of the tyre pressure in psi. 12 bar is roughly 174 psi, and 9 x 13.2 gives about 119 kt. It depends on tyre pressure alone - crosswind and aircraft mass have no bearing on the threshold.
YV1PftxughbwYNJp4K0y: ILS obstacle clearance surfaces assume half a scale deflection maximum deviation from centreline after being established on track.
YVF8SKGy0Ffds0LOKX5C: Flight path modes are those which control where the aeroplane goes: speed or Mach hold (2), altitude hold (3), and glideslope capture and track (4). Pitch attitude hold is an inner-loop attitude mode - it holds a body angle and takes no account of the resulting path.
YWBNjoGBolTjhZTgSr0v: A NOT gate has one input and one output and simply inverts: a logical 1 in gives a 0 out and a 0 in gives a 1 out. It is the building block from which NAND and NOR gates, and hence every other function, are made.
YX3DnVkE2O13hbHqASh6: People beat machines at qualitative judgement - weighing incommensurable factors and deciding what a situation means (1) - and at noticing that something is unusual without having been told what to look for, such as an unexpected smell or noise (4). Machines are better at the other two: sustained monitoring against a limit and waiting patiently for a rare event, both of which defeat human vigilance.
YX4kYWohkdZi1tcr6FBK: In incompressible terms the stalling IAS is constant at all altitudes, since IAS is a direct measure of dynamic pressure. But at high altitude the true airspeed for a given IAS is much higher, so compressibility effects appear: local shock waves reduce the achievable CLmax and the stalling IAS therefore INCREASES. This rising low-speed boundary, meeting the falling high-speed one, creates coffin corner.
YXMvHUXfokC39VAk9ag5: The brake energy limit is about how much kinetic energy the brakes must absorb in a rejected take-off. An UPHILL slope means gravity helps the deceleration, so the brakes absorb less energy for the same speed - and a higher mass therefore becomes acceptable. Note the trade: the same uphill slope lengthens the take-off distance, so if the take-off were field-length limited instead, the effect would be the opposite.
YXeQiohLCcisPx1S8DiS: Fuel flow comes from what has actually been burned: 160 - 100 = 60 lbs in 38 minutes, about 1.6 lb/min. Of the 100 lbs left, 30 must be kept for the alternate and 50 as final reserve, so only 20 lbs may be used to reach the destination, which is 20 / 1.6 = about 12 minutes. Reserve fuel is not available for continuing the trip.
YYIX0EQuaRDdtBwOLEJU: Both calibrated airspeed and Mach number derive from the dynamic pressure and the static pressure, and at a fixed flight level the static pressure is fixed. Holding CAS therefore holds Mach, whatever the temperature is doing; only the true airspeed changes.
YYLTPTs0Cb41EDGxpEVW: The wind from 205 is on the starboard quarter of the 053 heading, so it gives a small left drift and a useful tailwind. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 050 and a groundspeed of about 145 kt.
YYeJvCBgVEKGo75Cnwjz: Freezing rain requires a specific vertical structure: a layer of above-zero air aloft in which precipitation is liquid, sitting over a layer below 0 C. The rain falls out of the warm layer, becomes supercooled in the cold layer without freezing, and then freezes instantly on impact. That structure occurs where warm air overrides cold air - classically ahead of a winter warm front - and it produces the most severe icing conditions there are.
YYt4LsAzT9HrJeSZNslo: A pure monocoque has no internal framework carrying load - the skin takes the bending, shear and torsion by itself, with formers only to hold the shape. It is efficient in theory but any dent or hole is critical, which is why real aeroplanes use semi-monocoque construction.
YZn2qtmM1PihX0js6i9k: Apply each correction in turn to the 800 m baseline. Elevation 2000 ft: +2 x 20 = +40. Temperature: ISA at 2000 ft is 11 C, so 21 C is a +10 C deviation, giving +10 x 5 = +50. Up-slope 2%: +2 x 15 = +30. Tailwind 5 kt: +5 x 10 = +50. Total = 800 + 40 + 50 + 30 + 50 = 970 m. The step most often missed is computing the ISA deviation at FIELD elevation rather than against 15 C.
YaJLyARdaDM3vlMvPkSN: An uphill slope means gravity opposes the acceleration all the way to V1, and although it then HELPS the braking, the extra distance used in accelerating outweighs the saving in stopping - so the accelerate-stop distance increases overall. All the other options shorten it: a headwind, a lower mass and colder (denser) air all improve both acceleration and deceleration.
YaYw2WLXpPf8vZgueFoR: The decision point procedure carries contingency fuel only for the sector from a nominated en-route point to the destination, which lowers the minimum fuel required and so releases mass for payload. It is a commercial optimisation, applied within the rules, not a safety enhancement.
Yb6b2I15sRrfXZLGGNPy: A double white cross = glider operations. This warns powered aircraft to exercise caution for glider activity.
YbBUld3mpMHaP5wdvi26: Gas exchange is driven entirely by partial-pressure gradients: each gas diffuses from where its partial pressure is higher to where it is lower, and the steeper the gradient the faster the transfer. Nothing is actively transported, which is why a fall in inspired oxygen pressure translates directly into a fall in the rate at which oxygen enters the blood.
YbIpm9kZd2yND3K5KNUv: Static air temperature is the temperature of the undisturbed air the aeroplane is flying through - what a thermometer moving with the air would read. It is displayed in degrees Celsius but must be converted to kelvin for every calculation involving the speed of sound, Mach number or ram rise.
YbVyOUwU8vajTWS3kiZl: A FIR provides Flight Information Service and Alerting Service. Both services are always provided together.
Yba0Qg82OLOSEcAtejz4: MNPS is Minimum Navigation Performance Specification - a navigational accuracy standard aircraft and crews must be approved against before entering the North Atlantic track structure, where tracks are 60 NM apart and there is no radar.
Yc7KHSO6d6WTJGCr6DUq: Large supercooled drops carry a lot of latent heat, so only part of a drop solidifies on contact; the remainder runs back over the surface and freezes progressively, building a dense, transparent, tenacious layer well aft of the leading edge - clear ice, the most dangerous form. Small drops freeze essentially instantly, trapping air and giving opaque, brittle RIME, and hoar frost is a deposit from water vapour.
YcFAUdxJWcdJLcR8RdfF: The wind from 190 is almost exactly behind the 003 track, so it is a near pure tailwind: the groundspeed rises from 130 to about 170 kt and the drift correction is only a couple of degrees, giving a heading of about 001.
YcK4rzWhx4l8EipO74R1: Westerly variation means MAGNETIC north lies west of true north, which is the same as saying TRUE north lies EAST of magnetic north. The check is the standard rule 'variation west, magnetic best': magnetic = true + westerly variation.
YcRS0sPkKtqE4gPg61LL: Where the oceanic clearance must be obtained before entry - Shanwick being the case in point - an aeroplane that has not received it holds outside the boundary rather than entering unclear. Elsewhere in the NAT the crew may continue on the current flight plan while still requesting the clearance, so read the stem carefully to see which case is being asked about.
YdEBY62KDuuprj2CeMJJ: Attention is a limited pool drawn on by every task requiring conscious processing, so two genuinely attention-demanding tasks cannot run at once - what looks like it is rapid switching, and both tasks suffer. Tasks combine successfully only when at least one has become automatic and needs almost no attention.
YdUvJhJDPyoSJdyfytie: An aeroplane certificated for single-pilot operation may be flown single-pilot in VFR public transport - the certification is what governs, and neither the number of engines nor the sector length changes it by itself. Night and IFR single-pilot operations are the cases that attract extra requirements, including a serviceable autopilot and the additional recency of five IFR flights with three instrument approaches in 90 days.
YerOQhPBXJkjSO1ZD8Ko: The seat-of-the-pants sense reports the resultant of gravity and acceleration and cannot separate the two, so once the outside visual reference is lost it produces confidently wrong information about attitude. No amount of training or experience makes it usable for orientation in IMC - the response is to disregard it and fly the instruments.
Yf6XkqwKZ9ku5xi4n6TV: A persistent overvoltage will damage everything on the bus, so the protection kills the machine at source: it opens the exciter breaker to collapse the field and the generator breaker to take it off the bus. The tie breaker is left alone, since the remaining generator can pick up the load through it.
YfNDAmdS8BJTmcSkWw05: Morning civil twilight begins when the CENTRE of the sun is 6 degrees below the celestial horizon and ends at sunrise. Nautical twilight uses 12 degrees and astronomical twilight 18. The 6 degree figure is roughly the point at which the brightest stars fade and outdoor activity no longer needs artificial light.
Yg4Y0zgv3z3q7FWCylFr: The navigation display uses magenta or white for the active TO waypoint, and the weather radar returns are painted green for light, amber for medium and red for heavy precipitation. Keeping those colours consistent is what lets a glance at the display be interpreted without thought.
YgLjdskbeJ9NtIP8MMDm: Distance travelled is the integral of speed over time, and no starting value is needed because it is a change rather than an absolute quantity. It is knowing where you are that requires the initial position - distance run and position are different questions.
Yh7Q5uZad40AsKjwhlpJ: Wake turbulence separation: Light behind Medium, same runway departure = 2 minutes. Some sources cite 3 minutes based on the specific departure scenario.
YhQggo08vhSUhHKgdqok: Marker beacons transmit on 75 MHz, which gives a wavelength of about four metres - the metric band. That short wavelength allows the narrow fan-shaped beam that defines the position at which the aircraft passes overhead.
YhsPpf0gpHd4xJxmogPo: A non-return or check valve passes flow in one direction and blocks it in the other, exactly as a diode does with current. It is used to stop fluid returning towards a failed pump or leaking back out of a pressurised part of the system.
YkTwafoQOGVmo18tg9Oc: An aircraft compelled to land (emergency) has the highest priority. All other traffic must give way.
YkXiSlIItFtrGzrrPiRr: Circling visibility runs 1500 m for Category A, 1600 m for B, 2400 m for C and 3600 m for D. A Category B aeroplane therefore needs at least 1600 m.
Yl0poUlbNo6HBYsmP0NN: JAR-OPS 1.135 requires four things to be preserved on the ground: a copy of the operational flight plan (with mass and balance where required), copies of the relevant parts of the aeroplane technical log, operator-issued route NOTAM documentation, and the special loads notification. The day's weather and the performance charts are used in preparation but are not retention items.
YlPLv4SdJAELMGmVrDfh: A float follows the surface of the liquid, so it measures the volume in the tank. Fuel expands as it warms, so the same mass occupies a larger volume and the gauge reads high - which is why a mass-measuring capacitance system is preferred for anything but light aircraft.
YlngIWX68dL75QaB2WHQ: The nitrogen charge is the spring: it takes the weight of the aeroplane and returns energy slowly. The oil is the damper - forced through a metering orifice as the strut compresses, it converts the landing energy into heat so the aircraft does not bounce back off the runway.
Ylqsx9t0gSRAe6wxtP5E: RVSM in the NAT applies from FL290 to FL410 inclusive, where approved aircraft are separated vertically by 1000 ft. Above FL410 the 2000 ft minimum returns, which is why the contingency offset changes at that boundary.
YmWCdl01aZJq3YP1gcKN: The mixture control varies the amount of fuel reaching the discharge tube, either by a needle in the fuel passage or by back-suction on the float chamber. It does not touch the air side at all, which stays under the control of the throttle butterfly.
Yo9tkjMvMWx97C8b2ZdB: SSR codes are four OCTAL digits, so the digits run 0 to 7 only: 9999 and 4096 are not valid codes at all, and 4096 is simply the NUMBER of codes available. Code 0000 is not normally assigned, and its appearance is treated as a transponder malfunction or an unauthorised setting.

Noise-induced loss is not reversible once established, which is precisely why early detection matters; the test says nothing about the vestibular system or the eyes.
ZUvY3MQ8MRriQKwe802q: Long range cruise deliberately accepts a specific range 1% below the maximum in exchange for the HIGHER of the two speeds that deliver it. Because the specific range curve is very flat near its peak, that 1% fuel penalty typically buys 3-5% more speed - which is almost always worth it once crew time, maintenance and schedule are costed in. Operating near buffet onset is a hazard, not a reason.
ZWAzJ70YsXwVXzL8q2ju: A mechanical latch in the gear lever gate physically prevents the lever being moved to UP while the aircraft is on the ground, released by the weight-on-wheels signal. A light or a horn would only tell the crew afterwards, which is too late.
ZWChwYR31nL7imY56Qmt: A straight line on a Lambert changes its true direction by the CHART convergency between the two meridians, dlong x the constant of the cone. Earth convergency uses the sine of the latitude and would only agree at the parallel of origin, and conversion angle is half of the convergency, not all of it.
ZWGB46bwCNfTCWOVAyj7: The stall depends on the angle of attack (1) and on the angle at which the stall occurs, which changes with the flap and slat setting (3). Those are the only two inputs needed. Engine speed, attitude and sideslip tell nothing about how close the wing is to its stalling angle.
ZWW8sXbh0DVUp3msv9OX: In transonic flight shocks form wherever the local flow first goes supersonic, so they appear at several places independently as Mach increases - typically the wing upper surface first, then the lower surface, then the tailplane, fin, canopy and nacelles. ZWnzQzGY997phWdaYUUd: The area rule states that transonic wave drag depends chiefly on how the total cross-sectional area of the whole aircraft varies along its length, so that distribution must change as smoothly as possible. Waisting the fuselage where the wing joins - the 'coke bottle' shape - compensates for the wing's area and smooths the curve, cutting WAVE drag substantially. Form, skin friction and induced drag are unaffected.
ZWrheIklBXnu27KVhvNL: With a constant speed propeller the governor holds the RPM constant, so the loss of power shows instead as a falling manifold pressure - the RPM needle stays put and gives no warning at all. On a fixed pitch aeroplane it is the RPM that drops first.
ZWv00GG3f761k8tEryeH: At -50C the local speed of sound is 38.94 x root(223) = about 582 kt, so M0.80 is a TAS of about 465 kt. Applying 20W variation, the true heading is 120 and with 11 degrees of right drift the track is 131. Resolving the 120/465 air vector against the 131/490 ground vector gives a wind from about 020 degrees at about 95 kt.
ZXGUAR4mlaM3erTtxgBd: Breathing 100% oxygen removes the nitrogen from the alveolar gas, so the whole available pressure less water vapour and carbon dioxide is oxygen. That maintains alveolar oxygen at the value normally found around 10,000 ft until roughly 40,000 ft, which is where hypoxia symptoms reappear and positive-pressure breathing becomes necessary.
ZXQFNprSOacKTMrSzosW: Moving the head while the aircraft is banking - that is, while a rotation is in progress - brings a second pair of semicircular canals into the plane of rotation while the first is still responding. The brain interprets the combination as tumbling in a different axis, and this Coriolis illusion is the most powerful vertigo-inducing situation in flight.
ZXizWZEwZ9UWb4KbykWd: A red band inside the green arc marks a speed at which the engine, propeller or airframe suffers a resonance. Passing through it is acceptable but continuous operation there is prohibited, because the fatigue damage accumulates quickly.
ZXk43GFcTLlgfUJllUZQ: A fixed pitch propeller is at its best blade angle at one combination of speed and RPM only. A constant speed unit adjusts the pitch continuously, keeping the blades at an efficient angle of attack for climb, cruise and descent alike, so good efficiency is available across a far wider speed range.
ZYI3f2RRD0XMyjTi4Iy4: The skip distance is the gap between the point where the ground wave dies out and the point where the first sky wave comes back down after refraction in the ionosphere. Inside it nothing is heard, which is why an HF frequency that works at long range may be useless close in.
ZYQsEPmZt1q8S16mYh7b: Hyperventilation blurs vision through the alkalosis and cerebral vasoconstriction it produces (1), hypoxia degrades acuity and narrows the field because the retina is highly oxygen-dependent (2), and fatigue impairs accommodation and makes the eyes hard to focus (4). Hypertension does not produce acute visual disturbance in the way the others do.
ZYkDJDsoVyUNoM0s2Jbl: The COMMANDER must be satisfied before flight that the mass permits a safe flight and that the cargo is properly distributed and secured. The operator prepares the loading instructions and the mass and balance documentation, but the acceptance - and the signature on it - is the commander's.
ZYp85S1U6xxW9oSh9ejr: Two factors compound. First the turboprop dispatch rule: the landing distance required must not exceed 70% of the LDA, so 0.70 x 2200 = 1540 m is the maximum permitted WET landing distance. Then the wet correction: a wet runway requires 15% more distance than a dry one, so the dry-runway figure must not exceed 1540 / 1.15 = 1339 m. Applying only one of the two factors is the usual error.
ZZ8EMRatx9UVBOSr0Mao: ISA temperature falls at 1.98 C per 1000 ft from 15 C at sea level, so at 10,000 ft it is 15 - 19.8 = -4.8 C, taken as about -5 C. The handy mental shortcut is 2 C per 1000 ft, giving 15 - 20 = -5 C directly. This is the reference against which any ISA deviation is measured.
ZZ90acwiTOaKTbob4a1g: The flowmeter is placed downstream of the fuel control unit, in the line feeding the burners, so that it measures the fuel actually being delivered to the engine. Measuring further upstream would include the spill and recirculation flows and would not reflect what is being burnt.
ZaMmojOrJ2VIHH9Qk0id: Integration is multiplication by time - acceleration multiplied by time gives velocity, and velocity multiplied by time gives distance - so integrating the measured accelerations twice yields position. Going the other way, from position to acceleration, would be differentiation.
ZaPpmcf8WLEffllC9y7w: A CTA extends upwards from a specified limit above the earth — not from the surface (that's a CTR) and not from a fixed height.
Zc9ItfEu0VatbH9chefH: ICAO Doc 4444: DME longitudinal separation at same level/track = 20 NM with simultaneous readings.
ZcWGQHoW9rO9yqWoZzlp: Saturation falls as the alveolar oxygen partial pressure falls, which happens as air pressure drops and therefore as altitude increases (1 and 3), and it falls when carbon monoxide occupies haemoglobin that would otherwise carry oxygen (2). Increasing air pressure has the opposite effect, raising the partial pressure and the saturation with it.
ZcwLh1SYsIIf2jCLbdwl: Calibrated airspeed is the indicated airspeed corrected for instrument and position errors, so with neither error present the two are identical. Equivalent airspeed and true airspeed still differ from them, because compressibility and density have not been accounted for.
ZcyLX0x84KX2wngiNUYe: Below the tropopause the temperature falls with height, so at a constant Mach number the true airspeed falls with the speed of sound. The density falls faster still, so the dynamic pressure and with it the calibrated airspeed also decrease - both go down together in this part of the climb.
ZdOjGgyQYwnXjjRLp9hY: An INS flies great circles, whose true track changes continuously with longitude. Convergency over each 10 degree leg is dlong x sin lat = 10 x sin60 = 8.7 degrees. Arriving at WPT 2 the track is about 094 and leaving it about 086, so the autopilot commands a track change of roughly 9 degrees DECREASE.
ZddpSK798yFZfcwcFL8k: The centre of pressure is by definition the point at which the resultant aerodynamic force - and hence the lift - can be considered to act. On a cambered aerofoil it moves forward as angle of attack increases, which is why the fixed AERODYNAMIC CENTRE at about 25% chord is preferred as the reference point for stability calculations.
ZeQOvw0uXZfzQyvQJY26: Cloud, fog and dew are all simply liquid water that has come out of the vapour phase, so the one thing that must happen in every case is CONDENSATION. Water vapour being present is not enough - it must be brought to saturation and then condensed. A relative humidity of 98% or a small temperature-dewpoint spread makes condensation likely but does not guarantee it; only condensation itself always produces the result.
ZedsSGgGB9YU5WP3bQJ9: The layer cools 2 C in 1000 m, an environmental lapse rate of only 0.2 C per 100 m. That is far less than the saturated adiabatic rate, let alone the dry adiabatic rate of 1 C per 100 m, so a parcel displaced upward - saturated or not - immediately becomes colder and denser than its surroundings and sinks back. The layer is absolutely stable, which is consistent with the absence of cloud.
Zencc7nuLVQ0xzYNZ6xv: Below about 200 ft the barometric altimeter is not accurate or responsive enough for an automatic flare, and it measures height above a pressure datum rather than above the runway. The radio altimeter measures the actual distance to the ground, and it is what triggers and shapes the flare and the retard.
Zet2Tp2MPvRSXm0GUMQl: The speed of sound in a gas depends only on its absolute temperature, being about 39 times the square root of the temperature in kelvin, in knots. Pressure and density both appear in the derivation but their effects cancel, which is why only temperature is quoted.
Zexol1mslfk1pvOHOYB8: At 2010 there are 50 minutes to run at 441 kt, so the distance remaining is 441 x 50/60 = about 368 NM. To take 55 minutes instead, the groundspeed must be 368 x 60/55 = about 401 kt, a reduction of about 40 kt, and with the same wind the TAS reduction is the same 40 kt.
Zf1KrqTNByfK7PdEJs8q: Scale is chart length over earth distance in the same units. 150 NM = 150 x 1852 = 277 800 m = 27 780 000 cm, so the scale is 4.63 : 27 780 000, which reduces to about 1 : 6 000 000.
ZfKIa5JPy5EMRAEaNfrA: A basic RNAV builds its phantom station from the reference beacon it is actually receiving, so what it needs is the RADIAL and DISTANCE of the waypoint FROM that VOR/DME. It cannot use a bearing and distance from the aircraft, because the aircraft's own position is what the system is trying to work out.
ZhAX5klLSODmsC4nhuqh: Work each level: the local speed of sound depends only on the temperature, and groundspeed is Mach x LSS plus the wind component. FL370 gives about 455 - 15 = 440 kt, FL330 about 443 - 5 = 438 kt, FL290 about 460 - 15 = 445 kt, and FL270, with the warmest air and no headwind, about 449 kt. The warm, low level wins despite the lowest Mach number.
ZhCtAJPS4mI1HYkOB6Bn: Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome runs alarm, in which adrenaline mobilises the body; resistance, in which an elevated but sustainable level of coping is held; and exhaustion, in which the reserves are spent and performance and health break down. Recovery is not one of the three phases - it is what may or may not follow.
ZhNTePMZev0KG2jtQ1AD: Ground-air visual signal code: X = require medical assistance. V = require assistance (general). N = negative. Y = affirmative.
ZiKkdX2m9pjUFNvsVl1d: A demand regulator opens only when the wearer breathes in, so no oxygen is wasted between breaths and the supply lasts far longer than a continuous flow system. The diluter part adds cabin air in a proportion that decreases with altitude, until it delivers pure oxygen high up.
ZiLqnmbExziM9QqQXlaP: Active errors are made by the person at the sharp end, at the human-system interface, and their consequences appear immediately in the action being performed. That immediacy is what makes them visible and what makes them the errors that get investigated. Latent errors, built into the system beforehand, have delayed effects and are far harder to see.
Zicw10q6Bxy1iuwA3h8x: In a stall the compressor can no longer pass the airflow, so the fuel that is still being delivered burns in too little air and the turbine gas temperature climbs sharply. The breakdown of the flow is violent and unsteady, so the vibration level rises at the same time - often with banging and thrust loss.
Zil3F0OFf2vdP7ZrtlHr: Refuelling facilities and limitations are published in the AD (Aerodrome) section of the AIP, within each aerodrome's entry.
ZipHu2kaEJRizGDG4fMz: Self-concept is the picture a person holds of himself - his abilities, his standing and his worth. It matters operationally because it governs how criticism is received, how readily help is asked for, and how a change of role such as upgrade to command is handled. How others actually see him, and how he would like to be seen, are separate things.
Zk5Ybf6qsexm9ijv72gr: Two things must be shared: the real load, which is set by the torque the drives supply and is matched by trimming the drive speeds, and the reactive load, which is set by the excitation and is matched by trimming the field. Getting one right and the other wrong leaves circulating current flowing between the machines.
ZkiZj9DsfNlT1WMdTWKm: The stress response is mediated by the autonomic nervous system - the sympathetic branch releasing adrenaline and driving up heart rate, blood pressure and breathing, and diverting blood to the muscles. It is autonomic precisely because none of it is under voluntary control, which is why stress cannot simply be decided away.
ZlKLenH5yV2GyGY7rbr7: The Indian monsoon is a seasonal reversal driven by the differential heating of the Asian landmass. In July the heated continent generates a deep thermal low, drawing the moist SOUTH-WEST monsoon in off the Arabian Sea and giving the west coast its torrential rains. In January the continent is cold, a high builds over Siberia, and the dry NORTH-EAST monsoon blows offshore.
Zm1ljnTpWh374Ev1Y0UK: This captain is investing everything in relationships - atmosphere, encouragement, compromise, freedom - and nothing in driving the task, since he accepts a more difficult process to preserve the harmony. That is high relationship orientation with low task orientation. Effective command needs both: the job done, and the crew used and supported in doing it.
Zmp02jYIKGR3zEJH5hqD: Alternative procedures to Subpart M are permitted only where they are needed and an equivalent level of safety has been demonstrated and APPROVED IN ADVANCE by the Authority, with the support of the other JAA Member Authorities. Establishing an equivalent safety case without that approval is not enough.
ZnsHBwR4HGgT7djroTUF: A cold swells the Eustachian tube lining so it cannot open, and descent is the dangerous phase because the tube acts as a one-way valve: expanding air escapes easily on climb, but on descent the rising outside pressure has to force air in. A rapid descent gives it no chance, so the eardrum is driven inwards.
Zo1PqliZrexaY9l3JrD9: Manifold pressure can never exceed the ambient pressure in a normally aspirated engine, so as the aeroplane climbs and the ambient pressure falls the manifold pressure falls with it at any fixed throttle position - roughly one inch per thousand feet. It is why full throttle produces steadily less power with height.
ZoEjA1qjpbJNk6TdwGA9: Independent parallel approaches require an NTZ of at least 610 m between extended runway centrelines, displayed on radar.
ZoXn8eyVo8S47UjTZGge: QUADRANTAL error belongs to the ADF: it is caused by the incoming wave being re-radiated and bent by the aircraft's own metal structure, and it peaks at relative bearings near 045, 135, 225 and 315. VOR does suffer site error, from reflections off terrain and buildings near the beacon, and propagation and interference errors, so those three all belong to it.
Zp0f98cGiB69RjKTvIHz: Jet fuel holds dissolved and entrained water which freezes into ice crystals at the temperatures reached in the cruise, and those crystals block the low pressure filter. Warming the fuel with engine oil in a heat exchanger keeps the filter clear, and cools the oil at the same time.
ZpIFewGpy5RdRERPWrQb: Perception is not the passive receipt of sensory data - it is the interpretation of that data against what is already known and what is expected. The same input yields different perceptions in different people, and expectation can make a pilot hear the clearance he anticipated rather than the one that was passed.
ZpblZJV8SUZsQIbA6xm9: Permanent, or hard iron, magnetism is built into the airframe during construction: hammering, riveting and machining while the structure sits in the earth's field align the domains in the ferrous parts. It is fixed in the aircraft's own axes, which is why it produces a deviation that varies with heading and has to be swung out.
ZpcdMRqPhITC40ujIVFa: The tanks are open to atmosphere through vent lines that end at NACA scoops on the wing underside, usually near the tip. The scoop gives a slight positive pressure that helps the boost pumps and stops the tank collapsing in a descent or bursting in a climb as the fuel level and ambient pressure change.
ZqJYvL2K1AiMRlNGPaRX: The two adaptations are wildly asymmetric: about ten seconds to adjust to bright light, as the pupil constricts and the cones take over, but around 30 minutes to regenerate the rhodopsin needed for full dark adaptation. That asymmetry is why a single careless white light costs half an hour of night vision.
ZryAmEbBfy3Tq3ZfBv9K: Aperiodic, or dead-beat, means the card settles without overshooting. That is achieved by keeping the mass of the magnet assembly concentrated close to the pivot, so the moment of inertia is small, and by adding damping wires or filaments that drag through the liquid. Long magnets and thin liquid would make the oscillation worse, not better.
ZsAmpBKkbHKjmVNNSjE3: The geostrophic wind is the speed at which the Coriolis force balances a given pressure gradient force, and Coriolis is proportional to the sine of the latitude. Nearer the equator Coriolis is weaker, so a HIGHER wind speed is needed to achieve the balance. For the same isobar spacing the geostrophic wind is therefore greater at 30 N than at 60 N - which is why isobar spacing alone cannot be used to estimate wind speed without knowing the latitude.
ZsWBXf19iWTkGMvYOsr0: Note the stem says TRUE altitude, not pressure altitude. At -32C the air is about ISA-29, so a true altitude of 9000 ft sits at a pressure altitude of roughly 10 200 ft. Working the density ratio at that pressure altitude and -32C gives about 0.816, so TAS = 200 / root(0.816) = about 220 kt.
ZtZnN5Y9yjK0QD1CiJxS: A chip detector collects the ferrous particles that a wearing bearing or gear sheds into the oil, and either annunciates them in flight or reveals them at inspection. It captures a diagnostic sample - filtering the oil is the filters' job.
ZuWT5Amg0R6vniqILz3o: Cumulonimbus concentrates every serious hazard in one cloud: severe turbulence, hail, lightning, severe icing, heavy precipitation, microbursts and gust fronts, with tops that can exceed FL450. Its hazards also extend outside the visible cloud - hail thrown from the anvil and gust fronts 15-20 NM ahead - which is why the standard rule is to avoid a CB by at least 10 NM rather than to fly between cells.
ZugbzGKuWs0FOuKJnTm2: Low pressure boost pumps are centrifugal because they must move a large volume against a small head, are tolerant of running dry briefly, and fail open - fuel can still be drawn through a failed centrifugal pump by the engine-driven pump, which a positive displacement pump would block.
ZvRGCFctAJeefRP8aObR: A MEDIUM following a HEAVY on approach to the same runway requires 5 NM (9.3 km) of radar separation, or 2 minutes where time is used. The 6 NM / 3 minute pairing belongs to a LIGHT following a HEAVY.
ZvXYVhqEbq9Mfq1y6d4M: A circuit breaker is a thermal or magnetic device that responds to current, so it works equally well on AC and DC circuits and both are protected by them. What must not be done is to reset one repeatedly: a breaker that trips again is reporting a real fault, and resetting it may start a fire.
Zw8NhGZ4h6Lm6u7HhLiw: A constant delivery pump keeps pumping whatever the system needs, so something must dispose of the surplus: the pressure regulator, or cut-out, returns the excess flow to the reservoir once the pressure is reached and puts the pump off-load. A variable delivery pump regulates itself by destroking and needs no such device.
ZwdYrv4NDwrsYG1MOp7J: Nicotine is the addictive agent in tobacco - it acts on the brain's reward pathways and produces dependence and withdrawal. The other constituents do different damage: tar carries the carcinogens, and carbon monoxide occupies haemoglobin and raises the smoker's physiological altitude, but neither is what makes the habit hard to break.
ZwlebcUC7eODMqmFDPSm: Stress arises from the individual's appraisal of a demand against his own perceived resources, so the reaction depends on the person and on how he manages that particular stressor - the same situation stresses one pilot and not another. Reactions also vary with the environment and with the situation, and no universal ranked list of stressors applies to everyone.
ZxITozJNaHpZBcUsNItA: Earth distance = chart length x scale denominator = 12 cm x 2 000 000 = 24 000 000 cm = 240 000 m, which is 240 000 / 1852 = about 130 NM. A handy check for a 1:2 000 000 chart: 1 cm is about 10.8 NM.
ZxziU31mpnzviCQQ7BWZ: An occlusion is cold when the air behind the cold front is colder than the air ahead of the warm front. Over Europe that comparison is decided by the continent: in SUMMER the land ahead of the system is warm, so the maritime air arriving behind is the colder of the two and cold occlusions predominate. In winter the continental air ahead is very cold and the milder maritime air behind rides over it, giving warm occlusions instead.
Zy1MGvAtEmpmy4H1SES3: Weight is the force of gravity acting on the mass, so it always acts vertically downwards, parallel to the gravity vector, whatever attitude the aeroplane is in. It is unrelated to the aircraft's own axes, which is exactly why the moment arms change in a manoeuvre.
Zy8rTvJrv9XoQSrTL4El: All three are true. Glaucoma damages the optic nerve fibres from the periphery inwards, so the visual field narrows unnoticed (2); central acuity, which is what the person actually uses, is only affected at the end (3); and untreated the process continues to total, irreversible blindness (1). That is why intra-ocular pressure is measured routinely.
Zy9D8ZZFXvfxaL3ktvD6: Weight = 150,000 x 10 = 1,500,000 N, and total thrust = 4 x 75,000 = 300,000 N. In a climb the lift is close to the weight, so drag = W/(L/D) = 1,500,000/14 = 107,143 N. Gradient = (T - D)/W = (300,000 - 107,143)/1,500,000 = 0.1286, i.e. 12.86%. The two traps are forgetting to use ALL FOUR engines' thrust and forgetting to derive the drag from the L/D ratio.
ZyGjuJzLznBBhX8EcoSX: In procedure A the aeroplane holds take-off thrust and take-off configuration through the initial climb, reduces to climb thrust at 1500 ft, continues at V2 + 10 to 20 kt, and only accelerates and retracts flap at 3000 ft. 3000 ft is therefore the ACCELERATION height, not the thrust reduction height - and no noise abatement procedure may begin below 800 ft in any case.
Zz2GcknMAtLLJsAEkoZz: A safe forced landing is an unavoidable landing or ditching with a reasonable expectancy of no injuries to persons in the aircraft OR ON THE SURFACE. Two elements distinguish it: it is forced rather than voluntary, and the expectation is reasonable rather than guaranteed - no landing can be guaranteed injury-free.
a0Vc9ZmAtiBHBS2x1wZi: Oxygen and burning tobacco are a direct fire risk, so smoking must be prohibited - and the sign illuminated - whenever oxygen is being supplied in the cabin. In practice the sign is also on for take-off and landing, so read the question as asking for the oxygen-specific rule.
a0XGCnhNDKtPScQ4biPM: Taking moments about the centreline, the helicopter gives 1 800 x 5 = 9 000 kg cm to the left and the load 200 x 60 = 12 000 kg cm to the right, a net 3 000 kg cm to the right. Divided by the new total mass of 2 000 kg that puts the centre of gravity 1.5 cm to the right.
a2sT4a4V7FuVsKSlXgPq: The exchanger runs the hot scavenge oil against the cold fuel on its way to the burners, so the oil is cooled without any weight or drag penalty and the heat goes back into the engine with the fuel. Warming the fuel enough to keep the filter free of ice crystals is a useful by-product.
a5CMv0PVvmKSTF9rQoD3: Compression = (a - b) / a, so the semi-minor axis b = a x (1 - 1/297) = 6378.4 x 0.99663 = about 6356.9 km. The difference between the two axes is only about 21 km, roughly 0.3 percent, which is why the earth can be treated as a sphere for most navigation but not for satellite geodesy.
a5Iwlx3zMk14Vs5HSf6g: Pressing the test switch passes a current through the whole loop and into the control unit, so it proves both that the sensing element is electrically continuous - a broken loop fails the test - and that the warning circuit, bell and light all work. A test that only rang the bell would prove nothing about the detector.
a5QO2piQxYKti8kVvGVK: Very heavy rain roughens the wing surface with an irregular water film and adds impact drag, which thickens and separates the boundary layer, reduces maximum lift coefficient and raises the stalling speed. The remedy is an increased approach speed for margin - reducing speed, or approaching with flaps up, removes margin instead.
a5ZttPdpt4vJLiCg9ne8: The rods are the photoreceptors of night vision - they contain rhodopsin, are far more sensitive to light than the cones, and give no colour and poor resolution. Because there are no rods in the fovea, a faint object at night is seen only by looking slightly to one side of it.
a5wQx0BVsX2LBMcyYZZ3: ICAO Doc 8168 specifies the outbound timing in a holding pattern: 1 minute at or below FL 140, and 1 minute 30 seconds above FL 140. Some references state 2 minutes above FL 140 based on older or national procedures. The marked answer of 2 minutes reflects a common exam convention.
a7DeeNUhowehYhGzgfkJ: A representation error is a wrong internal picture of the situation, and it originates in the information the picture was built from: the observed world itself supplying misleading indications (3), or a single bad item of information being received and accepted (4). Gathering all available information is a defence against representation error, not a cause of it.
a7EY8WTmpo9p8TWdKeKO: The wing stalls at an angle of attack, not at a speed, so the warning system measures angle of attack directly with a vane or probe and compares it with the stalling angle for the current configuration. That is why the warning is correct at any weight, bank angle or load factor.
a7Hoosuo8pAx7czjpmPQ: The ground interferes with the formation of the tip vortices, so the downwash behind the wing is reduced. Less downwash means the effective angle of attack at the wing INCREASES for a given attitude, so more lift is produced, while the lift vector is tilted less far rearward, so induced drag falls - by up to 40-50% at very low height. More lift and less drag together are why an aeroplane floats in the flare.
a7QplSRxEau8k8w9kbGs: Pressing the discharge switch fires an electrical squib in the bottle head, whose explosive charge ruptures the frangible disc and releases the extinguishant into the engine zone. It is instantaneous, needs no mechanical run to the bottle, and can be duplicated for two shots.
a8C653w2CGaw2VkhTzZo: ISA at 29 000 ft is 15 - 58 = -43C, so -55C is ISA-12, i.e. colder and therefore denser than standard. Density altitude = pressure altitude + 118.8 ft per degree of ISA deviation = 29 000 - (118.8 x 12) = about 27 500 ft. Colder than standard always gives a density altitude BELOW the pressure altitude.
a9NpRTIv8EcFwDMmDpJ6: A narrower-than-normal runway subtends a smaller angle, so it looks farther away and the pilot judges himself too high. Correcting for a height error that does not exist, he flattens the approach and descends below the correct path, arriving low and short - the classic undershoot onto a narrow strip.
a9sYYxzaGNcff7YYc4nP: The centre of a stationary high has a very weak pressure gradient, so surface winds are light or calm, and subsidence builds a strong inversion at low level. That inversion traps moisture, dust and pollution beneath it, so summer conditions over land are typically hazy with poor horizontal visibility but no significant cloud. Thunderstorms need lifting, which the subsidence suppresses.
a9yF50HWTdqRKDPQecRX: Thrust is the rate of change of momentum, so with the aircraft stationary it is simply the exhaust mass flow multiplied by the jet velocity (1). And since power is force times speed, an aeroplane going nowhere is producing no mechanical power at all, however much thrust it develops (3).
aAjNlGH5Hepp3pm3FjhR: Mode S was designed to do two things: give each aircraft a unique 24-bit address so it can be selectively interrogated, which sharply improves surveillance in dense airspace by removing garbling and over-interrogation, and to provide an air/ground data link. TCAS uses Mode S transponders but collision avoidance is not what Mode S was designed for, and it does nothing for HF communications.
aCRwg3iWpF41R3xr722W: The wind from 110 is on the starboard beam of the 005 heading, so it pushes the aircraft left and adds a small tailwind component. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 359 and a groundspeed of about 490 kt, so the drift is about 6 degrees port.
aCZYlTRqYDppa8EBIptm: A cargo hold fire needs its oxygen supply cut: turn the hold ventilation OFF, then extinguish. Merely reducing the air conditioning keeps air moving through the compartment, feeding the fire and carrying smoke and flame into the rest of the aeroplane.

aF39FtqlGPTYqdG2dA1g: The agonic line is the isogonal along which variation is zero, i.e. where true and magnetic north coincide. Any other line of equal variation is simply an isogonal, the aclinic line is the line of zero DIP, and an isotach is a line of equal wind speed on a met chart.

aJTNNvQqHRFzRJ7mycrU: Work inwards from both ends. True heading = true track minus right drift = 256 - 10 = 246. Magnetic heading = compass heading plus deviation = 233 + (-3) = 230. Variation = true minus magnetic = 246 - 230 = +16, and a positive result means EAST, so 16E.

aKcYGVdPjfr5cTyoGtyG: Rolling out on south, the compass overshoots: it shows the aircraft as already past the heading it has reached. The turn must therefore be continued beyond 180° in the direction of turn by roughly the latitude, so a left turn is stopped with about 160° indicated.

aKhsWvojEhpeJmhJ4a2M: From E008 to W008 is 16 degrees of longitude, which at 60N is 16 x 60 x cos60 = 480 NM = 888 960 m. At 1:5 000 000 that is 888 960 / 5 000 000 = 0.178 m = 17.8 cm. Note the scale quoted is the one at 60N, so no further secant correction is needed.

aLtH2u8FtC7U48wnN3Gi: Supplemental oxygen is the reserve provided for the occupants in the event of a pressurisation failure. It is distinct from first-aid oxygen, carried for a passenger who becomes unwell, and from protective breathing equipment, which protects the crew against smoke and fumes.
aMJIsjM6qWwDFT37QshL: Parasite drag = CDp x 1/2 rho V2 S, and with CDp essentially constant it therefore varies with the SQUARE of the speed - double the speed and parasite drag quadruples. aMSLap1xuzT9kJkUdjTw: The crankshaft, through the connecting rods, converts the pistons' up and down movement into rotation. The camshaft is driven from it to operate the valves, and the reduction gear, when fitted, merely lowers the propeller speed.
aMecZiL7GU1J6tHl8tg4: An expansion wave is the opposite of a shock: the supersonic flow turns around a convex corner and ACCELERATES, and because the process is isentropic, static pressure, density and temperature all DECREASE steadily through it. aMoNPwTEIAQfUhHSlpN9: In a no-gyro approach the aircraft has lost its heading reference, so the controller issues 'turn left' and 'stop turn' instructions and the pilot flies them by timing on the turn coordinator. aMtlbTrzV933Yzq5rC21: At normal latitudes alignment can be started either by selecting ALIGN or by selecting NAV directly, since selecting NAV runs the alignment first and then enters navigation automatically. ATT mode is an attitude-only reversion with no navigation, so it cannot be used to align.
aNjwZimHWxKAvY5yOA6t: With no ground lights, no horizon and no texture between the aircraft and the runway, the only cue left is the aerodrome lighting itself, which the pilot reads as nearer and lower than it is - so he feels too high and too far out. aOtkNOAzT7SmwHxHbi8v: A noise abatement departure procedure may not be started below 800 ft above aerodrome elevation. aQbEhjxUHLxb2wCfiSpY: Convergency = change of longitude x sine of the mean latitude = 6 x sin60 = about 5 degrees. aRC8xquRerM0P8dvhIy2: A single loop system decides there is a fire when current flows between the sensing element and earth. aReirvZilktcDluOIDEm: Turboprops have neither the bleed air nor the electrical capacity for a hot or heated leading edge of that area, so they use pneumatic boots: rubber tubes on the leading edge inflated in sequence to crack off ice that has already formed. aTv1cSE5tLjQL3KMSR72: Dalton's Law: in a mixture of gases the total pressure is the sum of the partial pressures, each gas behaving as though the others were not there. aUDdYg72HEZGZvsIv1jc: The unit takes the battery off the bus when it is fully charged and no longer needs the charger (1), when it overheats, as a lead-acid or nickel-cadmium battery in thermal runaway will (2), and when an internal short develops (3). aUOiMw2GhLGuSKlD8gkH: A frontal depression is steered by the flow in its own warm sector, so the centre moves roughly parallel to the warm sector isobars, with the low pressure on the left in the northern hemisphere. aV3XXlGf5j36btoyCiJx: The air data computer derives altitude the same way a barometric altimeter does: it measures the absolute static pressure from the fuselage static ports and converts it to a height using the standard atmosphere. aV3zZXcpQGClyoLpFvrd: The operator's records for each crew member must cover training given, the results of the tests and checks, a record of flying hours, and a summary of training by reference period so that currency can be demonstrated at a glance. All four items are required.
aWucwMGJe35jAF4oF4AT: Only HF, roughly 3 to 30 MHz, is refracted back to earth by the ionosphere in a usable way - lower frequencies are absorbed and higher ones pass straight through into space. That is why HF gives the long oceanic ranges and VHF and UHF are limited to line of sight.
aZCv7ehLTxm5NmRMRIxA: Checklists matter most where memory and habit are least reliable - on an unfamiliar type, where the stored routine is either absent or belongs to a different aeroplane, and under mental pressure, which is exactly when items are skipped and negative habit transfer occurs. aZIWZAv0eSPDVkWH7SGp: Coastal refraction bends the signal as it crosses the coast, introducing a fixed angular error in the bearing. aZYOiX0MIKUa4r4QxFDy: Of the 1 000 kg/s entering, 889 kg/s bypasses the core, so 111 kg/s goes through it. Bypass ratio is bypass divided by core: 889 / 111 = 8.01. Dividing the total flow by the core flow would give one too many.

aa7AqETEsPvehqnQq8Nl: Density is mass per unit volume, so its SI unit is the kilogram per cubic metre; ISA sea-level density is 1.225 kg/m3. The distractors are all pressure units: psi is pounds per square inch, kg/cm2 is a metric pressure unit, and the bar is 100,000 pascals.
aah6Jgr0dIfGhu5Rpliy: The reservoir is pressurised with air or bleed air so that the pump inlet always has a positive head, even at altitude where the ambient pressure alone would allow vapour to form and the pump to cavitate. The pressure involved is only a few psi and is separately relieved.

abHTOSilGteRakF3DX6k: During the ground run the requirement is a precise, repeatable thrust, so the autothrottle sets and holds the computed take-off N1 and then locks the levers there. Speed modes are meaningless during the acceleration and are only armed later in the climb.

abqUokOaXu4HBMfgYyib: Rate of descent on a glide path is about groundspeed x 5 for a 3 degree path, scaled in proportion to the angle. For 3.5 degrees that is 150 x 5 x 3.5/3 = about 875, and the exact figure, GS x 101 x tan3.5, is about 930 ft/min. Either way the answer is about 900 ft/min.
acOynzMrBhf2Pg5QG5rA: Working outwards from the instrument: removing instrument error and position error turns IAS into CAS, and removing compressibility turns CAS into EAS. Density is what takes EAS on to TAS, so it plays no part in reaching equivalent airspeed.
acjgkRj0uIAtS1Xaf9kk: With no brushes or slip rings there is no external path to the field, so the machine starts itself: a permanent magnet pilot exciter generates the first AC, which is rectified to feed the exciter field, and the output builds up from there. adUNLcA7bV0ePCGcVJbd: Within the NAT region, IFR applies at or above FL60 or 2000 ft above ground, whichever is the higher. The 2000 ft AGL element matters over Greenland and Iceland, where terrain puts the surface well above FL60.

ae0WFtmxfxxelh4XZpcR: Self-sustaining speed is the point at which the turbine produces enough power to drive the compressor and accelerate the engine by itself. The starter is normally kept in beyond it, to shorten the start and hold down the peak temperature.
aeTzIZi45yQjvLUrbuG1: The emergency transponder code on Mode A is 7700, not 7500. Code 7500 indicates unlawful interference (hijacking), code 7600 indicates communication failure, and code 7700 indicates a general emergency.

afHakDsctnmjoMTfZdJ7: Falling vigilance shows as a general damping down: sensory perception dulls so that indications are looked at without being seen (1), and there is a physical heaviness in the muscles and eyelids as arousal drops (3). agZxtkJ3I9VDaNjXyfhp: The crank assembly is the rotating and reciprocating group that turns gas pressure into rotation: the crankshaft, the connecting rods and the pistons. The crankcase is the structure that houses it, and the valve gear is a separate assembly driven from it.

ahDi4oAmtRYNHW5v20NB: Over-breathing washes out carbon dioxide, and the alkalosis that follows constricts cerebral vessels and disturbs nerve and muscle function: dizziness (1), tingling progressing to carpopedal spasm and tetany (2) and blurred or disturbed vision (3). ahV7fpWy4GNxyijInk3C: The MMEL is the manufacturer's master document, approved for the type. The operator writes its own MEL from it, taking account of its route structure, equipment fit and crew training, and the MEL may be MORE restrictive than the MMEL but never less.
ahakcSGfYDk7SfmRuXbV: At 2010 there are 50 minutes to run at 441 kt, so the distance remaining is 441 x 50/60 = about 368 NM. To take 55 minutes instead, the groundspeed must be 368 x 60/55 = about 401 kt, a reduction of about 40 kt. With the same wind, the TAS reduction is the same 40 kt.

amG1oW1IKlXWal9KVTmN: The first action for a class E cargo hold fire is to shut off the ventilating airflow to that compartment. amagZHGqEacjCAQc7ZBn: ICAO Doc 4444 requires that when radar identification is achieved, the controller shall inform the aircraft before issuing any instructions or advice based on radar. The pilot must know they are identified so they can expect and act on radar-based instructions.
ams0aSRf7l4QiYmuB4kP: Traffic load is what is left of the maximum take-off mass after the operating mass and the fuel have been accounted for. an7x5KaEe1deprbHkfBz: The co-pilot must have made three take-offs and three landings within the preceding 90 days, on the same type or class, or in an approved flight simulator of the type to be used. Generic experience on any aeroplane, or a 60-day window, does not meet the rule.
angGH6J2CdAICo0pvM3r: The wind from 200 is 50 degrees off the port bow of the 250 course, giving a crosswind of 60 x sin50 = 46 kt and a headwind of 60 x cos50 = 39 kt. aniaX6ZwarYCCwXxG3iX: Attention comes in two forms. Divided attention alternates rapidly between several matters, at the cost of doing each of them less well.
aoZsNlB2TyrdXQP17jFF: In fully supersonic flow the pressure over each surface is essentially constant between the shock waves, so the pressure distribution is broadly rectangular rather than the peaked, rounded subsonic shape. apGm7TUkD68sDCtNGC0f: Airmass (or heat) thunderstorms develop within a single warm, moist, unstable air mass when strong afternoon surface heating over land triggers convection. apXf8Au3xOCLdoEBT7u7: Alerting Service is provided by the ATS unit responsible for the aircraft at that moment. This may be an ACC, approach control, or aerodrome control — whichever is currently providing service. It is not limited to units equipped with 121.5 MHz.
apiH8x6rsXtRok4lTQCy: Apply the 1-in-60 rule: 1 degree subtends 1 NM at 60 NM, so at 200 NM it subtends 200/60 = 3.3 NM, and the exact value 200 x tan1 is 3.5 NM. aqOwpEiOrJW6qHlovVhm: Both are true, and together they explain why hypoxia is so lethal. aqmu063lXSzBiq0NubNJ: Metacommunication is communication about the communication itself: stepping outside the content to comment on how the exchange is going - 'I don't think we're understanding each other', 'that came out sharper than I meant'. arhOJV6AyPlXusZCkNRw: Automation is a tool for the pilot, not a replacement for him: it should reduce workload and improve precision where it does those things well, while the pilot remains in command, monitoring and able to take over. arhatGP1HFo6a2G6ov4I: Thermal anti-icing keeps the leading edge clear, so the wing's aerodynamic performance is preserved. The hot air comes from the compressor, though, and every kilogram bled away is thrust lost - so the maximum thrust available is reduced whenever the system is on.

aswNozoQZobBagf2ZIEt: The horizontal stabiliser provides LONGITUDINAL (pitch) stability. at5gLRrqjEtAdsYC3Hky: Because the automatics almost always work, the crew stops checking that they are doing what was intended - automation complacency. at8G2965weW9o1Ck6bPD: Rate of descent depends on GROUNDSPEED, not TAS. With a 15 kt headwind the groundspeed is 150 - 15 = 135 kt, and on a 3 degree path the rate of descent is about groundspeed x 5 = 675 ft/min. Using the TAS would give 750 ft/min and would leave the aircraft above the path.
auYYVXKPeXawWW9ndNRm: Serious icing requires abundant supercooled liquid water, which means a thick cloud with a high water content, sub-zero temperatures and continuous droplet supply. avxdNNTjiT863jeCwuM3: Water cools the fuel below its ignition temperature, which is what a class A fire - solid organic material - needs. It is dangerous on flammable liquids, which it floats and spreads, on electrical fires, where it conducts, and on burning metals, which react violently with it.
awGOthUAdu7RRV8R405U: A chemical candle burns for a fixed time of about 15 minutes once fired, which is sized to cover the emergency descent from cruising level to an altitude where oxygen is no longer needed. It cannot be stopped or regulated once lit.
axEurJa3G4I5bizKPlGQ: Once freezing is found on the surfaces after treatment, the anti-icing fluid has failed and its holdover no longer means anything - the aeroplane is contaminated. ay79X87SOObcMDWue7vU: Fatigue produces tiredness (1), degraded motor skills so that handling becomes clumsy (3) and a narrowing of concentration onto one item at the expense of the whole picture (4). ayfLTuTbgbLL2kphKSRR: The automatic system is certificated against demonstrated limits, and both crosswind and turbulence are among them: beyond the demonstrated crosswind it cannot be relied on to track the localiser, and in severe turbulence the approach must be flown manually or abandoned.
aym8NNFQwVXDgFJdWzEv: Vortices sink 500-1000 ft below the generating aircraft's path and then drift downwind, so the safe air is above the preceding aeroplane's flight path and on the upwind side. Below and downwind is precisely where the vortex core will be.
az1XlY0baN4M9EQdoSPH: In Class G airspace above 10,000 ft MSL, the VMC minima are the same as for all airspace at that altitude: 8 km visibility, 1 nautical mile (1500 m) horizontally and 1000 ft vertically from clouds. Some question banks express the horizontal distance as 1 NM rather than 1500 m.
azL8eqIe4OqU8tVIcShu: Carbon monoxide starves the tissues of oxygen, so the picture is that of hypoxia: headache (2), impaired judgement (3), weakness and loss of muscular power (1) and eventually unconsciousness (5).
