b03fii8S0xVp1WQcyxYX: The semicircular canals are part of the inner ear, alongside the otolith organs and the cochlea. The outer ear collects sound, the middle ear transmits it through the ossicles, and the inner ear contains both the hearing organ and the whole vestibular apparatus.
b08GOgwzYLVT7iUane3c: The defence against automation complacency is to treat the automatics as another crew member: told what to do, then monitored to confirm it is actually doing it, with every mode change and entry verified against what was intended. Flying everything by hand is neither practical nor the point, and complacency is a behaviour rather than an unavoidable property of the system.
b18PEezcLcq5gB2DFb9S: VS is the stalling speed, or the minimum steady flight speed at which the aeroplane remains controllable. It is the reference from which many operating speeds are derived - V2, VR and VREF are all defined as multiples of a stall speed. Note the variants: VS1 is for a specified configuration and VS0 for the landing configuration.
b1SjnWH0vU5WLJVCzrvG: Statements 2, 3 and 4 hold. The tailplane load, whether up or down, forms part of the aeroplane's total lift; a tailplane CAN stall before the wing when ice has reduced its stalling angle and a large flap setting has increased the downwash meeting it - the classic tailplane icing stall, recovered by RAISING the nose and reducing flap; and balancing the total pitching moment is the tailplane's fundamental job. Statement 1 fails on the word 'always': with an aft CG the tailplane load can be positive.
b1W9z7VK0zW9NP2SpT7O: Ahead of an approaching warm front the pressure falls steadily as the depression approaches. QFE (pressure at aerodrome level) and QNH (that pressure reduced to sea level) are two expressions of the same atmospheric pressure separated only by the fixed aerodrome elevation, so they always move together. Both therefore decrease. Any answer showing them moving in opposite directions is physically impossible.
b1YFpeb1ztYlJ87J5Z79: The tailplane dominates because it combines a useful area with a very long moment arm behind the CG - and stability contribution scales with area multiplied by arm. A pitch disturbance changes its angle of attack and generates a restoring moment large enough to overcome the destabilising contributions of the fuselage and, usually, the wing. This is why tailplane size is set by stability rather than by control requirements.
b1YHb5AGVSJROyhEk2Qp: Pressure altitude = elevation + (1013 - QNH) x 27. With QNH 988 that is 1000 + (25 x 27) = 1000 + 675 = 1675 ft. A QNH below 1013 always puts the pressure altitude ABOVE the true elevation, which is the same reasoning behind 'high to low, look out below'.
b1y4HBkS4MXtGXTMf7Fi: Vortices sink and then drift with the wind, so with the wind from the right they move to the LEFT of the preceding aircraft's path. Staying on the right - the upwind side - and above its path keeps you clear of both the sinking core and the downwind drift.
b2fTPTJquVoPqgy7iXhm: VHF range is line of sight: range in NM = 1.23 x (root of aircraft height + root of station height), both in feet. That gives 1.23 x (root 10 000 + root 100) = 1.23 x (100 + 10) = about 135 NM. Note how little the ground station's height contributes compared with the aircraft's.
b3hKdLa18LZiw3Hgk4oR: A strayed aircraft is defined as one which has deviated significantly from its intended track OR which reports that it is lost. Both conditions qualify independently — the aircraft need not report lost to be considered strayed if the deviation is observed.
b3yX1OOr0QAt0YGKLumG: A gaseous system can be regulated - the flow can be set to suit the cabin altitude and turned off when no longer needed (2) - and it can carry a far larger and rechargeable quantity (3). It is not free of fire risk: high pressure oxygen is itself a serious hazard, which is one of the reasons chemical generators are used in the cabin.
b4Q0ItqWuaLHiCOzlQW1: A hard disk holds data, so it is a storage peripheral - it both reads and writes and is neither purely input nor purely output. A keyboard is an input device, and a screen and a printer are output devices.
b4R2EOq6SQnGDVdxA1BJ: Supplemental oxygen exists for one purpose: to supply the occupants after a loss of cabin pressurisation. Oxygen for a passenger with a breathing disorder is first-aid or therapeutic oxygen, and crew fighting a fire use protective breathing equipment.
b4Wk0jesMizLN9kx5S0F: Flight deck oxygen is stored as a high pressure gas in steel or composite cylinders, because the crew need a supply that can be regulated, checked before flight, used for as long as necessary and recharged. Chemical generators, used in the cabin, burn for a fixed time and cannot be turned off.
b4ZNRAZPAuktVrXitFmh: Aerodontalgia is toothache caused by pressure change acting on gas trapped under a filling, in a decayed cavity or around an abscess. It is commonest on climb as the trapped gas expands, but it certainly occurs on descent as well, when rising outside pressure acts on gas that cannot equalise - so the answer is yes.
b4ZUvybycO64Vfw8WHw9: Synchronous speed is 120 times the frequency divided by the number of poles: 120 x 400 / 4 = 12 000 rpm. An asynchronous machine runs a few per cent below that, because it needs slip to induce any rotor current at all, so 12 000 rpm is the figure it approaches.
b4jpse5H7JlUAq5bdRSC: The 0 C to -10 C band holds the greatest concentration of large supercooled water droplets, which freeze on impact and produce the heaviest, most tenacious clear ice. Between -10 C and -20 C the cloud is increasingly mixed and rime becomes typical, and below about -20 C to -40 C most cloud is glaciated into ice crystals, which bounce off rather than adhere.
b5DMIinkZp6ckkRhANmi: The set must hear the echo from the furthest target before firing the next pulse, so maximum unambiguous range = 81 000 / PRF in nautical miles = 81 000 / 1200 = about 67 NM. Equivalently, the 1/1200 second interval lets the pulse travel 125 km out and back, which is 67 NM each way.
b5EJe1LWsvaLSP69WgTt: In LNAV the FMS does the navigating and hands the autopilot a roll or heading command; the autopilot simply flies it. That division of labour is why the same autopilot can follow an FMS route, a selected heading or a localiser without knowing anything about the flight plan.
b6WlS8CEuq9XAWrvuaql: In a hung start the engine has lit but will not accelerate, so it sits at low speed with fuel burning and little cooling airflow - the temperature climbs and the engine is being damaged. The only correct action is to shut it down and investigate; adding fuel would simply overheat it faster.
b6X0veN0GufwAQjOsMLt: On a 5-dot CDI each dot is 2 degrees. The FROM flag with 090 set means the aircraft is outbound on or near the 090 radial. A CDI deflected LEFT means the selected course lies to the left, so the aircraft is right of it, i.e. south of the 090 radial when heading east, which is the 092 radial.
b78G9nrv925IIWUH4Qpx: Superchargers use a centrifugal, or radial, compressor: a single impeller gives a large pressure rise in one stage, tolerates the wide speed range of a piston engine, and is small and robust enough to be driven off the crankshaft. Axial compressors need many stages to do the same job.
b7gtn9ddFd7iAlsLOMSM: The point has been made and refused; pursuing it in the cruise turns a minor irritation into a cockpit argument that damages the crew's ability to work together for the rest of the flight. The correct handling is to let it go for now and raise it in the debriefing, where it can be dealt with properly and without an aeroplane to fly.
b8MfpP4xioH0T3fU0I38: Test all three limits. Zero fuel mass is 35 500 + 14 500 = 50 000 kg, within the 53 000 limit. Take-off limit: 64 400 - 50 000 = 14 400 kg of fuel. Landing limit: 50 000 + fuel - 4900 must not exceed 56 200, so fuel is at most 11 100 kg. The lowest of the limits governs, so the maximum take-off fuel is 11 100 kg.
b8bYe1CRVuGjWK2BUaDn: Airspeed indicators are calibrated with Saint-Venant's compressible flow relation, applied to standard sea level conditions. That is why the reading is the true airspeed only at sea level in the standard atmosphere, and why compressibility has to be taken out again to get from CAS to EAS at height.
b8hjfF54fPpA7DQxeGAH: Generators running independently feed separate isolated busbars, so their outputs never meet and their phase relationship has no consequence at all. Phase only matters when they are to be paralleled, which is exactly why paralleling requires synchronising first.
b8jfEEw9x3rerHzOclkv: Jet A freezes at about -40°C and Jet B at about -50°C, so Jet A's freezing point is the higher of the two and statement I is the wrong way round. Jet B contains far more volatile material, so its flash point is far lower - around -20°C against Jet A's +38°C - which makes statement II correct.
b9NHU5SAuHsAv739jynv: A white dumbbell with a black perpendicular bar across each circular portion indicates that taxiing need not be confined to the taxiways. Aircraft must still land and take off on runways, but may taxi on other suitable surfaces.
b9e4WIO3WegrSXhY9lfw: The crash axe is there for forcing entry: to reach a fire behind a panel or a lining that cannot otherwise be opened, and to serve as a general purpose tool during an evacuation. It is a firefighting and rescue tool, never a weapon, and it is carried on the flight deck for that reason.
bAaBdZUq2XXqzwk59BLj: QFE is the pressure at aerodrome level, QNH is that value reduced to sea level using ISA, and QFF is the same value reduced to sea level using the ACTUAL temperature profile. The temperature only matters over the height being reduced through. With the aerodrome exactly at sea level there is nothing to reduce, so QFE, QNH and QFF are all the same 1022 hPa and the missing temperature is irrelevant.
bBNGDqMcUXkqlGQ6kRyG: It is entirely usual - confirmation bias is a normal feature of human cognition, not a defect of poor pilots. Once a plausible explanation has been adopted, information that fits it is accepted and information that does not is discounted or not noticed. Experience and training reduce nothing here; the defence is deliberately asking what would show the explanation to be wrong.
bByFhiBGvIsJyuL3K05F: Category I is a precision approach with a decision height not lower than 200 ft and an RVR of not less than 550 m (or a visibility of not less than 800 m). A DH of 100 ft belongs to Category II, which also requires 300 m RVR.
bC1yhOAegB6kcz4t7o35: This question needs an Air Almanac extract that this text-only version cannot show, so learn the method instead. Enter the almanac's twilight table with the date and the nearest tabulated latitude, interpolating for the exact latitude, which gives the LMT of morning civil twilight. Then convert LMT to UTC by adding the longitude in time, 4 minutes per degree, WEST longitude being added. At 095 26'W that correction is about 6 h 22 min.
bC6sWWQ3DhsmdBJBZKd2: The freezing points are not the same - about -40°C for Jet A against -50°C for Jet B - so statement I is wrong. Statement II is right: Jet A's flash point of around +38°C is far above Jet B's, which is below freezing, because Jet B is a much more volatile wide-cut fuel.
bDE93pqh9UVaaUABBSej: Below the jet core the cold air lies on the polar side, so a rising outside temperature means you are tracking toward the equator, i.e. southward in the northern hemisphere. The jet itself blows from west to east, so on a southerly heading that westerly flow arrives on the aircraft's right-hand side. The reverse holds above the core, where the temperature gradient is inverted.
bDLRm47G1wgHihhMSwyH: Two minutes is the wake minimum for a MEDIUM (or LIGHT) landing behind a HEAVY. Three minutes applies where the following aircraft departs from an intermediate point of the runway, and to a LIGHT landing behind a MEDIUM.
bEdhdDdSDtTu0iDOSlKF: Active listening - hearing the other person out, checking that you have understood what he actually means, and showing that you have - is what makes a constructive resolution possible, because most conflicts rest partly on each side misreading the other. Counter-arguing entrenches both positions, and simply capitulating or refusing to move resolves nothing.
bExnQDt9UdKC9tNKp0S9: Standard masses are only statistically valid over a reasonable sample, so they may be used for baggage on aeroplanes with 20 or more seats. Below that the actual masses must be used, since one heavy bag in a small aeroplane makes a real difference to both mass and balance.
bFsiDCEyvdREn8DBmvTJ: On a polar stereographic chart a straight line has a CONSTANT grid track, so it can be computed at any convenient point. On a south polar chart gridded on Greenwich, grid track = true track + east longitude. At 100E, where the true track is 090, that gives 090 + 100 = 190 grid, and that value holds for the whole route.
bGGB1YMuPjOUKTxOQHVE: An underspeed is a drive fault, not an electrical one - the machine's frequency has fallen out of limits but the generator itself is healthy. Opening the generator breaker takes it off the busbar, which is all that is needed; there is no reason to collapse its field or to split the tie.
bGgwU4QT6FUtYxxE65Vm: Pitch trim on a conventional transport is by moving the whole stabiliser, so the column returns to its centred zero-force position and that position does not change - statement I is wrong. Roll trim has no such surface: it works by shifting the datum of the aileron feel and centring unit, so the wheel's zero-force position does change.
bGwwojm2ORUszajIR6Fr: Carburettor icing is driven by the temperature drop in the venturi and by fuel vaporisation, which together can remove 20-25 degrees. At +30 C with 40% relative humidity there is enough moisture for serious icing, but only at low power settings, where the throttle butterfly is nearly closed and the local pressure drop and cooling are greatest.
bHcIgUxlhK7SbPZuH8qs: Tip vortices are the direct product of the pressure difference that generates lift, so they exist from the moment lift is established - at rotation - and cease at touchdown. Wheel spin-up and drag have nothing to do with their formation.
bHlZEKJei3hKjhnM772q: Coping divides into action-based coping, which attacks the stressor itself, and cognitive coping, which changes how the stressor is thought about - rationalising it, playing it down, or setting it aside for now. Cognitive coping is useful when nothing can be done about the cause, but it becomes dangerous when it is used to ignore a problem that could and should be acted on.
bHoD8OW2QBJMpOC6GbJ9: ICAO establishes Standards and Recommended Practices (SARPs) for contracting member states through its 19 Annexes to the Chicago Convention. These are not binding regulations but international practices that States undertake to apply, with differences notified to ICAO.
bIDl0IczGKHqVMOYijaa: Decompression sickness is caused by nitrogen dissolved in the body's tissues and fluids coming out of solution as bubbles when the ambient pressure falls - in aviation, typically after a pressurisation failure at high altitude. It is rare in normal commercial operation precisely because the cabin altitude is kept low, and it is a serious condition, not a harmless one.
bIUjyAU7jGKW7TrcqGRq: Maximum drift occurs when the wind is at 90 degrees to the HEADING, not to the track, and its size is given by sin(drift) = wind / TAS = 30/120 = 0.25, so about 14.5 degrees. With a course of 040 and the wind from the right, the heading is 040 + 14.5 = 054.5, and the wind perpendicular to that comes from 054.5 + 90 = about 145 degrees.
bIf7TzbJOmMEhHmPRPXa: The lethal feature of hypoxia is that the first faculty it removes is the one needed to notice it. Judgement and self-criticism go early, accompanied by euphoria, so the pilot feels well and is satisfied with his own performance while his performance deteriorates. Any symptom that felt unpleasant would at least prompt action.
bIkgnLBNLHIb68fYjUNr: The cabin rate of climb indicator shows the rate of change of CABIN altitude. A leak lets the cabin lose pressure, so cabin altitude rises and the instrument shows a rate of CLIMB - the aeroplane's own vertical speed is unchanged in level flight. The rate of climb shown grows as the leak widens.
bIuqdg9DcnMguMKCPY5D: When a controlled flight inadvertently deviates from its track, ICAO Annex 2 requires the pilot to adjust the heading to regain track as soon as practicable. This is the pilot's immediate responsibility — ATC notification follows but the correction comes first.
bJ6Dh0sE5zm9aJPN8wPs: The polar front jet is the jet directly associated with a surface front, because it exists as the thermal-wind consequence of the sharp temperature contrast across the polar front, and it lies above and slightly on the cold side of the surface front. The subtropical jet sits at the poleward limit of the Hadley cell with no surface front beneath it, and the arctic and equatorial easterly jets are seasonal features unconnected to a frontal system.
bJnapuusnNhC6g8s7DoE: Generators that are not paralleled feed separate busbars, so their outputs never appear at the same point and their relative phase is irrelevant. Synchronising is a prerequisite of paralleling, not of running independently.
bK72ONc7zZb2WgKu2FrD: The bootstrap sequence is compress, cool, expand: the cold air unit's compressor raises the pressure, the secondary heat exchanger takes out the heat of that compression with ram air, and only then does the air expand through the turbine, doing work and cooling sharply. Expanding first would waste most of the available temperature drop.
bKAvMRHfBHQgiAapIpHj: Isochrone construction alternates between air positions and ground positions: the air isochrone is where the aircraft could reach in still air, and it is converted to the ground isochrone by adding the wind vector for that interval - the mean wind acting from the preceding ground isochrone onwards. The technique repeats interval by interval to build the minimum time track.
bKaa8BEQhCG5Riyfculs: Only the leading edge is protected, and often only part of it - typically the outboard slats, with inboard sections left unheated. Bleed air is limited, and ice on the inboard leading edge has the least effect on handling, so full protection is neither necessary nor affordable.
bLy3RReS4oF4oy9hdZSZ: Turbine temperatures are measured with thermocouples - chromel-alumel junctions whose emf varies with temperature. Nothing else survives there: a liquid or bimetallic thermometer would be destroyed, would respond far too slowly, and could not be read remotely.
bLztLodBlTmRhWtC5dzB: Civil twilight runs from sunset until the CENTRE of the sun is 6 degrees below the celestial horizon, and the same 6 degrees defines the start of morning civil twilight. The 12 degree figure defines nautical twilight and 18 degrees astronomical twilight. Duration is not fixed: it lengthens markedly with latitude.
bMV4ACRI9NWbhIhGlIKK: Climbing at constant CAS, the falling density means a higher true airspeed is needed to produce the same dynamic pressure, so TAS increases. The speed of sound is falling at the same time, so Mach number increases faster still - which is why a constant CAS climb eventually runs into the Mach limit.
bMVz9IaGOV7Uv8uM8xTr: Report C shows Q1009 (low and, by inference, falling), a south-westerly 15 kt, a lowering multi-layer cloud sheet at 3000 and 7000 ft, a temperature-dewpoint spread of only 3 C, and BECMG 4000 forecasting deteriorating visibility. That is the signature of an approaching warm front. The others show high pressure with NOSIG, or fog under a high, none of which imply frontal rain.
bNJuUg9lRgh1l1CNnebd: The basic or inner-loop modes are those which simply hold an attitude: pitch attitude hold and roll attitude hold. Altitude and speed holds are outer-loop path modes, which work by commanding the attitude loops rather than by driving the surfaces directly.
bNNQL8gsSb1vmqnDmBlI: The slot between the extended slat and the wing forms a converging duct, so air from the high-pressure region beneath the wing is ACCELERATED as it passes through and emerges as a fast-moving jet over the upper surface. That jet re-energises the boundary layer, letting it resist separation to a much higher angle of attack - typically an extra 5-10 degrees of stalling angle. The slat does not reduce wing loading, and the flow through the slot speeds up rather than slowing down.
bNPJRGTFUGFkIHH3sp69: An exit is only usable if every part of the chain works: the door can be opened from either side, the assisting mechanism operates, the door locks in the open position so it cannot swing back, the slide or other escape means is available, and the lighting shows the way to it. Any one of them unserviceable puts the exit out of service.
bNaC6iQWuJFVWlJ68QZn: Aircraft on the same track and level at the same Mach number are separated by 10 minutes in MNPS airspace. That is the baseline; 5 minutes is available only when the Mach number technique keeps the leading aircraft the faster of the two.
bNplJblBIt6G9EdztfJE: A ring laser gyro has no spinning mass, so there is virtually no spin-up time and it is unaffected by g loading, shock and vibration. It DOES suffer lock-in at very low input rates, which is exactly why a dither motor is fitted, so any option claiming freedom from lock-in is wrong.
bP31uL6vHb8jy7C6qZii: ICAO Doc 4444 states that aircraft under radar control shall not be vectored closer than 2.5 NM to the boundary of controlled airspace, unless otherwise prescribed or agreed. This buffer prevents aircraft from inadvertently leaving controlled airspace.
bPnAbBjXsGWVh47LigPT: PAPI stands for Precision Approach Path Indicator. It is a visual approach slope indicator system using a row of sharp-transition light units that show red or white depending on the aircraft's position relative to the correct glide path.
bQ5RNtxZruPJig4iB9sd: The drive's health shows in its oil, so the crew are given oil temperature and oil pressure - a rising temperature or a falling pressure is the warning to disconnect before the unit seizes. The generator's own output is monitored separately by the electrical instruments.
bQyNJjHVGKuxKHZq7hUG: The horizontal component H is what drives a compass. It is greatest at the magnetic equator and falls to zero at the magnetic poles, so it depends only on magnetic latitude and is symmetrical about the equator: 50N and 50S give approximately the same value. Note that two of the distractors have the variation the wrong way round.
bRfqbynFA7VF0VV77da2: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies that longitudinal DME-based separation at the same cruising level and track, with simultaneous DME readings and no speed differential, is 20 NM. With a speed differential of 20 kt or more (leading faster), it reduces to 10 NM.
bS52KBTe2gCawtZbS36Y: EPR compares what comes out with what went in: total pressure at the turbine outlet divided by total pressure at the compressor inlet. It is used as the thrust indication on many engines because that pressure ratio is closely related to the thrust being produced.
bSxsiG5m4k3DHtlG60vc: A change from IFR to VFR flight is always initiated by the aircraft commander, not by ATC. The pilot decides when conditions permit VFR flight and requests cancellation of the IFR flight plan. ATC cannot unilaterally change a flight from IFR to VFR.
bTTggxLMt38RfZagBACo: The command bar is not a heading error display: it commands a bank angle. With 20° of heading still to make up it calls for a definite angle of bank, and it centres only when the aeroplane has actually taken up that bank - so a centred bar means the correction is being flown correctly, not that the turn is finished.
bU279jG7FgbeA786KUeo: An Aerodrome Flight Information Service (AFIS) can only supply limited services to users and under no circumstances may it supply ATC services. AFIS provides information and advice but has no authority to issue clearances or instructions.
bUXNekFpaotZGxpMMAso: Only statement 2 is right - the altimeter setting is displayed on the primary flight display. The flight director bars, the attitude display and the flight mode annunciator are all on the PFD as well, not on the navigation display, which shows the route, the weather and the traffic.
bV9YkxM7NLVOLHudV1cW: Both statements are false. The ELLIPTICAL spanwise lift distribution is the theoretical optimum, producing uniform downwash across the span and therefore the MINIMUM induced drag for a given lift - a rectangular distribution produces more, not less. And induced drag is inversely proportional to aspect ratio, so REDUCING aspect ratio increases it, which is why long slender wings are used where efficiency matters.
bVFPBHJDZS4dpzxkfi1X: A force acting below the centre of gravity produces a nose-up couple about it, so on an aeroplane with underslung engines a sudden thrust increase pitches the nose up - and a thrust reduction pitches it down. This coupling is why a go-around from a low-speed, high-drag configuration demands prompt forward pressure, and why the effect is most pronounced on aircraft with large-diameter engines slung well below the wing.
bVPiS7hLMcXNtSWHVhbY: The earth distance is 10 x 60 x cos47 = 600 x 0.682 = 409 NM = 757 800 m = 75 780 000 cm, and 5 inches is 12.7 cm. Scale = 12.7 / 75 780 000, which is about 1 : 6 000 000. Convert the inches to centimetres before dividing, and do not forget the cosine of latitude.
bVrORMisgr3ggbYp3xwT: Large transport aeroplanes certified under CS-25 have a positive limit manoeuvring load factor of 2.5 (with the negative limit at -1.0), reflecting an operating regime in which deliberate manoeuvring is gentle. The ultimate load is 1.5 times the limit, i.e. 3.75. The higher figures of 3.8, 4.4 and 6.0 belong to the CS-23 Normal, Utility and Aerobatic categories.
bW6Me48osQ7sF0KxUT3h: Group norms are the unwritten rules a group develops about how its members behave - what is said and not said, what standards are kept, how much challenge is acceptable. They are powerful precisely because they are informal and unstated, and they can support good practice or quietly erode it.
bWSv36aUUd0mbnah86mR: The smoker's haemoglobin already carries several percent carboxyhaemoglobin, so less of it is available for oxygen. At a real altitude of 10,000 ft his blood oxygen content matches that of a non-smoker somewhere higher still - his physiological altitude is above his actual altitude, by several thousand feet for a heavy smoker.
bWpffTKlaKwe9W2Pnod6: A lightning strike or a passage through a severe electrical storm can remagnetise the airframe, so a compass swing is required afterwards. Note the wording of the other options: a swing follows a large and PERMANENT change of magnetic latitude, it is not done in anticipation of one, and it is the carriage of ferrous freight, not any large load, that matters.
bXQr64IMwX521TNOe7CL: The classic passage sequence is: several hours of continuous rain or snow from nimbostratus ahead of the warm front; a break in the warm sector, where precipitation largely stops and low stratus, drizzle and mild, murky conditions prevail; then a short, sharp burst of showers or thunderstorms as the cold front goes through, followed by clearing skies, good visibility and cumulus in the cold air behind. Precipitation increasing in the warm sector would be the wrong way round.
bXXGENzz2CalZqu42mrO: Turn radius = V2 / (g tan(bank)), so at the same bank angle the slower aeroplane flies the tighter circle - A's radius is less than B's. Checking the others: load factor is 1/cos(bank), identical for both; rate of turn is g tan(bank)/V, so A's is HIGHER; and with the same lift required at a lower speed, A must fly at the HIGHER lift coefficient.
bXXXo6CYSFCFoJthUmLn: A Timed Approach Procedure requires aircraft to pass a specified point inbound at a previously notified time. This sequences arriving aircraft with precise spacing, allowing efficient use of the approach path without radar.
bYHzgJCSeybRQmeeRZmq: The generator must produce 400 Hz whatever the engine is doing, and frequency is set by rotational speed, so the constant speed drive takes the varying engine input speed and delivers a fixed output speed to the generator. Voltage is regulated separately by the field excitation.
bYc6z9dHPVOaufkjpQRC: A healthy adult at rest has a pulse of about 60-80 beats a minute, within a normal range of 60-100. It falls with physical fitness, and rises with exertion, emotion, stress, illness, fever and hypoxia - which is why it is a sensitive but entirely non-specific indicator.
bZqLBEwZl0zFGJ4uyfU3: The LP turbine drives the fan through the LP shaft. If the shaft breaks, the turbine loses its load instantly while the gas flow through it continues, so it accelerates without limit - and an N2 governor does not see it, because the HP spool is still running normally. It is why LP shaft failure protection is fitted.
bZsTxUGCAfH9oSCLuMaD: Divided attention is the rapid alternation of attention between activities (1) and, in its practical form, running an automated motor programme with little conscious input while devoting conscious attention to something else, such as flying while making a radio call (2). Statement 3 describes selective attention, and statement 4 describes delegation, which is task management rather than attention.
baDEItYK3td1U5nTPq84: VHF direction finding is done entirely by the ground station, which measures the bearing of the aircraft's transmission. The aircraft therefore needs only a normal VHF transmitter-receiver in the 118 to 136 MHz band - a receiver alone would give the ground station nothing to take a bearing on.
baZiHQkhCkEg4WbTtVWs: The fuel prediction works from the performance model and the wind, using the wind entered or the wind it is computing from the difference between air and ground speed. It has no way of knowing that the gear is down, the flaps are jammed or a panel is missing - those are non-normal drags the crew must allow for themselves.
baab61Qe894BW6xNU1e1: The computer applies the position error correction from a stored calibration, which no simple instrument can do, and it puts the results on a data bus so that every system needing altitude, airspeed or Mach gets the same figures from one source. Hysteresis is a mechanical instrument fault and gimballing errors belong to gyros.
bbLvcHPmMoSRwze9yihb: Both statements are false. The gust load factor is inversely proportional to wing loading, so a lighter aeroplane suffers a LARGER load factor - decreasing mass increases the gust load. And the gust alleviation factor increases as altitude decreases, so descending makes gust loads WORSE, not better. The practical lesson is that turbulence penetration is most punishing when light and at low level.
bcD5UpihVdErdRnJRIUd: Runway edge lights are white, not blue. Blue lights mark taxiway edges. On instrument runways the last 600 m of runway edge lights may show yellow to warn of the approaching end. Red lights are used for runway end lights.
be70uZ8GaiEHfUyBiZSB: The cooler deals with the heat the oil has picked up inside the engine, so it sits in the return line, downstream of the scavenge pump and upstream of the tank. Cooling the oil before it entered the engine would achieve nothing.
bey3sVTUaaGgZlrkdJy5: V1 must be at least VMCG, the minimum control speed on the ground: below that speed the rudder cannot hold the aeroplane straight after an engine failure, so a decision to CONTINUE would be meaningless. bocnZyr77hjpCNZosd0P: A cold engine needs an over-rich mixture because only the lighter fractions of the fuel vaporise, so extra fuel is needed to get a combustible mixture at the plug. At idle the surplus fuel also carries heat away, and a lean idle would run rough and hot.
boi8dEePtRr9rnjO1ALt: By definition a downburst is classed as a microburst when its damaging outflow spans 4 km or less; anything larger is a macroburst. boqhM3L2InXlYhYC2Bk2: A jet stream is a very flat feature: typically a few thousand feet deep (about 2 km) but 100-300 km wide, so the depth-to-width ratio is on the order of 1:100. brH1F26Zn5Z7Q4kIeH2u: ICAO Annex 17 requires States to provide assistance to aircraft subjected to unlawful seizure, including provision of navigation aids, air traffic services, and permission to land. Catering and refuelling may be provided but are not part of the core obligation.
brOlsD4t7KwIi7Yz8h61: The computer compares the speed of a braked wheel with a free-rolling reference and works out the slip ratio, then modulates the brake pressure to hold that slip near the value which gives the most friction. Brake temperature and tyre pressure play no part in the control loop.

brykwHK46IgCMpiI6WI7: Speaking between the lines leaves the sender room to retreat: nothing definite was said, so if the outcome is bad he can claim to have been misunderstood. bs2GALWUjzXQskdi5njl: The 60% rule applies at the alternate exactly as it does at the destination: a turbo-jet must be able to make a full stop from 50 ft above the threshold within 60% of the landing distance available on a dry runway. bsIKrijDGttIpZ6AxERy: ICAO Doc 8168 (PANS-OPS) specifies that turning departures provide track guidance within 15 km of the departure end of runway. Beyond this distance, en-route navigation takes over.

bsui9q1llFTWQGNdLV6K: A descent or climb conducted in a holding pattern is termed a shuttle. A procedure turn is a manoeuvre to reverse direction on the approach track, and a racetrack pattern is used for course reversal, not for gaining or losing altitude in holding.

btAncvjHyNmZxLBBins8: Because a Lambert's chart convergence closely matches earth convergency over the band of latitude it covers, a great circle plots very nearly as a straight line, and for normal flight planning it is treated as one. bttKghwm0CKVX2rOVwNu: The value of a briefing is in what is specific to this flight: what about today's weather, aircraft, route or crew composition will need particular coordination, and how the crew will handle it. bu91EGasWBOPiBq5OBIL: JAR-OPS 1.515 requires a turbo-jet to be able to land within 60% of the landing distance available - at the destination and at any alternate. The turbo-propeller figure is 70%, and if the runway may be wet the required distance increases by a further 15%.

c0Lx0sehK2ZNQXyjsBpJ: Low range radio altimeters work in the 4200 to 4400 MHz band, a wavelength of about 7 cm, which gives a small aerial and the resolution of a foot or two needed for the flare and for Cat II and III minima.
c0re3LfhuJ5utwYWD9H9: Flutter is a coupling between the structure's twisting and the surface's inertia, so it is attacked from both ends: a torsionally stiff structure raises the speed at which the coupling can occur, and a balance mass ahead of the hinge brings the surface's centre of gravity onto or in front of the hinge line so the inertia no longer drives it.
c2UNECD3CRQNIhys4qaN: Between 108.00 and 111.975 MHz, ILS localisers take the ODD tenths and VORs the even ones. 109.15 has an odd first decimal, so it is a localiser. 110.20 and 108.25 have even first decimals and are VOR, and 112.10 is above 111.975 and therefore VOR territory entirely.

c3ehKMu4ng7Nsi2Xn3We: Datalink clearance services cover the departure clearance, delivered at the gate, and the oceanic clearance, obtained before the boundary - both long, error-prone messages that are far better sent as text. Take-off and landing clearances are time-critical and stay on voice.

c5O9c41dlYFU0WXLf5KN: Cosmic radiation exposure rises with altitude and latitude, and above about 49,000 ft the dose rate is high enough that individual records must be kept and the crew's cumulative exposure monitored - which is why the requirement bit on Concorde and applies to business jets operating in the upper levels.

c6IOVOPkciFRE0g54cfa: Alcohol and drugs potentiate each other: the sedation from an antihistamine or a tranquilliser taken with alcohol is greater than either alone, and often greater than the sum. c6Pp4swNCLAxr2oSdBbl: A prepared action plan brings the necessary information within easy reach (1), primes the crew for a situation that may develop so it is recognised early (2), and sets out a framework and a probable strategy for handling it (4). c82Ttnn7N22IayiyHA9j: Feedback is the return message telling the sender what was actually received, which is what closes the loop and turns transmission into communication. c8KEmCt7AiH2Z29epnnk: Phosphate ester fluids such as Skydrol are deliberately fire resistant, which is why they are used, but they attack skin and are seriously damaging to the eyes, as well as stripping paint. Gloves and goggles are required when handling them.

c9K3INAVqtFvXf1KPfQy: Exhaust gas temperature is measured by thermocouples - chromel-alumel junctions producing an emf proportional to the temperature difference between hot and cold junctions. cHcZwI6wpi3Ii3VOthie: NAT MNPS airspace runs from 27N to the North Pole (90N), between FL285 and FL420. The southern boundary at 27N takes in the whole of the organised track structure and the routes to the Azores and the Canaries.

cI0Mti0ETVoxWj3VKQnC: The pressure drop in the venturi and the evaporation of the fuel can cool the induction air by 20 to 25°C, so air at +20°C and high humidity can be taken well below freezing inside the carburettor. Carburettor ice is therefore a warm, humid day hazard as much as a cold one.

cKs9MO8yWcsaOSSTyaZk: The crash axe requirement steps up when the maximum approved passenger seating configuration EXCEEDS 200. At exactly 200 seats one is required; at 201 the second becomes necessary.

cMELhmXqtO8A3TWlBPXw: Aircraft wishing to conduct IFR flight within advisory airspace but not using the advisory service shall nevertheless submit a flight plan and notify changes to the ATS unit providing that service. This ensures traffic information can be passed to other aircraft.

cMV7NFtSz8E8Y9BAbft6: TCAS II shows where the intruder is relative to the aeroplane and, if the conflict develops, issues a resolution advisory - but only in the vertical plane, because it knows the intruder's altitude accurately and its bearing only roughly. It never commands a turn.

cOvEzqu77LiV1b9z922Y: A magneto generates its own primary current from a rotating permanent magnet, so once the engine is turning the ignition needs nothing from the aircraft. The engine will keep running with the master switch off, and the propeller must always be treated as live.

cQZBVuL8adiEZk5KlncC: What a passenger may and may not carry is set out in the ICAO Technical Instructions for the Safe Transport of Dangerous Goods by Air, which give effect to Annex 18. The IATA regulations restate them for industry use and the Flight Manual has nothing to say on the subject.
cQbOKdswEL9LxKlrjtWg: A synchroscope compares the speed of one engine with another and shows which is running faster and by how much, so the throttles can be trimmed until the pointer stops. Matching the speeds removes the slow beat of the propellers or fans going in and out of phase.

cRXZi9kycMdybtv7nl9I: The extinguisher table steps up every 100 seats above 200: four for 201-300, five for 301-400, six for 401-500, seven for 501-600 and eight beyond 600.

cRuFOahjEgszkg7cQA1M: Time = distance / groundspeed = 43 / 510 hours = 0.0843 h, which is about 5 minutes. A quick mental check: at 510 kt the aircraft covers about 8.5 NM per minute, and 43 / 8.5 is about 5.

cSeJeMc0LJgZu00fBIG5: Under JAR-FCL, single-pilot single-engine class ratings are valid for two years until the pilot reaches age 40, then one year thereafter. The shorter validity at older ages ensures more frequent proficiency checks.

cbZc5pLk1zATHi4OG3pu: An unaided inertial system drifts at roughly 0.5 to 2 NM per hour of flight, the error growing steadily because the small residual sensor errors are being integrated. It is why long flights mix the inertial position with radio or satellite updating.
cbfmHUhr12EEM8fbzhsu: Leaning reduces the fuel delivered for the same airflow, so the mixture becomes weaker. The air side is untouched - the throttle butterfly alone determines how much air the engine receives.

cckKZpJRbPlNHBIqmSBQ: The local speed of sound depends only on temperature: LSS = 38.94 x root(T in kelvin) = 38.94 x root(218) = about 576 kt. TAS = Mach x LSS = 0.80 x 576 = about 461 kt. The flight level is a distractor, since it affects the answer only through the temperature that goes with it.

cjFhWNHK7qwyp96Thx25: Typical polar front jet core speeds are 60-100 kt in summer and 150-200 kt in winter, with 250 kt considered exceptional. cmcoMRuwQejFiNvZrVg3: Category IIIA is flown to a decision height lower than 100 ft, or with no decision height, with an RVR of not less than 200 m. Category IIIB takes the RVR down to 75 m, and Category II stops at 300 m.
cpDF7jIf2A3nsZM7KAUN: Runway threshold identification lights (RTIL) are flashing white lights placed symmetrically about the runway centreline at the threshold. They help pilots identify the runway threshold during approach, particularly in low visibility.
cpwjUuYV65FJkVKXikLl: With QFE set, the altimeter datum is the official aerodrome elevation, so it reads zero on the ground and shows height above that reference - but only in ISA conditions, since the instrument is calibrated to the standard atmosphere and non-standard temperature introduces an error. cqCjQU2VO339cT981tmm: Induced drag coefficient is proportional to CL squared divided by aspect ratio, so INCREASING aspect ratio reduces it directly. css3cAAmo6fJ8K4tPE9A: Habit and experience are what make an expert fast and efficient: the situation is recognised and the response runs automatically. cw4JbhdoxJh9wDCRM08e: In Class B airspace above 10,000 ft AMSL, VMC minima per ICAO are 8 km visibility with 1500 m horizontal and 1000 ft vertical distance from clouds. The 'clear of clouds' provision for Class B applies only below 10,000 ft.
cwFMM25AEviKvsiivxan: Over-the-counter does not mean flight-safe: antihistamines, decongestants, cough preparations and analgesics can all cause drowsiness, blurred vision or reduced concentration, and the illness being treated may itself be disqualifying. cwVwEy6oW4CJTpXFbxU4: The earth distance is 10 x 60 x cos65 = 254 NM = 469 600 m = 46 960 000 cm, and 3.75 inches is 9.525 cm. Scale = 9.525 / 46 960 000, which is about 1 : 4 900 000, so approximately 1 : 5 000 000. Convert inches to centimetres first and remember the cosine of latitude.

cy9KMMcYNxDezmOSwkfU: Alternate extension is mechanical: a handle or crank releases the uplocks and the gear falls under its own weight, assisted by the airflow, and locks down. It works with no hydraulic power at all, which is the whole point of it.

cyxcOJPJ2686sc1vpR5d: Detonation comes from high pressure and temperature in the cylinder with time for the end gas to explode: high manifold pressure supplies the pressure, and low RPM gives the slow-burning charge the time. That is why running at high boost and low RPM is specifically prohibited.

czMeBtHgLhSpZnVQy21v: Energy comes from the macronutrients - carbohydrates, proteins and fats. czVdmFyGqdQtJhfC78Lw: The human ear responds to vibrations from roughly 16-20 Hz at the low end up to about 20,000 Hz in a healthy young person. Below that range the vibration is felt rather than heard, and the upper limit falls steadily with age and with noise exposure.

d0TmB3k3jGiAW3i8ZvyF: Opening the throttle raises the manifold pressure and the engine tries to speed up, so the governor senses the overspeed and coarsens the blades. The extra power is absorbed at the same RPM by a larger blade angle - which is exactly what a constant speed unit is for.

d1B4xrIWD5d9pUAiBa3R: A high cost index tells the computer that time is expensive relative to fuel, so it chooses higher climb, cruise and descent speeds. The flight is quicker and the fuel burn correspondingly higher; a cost index of zero would give the maximum range speed instead.

d34AbtbngoIQo2hwEeFi: Machines to be paralleled must produce the same voltage and the same frequency - and be in phase - before their breakers are closed, otherwise heavy circulating currents flow between them. Current is a result of the load sharing, not a condition for connecting.

d6zj5IrmS2hzoAlrB93a: The bootstrap sequence is compress, cool, expand: the cold air unit's compressor raises the pressure, the secondary heat exchanger removes the heat of that compression, and only then does the air expand through the turbine, where it does work and cools sharply.
d8W3ujcjVcypvTlq4X2w: Holding, approach and departure procedures are published in the ENR (En-route) section of the AIP. There is no MAP section in the current ICAO AIP structure; the three parts are GEN, ENR, and AD.

dA4kK5Jd6HszdeXD6TV6: Statement 1 is the correct definition: psychosomatic means mental or emotional stressors producing genuine physical illness - ulcers, hypertension, headaches, skin conditions. dAHHyBT9Ok3vZvsSk5Ip: Fair weather cumulus (cumulus humilis) is the visible top of convective thermals, so its presence means the air below and within cloud level is convectively active and therefore turbulent - a familiar bumpy ride for light aircraft on a sunny afternoon. dCIoJH2ZRi2sfOy1dLfc: Heavy freezing rain (+FZRA) is the most severe airframe icing condition there is: large supercooled drops strike the airframe, run back and freeze as dense clear ice well aft of the protected leading edges, at accretion rates that overwhelm de-icing systems. do5uSBHVByBRdXilC8do: CO2 displaces oxygen and leaves no conductive residue, so it covers class A solids, class B liquids and electrical fires. Burning metals are the exclusion: they supply their own oxygen and react with CO2, and they need a dedicated class D agent.

elM5ivg85irBl5eNFzFX: Lift and drag are defined relative to the RELATIVE AIRFLOW, not to the airframe or the horizon: lift acts perpendicular to it and drag parallel to it, opposing the motion. emuYsoJVoajcOEb8BWCN: An EPROM is an erasable programmable read-only memory: in normal operation it is read only (1), and being non-volatile it retains its contents with the power off (4). Erasing it needs a deliberate process - ultraviolet light or a programming voltage - not simply switching off.
enU0OKeOknj7B3xYMSOS: The PET is where the time to continue equals the time to return, which gives X = D x H / (O + H). enZbg2TqBS6JrmVuy8if: Boots work by cracking off ice that has already formed, so they are de-icing devices and are used cyclically. They cannot anti-ice - inflating them continuously would simply hold a distorted profile - and they must not be operated before enough ice has accreted to be shed.
enw5kRXdsYkmn3zP0Zt4: With no frame of reference the brain attributes the eye's own small involuntary movements to the light, so a fixed star appears to move - and a moving light in the night sky is read as another aircraft. eoWmKVMkvZvsRGJvMPzl: With the outflow valve open the cabin air escapes freely, so the cabin altitude climbs towards the aircraft altitude - the rate of climb indication goes positive, the cabin altitude increases and the differential pressure collapses. eonJU90WbrD2k0Nekz84: Carbon monoxide and altitude attack the same thing - the amount of oxygen delivered to the tissues - so their effects compound. eoneAWHqfcmHZA5hRWd1: Static directional stability is the tendency to weathercock into the relative airflow. In a sideslip to the right the airflow arrives from the right, striking the fin and generating a sideforce that pushes the TAIL to the left - which swings the NOSE to the right, into the sideslip, until the slip is eliminated. The fin's long moment arm behind the CG is what makes this restoring moment effective.
eoqL5gJ1UcGVZHtA5LMe: A reclined seat reduces the vertical distance between the heart and the brain, so less pressure is needed to perfuse the head and the G level at which blackout occurs is raised - which is why fighter seats are tilted back. eot8ok0Q0NfltWTr4KZZ: Fail-safe works by having more than one load path: members are mounted in parallel (1), the design is deliberately redundant (5), and if one member fails the others share the load until the damage is found (6). eozJ6EUqe2nomUd1SHrW: The angle on the bow doubles from 45 degrees (relative bearing 315) to 90 degrees (relative bearing 270), so the range when abeam equals the distance run: 3 minutes at 180 kt = 9 NM. Abeam is also the point of closest approach, so 9 NM is the minimum distance.
ep4ET7eYh7hMbWrl1hzk: ICAO Annex 1 limits the credit for synthetic flight trainer time towards the 1500-hour ATPL requirement to a maximum of 100 hours, of which not more than 25 hours shall have been acquired in a flight procedure trainer or basic instrument flight trainer.
epxDVLzXgNBqC50XOVZc: In altitude hold the autopilot is using the elevator to keep the aeroplane on the level, so speed control is left entirely to the thrust. The autothrottle therefore holds the selected indicated airspeed by moving the thrust levers.
eqGvJEQzLnnqDmOCnEJE: Category II runs from a decision height below 200 ft down to no lower than 100 ft, with an RVR of not less than 300 m. Below 100 ft you are in Category III, and 200 ft is where Category I stops.
eqJsirbGVVkW1fs9SWCX: Power depends on the mass of charge burnt and on how much work can be extracted from it, and as the aeroplane climbs the exhaust back pressure falls while the manifold pressure is held constant. The engine therefore breathes out more easily and the power rises slightly - about one per cent per thousand feet.
eqtTQK9IksEri3rLP9wP: All four reasons hold. The condition being treated may itself be disqualifying (1); reduced pressure, dehydration and low humidity can alter how the body handles a drug (2); side effects such as drowsiness or blurred vision threaten flight safety directly (3); and drug effects persist after the last dose, which is why a grounding period follows the end of treatment (4).
eqvcw6X7Uee7MO4gkqlR: Position error arises from the way the flow around the fuselage disturbs the pressure at the static port, and that flow pattern is governed by Mach number, changing sharply as the aeroplane approaches the transonic range. Corrections are therefore tabulated against Mach and configuration.
er8CDFYWkMHIrZ5i02K8: Wavelength is the speed of light divided by the frequency: 300 000 000 divided by 300 000 gives 1 000 metres. That is why NDB aerials are long wires and why the beacons are in the kilometric band.
erkFD0vjeh10uAQlHFrw: Runway threshold identification lights (RTIL) are flashing white lights placed on each side of the runway threshold. Their purpose is to help pilots identify the threshold during approach in reduced visibility conditions.
esbH2nJDKlqo0NnvqPXs: The bootstrap sequence is compress, cool, expand: the cold air unit's compressor raises the pressure, a heat exchanger removes the heat of that compression using ram air, and only then does the air expand through the turbine, where it does work and cools sharply.
esdqAbHEJN7e2cSIH6qQ: At a constant Mach number the true airspeed falls with the falling temperature, and the density falls faster still, so the dynamic pressure and with it the calibrated airspeed decrease. It is why a climb is flown on a fixed CAS first and on a fixed Mach above the changeover.
esjBz9enUJ13wQpHN46s: Below 10,000 ft MSL, turbine-powered and all other aircraft are limited to 250 kt IAS. This standard speed restriction reduces closing speeds in busy terminal airspace and applies in most jurisdictions.
et0r0aPFEwf0H37FYedA: The requirement is that the remaining rafts can still take everybody if the largest one is lost - which is entirely possible, since a raft may be destroyed in the impact or be on the side of the aeroplane that is burning or under water. Simply matching raft capacity to the number on board would not survive that.
etePu822mYJjnBEJclaI: Calibrated airspeed has already had instrument and position errors removed, so only the compressibility correction remains before equivalent airspeed is reached. Density is the correction that takes EAS on to TAS.
eu9X65HcJXAffVHbCKBz: The Gestalt laws describe how the brain organises raw sensory input into meaningful wholes - separating figure from ground, and grouping elements by proximity, similarity, continuity and closure. They explain why perception is constructive and therefore why it can be confidently wrong, which is the basis of most visual illusions.
evxdqb8DgGr5nXTe2gsW: The condenser absorbs the current that would otherwise arc across the opening points, so the primary circuit is broken cleanly and the magnetic field collapses far more rapidly. A faster collapse means a higher induced voltage and a hotter spark in the secondary - and the points survive.
exPJSU8paYlqVI1pPCIb: Weather radar works around 9 GHz, a wavelength of about 3 cm. That is short enough to be reflected by raindrops - which is what makes weather detection possible - and to give a narrow beam from an antenna that will fit in the nose.
exWtfwAIQYo4Em3G30zm: QFF reduces the station pressure to sea level using the ACTUAL temperature, while QNH uses the ISA profile. Air 10 C colder than ISA is denser, so the real column between the airfield and sea level weighs more and QFF gains more pressure in the reduction than QNH does. QNH is therefore lower than QFF: less than 1016 hPa. (Cold air, QFF above QNH; warm air, the reverse.)
exyHytfS1OcDvoS5pF6f: Rate of turn is the rate at which the heading is changing, quoted in degrees per second - rate one being three degrees per second, a complete turn in two minutes. It is closely related to the yaw rate but is defined by the change of heading, whatever the bank.
ey8FWbpAWqC5p7SZdZzw: Early hypoxia shows as euphoria with loss of judgement (1), loss of concentration (3) and visual disturbance, since the retina is affected early (4). Breathing rate increases rather than decreases, because the falling oxygen level provides a weak respiratory stimulus - and it is the absence of any strong air hunger that makes hypoxia so insidious.
eyLM8KLg20XXQKxhb7DA: A plain jet delivers fuel in proportion to the square root of the pressure drop, so the mixture richens as the airflow increases. The diffuser, or air bleed, admits air into the discharge tube to break up the fuel and weaken that tendency, holding the fuel flow proportional to the airflow.
eyu2QkUlah6FsbFXuR7a: The maximum zero fuel mass is a structural limit set by the wing root bending with no fuel in the wings, so it is a fixed figure published in the manual. It does not change with what is loaded - what changes is how much traffic load can be carried before it is reached.
ez4yz61j5kyzLbDYCkQt: Hot air anti-icing is simple and reliable, with few moving parts (1), and because it prevents ice forming at all the aerofoil profile is maintained (2). It is not free, though: every kilogram of bleed air costs thrust, so the fourth statement is wrong.
ezRHIpAfZpIUyrBjVjrM: MIFG is shallow fog: a layer less than 2 m deep over land, so it lies below the observer's eye level. Horizontal visibility is measured at eye level, above the fog layer, so a reported visibility of 5000 m is entirely consistent with shallow fog beneath. The temperature and dewpoint both being 2 C confirms saturation at the surface, exactly as expected. The report is valid.
ezV3FtQlTIOPnv155aoe: Propulsive efficiency is best when a large mass of air is given a small increase in velocity, and at high subsonic speeds the bypass engine does exactly that - better than a propeller, which runs into compressibility trouble, and far better than a pure jet, which throws a small mass out very fast. Lower noise and lower fuel burn follow from the same thing.
ezWoEBVubgysRnVpvJHZ: In severe turbulence the aeroplane is squeezed from both sides: a gust can raise the load factor toward the structural limit, while the same gust can raise the angle of attack toward the stall. That is why a turbulence penetration speed is published - it sits between the two. Extending flap is exactly the wrong response, because the flap-extended structural limits are much LOWER than the clean ones.
ezjgTxbeu67qyJ9t6BWD: The commander must produce the documents carried on board to an authorised representative of an Authority within a reasonable time of the request. The documents exist to be inspected: there is no right of refusal, no automatic 48 hours and no need to seek the operator's permission first.
f0JXZVT6AXbncbizfMNz: On a Lambert the scale error depends only on how far the latitude is from the standard parallels, so scale is constant along any parallel and varies along a meridian: correct at the two standard parallels, too small between them and too large outside them. Over a typical chart band that variation is under 1 percent, which is why the chart is treated as constant scale in practice.
f0RfDO6zSkvP7QYrbljl: Anti-icing fluid is designed to shear off progressively during the take-off roll, and the requirement is that the aerodynamic surfaces are clean of it by ROTATION - the moment the wing must work at a high angle of attack. Brake release is far too early: the fluid is deliberately still in place then.
f0TwduwW0caBnniUYyO2: The computer needs to know the aircraft's attitude (1), its air data - altitude, speed and Mach (3) - and what the crew have asked for, which comes from the mode control panel (4). The annunciator panel is an output: it displays what the computer has decided, and tells it nothing.
f1B9y49lu6zyEja64Y89: Transport aeroplanes use multiple disc brakes: a stack of rotors keyed to the wheel alternating with stators keyed to the axle, squeezed together hydraulically. Stacking the discs gives an enormous friction area and heat sink inside the wheel, which no drum or single disc could match.
f1j6MnjwXV9Q8RzoFAne: At a fixed flight level the pressure is fixed, so colder air is denser air. The same calibrated airspeed - the same dynamic pressure - is then produced by a lower true airspeed, which is why a cold day gives a lower TAS for the same indication.
f2M81rnFtlD9LrDBamtj: The estimated total time in block 16 of a VFR flight plan is the estimated time from take-off to arrival overhead the destination airport. It does not include taxi time — that would be block time, which is a different measurement.
f2Scre8GVzNkjsQgFY2e: The gas charge makes the accumulator compressible, so it absorbs the surges produced when a selector opens or an actuator hits its stop, and smooths the ripple from the pump. That damping saves the pipework and the seals as much as the energy storage saves the pump.
f2hDxaSCsazMHoyyo45L: On a polar stereographic chart the convergence between the local meridian and the grid datum meridian is the full change of longitude. Between 140E and 054W that is 166 degrees, and applying it to a true course of 330 degrees gives a grid heading of 330 + 166 = 496, that is 136 degrees.
f2qk1EbMiL2GxbmlriXv: The feed box, or collector cell, is a small compartment around the boost pump kept full by flap valves, so that the pump inlet stays submerged even when manoeuvring or with a low tank contents. It is what prevents the pump from ingesting air and losing suction.
f3Vc9ORPBrW7fWNhrcJx: The vestibular apparatus of each inner ear consists of the three semicircular canals, sensing angular acceleration, and the two otolith organs - the saccule and the utricle - sensing linear acceleration and gravity. Ventricles are chambers of the heart and brain and have nothing to do with it.
f3eDJolW2PjZOs6SJcrw: ICAO groups aircraft for wake turbulence by maximum certificated take-off mass: HEAVY at 136 000 kg or more, MEDIUM from 7000 kg up to but not including 136 000 kg, and LIGHT at 7000 kg or less.
f49XR5zM7qdR3DlEFoR6: Variation is the angle between true north and magnetic north. Deviation is the angle between magnetic north and compass north and is a property of the individual aircraft, drift is the angle between heading and track, and compass error is the two errors combined.
f4U5pA2vpxXxAJptkQ58: On a sunny afternoon the sea breeze blows from sea to land, and since the runway lies parallel to the coast that flow is essentially perpendicular to the runway - a pure crosswind. Final is flown in the opposite direction, so the sea is now on the right, and the crosswind comes from the right.
f4knn8QhXU1xwq0gL3Fu: Longitudinal static stability depends on where the centre of gravity lies relative to the neutral point: ahead of it the aeroplane is stable, and the further ahead, the stronger the restoring moment. The distance between them, as a percentage of MAC, is the static margin.
f4uPuM5gvHtGHIW2qQex: Accommodation is produced by the ciliary muscle encircling the lens: when it contracts the suspensory ligaments slacken and the elastic lens becomes more convex for near vision; when it relaxes the lens flattens for distance. Age stiffens the lens so it can no longer respond, which is presbyopia.
f5F66DbbeJtvBQFiam2c: The flight deck door must be lockable from WITHIN the compartment, so that control of access stays with the flight crew. A door that could be locked or unlocked from the cabin side would defeat the purpose of having it.
f5JstyNOGvMcwNAessRo: Calibrated airspeed has already had instrument and position error removed, so what remains between it and TAS is compressibility, which gives EAS, and then density, which gives TAS.
f5bygPYrhlaSLR7gXu1c: Excess power can be spent in only two ways: gaining height or gaining speed. Accelerating at a constant power setting therefore diverts energy that would otherwise have gone into the climb, so both the rate of climb and the angle of climb fall while the acceleration lasts. This total-energy view is why a level acceleration segment is scheduled after take-off rather than trying to do both at once.
f5pcfJIeqAoUPiuLxMqz: The maximum ramp mass is a structural limit - what the gear and airframe will take standing still and manoeuvring on the ground - so it is a single fixed figure in the flight manual. It is the performance-limited masses that vary with temperature and altitude.
f618BlqOfb3KkqP2hK4u: In the JAR-25 EFIS colour code white denotes present, current status data and scales, while magenta is reserved for SELECTED targets such as the heading bug and selected altitude. Green marks present-status dynamic data, cyan is used for sky and non-active information, and amber and red are warnings.
f61Ttmsi9fyGxPrPI4Fb: Both methods produce a frequency proportional to speed: a three-phase tachometer generator, whose output frequency is read rather than its voltage, or a phonic wheel whose teeth induce pulses in a magnetic probe. Frequency measurement is immune to line resistance and voltage drop, which is what makes it accurate.
f6kqf9lxDt1fgD6oLr9e: A hold fire is fought by starving it of air, so the cargo compartment VENTILATION is what is switched off. Shutting down the whole air conditioning system or the pressurisation would penalise the entire aeroplane without isolating the compartment that is burning.
f6u31u6SfpnPGbm1VoAc: The air is at its coldest immediately after the expansion turbine, and that is where the moisture condenses out, so the separator is placed there to collect it before the air reaches the cabin. Separating earlier would leave the water still in vapour form.
f77amPWgnEjXrSNfvz3T: The MEL is a dispatch document: it governs whether the aeroplane may set off with the item inoperative, so it is consulted before the flight begins. Once the flight is under way a failure is handled by the abnormal and emergency procedures in the Operations Manual and by the commander's judgement, not by the MEL.
f84orr3RKytpvD1mj2Bw: The false statement is that acute fatigue generally has psychological roots. Acute fatigue follows a period of physical exertion, mental effort or emotional demand and is relieved by a normal rest. It is chronic fatigue, accumulated when recovery is repeatedly incomplete, that acquires a psychological dimension and produces the apathy and indifference described.
f935FYXgz9W3vfhBWgCS: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are the two gases the body actually exchanges and depends on: oxygen for the oxidation that releases energy, carbon dioxide as the waste product whose blood level also drives breathing. Nitrogen is inert and matters only when it comes out of solution, and carbon monoxide is a poison rather than a physiological gas.
f9IXSKa29sxQvz3JChKR: The international nautical mile is defined as exactly 1852 metres, chosen as the mean length of one minute of latitude on the earth's surface. 1609 metres is the statute mile, which is the trap: statute miles appear in visibility reports and in some performance data, so the two must never be mixed.
fBHjTBe4mfObb3I8KIxH: Mach buffet is the airframe shaking produced by shock-induced separation, and a shock wave cannot exist until the LOCAL airflow reaches M1.0 - which by definition is the critical Mach number. So Mach buffet is uniquely a supercritical phenomenon. Speed instability occurs at low speed behind the drag curve, and Dutch roll is a lateral-directional oscillation independent of Mach number.
fC0iKTfdlVaJm05IDi1o: ICAO Annex 1 requires a CPL applicant to complete at least 10 hours of instrument instruction time, of which not more than 5 hours may be instrument ground time (simulator). This is the minimum for the commercial licence.
fCWxQt6uyXBpb3niAw9c: The receiver has the right and the duty to control when the exchange happens: he may decline or defer a communication if he is too busy (3), and he should stabilise or complete a demanding manoeuvre before entering a discussion (4). Giving the sender's situation priority regardless of workload, or acknowledging only when in doubt, would destroy both the flying and the communication loop.
fCiqmuCYvDizZ7SbLf1b: The heat exchangers are cooled by ram air, and there is none on the ground and little at low speed. The pack cooling fan draws air through them in those conditions and is shut down in the cruise, when ram air does the job on its own.
fDoy7rDkmyBtsSB47PWC: Life jackets are put on inside the aeroplane but inflated only once OUTSIDE it. An inflated jacket makes it hard to get through an exit, and if the cabin floods it will pin the wearer against the ceiling - which is why several ditching accidents have killed passengers who inflated early.
fEN97ySfzA9jujCJ3YFG: Behind the drag curve, below VMD, induced drag dominates and rises steeply as speed falls - so slowing down requires MORE thrust, not less. This reversed relationship makes the speed unstable: any decay increases drag, which decays the speed further unless thrust is added promptly. It is why an approach flown too slow demands continuous thrust attention.
fEriIfTZUcfnJXKGmGFk: The torque link joins the fixed upper part of the strut to the sliding lower part, so the oleo can telescope freely but the piston, and with it the wheels, cannot rotate about the strut axis. On a steerable nose gear the steering actuator works through the same linkage.
fFCKgtN39suiRavbi9lU: ICAO grades icing as light, moderate or severe. Severe means the accretion rate is such that de-icing and anti-icing equipment cannot control it and the ice is degrading performance to a dangerous degree, so an immediate change of heading and/or level is required. Moderate makes a diversion desirable, and light needs action only if the encounter is prolonged beyond about an hour.
fFU6BwqhahOY3Skp5FX1: On a Direct Mercator the meridians are drawn parallel, so chart convergency is ZERO everywhere. Earth convergency is dlong x sin(latitude), which is also zero only at the equator. The two therefore agree at the equator alone, and the disagreement grows towards the poles.
fGmxv5VkkqNkWPAH40Cj: Opening the door from outside automatically disarms the slide, so that ground staff cannot fire it accidentally - the girt bar is released as the handle is operated from the outside. From inside, an armed door fires the slide as it opens, which is what an evacuation needs.
fGrtdpE4bUxf8gJZJ2kT: A magnetic sensor is a coil and magnet facing a toothed wheel: each tooth induces a pulse, so the output is an AC signal whose frequency is proportional to the shaft speed. The indicator squares those pulses and counts them, which is why the reading is unaffected by line resistance, voltage drop or temperature.
fHYS5C8Hx77EoBGFWVjN: The inverted-U means a moderate level of stress is where performance peaks: arousal is high enough for alertness and engagement without narrowing attention or degrading judgement. Stress cannot be trained away, severe stress impairs learning rather than accelerating it, and domestic stress travels with the pilot onto the flight deck.
fHnXFEt0pIgO5P5Ws0iL: The magnetic poles wander and the shape of the field changes from year to year, so charted variation drifts. Whether a particular place sees its value grow or shrink depends on where it lies relative to the moving pole, so the change is published per chart and old variation data must never be used.
fHqT9trbUUPIcXhLXZy0: Turning and acceleration errors both come from the magnet dipping and being displaced, and their effect on the indicated heading vanishes on east and west. Rolling out on 090° therefore needs no allowance at all, whatever the bank angle.
fINcSMrrwRp8UEchGNEK: When SSR is available, aircraft identification can be achieved by observing the pilot's compliance with an instruction to operate the transponder from ON to STBY and back to ON. The brief disappearance and reappearance of the radar return confirms the target.
fIh6xasY15KQVxov94np: A short stroke means a shorter crankcase, a lighter crankshaft and lower piston speeds for the same RPM, so the whole engine can be built lighter - which matters more in an aircraft than the slightly better efficiency a long stroke would give.
fIx8LMf86nxEfNx0WcSN: A normal shock stands perpendicular to the flow, so the airflow does not change direction - it simply decelerates abruptly from supersonic to SUBSONIC. Static pressure, density and temperature all rise sharply across it while total pressure falls, and that total pressure loss is wave drag. An OBLIQUE shock does turn the flow and can leave it still supersonic; an expansion wave accelerates it.
fIzP0SAtlqvGB0nbf7cs: Mixture strength is expressed relative to the stoichiometric ratio of about 15:1 by mass, so a mixture is called rich or weak according to how it compares with that chemically correct value. It is always a mass ratio, since it is the masses that react.
fJlIj2WI5gwQxypA7PAz: A vapour lock is a bubble of fuel vapour in the line which the pump cannot shift, so the fuel supply is interrupted. It forms when the fuel is hot or the pressure low - at altitude or after a hot soak - which is why the boost pump is switched on for those phases.
fJzkbLI0ucABA0Czi0aI: A FADEC has two independent channels and duplicated sensors, so the loss of one input is detected and the control simply uses the other source or a modelled value. The engine goes on running normally, with the fault recorded for maintenance.
fKNCHs2nFSZrWFkOVPhX: Safety matches may be carried on the person only - one small packet. They are forbidden in checked baggage, where a fire could not be reached, and they are not permitted loose in cabin baggage either; the rule keeps the item under the owner's direct control.
fL38fRQz8nysRW8Mjr8E: A runway wider than the pilot is used to subtends a larger angle, so it looks nearer and the aircraft feels lower than it is. The pilot holds off in response, and the round-out is begun too early and too high - with the risk of a heavy landing or of running out of speed above the runway.
fLXTtUpnRPwhqhED1Cro: Dutch roll appears when the dihedral effect (lateral stability) is strong relative to the fin's weathercock effect (directional stability): a sideslip produces a powerful rolling moment before the aeroplane has straightened out, so roll and yaw drive one another in an oscillation. Swept-wing jets are prone to it, which is why they carry yaw dampers. The opposite imbalance gives spiral instability.
fLiE6X3NBoOSaygxoZhB: Climb angle is governed by the excess of thrust over drag, divided by weight: sin(gamma) = (T - D)/W. All three quantities therefore appear. Lift does not enter, because in a steady climb lift merely balances the component of weight perpendicular to the flight path - which is why the question specifies that the required lift exists.
fNYq2K6UhlHscazezEAV: For a turbojet, the landing distance required at destination must not exceed 60% of the landing distance available on a dry runway (70% for a turboprop), with a further 15% added if the runway is expected to be wet. The certified landing distance is measured from a 50 ft screen height, not 35 ft; reverse thrust is normally not credited on a dry runway; and an anti-skid failure lengthens the distance materially.
fOM8jYzGeELcVjJG1nlH: A rhumb line, or loxodrome, cuts every meridian at the same angle, which is why it can be flown on a constant heading. It is not the shortest route (that is the great circle), and on a Mercator it is the straight line while on a Lambert it is the curve concave to the pole.
fOh8mjdQsv5C95eiqI5b: Time = distance / groundspeed = 3560 / 345 = 10.32 hours. The decimal 0.32 of an hour is 19 minutes, so the answer is 10 HR 19 MIN. Converting the decimal part of the hour is where the 10 h 05 and 11 h 02 distractors come from.
fOqJYSz7LnbpAniNP427: A hot wheel fails along the axle line - a fuse plug releases or a tyre bursts sideways - so anyone approaching must do so from the FRONT or the REAR, never from abeam. The same reasoning governs positioning fire vehicles and ground crew after a heavy or overweight landing.
fOvMFt78mPMzVTBVf64d: Laminar flow consists of smooth parallel layers sliding over one another with no mixing between them, so there is no velocity component perpendicular to the surface. That lack of mixing gives low skin friction but leaves very little energy near the wall, which is why a laminar layer separates far more readily than a turbulent one when it meets an adverse pressure gradient.
fPd3AAdLVPucVq6btDXn: With earth rate compensated, the gyro holds its direction and the aeroplane coupled to it flies the shortest path across the surface - a great circle. Following a rhumb line instead would require the heading reference to rotate with the local meridian along the whole route.
fPkFogMnM8qX6Do94PuI: At an isolated aerodrome no alternate exists, so additional fuel replaces alternate fuel: for a turbine-engined aeroplane, two hours at normal cruise consumption computed after arrival overhead the destination, and that quantity includes the final reserve. The 30-minute holding figure is the final reserve alone.
fPlxxhQIPVqFBG8OjQFr: The take-off alternate must be within one hour at the ONE-ENGINE-INOPERATIVE cruising speed in still air, because the case it covers is an engine failure at or after V1 with a return to the departure aerodrome impossible. Using an all-engines speed would put the aerodrome further away than the crippled aeroplane could reach.
fPu8Lf5NpkgoZk2q000S: Wake vortices from a wide-body decay over roughly two to three minutes in typical conditions, which is exactly why the ICAO wake separations are set at two and three minutes. In calm air with no crosswind to break them up they can linger longer, so the minima are treated as a floor and not as a guarantee.
fQATcwJMnRrZzvM0msmf: The tyre speed limit caps the GROUNDSPEED at lift-off, and the lift-off groundspeed is set by the lift-off IAS (a function of mass and configuration) and the wind - not by how quickly the aeroplane got there. A downhill slope shortens the ground run but the aeroplane still leaves the ground at the same speed, so a tyre-speed-limited mass is unaffected. Slope matters when the limit is field length or brake energy.
fQWWUeGoKieS2xZ5Z6an: Track 066 against heading 074 is 8 degrees of port drift, and the groundspeed of 242 kt exceeds the TAS of 230 kt, so the wind is on the starboard quarter. Resolving the vectors gives a wind from due south at about 35 kt, i.e. 180/35.
fQYGtiJIv5v0DDiU0pYp: When two aircraft of the same category are approaching to land, the aircraft at the lower altitude has right of way, but shall not take advantage of this rule to cut in front of or overtake the other aircraft. Safety and orderly flow take precedence.
fQhA6k3QHUPBKuXd8MoF: The mixture control adjusts the fuel side only, so that the ratio of fuel to air remains correct as the air density changes with altitude. It has no effect on the air or the oxygen reaching the engine, which is the throttle's business.
fQjlljze41Jo9KCvSpdK: All five apply. Carbon monoxide is colourless and odourless so there is no sensory warning; it is highly toxic because it binds haemoglobin over 200 times more readily than oxygen; the early symptoms - headache, mild nausea, poor judgement - are vague and easy to attribute to something else; and it accumulates because it is cleared far more slowly than it is acquired.
fRDjRZKzmnxKkAqpcXPY: If a flight lands anywhere other than the filed destination, the ATS unit at that destination must be told within 30 minutes of the ETA there.
