fROskXZyhLgFBGiAbEiF: The operator carries the duty to satisfy itself, on acceptance, that the consignment is not forbidden and is properly classified, packed, marked, labelled and documented - that is what the acceptance checklist is for. The shipper makes the initial certification on the shipper's declaration, and the commander must be informed of what is aboard.
fRSyAZ1PJU2xoE5yXaKA: Above a cabin pressure altitude of 13 000 ft, 100% of the passengers must be supplied for the entire flight time, with no percentage and no grace period. Between 10 000 and 13 000 ft only 10% need be supplied, and only after the first 30 minutes.
fRvhDK0ry54upnJGx2Op: On IFR flights, the altimeter setting change from QNH to standard pressure (1013.25 hPa) is made at the transition altitude during climb. This is when the pilot switches from reporting altitude to reporting flight levels.
fSqIaraDI6UPgCt2tCuJ: The wind from 310 is on the port quarter of the 075 heading, so it pushes the aircraft right and adds a little speed. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 084 and a groundspeed of about 108 kt, i.e. about 9 degrees of starboard drift.
fSxT7WkyDaZJ6M0Hhe7L: In the northern hemisphere air circulates ANTICLOCKWISE around a low, and below the friction layer it also spirals inward. Flying directly toward the centre, the circulation therefore comes at you from the left, and the inflow component - directed toward the centre, i.e. the way you are already going - shows up as a slight tailwind. Hence from the left and behind. Buys Ballot: back to the wind in the NH puts low pressure on your left.
fT6KjKSZrgydetM4sMdA: Mach number is TAS divided by the local speed of sound, and the speed of sound rises with the square root of the absolute temperature. Warmer air therefore means a higher speed of sound, and holding the same Mach number requires a higher true airspeed.
fTNTDPz9uSHgIbPecl5m: The passenger mask is a continuous flow type with a rebreather bag, and the wearer draws cabin air in through it as well as oxygen. That makes it useless against smoke or fumes - it offers no protection at all from what is in the cabin, which is why smoke hoods exist for the crew.
fTUXadarDAVESwn1hM6r: Dumping is required only where the maximum take-off mass is far above the maximum landing mass, so that the aeroplane could not return and land immediately after take-off. Where the gap is small, the aircraft can burn or hold off the difference instead.
fUHKNVIGt45Xi4w4ghoh: The scale is exact at the two standard parallels, too SMALL between them, reaching a minimum at the parallel of origin, and too LARGE outside them. 28N lies between 26N and 48N so its scale is below the stated value, while 24N lies outside and is above it, making the scale at 28N the smaller of the two.
fULU3uCLZpAbBuomrju8: In fog, haze, snow or rain the contrast and texture cues the brain uses to judge distance and closure are stripped out, so speed and distance are misjudged even though objects can still be seen. The instruments are not subject to that misjudgement, which is why they become the primary reference in poor visibility.
fVMCdJ2jqEVeXBNLdfMi: Stress follows the inverted-U, so a moderate level improves performance - eustress - while only excess degrades it. Fatigue has no such beneficial range: it only ever reduces capability. Stress is also distinct from anxiety, which is one possible response to it.
fVTTRYNa1tzMEbyf2cGn: De-icing fluid REMOVES existing contamination and is heated to do it. Anti-icing fluid is a thickened film applied COLD, which must stay in place to prevent new accretion - heating it would thin it and destroy the holdover it exists to provide.
fVltQh8Dc6l73Q6e7DKk: Tiredness reduces the attentional capacity available, so the first thing to go is the ability to keep several matters running at once - divided attention. The tired pilot can still do one thing, but the monitoring, the anticipation and the background tasks fall away, which is why fatigue shows up as omissions rather than as gross handling errors.
fXvQerP04GWnjPUVvbsv: The display convention makes green the engaged or active mode and white or cyan the armed one, so that a glance at the flight mode annunciator separates what is happening now from what will happen at capture. Amber is caution and red is warning.
fYDxqvb9MegWx2XYr0M9: Equivalent airspeed is true airspeed corrected to sea level standard density, so at sea level in the standard atmosphere the correction is nil and the two are equal. Above that, EAS is always the smaller of the two.
fYGi37urBsBDwq4YmEMM: On 21 November the sun's declination is about 20S, so the southern hemisphere is heading into summer and the northern into winter. At 50S the day is long, giving an early sunrise and a late sunset, while at 50N it is short. The sun therefore rises earlier at B, and the difference is hours rather than minutes.
fYU9wNUgVHDgZCutKbqb: Decision-making is a conscious, deliberate selection between possible solutions to a defined problem. That distinguishes it from applying a procedure, which involves no choice, and from a spontaneous or automatic reaction - and it is why decision-making takes time and degrades under time pressure.
fYlp6Q6LVt4c4yhdmxag: The wind from 090 is about 33 degrees off the port bow of the 123 heading, so it gives left drift and a headwind component. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 134 and a groundspeed of about 178 kt. Any option with a groundspeed above the 225 kt TAS can be discarded at once.
fYuxLUDsftKl9QNkMJN5: Colour vision defects are usually partial rather than absolute and the affected person is often unaware of them, since he has never seen anything different. Detection therefore needs specific testing such as Ishihara plates or a lantern test. It is congenital, far commoner in males, cannot be treated, and does not affect visual acuity.
fZSMdjKHZZUIPri8Bg2X: A change from IFR to VFR flight is made on the initiative of the aircraft commander. ATC cannot unilaterally change a flight from IFR to VFR; the pilot must decide when VMC conditions permit visual flight and request cancellation of the IFR flight plan.
faWGBZksLjNEMJq4GbQm: Motivation follows the inverted-U like any other source of arousal. Combined with high stress, excessive motivation - the determination to complete the flight or to prove something - pushes arousal past the optimum, narrows attention and degrades the management of competing demands. Low motivation guarantees nothing, and motivation neither reduces risk nor suppresses illusions.
fbHW8tzBi6ms6FVB8Pf3: Left full rich in the climb the mixture becomes progressively richer as the air thins, so the fuel does not burn completely and carbon deposits build up on the plugs. Fouled plugs, rough running and a loss of power follow - which is why the mixture is leaned as the aeroplane climbs.
fbWRH2LFoPu9ZCCRoeo2: Photochromic lenses darken in response to ultraviolet light, and aircraft windscreens block most of the UV - so in the cockpit they may fail to darken when the glare is worst, and having darkened at altitude they clear slowly on descent, which is the wrong behaviour when approaching a runway at dusk. Fixed-tint, non-polarising sunglasses are preferred.
fbw0B0LsQphfJszUDeIE: CAVOK requires all three of: visibility 10 km or more; no cloud below 5000 ft or below the highest minimum sector altitude, whichever is greater, and no CB or TCU at any level whatever; and no significant weather. Low drifting snow (DRSN) counts as significant weather, so its absence is guaranteed. Cloud above 5000 ft may still be present, and CAVOK says nothing about wind shear.
fc2c4JPFLBI6jRG77SsP: Of the 300 kg/s entering, 250 kg/s bypasses the core, leaving 50 kg/s through it. Bypass ratio is bypass divided by core: 250 / 50 = 5. Dividing the total by the core would give six, one too many.
fc4sdEfoHZSUUzviUUjZ: Windscreens are heated electrically by a transparent conducting film laminated into the glass and held at a controlled temperature. The heat also keeps the interlayer warm and pliable, which is what gives the screen its bird strike resistance - so the heating is used in warm weather too.
fd86g1T1KB7lPKwSiQrj: Two corrections. QNH 1003 is 10 hPa below 1013, so the indicated altitude is 15 000 - (10 x 27) = 14 730 ft. ISA at 15 000 ft is -15C, so -5C is ISA+10, i.e. warmer and less dense, and the aircraft is HIGHER than indicated: adding 4 ft per 1000 ft per degree gives about 590 ft, so the true altitude is about 15 300 ft, closest to 15 280.
fdXNp4EnfipHIYCCb4tD: Three points are the minimum: three scales, one under each leg or jacking point, give both the total mass and the moments needed to locate the centre of gravity longitudinally and laterally. Fewer points cannot resolve the distribution at all.
fdl2bUNj5Qjwh3BSWGPC: Only 6 200 kg of fuel has been burnt, so the landing mass is 93 500 - 6 200 = 87 300 kg. That is above the maximum certificated landing mass of 86 300 kg, so the limit exceeded is a structural one - the landing gear and airframe are being asked to absorb more than they are certificated for, and a diversion is no exemption.
fe9fMaB9M5wfifjTGUXA: QNH is the setting which makes the altimeter read the aerodrome elevation when the aircraft is on the ground there, so that in flight it reads altitude above mean sea level. QFE is the setting which would make it read zero on the apron.
fewS8R7CBjpIN4UYWQA7: Both are leading-edge high-lift devices and both raise the stalling angle of attack, so that is not the distinction. The difference is geometric: a SLAT moves forward on tracks and leaves a SLOT between itself and the wing, through which high-energy air is ducted onto the upper surface. A Krueger flap hinges down and forward from the lower surface, increasing camber but forming no slot.
fg2PZ9tKKUs4jD4mPomw: Stability is determined by comparing the environmental lapse rate - the actual temperature profile of the surrounding air - with the adiabatic rate at which a displaced parcel would change temperature. The ELR is the variable in that comparison and is what a radiosonde ascent measures. The adiabatic rates are fixed constants, and surface temperature or pressure alone say nothing about the profile aloft.
fgTbFUBns0GUlZCdxKhp: The angle of attack of the compressor blades is set by the ratio of axial velocity to blade speed. If the axial velocity grows faster than the blade speed the angle of attack falls, so the blades move further from the stalling angle and the stall margin increases - which is why bleed valves are opened at low RPM to increase the axial flow.
fhv5VlwnrqmS1VHxEKob: Batteries in parallel keep the same voltage - 12 volts - but their capacities add, giving 80 ampere hours. Series connection would do the opposite: 24 volts at 40 ampere hours.
fi32GkoIgzAHCtgtjbgN: Rime ice forms from small supercooled droplets, typically at temperatures below about -10 C. Each tiny drop freezes almost instantly on impact, trapping air between the frozen droplets, so the deposit is white, opaque, brittle and relatively light. It builds forward from the leading edge and, being brittle, is readily shed by de-icing boots - unlike clear ice, which comes from large drops that run back before freezing.
fiatEwEQbP5RDb7MuAPW: Over congested areas of cities, towns or settlements, and over open-air assemblies, a VFR flight must be at least 1000 ft above the highest obstacle within 600 m of the aircraft. Elsewhere the minimum is 500 ft above ground or water, or above any person, vessel, vehicle or structure.
fjSDUUPSK1kokOni01P4: Circling visibility runs 1500 m for Category A, 1600 m for B, 2400 m for C and 3600 m for D. Category A is the slowest group - VAT below 91 kt - so its visual manoeuvre stays closest to the runway and needs the least visibility.
fjjTJqxcsfeEVIzLpfhM: Pressure altitude = elevation + (1013 - QNH) x 27 = 1000 + (25 x 27) = 1000 + 675 = 1675 ft, which the option set rounds to 1680. A QNH below 1013 always puts the pressure altitude ABOVE the true elevation.
fkBbv0tJgV9jd2n6C3sq: Remember ANDS: Accelerate North, Decelerate South, on east/west headings in the northern hemisphere. Accelerating on an easterly heading therefore gives an apparent turn towards the NORTH, and because the indicated heading moves from 090 back towards 000 the card itself turns clockwise.
fktE07Tu36rskcuHtD7A: The wind from 045 is well onto the starboard quarter of the 302 heading, so it both pushes the aircraft left and adds speed. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 286 and a groundspeed of about 156 kt, i.e. about 16 degrees of port drift with 16 kt gained on the TAS.
fl1VY5Cmb0TYmm43Yipu: Item D of the SNOWTAM is the cleared runway length in metres, entered as a four-figure group and completed only when the cleared length is less than the published length. Leaving it blank therefore means the full published length is available.
flH1mTdgPqDhRuTVIn4o: A TRACK is the direction of a line over the ground, so a magnetic track is that direction referenced to magnetic north. The direction of the aircraft's longitudinal axis is its HEADING, which is what the other options describe; heading and track differ by drift.
fleKEJH62Ya1kxJoKsrT: Time = distance / groundspeed = 84 / 120 = 0.7 hours, and 0.7 x 60 = 42 minutes. The near-miss options exist to catch anyone who reads the decimal 0.7 as 43, 44 or 45 minutes.
flyWrxGMhdOahXjjtmyS: Latent errors are built into the system in advance - by design, procedure, training or management decision - and lie dormant until circumstances let them combine with an active error. The delay between the condition being created and its finally causing damage is what makes them so hard to trace and so easy to leave in place.
fn5chaflOoqoyZCOt9lR: Decompression sickness is prevented by keeping the pressure up and the dissolved nitrogen down: avoid cabin altitudes above 18,000 ft, where the risk becomes real (1), keep cabin altitude below 8,000 ft in normal high-level flight (2), and pre-breathe 100% oxygen to wash nitrogen out of the tissues before and during exposure (4). Physical exercise does the opposite, promoting bubble formation.
foc2BZ5XZZVoZNz1fcil: Permanent danger areas and their normal hours are in the AIP, but temporary activations and changes are promulgated by NOTAM, so both sources are needed. A SIGMET carries en-route weather phenomena only, and a radio navigation chart shows the areas but not their activity times.
fpS2G1qefR4bhPA7Sz2G: The earth turns 15° in an hour, so a free gyro whose axis stays fixed in space appears to drift at up to 15° per hour - the full rate at the poles, and reducing with the sine of the latitude to nothing at the equator. This apparent wander is what the latitude nut or the computed correction offsets.
fpbYlSOjMa9FqIW0NQZo: After anti-icing the fluid film is the only protection the aeroplane has, and jet efflux or propeller wash from the aircraft ahead will strip or dilute it, and can melt contamination that then refreezes on cold structure. Both wakes are avoided, never used deliberately.
fpgCkUbZsh48cPqLm3Qq: Bending down during a turn brings a second pair of semicircular canals into the plane of rotation while the first pair is still responding, and the brain reads the combination as violent tumbling in an entirely different axis. The Coriolis illusion is one of the most powerful in flight and has caused loss of control, which is why nothing is retrieved from the floor in a turn.
fpmVI8yiXLu0ONeftl12: Lumbar support preserves the natural inward curve of the lower spine. With that curve maintained, the load is spread evenly across the intervertebral discs; without it the spine flattens and the discs are loaded unevenly at the front, which produces the back pain that comes from long periods in a badly adjusted seat.
fptf7DomAe5nfNyrDV7g: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that the approach lighting system for a precision approach Category II runway has a total length of 900 m from the runway threshold. This is the same length as Cat I; Cat II adds additional elements like inner barrettes.
fpz3dcrG4sUPbXLGQKiV: Useful load is everything above the dry operating mass, which is take-off mass minus dry operating mass: 64 280 - 35 000 = 29 280 kg. The landing and zero fuel figures are there as distractors and play no part in it.
fqSnudJIQp3VKHmCV7iD: The oxygen briefing and demonstration form part of the pre-departure passenger briefing and must be completed before take-off whenever the flight is planned above FL 250. Leaving it until a level is reached would leave the passengers uninformed throughout the climb, when a decompression is entirely possible.
fqgJPhulOTWBSacHIiex: An under-inflated tyre bulges so that the shoulders carry more of the load than the centre of the tread, and they wear accordingly - an over-inflated one wears in the middle for the same reason. The soft tyre also flexes more, runs hotter and aquaplanes at a lower speed.
fqp0rZhO9zarWKEnvXfj: Hypoxia is a serious threat to flight safety precisely because it removes judgement before it removes capability, so the pilot does not recognise it. Compensation fails above about 10,000 ft, effects appear well below 25,000 ft, and nothing about it improves any faculty.
fqtBWI82yU9h4pIoNdGv: Pressure falls exponentially with height, and half the mass of the atmosphere lies below about 18,000 ft - so at 18,000 ft the pressure is roughly 500 hPa, half the sea-level value. That is why the physiological effects of climb are concentrated in the lower levels and why a given gas volume doubles by 18,000 ft.
fr42DJfqdbxY8Gou4O1X: The altimeter is already set to the correct QNH, so there is no pressure error to allow for - only a temperature error. Warm air is the safe case; cold air is the one that kills.
frRjQ9bpsyDyAo88BrEU: Final reserve fuel for a turbine aeroplane is 30 minutes at holding speed at 1500 ft above aerodrome elevation in standard conditions, computed at the estimated arrival mass. The 45 minute figure belongs to piston aeroplanes. Final reserve is a fixed quantity and does not vary with the wind.
frgErpXYV3WcV5HgUw6S: Convective turbulence follows surface heating with a lag. The ground goes on gaining more heat than it loses until mid-afternoon, so thermals are strongest and the convective boundary layer deepest in the early afternoon, typically 1400-1600 local. Before sunrise the surface is at its coldest and the air is stable and smooth, and after sunset the thermals collapse.
frxwSVf8VN70dOHH3Ywj: Reflection is efficient only when the wavelength is comparable with the size of the target, so about 3 cm is chosen to return good echoes from the LARGE water droplets found in precipitation, while passing straight through the tiny droplets of ordinary cloud. That is why weather radar shows rain and wet hail rather than cloud, and why dry snow and ice crystals return so little.
ftgnMZ2wRUUrkupsyBEU: Equivalent airspeed differs from calibrated airspeed only by the compressibility correction, and the size of that correction depends on the speed and the pressure - hence the pressure altitude. Density and temperature would only be needed to go on to true airspeed.
ftxhXRhM5Tywx7cmZD3M: ICAO Annex 2 states that an IFR flight outside controlled airspace shall be flown at a level not below the minimum flight altitude, which is 1000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km of the estimated position of the aircraft.
fuaHVGP6EU9B56zo5Hst: On aeroplanes with fewer than six passenger seats the masses may be taken from what the passengers say, with a predetermined allowance added for hand baggage. With so few people the statistical basis for standard masses does not exist, and a single error matters far more.
fupgaOftxp9xFE0vuXC2: The CS-25 gust envelope pairs a specific gust velocity with each design speed: 66 ft/s at VB (rough air speed), 50 ft/s at VC (design cruising speed) and 25 ft/s at VD (design dive speed). fuyWU2sUqs1kzlfQoDAm: TCAS information can be presented on a dedicated display, combined with the weather radar picture, on an instantaneous vertical speed indicator carrying the traffic symbols and the advisory arcs, or on the EFIS navigation display. All four are in service, and the symbology is the same on each.
fvo9oZ4t0i9eyJ01yb3N: Two features a known distance apart, crossed at right angles, give a measured time over a known ground distance, which is groundspeed. Crossing at right angles gives no information about the direction being made good, so it cannot check track or drift, and a single crossing gives only a position line.
fvqT5aFG2Yw3YpucwWSz: In incompressible subsonic flow, continuity requires area multiplied by velocity to remain constant - so an increasing area means a DECREASING speed. Bernoulli then says the static pressure rises to compensate, which is how a diffuser works. Note that above M1.0 this reverses entirely: a diverging duct accelerates supersonic flow, which is why a convergent-divergent nozzle is needed.
fwSqSbLEqyR8n7QtanHN: ICAO Annex 14 specifies that the centreline and crossbar lights of a precision approach Category I lighting system shall be fixed white lights with variable intensity. White provides maximum contrast against the dark approach environment.
fwgosLx7NuSsix3uSxHw: Wake turbulence separation applies when a lighter aircraft is landing on the same runway in the opposite direction or on a parallel opposite-direction runway separated by less than 760 m from a heavier aircraft making a low or missed approach. The 760 m threshold marks when vortices may affect the parallel runway.
fx2lWlePDOTudwbzZq06: All three are true. Glaucoma damages the optic nerve fibres from the periphery inwards, so the visual field narrows unnoticed (2); central acuity, which is what the person actually uses, is affected only at the end (3); and untreated the process continues to total, irreversible blindness (1). Hence the routine measurement of intra-ocular pressure.
fxihUp1tr1B33GA6tDMp: Two conditions must be met. The water must be deep enough to flood the tread - at least the groove depth, so the grooves can no longer channel it - and the speed must exceed the threshold set by tyre pressure: 9 times the square root of the pressure in psi, which for 8 bar (about 116 psi) gives roughly 97 kt.
fyXgGTdzBc7c3Qkh536R: Wake turbulence category is fixed by the MAXIMUM CERTIFICATED take-off mass, not by the mass on the day, so an aircraft keeps the same category whether it is full or empty. fysXjDVF8cTqm4gcqhfs: Flexible or assumed temperature take-offs are used whenever the runway, mass and conditions allow the aeroplane to go without full thrust (3), and the benefit is a marked reduction in engine wear and overhaul cost (2). fz0lBlGNTKssNhSWxmJC: A spoiler is a plate raised from the upper surface that deliberately separates the flow behind it. fzJegftzLGu5EH1JuLsG: 685 km is 685 / 1.852 = 370 NM, and on a track of 180 that is all latitude change: 370 / 60 = 6 degrees 10 minutes. Starting at 02 20 N and going south, the aircraft crosses the equator and ends at 03 50 S.
fzU5MqE4pcTOWDZ1OT0f: The crossfeed manifold links every tank to every engine, so any engine can be fed from any tank. That is what allows a lateral imbalance to be corrected and the fuel of a shut-down engine to be used by the others.
fzhHp4hZ2ZxrwTNyV079: Hot air is less dense, so the same throttle setting admits a smaller mass of air while the carburettor goes on metering the same amount of fuel - the mixture goes rich. That richness, along with the reduced power, is why carburettor heat is selected off once the ice has cleared, and why the mixture may need releaning.
fzoJweUmmt1soZkqvxx4: Statement 1 is correct: positive static longitudinal stability requires the neutral point to lie BEHIND the CG, and the distance between them is the static margin. The wing's stabilising contribution comes from CG position relative to the aerodynamic centre, not from camber.
g2a2fX4yU5dDjOxBloC6: The organised track system has two validity windows at 30W: the day (westbound) structure from about 1130 to 1900 UTC and the night (eastbound) structure from about 0100 to 0800 UTC. A crossing at 0030 UTC falls before the night system begins, so the flight is outside the validity period of either structure and flies a random route.
g2jED2eDfGIb6RBqVfua: A parcel rising in an unstable layer keeps ascending only while it remains warmer than its surroundings. It stops where the layer becomes stable again - at an inversion, a subsidence lid or the tropopause. The depth of the unstable layer therefore sets the vertical extent of the cloud, which is why a shallow unstable layer capped by an inversion gives fair weather cumulus while a deep one gives cumulonimbus.
g3ENjJuXsFBuCTJy2NL4: Boots are de-icing devices: the crew allow ice to accrete visibly and then select the system, which inflates each tube for a few seconds in sequence to crack the ice off before deflating. They cannot prevent ice forming, and inflating continuously would simply hold a distorted leading edge.
g3NW4xT540CTGEdC5iob: Around a low the air follows a curved path, and in the rotating frame the centrifugal force acts outward, directly opposing the inward pressure gradient force. Less of the pressure gradient force is therefore left to be balanced by Coriolis, so a lower wind speed achieves balance: the gradient wind around a low is SUB-geostrophic. Around a high the centrifugal force acts with the pressure gradient force and the gradient wind is super-geostrophic.
g3coCM8ntVux6kC4pgqK: The passenger mask is a continuous flow type with a rebreather bag, and the wearer draws in cabin air through the ports as well as the oxygen flowing into it. That dilution is acceptable at the cabin altitudes involved and greatly extends the supply.
g3hwhGzR8LOwdpMj5894: A descending parcel is compressed and warms, which lowers its relative humidity, so any cloud droplets it carries evaporate. (Condensation and its heat release belong to the ascending case.)
g4GBq0ihqYFjjIbf7qho: The rate of turn gyro must precess when the aircraft yaws, so its spin axis lies along the lateral axis with its single gimbal along the longitudinal axis. That one degree of freedom is what makes it a rate gyro rather than an attitude reference.
g50XRvSp0ZmZuvAI2ufz: Ground that falls away towards the threshold increases the apparent distance between the aircraft and the surface, so the pilot judges himself lower than he is. Correcting for a height error that does not exist, he flies a higher-than-normal approach and arrives high and fast, with a long landing or an overshoot.
g5VtZwehzy1qikH778yf: Out, the groundspeed is 380 - 60 = 320 kt, so 480 NM takes 1 h 30 min. Back, it is 380 + 60 = 440 kt, so the same 480 NM takes about 1 h 05 min. The total is about 2 h 35 min. Note the round trip is always SLOWER than in still air, because the aircraft spends longer in the headwind than in the tailwind.
g5fRfmeBj3G0EYfTSA36: Barotrauma is tissue damage caused by a pressure difference between gas trapped in a body cavity - middle ear, sinuses, a tooth cavity - and the ambient. It is worst on descent, when the tissue is drawn inwards, and much more likely when a cold has swollen the passages that would otherwise let the pressure equalise.
g5x0X2LUPWnPMe7XUljM: Direct Mercator scale expands as the secant of latitude, so a fixed chart length represents a distance proportional to the cosine of latitude: 90 x cos30 / cos45 = 90 x 0.866 / 0.707 = about 110 NM. Less expansion at the lower latitude means the same chart length covers more ground.
g6R9nwq7PhN5Z356SC6N: The marshalling signal for 'apply parking brakes' is: arms down, palms facing inwards, moving arms from extended position inwards. This is part of the standard ICAO marshalling signals in Annex 2.
g6qpmTRKBrfPtimGHFDt: The radio altimeter transmits continuously, so it cannot share one aerial between transmission and reception: separate transmitting and receiving antennas are fitted, usually flush in the belly, spaced apart to limit direct leakage between them.
g7WPYRl3wd3pChMG1K48: An inertial system starts from a known point, so immediately after alignment its position is very accurate. The small residual sensor errors are integrated with time, so the error grows steadily - typically one or two miles an hour of flight - which is why the position is updated from radio or satellite sources.
g7kpHnEzmCejEE70cbOB: A forward CG demands a large tailplane download to raise the nose, so the forward limit is set by whether the ELEVATOR can still do the job - enough authority to rotate at VR and to flare at touchdown - and, in a mechanically controlled aeroplane, by whether the stick force needed remains within certified limits. Engine thrust and location affect the pitching moment but do not define the CG limits.
g7qUR0f6JSf5H7OoMK7o: Respiration is the whole chain: oxygen diffuses across the alveolar membrane into the blood, is carried by the circulation to the tissues, diffuses into the cells where it is consumed, and the carbon dioxide produced travels back the same way to be exhaled. Nitrogen is inert and is not part of the process.
g7qlsOE9nIswc2oJwpYc: Error is combated by designing out the mechanisms that produce it (1), by training crews to recognise and manage it rather than pretending it will not happen (2), and by improving detection and recovery so an error that does occur is caught before it causes damage (4). Sanctions are counterproductive: they suppress reporting, which removes the very information the system needs to improve.
g8CVY9YoxoRpbHFh5Iwl: V1 is the decision speed: at or above it, the take-off MUST be continued, because the accelerate-stop distance is no longer guaranteed to be available. Below V1 the take-off is rejected. That is the whole purpose of defining V1 - to remove the decision from the moment of the failure and settle it in advance. Rejecting above V1 is a classic overrun scenario.
g8vvgdZ8cOuHzw6Cocl8: An IFR flight may be planned without a destination alternate only if the required weather conditions are forecast to prevail from 1 hour before to 1 hour after the estimated time of arrival - plus the destination having a suitable instrument approach and a defined minimum flight duration. The window is symmetrical, which is what makes the three-hour options wrong.
g9rhYwBU87dQ6KL3zfC3: In winter the two dominant surface anticyclones affecting this region are the Azores high, over the eastern subtropical Atlantic, and the very intense, cold Siberian high over the Asian landmass, which is a winter-only feature driven by radiational cooling of a continental interior. Iceland and north-east Canada are the seats of winter LOW pressure, not high.
g9ur8nLP1NoL7Ot7nQUD: Three extinguishers cover the 61-200 seat band, so a maximum approved configuration of exactly 200 takes three. The count rises to four at 201 and then once per 100 seats.
gAQiMUWgDz0qoR2XfP74: Fog and mist reduce contrast, and the eye reads low contrast as distance, so the runway appears farther away than it is. With the perceived distance greater for the same height, the pilot judges his path to be shallower than it really is, holds off the descent and ends up above the correct profile - a steep approach with a long or fast landing.
gBm1646cMHSq0auYWbe2: A normal shock is an abrupt, irreversible compression: the flow decelerates from supersonic to subsonic and much of its kinetic energy is converted to heat, so static TEMPERATURE, pressure and density all INCREASE across it. Velocity decreases. The only property that falls is TOTAL pressure, and that loss is what constitutes wave drag.
gBxRhttO92y2Vl8N7nEJ: A TREND is a short landing forecast appended to a METAR or SPECI, valid for the two hours following the observation and expressed with BECMG, TEMPO or NOSIG. It covers only wind, visibility, weather and cloud. It is not a stand-alone product: the routine aerodrome forecast is the TAF, and the warning of hazardous en-route conditions is the SIGMET.
gCUQEkE88VjdDPCaZ5E9: ICAO Annex 11 lists ATS units as: Area Control Centre (ACC), Advisory Centre, Flight Information Centre (FIC), Approach Control Office, and Aerodrome Control Tower (TWR). An ATS Reporting Office may also be established.
gD0J2sad9Z3gpNpNQJpX: At 40 000 ft the time of useful consciousness after an explosive decompression is of the order of 12-18 seconds, and explosive decompression roughly halves it compared with a gradual climb to the same altitude because the lungs are emptied by the pressure drop. That is the whole reason for quick-donning masks above 25 000 ft.
gE08YBhlw1nlevYNo7wJ: VLO is the landing gear OPERATING speed - the highest speed at which the gear may be moved up or down, limited by the loads on the doors and the mechanism in transit. The limit with the gear already down and locked is VLE, which is normally the higher of the two.
gFZpIpjYWcu7aqCstiAe: Large jets have plenty of hot air available from the engine compressors, so leading edges are anti-iced thermally, with bleed air ducted through piccolo tubes inside them. It prevents ice forming at all, unlike boots, which allow it to form and then break it off.
gFcpungS5qpRQulVIreA: With a heading of 226 and the wind from 110, the wind is on the port quarter, so expect right drift and a tailwind component. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 235 and a groundspeed of about 533 kt, i.e. 9 degrees of starboard drift. Only one option pairs right drift with a groundspeed above the TAS.
gG70MJcFGIjxH9zLOFMB: Feedback closes the communication loop: the receiver returns what he understood, so the sender can compare it with what he meant. It adds no new information to the message - it simply confirms or corrects the transfer - which is exactly what the readback is for.
gG9fgHEezlToZdWIfdTS: Newton's third law: the engine turns the propeller to the right, so the propeller applies an equal and opposite reaction to the airframe, rolling it to the LEFT. The effect is greatest at high power and low airspeed - take-off - where it adds to slipstream effect and asymmetric blade effect to produce the familiar left-yawing and left-rolling tendency countered by right rudder.
gGmOpOdCqdyeyyRsrTbP: The operational items are the difference between the empty mass and the dry operating mass: 60 120 - 57 320 = 2 800 kg. The maximum traffic load is what the zero fuel limit leaves above the dry operating mass: 72 100 - 60 120 = 11 980 kg. Useful load would additionally include the fuel, so it is a larger quantity.
gH2wPX3XT1z3Le1eHO2d: Skill-based behaviour is automatic and highly practised, so its failures are routine errors - the well-learned sequence running when it should not, or running slightly wrong. Errors of technical knowledge belong to the rule-based mode and creative errors to the knowledge-based mode, where the operator has to reason a novel problem out.
gI6rm2DRiG5ZOcIp6vru: Bypass ratio compares the air that goes round the core with the air that goes through it - external divided by internal. A ratio of 9:1 therefore means nine kilograms bypassing for every kilogram through the core.
gITh3EFxF0GBKYHjuX9v: ICAO defines three progressive emergency phases: Uncertainty phase (INCERFA), Alert phase (ALERFA), and Distress phase (DETRESFA). There is no separate urgency phase in the alerting service framework.
gIah2cJXD585445SJ5ap: Hyperventilation means breathing out more carbon dioxide than the body produces, so the blood CO2 level falls. That deficit is what causes the symptoms: the resulting alkalosis constricts cerebral vessels and disturbs nerve and muscle function, producing dizziness, tingling, blurred vision and eventually tetany. Oxygen levels remain high throughout.
gIuUOErmyiGaPOVHKO9b: A radio position is accurate but only where there is coverage - within DME or VOR range (1) - while an inertial system needs no external signal at all and works anywhere on earth, including mid-ocean (3). Their complementary weaknesses are exactly why the two are mixed in a modern navigation solution.
gJAy2SaVku10UJjC6zwk: ICAO Annex 2 requires notification to ATC when the TAS varies by plus or minus 5% of the value in the flight plan. Track deviations and time estimate errors also require notification but are separate triggers.
gJkMQyV5IHzF2diWsHS6: Acceleration errors are greatest on easterly and westerly headings, where the displaced magnet swings furthest. In the northern hemisphere the rule is accelerate north, decelerate south - so decelerating on an easterly heading gives an apparent turn towards the south.
gJy90oXMmORLarm7X66I: Sleep runs in cycles of roughly 90 minutes, each passing through the light and deep stages of orthodox sleep and ending with a period of REM. Deep slow-wave sleep dominates the early cycles and REM the later ones, which is why a sleep cut short costs disproportionately much REM.
gKfiFwsB8ZISaBzEJrgU: Induced drag arises from the downwash produced in generating lift, and in level flight the lift is fixed at the weight - so the lift coefficient needed varies as 1/V2, and induced drag varies as 1/V2 as well. It therefore dominates at low speed and falls away rapidly as speed builds, which is exactly the opposite of parasite drag's V2 behaviour.
gLQWncJS2pQjAChvTTcR: The danger of a false perception is that it does not feel false - it is as vivid and convincing as a correct one, and the person acts on it with complete confidence. It can also be shared: both pilots can hold the same wrong picture at once, which is why an independent cross-check against the instruments matters more than asking the other pilot whether he agrees.
gLdGmpyiH647v62CKN6E: An occlusion is classed by comparing the two cold air masses. In a cold occlusion the air arriving behind the cold front is colder than the air that was ahead of the warm front, so it undercuts BOTH and the coldest air ends up behind the front. In a warm occlusion the rear air is the less cold of the two and rides up over the air ahead, so the coldest air lies ahead of the front.
gLiJeM3jMKCoBDnWu6y8: The extinguisher requirement is one for 7-30 seats and two for 31-60. A maximum approved configuration of 31 is one seat past the first threshold, so two are required.
gLlr9FKZF97jUaVFXpCH: A vertical gyro - the artificial horizon - must keep its spin axis on the local vertical, and the gravity erector does it: a pendulous device senses any tilt and applies a small torque which precesses the gyro back upright.
gLu6lGukj8fyJlzUmHqc: Calibrated airspeed is what is left after the two errors of the sensing system have been removed - instrument error in the mechanism and position error at the static source. Compressibility and density corrections come later, taking CAS on to EAS and then TAS.
gMZBGKvJDSFuqjyQ9sNl: Creep is the tyre slowly rotating relative to the wheel rim under braking and landing loads. It is watched for by the alignment of a painted mark across the tyre and the rim: if the marks move apart, the tyre is creeping, and on a tubed tyre that will eventually shear the valve.
gNFcEeurGBTdSvyvz1DW: ICAO Annex 14 states that aerodrome lights may be turned off provided they can be brought back into operation at least one hour before the expected arrival of an aircraft. This lead time allows for system checks and warm-up.
gNOFChxPbNFRkzRkzHKU: The gauge is connected downstream of the pressure pump, where the oil is being delivered to the bearings, because it is that delivery pressure which tells the crew the engine is being lubricated. A falling reading there is the first warning of pump or bearing trouble.
gQfCG32BvlVww2UOxD2d: In an alternator the output windings are stationary in the stator and the magnetic field rotates, so the heavy output current is taken straight from fixed terminals with no brushes or commutator to carry it. A DC generator has to do the opposite, taking its output from the rotating armature through a commutator - which is what limits its current and its reliability.
gR0W14RJMGRgYk4QsXlF: A straight line on a Lambert changes true direction by the chart convergence, dlong x sin(parallel of origin), and here the parallel of origin is 53S so the factor is 0.80. The route runs east across the 180 meridian, and by symmetry the track is 090 at the mid-meridian, 172.5E. 175W is about 12.5 degrees further east, giving about 10 degrees, and eastbound in the southern hemisphere the track DECREASES, so it is about 078.
gREYG4noTSJcWe7fDBMO: VAT is the speed at the threshold: 1.3 x the stalling speed in the landing configuration at maximum certificated landing mass (or 1.23 x VS1g where that basis is used). The five categories - A to E - are simply bands of VAT, and they drive the approach and circling minima applied.
gRtAxaObOYGp4CQHE9Jk: The dangerous combination is a much heavier aeroplane landing just ahead with high-lift devices deployed - a high lift coefficient means strong vortices - and a LIGHT crosswind that holds the vortex over the runway rather than clearing it. A strong crosswind disperses the wake, and a lighter preceding aeroplane is not the hazard.
gSL7OID8LpKvcKo2wIFa: The flight data recorder must retain the last 25 hours of recording, so that a whole duty cycle of flights is available and an event several sectors earlier can still be examined. It is the cockpit voice recorder that has the short duration - originally 30 minutes, now two hours.
gSfciLslK0dRV6W8Omuz: ICAO Doc 4444 states that during a radar approach, the aircraft should be directed to execute a missed approach if no landing clearance has been received by the time the aircraft reaches a distance from touchdown. Some references cite 2 NM, others 4 NM depending on the type of radar approach (PAR vs SRA).
gSmob9FjWrnEmNTMMGYp: On climb the expanding middle-ear air escapes through the Eustachian tube almost passively, but on descent the tube acts as a one-way valve and must be forced open. A rapid descent gives it no time, so the rising outside pressure drives the eardrum inwards - which is why barotrauma is a descent problem and why a cold makes it much worse.
gTyBmK1XtVXnPBMXpPjP: ICAO Annex 13 states that the sole objective of accident or incident investigation is the prevention of future accidents and incidents. It is not intended to apportion blame, establish liability, or provide evidence for court proceedings.
gUE9OUsf5foDuMTLe3pu: The atmosphere stays well mixed to about 80 km, so at 18,000 ft the air is still 21% oxygen. What has changed is the total pressure - about half its sea-level value at 18,000 ft - so the partial pressure of oxygen is halved, which is what causes hypoxia even though the percentage is unchanged.
gUcppVadNGrLhY8PzjJp: The GPWS modes cover excessive descent rate (1), excessive terrain closure rate (2) and unsafe terrain clearance with the gear or flaps not set for landing (5), along with altitude loss after take-off and descent below the glideslope. Collision with other aircraft is TCAS's business, and the two systems are entirely separate.
gUe9k2wrBZt8dBGvJtwz: ANDS: Accelerate North, Decelerate South on east/west headings in the northern hemisphere. Accelerating on an easterly heading therefore gives an apparent turn towards the north, and turning from 090 towards 000 is a DECREASE in the indicated heading.
gVO8IQC9FjlWY8lsdId7: A rhumb line cuts every meridian at the SAME angle, so its reciprocal is simply the track minus 180: 230 - 180 = 050. Convergency and change of longitude belong to great circle problems, where the track really does change along the route, and they are offered here purely as distractors.
gWrmSbPIaEiXUfiYoQqo: On a high bypass engine most of the thrust is in the cold stream, so reversing the fan flow alone recovers most of the available reverse thrust. Leaving the hot stream out saves the weight, cost and complexity of a second reverser for a comparatively small loss.
gYDnGV2d4Wcc5i3ZhTl0: Actively watching for the cues that would indicate a situation developing is exactly what maintains situational awareness, since awareness includes projecting the current state forward rather than merely perceiving it. Far from distracting from flying the aircraft, it is what allows a problem to be caught while there is still time and capacity to deal with it.
gYnGVm73rZ0mkL9JSpED: ICAO Doc 4444 states that RNP shall be prescribed by States on the basis of regional air navigation agreements. This ensures consistency across adjacent FIRs and international routes.
gZ4yDOs17XFEyas30r39: Mountain waves require a wind of at least 20 kt at ridge level blowing within about 30 degrees of perpendicular to the ridge, wind speed increasing with height, and a STABLE layer at and just above ridge height. Stability is essential: it makes the displaced air oscillate about its equilibrium level, setting up the standing wave train downwind. Unstable air would simply carry on rising as convection and no wave would form.
gZf7MmFhQsgZAF8CNdyW: A sandwich panel is two thin, strong facing sheets bonded to a light core - honeycomb, foam or balsa - which holds them apart and carries the shear between them. Separating the skins is what gives the enormous stiffness for the weight, exactly as the flanges and web of a beam do.
ga8xs36YpkFofDt9UPLI: Outside the published coverage, normally 35 degrees either side of the centreline to 10 NM and 10 degrees to 25 NM, the localiser radiates side lobes that can produce a convincing but FALSE course, sometimes with the correct ident and no warning flag. That is why an ILS must only be intercepted within the published coverage and the indication cross-checked against a heading or a VOR radial.
gaQWKYTnOXbUSg8VAORt: In air colder than standard the pressure levels lie closer together, so the aircraft is lower than the altimeter says - the instrument over-reads and the true altitude is less than the indicated one. That is why cold weather corrections must be added to minimum altitudes.
gapLOaQdrWz3Qgcs7ZB8: Three minutes applies where the following aircraft begins its take-off roll from an INTERMEDIATE part of the runway - or of a parallel runway less than 760 m away - because it starts inside air the preceding aircraft has already disturbed. Displaced-threshold and opposite-direction cases attract two minutes.
gar9yU7j0RKwrPhqDDAK: A summer cold front over Central Europe undercuts warm, moist, unstable air steeply, triggering cumulonimbus with tops far above FL100. Inside a CB the updraughts and downdraughts can exceed 3000 ft/min side by side, giving severe turbulence. FL100 is right in the most active part of the cell. Stratus and nimbostratus belong to a warm front and give far less turbulence.
gb6KaqRSdfjcseubh13r: The fuselage is destabilising in pitch: at a positive angle of attack the pressure distribution along a slender body produces a moment that tends to increase the angle further. The wing may be stabilising or destabilising depending on CG position, and the tailplane is strongly stabilising - large enough to overcome the fuselage and leave a net positive static margin.
gblEgXA0ZHmpTeVI5Vhh: With no surrounding frame of reference the brain attributes the eye's own small involuntary movements to the light itself, so a fixed star or distant light appears to drift or manoeuvre. Pilots have followed such a light believing it to be traffic; scanning rather than fixating breaks the illusion.
gd70EIaggpilEOuMQmft: Cabin altitude is the pressure inside the cabin expressed as the altitude at which that pressure would be found in the standard atmosphere. It is what determines how the occupants feel, which is why it is presented that way rather than in millibars.
gd9H0n7bvb8nrPE0Vv0T: ICAO Annex 1 requires ATPL applicants to have at least 200 hours of cross-country flight time, of which 100 hours shall be as PIC or co-pilot performing PIC duties under supervision. These thresholds ensure adequate navigation and command experience.
gdBsBPqnNFZWiMosLPGJ: The heading channel of a three-axis data generator uses a gyro constrained to one degree of freedom, whose spin axis is held vertical, so that it responds to rotation in azimuth alone. The other two axes are covered by their own sensors, which is what the three-axis arrangement means.
ge0Qnq4Qwj73TMT2F6rl: The turbocharger's turbine sits in the exhaust stream and is driven by energy that would otherwise be wasted, which is why it costs so much less power than a mechanically driven supercharger. The compressor on the same shaft then boosts the induction air.
ge3pAefsgCpWGqOoLDSv: In an unpressurised aeroplane, above a pressure altitude of 13 000 ft everyone on board - crew and 100% of the passengers - must be supplied for the entire flight time. Below that, in the 10 000-13 000 ft band, the requirement drops to flight deck occupants plus 10% of the passengers after the first 30 minutes.
gedgJ9pftO0mzi7ZXwiV: The flux detector goes in a wingtip or the fin because that is the point furthest from the engines, generators, wiring looms and ferrous structure that produce deviation. Note the wording: the aim is to REDUCE deviation, not to eliminate it, since no position on an aircraft is completely free of magnetic influence.
geh1jHjGKUZRGGiCSlif: Retracting flap reduces camber and therefore reduces the lift coefficient at a given angle of attack. If alpha is held constant, the lift simply falls below the weight and the aeroplane sinks. The correct technique is to allow the aeroplane to accelerate, or to raise the angle of attack, as the flaps come in - which is why flap retraction is scheduled against speed rather than done arbitrarily.
gg7IUDRJc4w9OxnPkDV9: During a visual approach in Class C controlled airspace, ATC continues to apply separation with all traffic — both IFR and VFR. Class C provides separation service to all participating flights.
ggEIncIJ1NnC3n6viO6u: The drive is disconnected when its own oil says it is about to fail - low oil pressure or high oil temperature (1 and 3). A generator's electrical misbehaviour is dealt with by the generator control unit tripping the machine off line; it is not a reason to break the mechanical drive.
gghcaEzigySdSWNgFMwt: The PET distance from departure is X = D x H / (O + H). Holding the other terms constant, X varies inversely with the SUM of the two groundspeeds, and it is directly, not inversely, proportional to the distance to go and to the groundspeed back. Endurance does not appear, which is what separates the PET from the PSR.
ghPfPo4jhRMxLRkMQn0d: A great circle needs its plane to pass through the centre of the earth, and through two points there is exactly one such plane (unless the points are antipodal). A small circle has no such constraint, so an unlimited number of planes, and therefore of small circles, can be passed through the same two points.
giVpO0QUjK46WUJsnIUa: Convective (cumuliform) cloud forms wherever a parcel lifted from below stays warmer and less dense than its surroundings and keeps rising - that is, in an unstable atmosphere. The trigger can be surface heating, orographic lifting, frontal lifting or convergence, so it is not confined to summer, to daytime, or to any latitude band. Stable air gives layer cloud instead.
gikFwNTrXoqwJvJEEXxb: Where fuses are used, spares must be carried for in-flight replacement: 10% of the number of each rating, or three of each rating, whichever is the greater. The 'whichever is greater' clause is what protects the aeroplane that carries only a handful of fuses of a given rating.
gjr4e1uJakLESrXBl0O2: At 35,000 ft the time of useful consciousness is of the order of half a minute to a minute for a seated, resting person, and a rapid decompression shortens it because gas is driven out of the lungs and the alveolar oxygen pressure collapses at once. Physical activity would shorten it further, which is why the drill is mask on and no exertion.
gkrpg8CbTK688rf3ibW4: The stress response is a preparation for physical action: adrenaline and cortisol raise heart rate, blood pressure and blood glucose and divert blood to the muscles, so physical capability increases. Mental performance does not benefit in the same way - attention narrows and judgement suffers - which is exactly the mismatch that makes stress dangerous in a job that is almost entirely cognitive.
glKQtrVPBVT0KPIxoO3i: A transformer will not work on steady direct current - only a changing current induces anything in the secondary. The vibrator, or trembler, chops the DC supply into a rapidly interrupted current so that the ignition transformer can step it up to the tens of thousands of volts the igniter needs.
gljFDB73BwrDd2En25Wd: VOR operates in the VHF band, 108.0 to 117.975 MHz, sharing the lower part of that range with the ILS localiser. That gives line-of-sight propagation with none of the sky-wave errors that affect MF beacons. UHF is where the ILS glide path and DME live, and SHF is radar territory.
goDEVvIxfrLts21cdCzP: A float follows the surface of the liquid, so anything that moves that surface moves the reading: pitch and roll attitude (1), accelerations and manoeuvres (2), and temperature (4), since fuel expands and the same mass then occupies a larger volume. Atmospheric pressure has no effect on a float at all.
goHjown0mLAJAnAzvnRW: Taxiway centreline lights (other than exit taxiway lights) are fixed green lights. This distinguishes them from taxiway edge lights (blue) and runway centreline lights (white).
goIktTpgHXs3sDDi9MhP: 2D RNAV navigates in the horizontal plane only. Adding a vertical profile makes it 3D and adding a time function makes it 4D. Reading the dimension count as literally counting planes keeps the family straight.
gocZMbPCbomABc89ejNf: Thrust falls with altitude at a constant EPR because the air is thinner and the mass flow smaller (1), and a given EPR setting still gives the rated thrust on a worn engine, since the pressure ratio reflects what the engine is actually achieving (3). EPR is a ratio, not a pressure difference, and probe icing makes the indicated EPR read HIGH, so the engine is actually producing less thrust than shown.
gojJFkcHVeZ8joWgU8Dw: All six matter. Holdover depends on the type and intensity of precipitation, the ambient temperature, the humidity, the wind, the temperature of the aeroplane's own skin (a cold-soaked wing after a long flight defeats fluid quickly) and the fluid's type, concentration and temperature. That is why holdover is read from a table rather than remembered as one number.
gp0a4UrbZPyFbBw59DR8: The gas charge makes the accumulator compressible, so it absorbs the shock when a selector opens or an actuator reaches its stop, and smooths the pump's ripple. That damping protects the pipes and seals as much as the stored energy helps the pump.
gp0n75oseZlajGiOLCs9: Convert to true first: 020(M) with 25W variation gives 355(T), since west variation is subtracted from a magnetic heading. The island is 30 degrees left of the nose, so it bears 325(T) from the aircraft, and the bearing of the AIRCRAFT FROM the island is the reciprocal, 325 + 180 = 145.
gpSoWIJ4Z3dEWkgh6KE9: Drift down performance is weight-limited, so if the calculated level-off altitude will not clear the terrain, the only way to raise it is to reduce weight - and the only weight available to shed in flight is fuel. Jettisoning must begin at the START of the drift down, so the weight reduction takes effect while the descent is still in progress; waiting until the obstacle altitude is reached would be far too late.
gpaQ5fYTcScSMyqjxGb2: The Minimum Sector Altitude (MSA) provides at least 300 m (984 ft) obstacle clearance within a radius of 25 NM from the navigation facility on which the instrument approach procedure is based.
gpj0L7qz0UEO7TnZinjG: Minimum drag occurs at the fixed angle of attack giving (L/D)max, so Dmin = W / (L/D)max - reduce the weight and the minimum drag falls in proportion. The speed at which that angle of attack is achieved also falls, because less lift is needed: VMD in IAS is proportional to the square root of weight. Both therefore decrease together.
gpsQqjdZLcIMtEDE2Ath: The semicircular canals are part of the inner ear, alongside the otolith organs and the cochlea. The outer ear collects sound, the middle ear transmits it through the ossicles, and the inner ear houses both the hearing organ and the whole vestibular apparatus.
gq8iIdfe7E4CYnvDnzSR: Haste substitutes the prepared answer for the actual situation: the crew applies the decision made at the briefing without checking whether today's circumstances still match it. Preparing decisions in advance is good practice, but it creates exactly this trap, which is why the prepared plan is confirmed against the real situation before it is executed.
gqBkr8s0YjHG2mcWJ0rq: Track 095 against heading 087 is 8 degrees of right drift, and the groundspeed of 130 kt is well below the TAS of 160 kt, so the wind is on the port bow. Resolving the vectors gives a wind from about 057 degrees at 36 kt. All four options offer 36 kt, so the whole question turns on getting the direction, not the speed.
gqcbyuJzXbBBp2FZNQeH: A hot wheel vents its energy along the AXLE line: a fuse plug releasing or a tyre bursting throws material sideways. Fireguards and ground crew therefore approach from the front or the rear and never from abeam, and the parking brake is released with chocks in place so the discs can cool.
grDM5wwUvSGvWPxFOJjX: Both matter. The primary effect may be desirable on the ground but unacceptable in the air - a sedative that works is a sedative that impairs - and the side effects, particularly drowsiness, blurred vision and slowed reactions, are the reason most preparations are incompatible with flying. The underlying illness must be considered as well.
grwbk3wCGHYAjOTrIZnh: The daytime (westbound) organised track structure is valid at 30W from about 1130 to 1900 UTC, so a westbound crossing at 1330 UTC falls squarely inside it. The night-time eastbound structure runs from about 0100 to 0800 UTC.
gs2sXjYmE4LspDF3V1OQ: An expansion wave is an isentropic acceleration of supersonic flow around a convex corner, and static pressure, density and temperature all DECREASE steadily through it. Velocity and Mach number increase. There is no reversal at any Mach number - the monotonic decrease is precisely what distinguishes an expansion fan from a shock wave, across which all three properties rise abruptly.
gs5ufdlHBskZYuKKfh8j: Taxiway edge lights are fixed blue lights per ICAO Annex 14. Blue distinguishes taxiway edges from runway edges (white) and taxiway centreline (green).
gsHMaeDQe2DD3eimtLEx: Composition does not change with altitude, so oxygen is always 21% of the mixture and its partial pressure is always 21% of the total. As barometric pressure falls, the oxygen partial pressure falls in exact proportion - roughly a third of its sea-level value at 30,000 ft - which is the whole basis of altitude hypoxia.
gsPISaxOHmr7Sw0Ikv0Z: An error of 3 minutes or more in an estimate must be reported to ATS without delay. Longitudinal separation over the North Atlantic is measured in TIME, so an estimate that slips by three minutes erodes the separation the controller is applying.
gspnO1Xrs4DlLHbf7Y43: At night, a pilot who observes a ground distress signal should acknowledge by switching landing lights on and off twice, or if not equipped with landing lights, by switching navigation lights on and off twice.
