Heavy rain and hail in mid-latitudes almost always involve ice crystals higher in the cloud.
mFequAm16WqugYFZQ4I1: On a transverse Mercator the cylinder touches the globe along a chosen meridian and its antimeridian, so the scale is exactly correct there and expands away from it. That is why the projection suits narrow north/south strips and why UTM divides the world into 6 degree zones.
mFsI9zamns9FdC7coVFq: The radial is unchanged and the range grows 30 NM in 5 minutes, so the aircraft is tracking straight out on the 211 radial at a groundspeed of 360 kt. Converting to true: track 211 - 31W = 180, and heading 200 compass + 1 deviation - 31 variation = 170. Resolving the 170/390 air vector against the 180/360 ground vector gives a wind from about 110 degrees at about 70 kt.
mHBinx82GTAwpczLOFNN: Around 30% of the fuel's energy becomes useful work in a piston engine; the rest goes out with the exhaust or into the cooling air. It is limited by the compression ratio the fuel will tolerate before detonating.
mHLRsuxDVdfboBtbMYJ0: A LIGHT following a MEDIUM on the same runway, or on parallel runways less than 760 m apart, takes 5 NM of radar separation on approach or departure. 4 NM and 3 NM are not wake minima for this pairing.
mHvp9fwrBauzB0zyoclQ: Calibrated airspeed is obtained by removing the two errors of the sensing system: position error at the static source (1) and instrument error in the mechanism (3). Compressibility takes CAS to EAS and density takes EAS to TAS, so neither belongs here.
mIFmdePybc5ohoek2Cox: The recorder must be running before the aeroplane can move under its own power and must go on until it can no longer do so, so that the whole of every ground manoeuvre and every take-off attempt is captured. Starting at line-up would miss exactly the pushback and taxi events investigators need.
mJ3ftNp1oshJhA7AjasY: ICAO Annex 14: low-intensity obstacle lights on mobile objects should be flashing red or preferably yellow. Yellow makes them more visible and distinguishable from fixed obstacle lights.
mJP6rNv2BnOk0G7w0kxl: Two corrections. QNH 993 is 20 hPa below 1013, so at 30 ft per hPa the indicated altitude is 15 000 - 600 = 14 400 ft. ISA at 15 000 ft is -15C, so -30C is ISA-15, and the aircraft is LOWER than indicated: applying 4 ft per 1000 ft per degree over the height above the station gives about 760 ft, so the true altitude is about 13 640 ft, closest to 13 660.
mK7ENZlFBoo26QgZ3SLW: Maximum lift means flying at the stall, and the critical Mach number is a compressibility limit - neither has anything to do with gliding endurance. The speed for minimum drag is the meaningful aerodynamic reference here: it gives the shallowest glide angle and the greatest distance. (Strictly, the greatest TIME aloft comes at the minimum SINK speed, at (CL^3/CD^2)max, which lies a little below the minimum drag speed.)
mKrZdIz0jssT5knVKO3d: DME works in the UHF band from 962 to 1213 MHz, paired automatically with the VHF frequency of the associated VOR or ILS. Watch the units in the options: the same numbers quoted in kHz would put DME in the LF band, well below even an NDB. 329 to 335 MHz is the ILS glide path and 108 to 118 MHz is VOR and the localiser.
mLM0wUooyJGV2uei8F8u: The initial approach segment commences at the Initial Approach Fix (IAF), not the FAF. The FAF marks the beginning of the final approach segment. The sequence is IAF → IF → FAF/FAP → MAP.
mM8lypHqXkmo1whW4lmh: A thermocouple is a junction of two DISSIMILAR metals - chromel and alumel, for instance - joined at two points, which generates an emf proportional to the temperature difference between the hot and cold junctions. Two conductors of the same metal would produce nothing at all.
mMBX3sFF8VrxBGoyjNzU: The command bar is not a deviation display: it shows the pitch change to make in order to regain and then hold the glidepath, having already combined the raw deviation with attitude and rate information. Flying the bar to the centre satisfies the computer's demand, not the raw signal.
mMQEql22FRwrbNUTZEWg: Alternate extension is mechanical: a handle or crank releases the uplocks and the gear falls under its own weight, helped by the airflow, and locks down. It needs no hydraulic power at all, which is the whole point of it.
mNvRJwlV4xRg1lxGoadc: The sideslip index below the roll pointer is driven by the inertial reference system's lateral accelerometers, not by a mechanical ball. Being electronic, it can also be given a different sensitivity for take-off and for engine-out flight.
mNz23JeZcIo7XBg795P5: The warning must work in every configuration the aeroplane will legitimately be flown in - any normal position of flaps and gear - because a stall is just as possible clean at altitude as it is on the approach. That is why the computer is given the flap position.
mOIJegPFLFyzBCvNVoDw: The FMC computes a radio position from DME/DME where two or more DMEs give good geometry, and falls back to VOR/DME where they do not. DME/DME is preferred because two ranges cross more sharply than a range and a bearing, and a VOR bearing degrades with distance from the station.
mP4CD4KXOcrwJgruPRPe: The resolution advisory is coordinated with the other aircraft's system, which is manoeuvring in the opposite sense; the controller does not know that. The RA is therefore followed and ATC told what is being done, so the controller can stop issuing conflicting instructions.
mPUZOkdEceXglBTKUM2J: The sun can only be overhead where its declination can reach the observer's latitude, and its declination is limited to 23.5 degrees by the tilt of the earth's axis. So 23.5 north or south, the tropics, are the highest latitudes at which the sun ever reaches the zenith, and there it happens on one day a year.
mPdJSTFJ3iWx4yb9s0a4: Only the airspeed indicator uses the pitot supply. The altimeter and vertical speed indicator work from static pressure alone, so a blocked pitot leaves them entirely unaffected - which is precisely how the failure is identified.
mRNR7ut83Sac6pYVSpmQ: At -44C the local speed of sound is 38.94 x root(229) = about 589 kt, so M0.86 is 507 kt TAS and, with 110 kt of headwind, 397 kt over the ground. 420 NM takes 63.5 minutes; five minutes more is 68.5 minutes, needing 368 kt groundspeed, hence 478 kt TAS, which is 478 / 589 = M0.81.
mRajTxRE57jX05xzmYDu: The Eustachian tube runs from the middle-ear cavity to the nasopharynx - the back of the throat - and exists to equalise middle-ear pressure with ambient. It opens readily on climb but tends to act as a one-way valve on descent, which is why blocked ears are a descent problem.
mRiuJRwxxaEO9dkTuhRE: Standard vertical separation applies. The aircraft at FL 150 can expect clearance to descend to FL 140 when the lower aircraft reports leaving FL 140, providing the required 1000 ft vertical separation.
mSEDIxAQFu0YYrwy4h6n: The strainer is placed at the carburettor inlet, upstream of the needle valve, so that any debris is caught before it can reach the float chamber, the needle valve seat or the fine metering jets. A particle downstream of it could jam the needle valve open and flood the engine.
mSHGwzoS97CeV6fLfiW2: A stick shaker vibrates the control column to give an unmistakable tactile and aural warning as the stalling angle is approached. A stall STRIP is a small triangular section fitted to the inboard leading edge to trigger separation at the wing ROOT first, so the resulting buffet reaches the tailplane and warns the pilot while the ailerons are still effective. Both are warning devices; an angle of attack indicator is an instrument rather than a warning.
mSZcVKTqTZdAj0iXTG4j: The Pseudo Random Noise code is a long, precisely known bit pattern unique to each satellite. It does two jobs at once: the receiver identifies the satellite from which pattern it is, and by sliding its own replica of that pattern until the two match it measures the signal's travel time, and hence the range. Being noise-LIKE rather than actual noise is exactly what makes that possible.
mSxhnP2HfFTZ0Qq48VWR: Flap extension raises CLmax, so the stall speed falls - but it also adds a great deal of drag and REDUCES (L/D)max, so the glide angle steepens and the maximum glide distance shortens. Both halves of that statement are correct. Note the corollary: flaps also increase the minimum rate of descent, so they shorten both the distance and the time available in a glide.
mSzINXhAkuntlVEgX6ij: Groundspeed out is 180 - 15 = 165 kt and home is 180 + 15 = 195 kt. Distance from A to the ETP = D x H / (O + H) = 360 x 195 / 360 = 195 NM, so the distance from the ETP to B is 360 - 195 = 165 NM. Note the question asks for the distance from the ETP TO B, not from A.
mT9P9RNxfA3y007MwWRy: All three describe the syndrome correctly. The alarm phase is the adrenaline surge - glucose released, pulse, blood pressure and breathing all up. The resistance phase is sustained by cortisol, which converts fat and protein into glucose to keep the energy supply going. And the exhaustion phase requires real recovery time, since the by-products of the preceding phases have to be cleared.
mTPGZ4H1b891XrvpTjWB: MNPS airspace occupies FL285 to FL420, so an aeroplane without MNPS approval must be planned at FL280 or below. The approval concerns navigation accuracy, so restricting speed or avoiding the track times does not substitute for it.
mU3HTFsZH4CAWvBMf0EF: Halon works chemically, interrupting the chain reaction of combustion rather than smothering or cooling the fire, which makes it extraordinarily effective for its weight. It also leaves no residue and does not conduct electricity, which is why it is used around avionics.
mUMqbKJD1soB94jJq2EY: Levelling is done by the accelerometers: with the aircraft stationary the only acceleration present is gravity, so any component appearing in the horizontal axes shows the reference frame is tilted, and the computer corrects until those components are zero. The gyros are then used to find north.
mUW1PYnsMdiKBzKGFSxW: A chip detector is a magnetic probe in the oil system that captures ferrous debris and, in an electrical version, completes a circuit when enough has accumulated to bridge its gap. Metal in the oil means a bearing or gear is breaking up.
mUr7dIG5ymzhfR4EUlMb: Climbing at a constant indicated airspeed, the falling density means an ever higher true airspeed is needed to give the same dynamic pressure, so TAS increases. The speed of sound is falling at the same time, so the Mach number rises faster still.
mV4KVPNhXdI1Yp19rbX6: The apparent sun is the real sun you can see, and because the earth's orbit is elliptical and its axis tilted, its transits are not evenly spaced. The mean sun is a fiction that moves along the CELESTIAL EQUATOR at a uniform rate so that civil clocks can run evenly; the difference between the two is the equation of time, up to about 16 minutes.
mW0NmQQOkb69cYSx7Yv5: The appraisal that produces stress has two halves: what the situation is judged to demand, and what the individual judges himself able to do about it. Stress arises when the first outweighs the second - which is why the same circumstances stress one pilot and not another, and why competence and confidence reduce stress directly.
mWQijT2pfgT5sarEolip: Reversion is the re-emergence of an older, better-learned habit in place of the current correct one - typically an action pattern from a previous aircraft type. It happens when conscious monitoring of the task is relaxed (1) and when stress strips away spare mental capacity (3). Medium workload is the condition of best performance, not a risk factor.
mWoM47BukOfcMs8sPhwj: Mercator scale expands as the secant of latitude, so the scale DENOMINATOR grows by dividing by the cosine as you move towards the equator: 3 000 000 / cos60 = 6 000 000. The equator therefore has the smallest scale on the sheet, and it is the only latitude at which the stated scale is exact.
mXqDxNha5hMlJZRlKvjD: The pain comes from gas trapped in the gut expanding as the cabin altitude rises, so the remedy is to reverse the cause: descend, which raises the cabin pressure and recompresses the gas. Climbing makes it worse, oxygen does nothing for trapped gas, and the Valsalva manoeuvre addresses the ears.
mY0oLqTTfV8x5SvvUgQ6: The flash point is the lowest temperature at which the fuel gives off enough vapour to flash momentarily when a flame is applied, without going on burning. The fire point, a few degrees higher, is where it continues to burn.
mY2x5nZD0qtSf1rEZ4QQ: Resolve the 200 NM on 240 into components: north/south = 200 x cos240 = 100 NM SOUTH, i.e. 1 40, taking the aircraft from the equator to 01 40 S. East/west = 200 x sin240 = 173 NM WEST, and at this latitude the cosine is essentially 1, so that is 2 53 of longitude, giving 097 07 E.
mYl7owcW67o77akN8ckF: A shell structure carries its loads in the skin, which is efficient in tension, compression and shear over a large area, so it takes bending in both senses and torsion well. Concentrated loads are its weakness, which is why fittings need frames and doublers.
mYviZU1xR9fkGdm3BQYy: Magnetic north at a place is simply the direction in which the HORIZONTAL component of the earth's field points there. It is not a great circle to the magnetic pole, because the field is not a neat dipole, and the field lines curve; this is why variation cannot be computed from the pole's position and has to be surveyed and charted.
mZEd4ZTuT60cJCbTQrFJ: The geostrophic wind blows with low pressure (low contour heights) on its LEFT in the northern hemisphere. A crosswind from the left means the wind vector points across the track to the right, and low heights lie to the left of that vector - which is directly AHEAD of the aircraft. Flying at a constant flight level into progressively lower contour heights means the pressure surface is descending, so the true altitude decreases.
mZFZUFqbswAlD7CXOnup: Lift and drag are simply the components - perpendicular and parallel to the relative airflow - of the single resultant force produced by integrating the PRESSURE DISTRIBUTION over the whole surface (plus skin friction for drag). They are always normal to each other by definition, at every angle of attack, and neither varies linearly with alpha once the stall is approached.
mZguPonPUt0ywoQYu8uw: The rods contain rhodopsin, which is bleached by light and takes time to regenerate, so full dark adaptation needs about 30 minutes and is destroyed within seconds by a bright light. Once adapted the rods give high sensitivity but no colour and poor resolution - and because there are none in the fovea, a faint object is seen best by looking slightly to one side of it.
mZniTNUUrQ4OHhvSMCTL: An emergency changes what the ground needs to know: the automatic dependent surveillance contract is switched to a high reporting rate so that the aircraft's position is updated frequently while the situation develops. It is done automatically, without the crew having to ask.
maQV905A8bzTx1eXRpXY: Very low frequency motion in the range of a fraction of a hertz to a couple of hertz is exactly what the vestibular system responds to, and it is the mismatch between what the balance organs report and what the eyes see inside the cabin that produces motion sickness. It is a sensory conflict, not a mechanical effect on the stomach.
mawk1LgrLyIGWH5z6yMi: The aerial is not at the wheels and the signal takes time to travel the cable, so the raw measurement is not the height that matters. A fixed correction for that residual height and cable delay is applied so that the indication reads zero at main wheel touchdown - which is what the flare and the decision height depend on.
mcTbNbZYOi3stztsxsoD: A marked surface-based inversion decouples the air above it from the surface, so the layer below stays light and often calm while the air just above retains the full gradient wind - a difference that can exceed 30 kt across a few hundred feet. Crossing that boundary on approach or departure produces the sharpest low-level shear, which is why a reported nocturnal inversion with a strong wind above it is an operational warning.
mcjbMnCpjZBxCfUHUzRV: Fuel is a solvent that defats and irritates the skin and is absorbed through it, so the affected area is flushed immediately with copious water to dilute and remove it. Soap is avoided initially because it can help carry the fuel into the skin, and letting it evaporate in place simply prolongs the contact.
mdaC35HC5YNiaDHsN2ux: Acceleration errors come from the pendulously mounted magnet being displaced fore and aft, and the effect is greatest on easterly and westerly headings and zero on north and south. Decelerating on a southerly heading therefore produces no apparent turn at all.
mdrkenO6xqiQzbesiJ3H: The tank unit is a capacitor whose dielectric is partly fuel and partly air, and fuel has a much higher permittivity than air. As the tank fills the capacitance rises, and because the permittivity is related to density the system indicates mass rather than volume.
mdxSGc4QURbmGv1z9YYH: The human ear responds to vibrations from roughly 16-20 Hz at the low end up to about 20 kHz in a healthy young person. Below that range the vibration is felt rather than heard, and the upper limit falls steadily with age and with noise exposure.
mf3oudEkiXGPGbXiP120: The neutral point is the CG position at which the aeroplane has zero longitudinal static stability. Positive stability therefore requires the CG to lie AHEAD of it, and the distance between them - the static margin - measures how stable the aeroplane is. Relative surface areas influence WHERE the neutral point sits, but it is the CG's position relative to that point that creates the stability.
mf50peNnStas8JGUHmKc: Transport wander arises because the aircraft moves over the earth and the local meridian changes beneath it. How fast that happens depends on how quickly the ground is being covered, in what direction, and at what latitude - so ground speed, true track and mean latitude all enter the calculation.
mfT4d5PKNieIM0DY9rz4: ICAO Annex 14: runway lead-in lighting consists of groups of at least three white lights flashing in sequence towards the runway, guiding pilots from the approach path to the threshold.
mg8gxxz0jqV073ARkrlU: Both conditions are needed. The water must be deep enough to flood the tread - at least the groove depth - and the speed must exceed 9 times the square root of the tyre pressure in psi. 16 bar is about 232 psi, and 9 x 15.2 gives roughly 137 kt.
mgEDOQOtuHW81nmi2UDl: Unless the chart says otherwise, a minimum sector altitude is valid within 25 NM of the facility it is drawn around, and it gives 1000 ft of clearance over everything in that sector. Sectors are normally 90 degrees wide but may be divided differently where terrain demands it.
mgFRUPoO4Z5LHq2gk0a6: Build it up in order: trip 5352, contingency at 5 percent of trip = 268, alternate 4380, and final reserve of 30 minutes at the HOLDING flow = 0.5 x 6000 = 3000. The total is about 13 000 kg. Taxi fuel is not included because the question asks for the fuel required AT TAKE-OFF, not at the ramp.
miKazcihIiAlYWkIvJgK: Virtually all atmospheric water vapour - around 99% - is in the troposphere, and most of that in its lowest few kilometres, because the source is evaporation from the surface and because the temperature falls rapidly with height, so the air's capacity to hold vapour drops away. The tropopause acts as a lid on vertical moisture transport, which is why the stratosphere is extremely dry.
mjTFq9htaAZBizqhnoWh: Dihedral INCREASES static lateral stability. In a sideslip the lower wing meets the relative airflow at a greater effective angle of attack than the upper one, so it generates more lift and rolls the aeroplane back toward wings level. It is not the only means to this end - sweepback, a high wing position and keel surface above the CG all produce the same dihedral effect, which is why swept-wing jets often need ANHEDRAL to avoid excessive lateral stability and Dutch roll.
mkVll4feQI12OlwNe12v: JAR-OPS 1.430 requires the operator to account for all five when establishing aerodrome operating minima: the equipment on the aeroplane, the dimensions and characteristics of the runways, the composition and experience of the flight crew, obstacles in the approach and missed approach areas, and the facilities for determining and reporting the weather. Crew composition genuinely belongs on the list.
mlDXsFV4Eo1v5WKTtAHO: The final reserve for a turbine-engined aeroplane is 30 minutes of holding at 1500 ft above aerodrome elevation in standard conditions, computed at the estimated landing mass. It is the fuel that must still be in the tanks on landing - not fuel available for the approach, and not measured at cruise consumption.
mlEsLhVa2BDkwkWOsGB5: The accumulator stores energy: gas is compressed as fluid is forced in, and that stored energy is given back to smooth surges, to supplement the pump during a heavy demand and to work the brakes after the pumps have failed. Fluid storage is the reservoir's job.
mlFUjk5j4HRAyeUZSUKt: Freezing rain gives the shortest holdover: it deposits liquid water on the wing faster than any of the other conditions and dilutes the fluid quickly. Frost is the mildest case, with freezing fog and steady snow in between.
mlaSrQq9IOXStRf0ufyE: 3 800 US gallons is 3 800 x 3.785 = 14 383 litres, and at a specific gravity of 0.79 each litre weighs 0.79 kg, giving 11 364 kg. The 14 383 figure is the volume in litres, not a mass.
mll1LMdfAcgLW4nrmEgM: The tip travels much faster than the root, so the airflow meets it at a much shallower helix angle. Twisting the blade - coarse at the root, fine at the tip - gives every section much the same angle of attack, so the whole blade works efficiently instead of just part of it.
mluoIttVjwSiL39JqjQF: The net take-off flight path may include turns, but the bank angle is limited to 15 degrees up to a height of 400 ft. Above 400 ft up to 1000 ft the limit is 20 degrees, and above 1000 ft it is 25 degrees. Banking reduces the vertical component of lift and hence the climb gradient, so the restriction is tightest where the aeroplane is lowest and closest to obstacles.
mmAmyHtXHLK1mncHqc9g: A tight turn drags the bogie sideways across the ground and the tyres scrub, which twists the wheels hard about the strut axis - and it is the torsion links that have to take that twist. Nothing in flight or in a straight-line landing loads them so heavily.
mmHD0wsMTVbEBoS08iJp: A servo tab and a trim tab are the same physical surface used two ways: the pilot's control run drives it to fly the main surface, and a separate trim input biases its neutral position so the surface settles at a new position with zero stick force. Combining the two functions in one tab is standard, which is why many aircraft carry a single 'servo/trim tab' on the elevator.
mmJzrjuvk91JcUZMI3jB: JAR-FCL establishes separate type ratings based on three criteria, one being that the aircraft has handling characteristics requiring additional training. Certification by manufacturer or non-member state is not a criterion.
mmaSIRuHFdwz3Hcksh0o: Pilot's vertigo is dizziness or a tumbling sensation produced when the central nervous system receives contradictory information - typically the semicircular canals reporting one thing while the eyes and the otoliths report another. It is a sensory conflict rather than a specific illusion, and it is resolved by flying the instruments and disregarding the sensations.
mmhwcIE49v4cpIZoAVO5: Arterial pressure is sensed by the pressoreceptors - baroreceptors - in the carotid sinuses and the arch of the aorta, which feed the cardiovascular control centres. Their position high in the circulation is what lets them correct for a fall in pressure at head level, and their response is what a rapid onset of +Gz defeats.
mmrf1Vee70WkHl645PjP: A two-engined Performance Class A aeroplane with 20 or more seats, without ETOPS approval, may not be further from an adequate aerodrome than 60 minutes at the one-engine-inoperative cruise speed. Smaller Class A twins and Class B or C aeroplanes get 120 minutes (or 300 NM, whichever is less).
mn5scvwFGPd2LouDiQSa: Freezing rain deposits the most liquid water on the surface in the least time, so it dilutes the fluid fastest and gives the shortest holdover. Frost, at the other end, adds almost nothing and gives the longest.
mnPtVMEemJR7qScnJr0W: PET distance from A = D x H / (O + H) = 2346 x 480 / 845 = about 1333 NM, and the TIME to reach it is that distance at the OUTBOUND groundspeed: 1333 / 365 = 3.65 hours = about 219 minutes. The question asks for time, so do not stop at the distance.
mnxWWJaLh0ZEh6kXYOd5: A shell structure carries loads in its skin, which is efficient in tension, compression and shear spread over a large area, so bending in both senses and torsion are all transmitted well. It is concentrated loads that it handles badly.
mo4hgBkvy0hrWUfd5r5h: Higher atmospheric pressure means DENSER air, which improves everything: the wing generates the required lift at a lower TAS so the touchdown groundspeed and landing distance are reduced, and the engines produce more thrust so go-around performance is better. Both effects work in the aeroplane's favour. It is LOW pressure - and high elevation or temperature - that penalises landing performance.
moX5BQEy6SFWVPKj52cg: The carburettor meters fuel against the volume of air passing through the venturi, and that volume does not change with height - but its density, and therefore its mass, falls. The fuel delivered stays the same while the air mass falls, so the mixture goes progressively richer.
moqE4YhD9vOuxZqpYcGr: The circumference of a parallel is the equatorial circumference times the cosine of latitude: 360 x 60 x cos60 = 21 600 x 0.5 = 10 800 NM. Anything LARGER than the equatorial 21 600 NM is impossible for a parallel, which disposes of two of the options immediately.
mqjoyDqL9i1VK1WyoNHS: Variation is an angle between two directions, so its largest possible value is 180 degrees, and values that large really do occur between the geographic and magnetic poles. It is not limited to 90 degrees, and it is certainly not zero at the magnetic equator, which is a line of zero DIP, not of zero variation.
mrGFZlsgZZboWYOyDIQq: The rule is to increase RPM before manifold pressure and to reduce manifold pressure before RPM, so that the engine is never asked to produce high cylinder pressures at low crankshaft speed. That combination is what causes detonation and heavy bearing loads.
ms51iyhDmPmjY2AVgKI7: JAR-FCL class ratings cover single-pilot aeroplanes not requiring type ratings. This includes self-sustaining gliders and other types as determined necessary by the authority.
msCYXzv9wrvo39vnSfA2: Relative humidity is the actual water vapour content of a parcel expressed as a percentage of the amount it could hold at saturation at that temperature. Because the saturation capacity rises steeply with temperature, simply warming air lowers its relative humidity without removing any water at all, and cooling it raises the value to 100% at the dewpoint.
mslAzo6fgPKEYzVgJxpF: Without DME/P the MLS has no precision range, so it cannot support the segmented or curved procedures, or the accurate along-track guidance, that are its whole advantage. What is left is azimuth and elevation guidance down a single straight path, i.e. an ILS-like approach.
mtfboboEr5U4CIJFUg0j: FADEC is the whole control system, not just the box: the electronic engine control together with its sensors, its wiring, the fuel metering unit and the actuators it commands. It is full authority because there is no hydromechanical backup behind it.
mubrN2f5JOTWaZN6MPg1: A tube facing directly into the airflow brings the air to rest at its mouth, so the pressure sensed is the total, or pitot, pressure - static plus dynamic. Dynamic pressure alone can only be obtained by subtracting the static pressure from it.
mvMEKBPZ6tnbv7tUBsDC: The autothrottle moves the thrust levers to hold either a thrust target - a computed N1 or EPR - or a speed target in IAS or Mach. It has no authority to shut an engine down, and it does not disable the manual levers, which move with it and can override it at any time.
mvOnnFjGEzLw8UuqlKVl: The pressure gradient force does start the air moving from high toward low pressure, but as soon as it moves, the Coriolis force - an apparent force arising from the earth's rotation - deflects it, to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern. The two forces come into balance with the wind blowing PARALLEL to the isobars rather than across them. Friction only modifies this near the surface.
mvSTs4qu58ArkSGdD2BV: Trip fuel is the fuel calculated to fly from departure to destination, and that calculation does not change because the captain uploads more fuel. The extra 1885 kg becomes EXTRA fuel; the operational flight plan still shows 4300 kg of trip fuel. Only the block, ramp and take-off masses move.
mvkizXykyOIwAvoUIHMp: The masks must present themselves without any crew action once the cabin altitude has risen to the value at which oxygen becomes necessary, well before the occupants would be incapacitated. The system is designed to fire automatically, with a manual override available to the crew.
mw4y7gorh1qdb7vhzMyo: ICAO Doc 4444: for dependent parallel approaches, missed approach tracks must diverge by at least 30 degrees. This ensures adequate separation during the missed approach phase.
mwNpp6L1ho8ELjOacZa9: Sound intensity is measured in decibels, a logarithmic scale in which every 10 dB represents a tenfold increase in power. Frequency, the pitch of the sound, is measured in hertz or cycles per second, and the curie is a unit of radioactivity.
mwWzjGZYJ1ETSU3KWpiT: The Rome Convention (1952) covers damage caused by foreign aircraft to third parties on the surface. The Tokyo Convention deals with offences on board aircraft. Do not confuse the two.
mwetrqWwMMa8zeYPkhjS: A fire is annunciated at warning level, which means both a visual and an aural indication: the red light tells the crew which engine and the bell reaches them wherever they are looking. Silencing the bell does not clear the warning.
mwhEtBxSazl8z0ngR5uA: An attitude indicator holds its spin axis on the local vertical, so the aircraft can pitch and roll around it while the horizon bar stays with the real horizon. A horizontal spin axis would give a heading or a rate reference instead.
mwj4uhYMIMhgGATOBpif: A spring tab is a servo tab whose linkage includes a spring, so it only comes into play when the hinge moment is large. At LOW speeds the aerodynamic loads are light, the spring barely deflects and the tab moves with the surface as if rigidly attached. At HIGH speeds the loads are heavy, the spring compresses and the tab deflects, acting as a servo tab to keep the stick forces manageable - exactly where the help is needed.
mx0QKsVCvWtM1tnC70wJ: Take the temperature error first: FL100 with an ISA deviation of -15 C gives 10,000 x (1 - 4 x 15 / 1000) = 10,000 x 0.94 = 9400 ft. mxuTJB1Lrsf2EZhg5phV: The flight director computes and displays what the pilot should do to fly the selected path, so that the aeroplane can be flown by hand to autopilot standards. It shows commands, not positions - deviation displays and waypoint information come from other instruments.
my0OLTYXUi78lrys9oFu: On a feathering propeller for a twin the springs and counterweights drive the blades coarse, towards feather, and oil pressure is used to oppose them and drive the blades fine. my6mCPr709HPuL8hl0Zt: ICAO Annex 2: IFR flights over non-mountainous terrain shall maintain at least 1000 ft above the highest obstacle within 8 km. Over mountainous terrain the minimum is 2000 ft within 8 km.
mycJW3q9KfdDvYBucIdT: If an emergency exit is in the flight crew compartment, the door between cockpit and cabin must be latched open during takeoff and landing to ensure passengers can access the exit.
mzTVR7Qwsa9YsmxoFYAD: The rods are more oxygen-sensitive than the cones, so night vision degrades measurably from around 5,000 ft - long before daylight acuity is affected and well below the altitude at which anything else shows. mzX5nEUb0M0de1BHtrHy: In an isothermal layer the speed of sound is constant, so Mach number follows the true airspeed. Descending at a constant CAS into denser air, the TAS falls, so the Mach number falls with it.
n2cxEJixCFoZ8QWgti9V: In steady level flight lift must equal weight, so at a constant IAS the dynamic pressure is fixed and the lift COEFFICIENT cannot change - the aeroplane simply flies at a lower angle of attack with the flaps out. n2to0C43us9NzbUQJCdZ: Take the drift out first, then the variation. Left drift means the track lies to the LEFT of the heading, so the true heading = 192 + 5 = 197. Then magnetic heading = true heading minus east variation = 197 - 7 = 190.
n3vhoaHcHp4TJCOwS1ki: Disorientation happens when the senses disagree and the pilot resolves the conflict in favour of his bodily sensations rather than the instruments. n4U7jS7snB4SKCgBtUpq: The carburettor meters fuel against the volume of air, but the density of that air falls with altitude, so the mixture would go progressively richer if nothing were done. The mixture control lets the pilot take fuel out again to restore the correct fuel to air ratio by mass.
n4xpcC8M1aOjJ1y9PjpV: Vortices sink below the generating aircraft's path and then drift downwind, so a wind from the left carries them to the RIGHT. Staying to the left - the upwind side - and above the preceding aircraft's path is the only combination that avoids both the sink and the drift.
n6GRPqDmoMnIW54sLw7u: Leading-edge ice reduces CLmax and, critically, lowers the angle of attack at which the wing stalls. During the ground run and the subsequent climb the angle of attack is lower and the margin correspondingly greater.
n6MZ9CfqkDoBcm7m0IDT: At holding speed the aeroplane is at (L/D)max, so the thrust required equals W/(L/D)max - directly proportional to weight. n7hSvE3WZmu6myn38BOI: Cabin air comes from the engine compressors, and it arrives hot enough that the problem is cooling it rather than heating it. Heating is done simply by adding some of that hot bleed air, through a trim valve, to the cold air leaving the packs.
n8XuYqkjqHGwvzeCP74Q: The two positions share the longitude 073W and the aircraft is the more southerly, so it lies due SOUTH of the VOR, a true bearing of 180 from the station. n8a0G898QXEx5Hjjivxa: Anhedral - wings angled downward from the root - reduces static lateral stability, because in a sideslip it lessens or reverses the effective angle of attack advantage the lower wing would otherwise gain. n8d6UtlLUCMrPDh6gBdS: A toothed wheel turning past a magnetised probe induces one pulse per tooth, so the pulse frequency is directly proportional to shaft speed and the electronics simply count it. n9UqQeEzezu058FH0efZ: Wind speed increases with height through the troposphere because the horizontal temperature gradient that drives it accumulates with altitude (the thermal wind). Above it in the stratosphere the wind falls away again.
nAKRblqqSnnPQwVhcSJF: The constant of the cone is the sine of the parallel of origin, which lies midway between the standard parallels. The mean of 07 40 N and 38 20 N is 23 degrees, and sin23 = 0.39. That same constant converts change of longitude into chart convergence anywhere on the sheet.
nBB5PrTCoaUyHJfphg6A: A bird strike, and any bird hazard, is the subject of a bird strike report to the Authority - the data feed that drives aerodrome bird control and engine certification standards. nBMkSBVD24aALhIDHwSV: ICAO Annex 11: the lower limit of a CTA shall not be less than 700 ft AGL (approximately 200 m). This provides minimum separation between surface operations and the CTA.
nBV0MO3EhpAdBsKo13T1: Variation is the angle between true and magnetic north at a place, and it is published as isogonals - lines of equal variation - on charts. Applying the variation to a true heading gives the magnetic heading; deviation then takes it on to compass heading.
nBZzaDdFiFcavRCgaG0Q: An INS produces track and groundspeed from its own accelerometers, with no air data at all. nBa5rPjRHRgQpJit60LY: In a spin the ailerons must be held NEUTRAL: at the very high angles of attack of autorotation an aileron input aggravates the rotation rather than opposing it, because the down-going aileron on the rising wing simply deepens that wing's stall. nC9D3PDlQHxV9HoBncNL: Stress arises from the appraisal of a demand against one's perceived resources, so having handled the situation once shifts that appraisal: the pilot now knows it can be done and how. The same event therefore produces less stress next time, which is precisely why simulator exposure to difficult situations is valuable.
nCYGiBt5t8lROJQO7iPS: Recent experience is three take-offs and three landings as pilot flying within the preceding 90 days, on the type or in an approved simulator of the type. Six months is not a JAR-OPS interval, and a count of six is not the requirement.
nD5vxiakPgDBGIds7ZGa: The wind from 205 is on the port bow of the 250 heading, so it pushes the aircraft right and takes a little speed off. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 252 and a groundspeed of about 223 kt, i.e. about 2 degrees of starboard drift.
nDwotTzBQyQ9JvbEukvm: A base turn is a turn between the outbound track and the intermediate/final approach track where the tracks are NOT reciprocal. A procedure turn has reciprocal tracks.
nEKKumThfEmEDbw3FnKW: Both matter. nEW2EQ27rrLZQkTeAP6t: The seat-of-the-pants sense is proprioception: pressure receptors in and beneath the skin reporting the force pressing on the body, together with stretch receptors in muscles, tendons and joints reporting limb position. nEexRBs3yj7EDhicoI5U: For the same capacity a nickel-cadmium battery is significantly lighter than a lead-acid one, and it also holds its voltage better under heavy load and survives more charge cycles. Its electrolyte is a caustic alkali, and it costs more, not less.
nFmQf0mCo8eTd0tstZmY: The altitude alerting system does two things: it warns as the aeroplane approaches the selected altitude (1), and it warns again if it subsequently deviates from it (3). Ground proximity, excessive descent rate and configuration warnings all belong to the GPWS.
nFuEYj43tjO1P3pTUsyk: Below 10,000 ft, non-safety related cockpit activities are prohibited. This sterile cockpit rule ensures flight crew focus on critical phases of flight including takeoff, landing, and low-altitude operations.
nGlGiavGOMjR43VT6p54: Below design speed the axial velocity falls faster than the blade speed at the front of the compressor, so the front stages meet the air at too high an angle of attack and stall first, while the rear stages are choked. nGq9d0KgwpH5iUuUT06M: ICAO Annex 2: when common language is not possible during interception, the intercepted aircraft should use 'CAN NOT' to indicate inability to comply. This is a standard interception phrase.
nGsgyRM6vW1Lux19yf8f: Short-term memory is limited in both dimensions: about seven items, held for roughly 10-20 seconds unless rehearsed. nGtxMhdsDrncuoeIEFm6: Variation is an angle between two directions, so its largest possible value is 180 degrees, and values that large really do occur in the region between the geographic and magnetic poles. The magnetic equator is a line of zero DIP, not of zero variation.
nGuhtFxBrcpQYlYQO7ZF: Mach number is computed from dynamic pressure divided by static pressure, so the machmeter needs only a pitot and a static input. Temperature cancels out of the relationship, which is why a machmeter needs no temperature probe while a true airspeed computation does.
nH79jbla8cnsodXN4cBf: Maximum level speed is reached at the high-speed intersection of the thrust available and drag curves - the point where the maximum thrust the engines can produce is exactly consumed by the total drag, leaving no excess to accelerate further. nHMxbNySSUKB3C27vGQ4: Optimum altitude is by definition the pressure altitude at which specific range - nautical miles per kilogram of fuel - is at its MAXIMUM for the current weight. nHnsxwxxdz2TPWKA2ZeG: PSR = E x O x H / (O + H) = 9 x 435 x 385 / 820 = about 1838 NM. The 1760 NM to R plays no part, and note the PSR here lies BEYOND R, which is quite possible: the endurance simply allows the aircraft to fly past R and still return to Q.
nHqyQGPvOrO3Z3jLepXm: Electrical heating is used where the area is small and the power modest - pitot heads, static ports, angle of attack vanes and windscreens - and it is used as an anti-icing device, preventing ice forming at all. nI1k0EZFD2wkzy5BzRE4: One degree of latitude is 60 NM anywhere on earth, which is 60 x 1852 = 111 120 m = 11 112 000 cm. Scale = 6 / 11 112 000, which is about 1 : 1 850 000. Along a meridian the answer never depends on latitude, which is what makes this the easiest scale problem of the set.
nJ8NdGIPVr0uidUST6Cm: Showers require convective cloud with strong updraughts and limited horizontal extent - towering cumulus and cumulonimbus - which is why shower precipitation begins and ends abruptly and varies rapidly in intensity. nJbGsq2osRXYmH1aw9hD: Anti-collision strobes reflecting off cloud produce a rapid, bright flicker in the cockpit that is disorienting, can induce nausea and in susceptible individuals can trigger a seizure. nJiGsjNr8zD8fjUznxkV: The line drawn midway between the upper and lower surfaces from leading edge to trailing edge is the MEAN CAMBER LINE. nKss1oBqKa3ujLAMWKcP: The vertical speed indicator compares the static pressure now with the static pressure a moment ago, using a calibrated leak, so what it really measures is the rate at which static pressure is changing. nL6BECO55MSHq1sJgyls: A rhumb line cuts every meridian at the same angle, and a parallel of latitude cuts every meridian at 90 degrees, so every parallel is a rhumb line. Only the equator is also a great circle, because only its plane passes through the earth's centre.
nLFRHxwcFKhRZXM4lsyR: An AC tachometer generator has no commutator, so none of the brush noise of a DC machine appears in the signal (1), and it generates its own output, so the indication does not depend on the aircraft supply (3). Its weakness is that line resistance does affect the reading.
nLiKvGIV2GlwtMZYRKt9: Tidal volume is the air moved in one quiet breath and is about 500 ml in an adult. nM1VrjH5ReFHN4pX1DAS: The flow control valves hold the mass flow into the cabin steady whatever the engines are doing, which guarantees the ventilation rate and keeps the outflow valve's job manageable. Pressure control itself is done on the way out, by the outflow valve.
nMRo5R2Kujpg7RTvUR3M: The container's base is 0.5 x 0.5 = 0.25 m². At 4 000 N/m² the floor will take 4 000 x 0.25 = 1 000 N, and with g at 10 m/s² that is a mass of 100 kg. Floor limits are a pressure, so the smaller the footprint the smaller the mass allowed.
nMU2jtnjBD13qIPX1CRd: Protection goes where ice would be dangerous: the engine intakes (1), the windscreen (2), the pitot probes and water drain masts (4) and the wing leading edges (5). nMj639OuIsrx9wZktaBj: The flux valve senses the direction of the earth's field and feeds it to the error detector, which compares it with the gyro's own heading. Any difference is passed to the torque motor, which slowly precesses the gyro into agreement - the slaving loop.
nN1uVJ5L5a7YDqEcUxxQ: The malleus, incus and stapes - hammer, anvil and stirrup - lie in the air-filled middle ear, transmitting the eardrum's movement to the oval window and amplifying it enough to drive the fluid of the inner ear. nNpvk2SX8SsBHAi0YXIW: Two effects cool the air in the carburettor: the pressure drop through the venturi as the air expands, and the latent heat absorbed as the fuel evaporates into it. nOIccNFkDYVYYHrp0q2h: VMCG is defined using PRIMARY AERODYNAMIC CONTROL only - essentially the rudder. nOTHi5mgZk53HtQfO3wC: An ageing anticyclone is maintained by slow, widespread subsidence. nOW6WIseYtkXyN8WYz5H: Viscous hydroplaning needs only a thin film of water, but it needs a SMOOTH, contaminated surface - typically a touchdown zone polished by rubber deposits - where the film cannot escape through the surface texture. nPIgrAT7d0oB0uNn68yk: On a 3 degree glide path the height is about 300 ft per NM, so at 4.6 NM the path is about 1380 ft above the threshold elevation. nPRSulFMoPiuUBV6RpT2: Lift means higher pressure beneath the wing than above it, and at the wing TIP - where the two regions meet around the end of the wing - air simply flows from high to low pressure: from BENEATH the wing, around the tip, to the upper surface. nPyZBrph4myXmgqjUu0m: Five degrees of longitude at 60N is 300 x cos60 = 150 NM = 277 800 m = 27 780 000 cm. Scale = 8 / 27 780 000, which is about 1 : 3 500 000. Omitting the cosine of latitude would double the earth distance and give 1 : 7 000 000, which is exactly the trap.
nQTZ2h7Pp0ZpbPZ5paID: A system is error tolerant when an error made within it does not produce a serious safety consequence - because it is trapped, contained, reversible or simply survivable. nQZMyXoFAc5RJVivg2r3: ICAO Doc 4444 specifies a tolerance of plus or minus 300 ft for Mode C level verification. This means the displayed altitude must be within 300 ft of the assigned level to be considered accurate.
nQsDzDESgUyuz9geLOzz: Carbon monoxide binds to the same site on haemoglobin as oxygen but with over 200 times the affinity, so it occupies carrying capacity and will not release it. nQuTlH7aJ9JiIvCvzRJf: In the beta range the pilot sets blade angle directly, and on the landing roll that angle is taken through flat pitch into reverse, so the propeller pushes air forward and produces thrust acting rearwards. nR1oEniw73QP87zGqEHc: Interrupting the power destroys the alignment, and full alignment can only be done on the ground with the aircraft stationary, so navigation cannot be recovered in flight. nRR68f6c9oJp70sbsic4: The value of a briefing lies in what is specific to this flight: what about today's weather, aircraft, route or crew will need particular coordination, and how the crew will handle it. Restating the obvious adds nothing, and delegating everything abandons command.
nSfZIy3287zFKY0hFhmN: The creeps are the skin form of decompression sickness: nitrogen bubbles under the skin produce itching, a crawling sensation and a mottled rash. The bends are joint pain, the chokes are chest pain and cough, and the leans is an unrelated vestibular illusion.
nSrMcJbrAjagBS1uqKuD: Per ICAO Annex 2 Appendix 1: the interceptor's signal for 'You may proceed' is an abrupt breakaway consisting of a climbing turn of 90 degrees or more without crossing the intercepted aircraft's flight path.
nT6nK6sYoWDyDenL72R1: The longitudes 008 08.4E and 171 51.6W add to exactly 180 degrees, so the two positions lie on opposite meridians of the SAME great circle and the shortest route runs over the North Pole. nTQR89AOqHgIwTb8jF6R: In Class E, the 250 kt IAS speed limit applies to both IFR and VFR flights below FL 100 (10,000 ft). Above FL 100, no specific Class E speed limit applies.
nTdofo2B96q1RcH7YERU: A technical landing (refuelling, maintenance, crew change without commercial traffic) is the Second Freedom of the Air. The First Freedom is overfly without landing, Third is disembarking passengers from home state.
nUGWKyanR3gHKSpXkf0n: Chronic stress is not fixed by a pill or by one intervention: it responds to a whole-person approach - sleep, exercise, diet, workload and duty management, relaxation techniques and dealing with the underlying stressors. nUcO3rOYVEsMQn950aC7: The cocktail party effect - hearing one's own name or callsign break through from a conversation not being listened to - is a demonstration of how selective attention works: unattended channels are still processed at a low level, and personally relevant material captures attention. It is an attention mechanism rather than a communication technique.
nUvBRGXzJVIBaksNcD8k: Moving the CG aft shortens the arm between the CG and the tailplane, so the restoring moment for a given disturbance shrinks - static longitudinal stability DECREASES. nXbqqVltNTVXRc633slw: On a polar stereographic chart the convergence between the local meridian and the grid datum meridian is the full change of longitude - here 130 degrees between the Greenwich meridian and 130E. nXsRv2m2zcKu03deYxMq: A minimum time track is the route chosen from the day's wind field so that the time flown is least - it is generally neither a great circle nor a rhumb line, and it is rebuilt for each flight from the isochrones. 'Spherical capable flight segment' is not a defined term.
nZdirvU0NOkJuD2EhrZO: The damper responds to yaw RATE, so it acts whenever that rate is changing - which is what an oscillation such as Dutch roll consists of. A steady yaw rate is a normal turn and is deliberately not opposed, or the damper would fight every turn the pilot made.
nZu2cVBXY5bbq20TW9GB: The slipstream is the corkscrewing column of air the propeller throws back, and its swirl matters most when the propeller is working hardest and the aeroplane is moving slowest - high power and low speed, as on take-off. na5dLyGf42MH4DHI88Qx: In lateral navigation the FMS does the navigating and hands the autopilot a roll or heading command, which the autopilot flies. The radio receivers feed the FMS's position solution but do not drive the autopilot directly in this mode.
naMvb0f5X84VDSoUfCoA: Both are correct. The circulation carries oxygen to the cells and carbon dioxide away (1), and it also carries hormones - chemical messengers released by one organ to act on another (2), which is how the adrenaline of the stress response reaches the whole body within seconds.
naQGdhCboFLlwtA3vrtw: On a Lambert the true direction of a straight line changes by the chart convergence, dlong x n. The course changes from 080 to 092, i.e. 12 degrees, so dlong = 12 / 0.80 = 15 degrees. The course is easterly, so B is 15 degrees east of 004W, i.e. 011E.
nbIem15GW53jR7dIqD8m: Once the engine is running the flame is self-sustaining and the igniters are not needed, so they are used for starting and for relighting after a flame-out. nbzEbY2o3DqV6AmLYpm3: Descending below the tropopause the temperature rises, so the local speed of sound increases. At a constant Mach number the true airspeed is that speed of sound multiplied by the Mach number, so TAS increases as well.
ncRQvg3yel57Uet38iZp: The intake adds no energy to the air, it only slows it, so the total temperature is unchanged through it. What the deceleration does is convert velocity into static pressure and static temperature, both of which rise.
ncSrfbqvxaxWPbcAhgeJ: The low pressure switch is set just below the normal regulated pressure, so the caption comes on as soon as the pump can no longer maintain the system - from a pump failure, a drive failure or a major leak. Reservoir quantity and accumulator charge are monitored separately.
ncgCfFt3whbXpWMHpF3R: A self-centred captain stops using the other pilot, and the other pilot responds by withdrawing - contributing less, responding more slowly, or becoming resentful. nck64d7pnpxYufOuQuUN: Each of the coloured navigation lights - green to starboard, red to port - covers 110 degrees, from dead ahead to 20 degrees behind the beam on its own side. The white tail light covers the remaining 140 degrees.
ncshIuuI01zlwj7K0T8o: The vent keeps the tank at or near ambient pressure, so that the heat of the oil and the crankcase blow-by gases cannot pressurise it and force oil out through the seals. It also lets the tank breathe as the level changes.
ncuv3cEJt1R3F2ZTXvuE: With the speedbrakes already deployed, both spoiler panels are part-raised. The net differential is what produces the rolling moment.
nd5E0bxaW5F7YGKUyVGU: A straight wing stalls from the ROOT outward, and losing the inboard lift - which lies ahead of the wing's overall centre of lift - moves the centre of pressure aft, producing a natural nose-DOWN pitching moment that begins the recovery. ndGVXLaVoLFSS6NMnyyg: Bending is carried as tension in one surface and compression in the other, so both skins share it with the spar booms - which is exactly what stressed skin construction means. The root fairing is aerodynamic and carries no primary load.
neTchOHAfouJWhTqe852: Work inwards from the track. True heading = true track minus right drift = 245 - 5 = 240. Magnetic heading = true heading minus east variation = 240 - 3 = 237. Deviation = magnetic heading minus compass heading = 237 - 242 = -5, and a negative result means WEST, so 5W.
nfFglUn1AkXqiRu2xExq: Selecting flaps is a highly practised action carried out at a moment judged from the developing picture, so for an experienced pilot it runs largely automatically at the skill-based level. ngOOfMarPQWj51VJ17eg: A shuttle valve is a free piston between two inlets and one outlet: whichever supply has the higher pressure pushes the shuttle across and feeds the unit, isolating the other. ngtO41Gww1ntXQl2UVcb: Each inertial system navigates entirely on its own accelerometers and gyros, so each accumulates its own independent error and drifts at its own rate. nhcq2WqTtVt1dXTvFQdu: Stable, stratiform cloud has small droplets (roughly 0.002-0.03 mm), and icing is most likely between 0 C and -15 C, becoming rare below about -18 C because most of the water is already frozen. nhuMZqxaL4TjOkqypDjS: The trim switch is split into two halves that must both be operated together, so that a single short circuit or a jammed contact cannot drive the trim. A stabiliser runaway is one of the most dangerous failures possible, and this is the cheapest defence against it.

Direction is the essential distinction.
niNbOa9WGzxoKQMpFYVt: The local speed of sound depends only on temperature: LSS = 38.94 x root(258) = about 626 kt. Mach = TAS / LSS = 250 / 626 = 0.40. The flight level itself does not enter the calculation except through the temperature that goes with it.
nivcjVU1J4RRggC7sc8A: Bonding the aircraft to the ground equipment before any cap is removed ensures there is no potential difference to arc across when fuel starts flowing and generating static. Once the connection is made and the caps are off, everything is at the same potential.
nkU7OsiMrW2bzvjCrBRJ: Stringers run lengthwise and share with the skin the tension and compression produced by fuselage bending, at the same time stabilising the skin against buckling. Shear is carried by the skin, and the frames give the section its shape.
nmNWbDxxC2mEzXEJmyJw: A single loop system decides there is a fire when current flows between the sensing element and earth, and an accidental short to the airframe does exactly that. nmq0pE2At6AzjT3Q7gLu: 123.45 MHz is the designated inter-pilot air-to-air frequency in oceanic airspace, used to pass position reports through another aircraft and to coordinate contingency manoeuvres when HF fails. 121.5 MHz remains the emergency frequency and is monitored throughout.
nn1uTcxQjZ8zJ5WrhS8R: ICAO Annex 17: a State shall take adequate measures for the safety of passengers and crew of an aircraft subjected to unlawful interference until their journey can be continued.
nnRxBkhQvmoam9bskYu9: Jet A freezes at about -40°C, Jet A-1 at about -47°C and Jet B at about -50°C, so in decreasing order of freezing point they run Jet A, Jet A-1, Jet B. It is why Jet A-1 is the international fuel and Jet A is largely confined to domestic use in the United States.
noAb2YR6LJuUDnk8BF1s: Halon interrupts the chemical chain reaction, so it works on solids, flammable liquids and gases, and is safe on live electrical equipment because it does not conduct. Burning metals are the exception: they sustain their own oxidation and need a class D agent.
noCHCVAE9TUjwo1Tl5B1: A 3° slope is a gradient of about 5%, so the rate of descent is roughly five times the speed in knots: 5 x 100 = 500 ft/min. The rule of thumb - half the groundspeed with a zero added - gives the same figure and is what is used on every ILS.
nowv8h1WZ4Wd05hB7RgG: Wake turbulence is the tip-vortex system, a purely aerodynamic by-product of lift. Propeller slipstream and jet efflux produce blast, a different and much shorter-lived hazard, and the size of the gear and flaps changes the vortex pattern without generating it.
npXdlF0N4qsN0EJR0BkJ: In a pure impulse stage the whole pressure drop takes place in the nozzle guide vanes, which convert it into a high velocity jet. nr09MXXl3jOpCrpRT4xV: Freezing rain is defined by rain arriving as SUPERCOOLED liquid, which happens when liquid rain descends into a layer whose temperature is below 0 C, becomes supercooled, and freezes on impact. The classic setting is a warm layer aloft over a cold surface layer ahead of a winter warm front.
nr2M1W6MIGYINvXxIVYB: Conditioning means bringing the air to the temperature and pressure the occupants need - the packs cool it, the trim air sets the temperature and the outflow valve sets the pressure. Its composition is not altered, beyond the removal of condensed water.
nrprz6esQyxEVGJ2VwfJ: A constant-speed unit senses rpm and adjusts blade angle to hold the selected value. ns0O5PyuuNAhOCFwaQkJ: Work the descent backwards. The height to lose is 37 000 - 8000 = 29 000 ft, which at 1800 ft/min takes 16.1 minutes and covers 232 x 16.1/60 = about 62 NM. That leaves 185 - 62 = 123 NM of cruise, taking 23 minutes at 320 kt, so descent must begin at 0422 + 23 = 0445.
ns2f4S0lgef7iuX1x4jE: Pressurisation works by keeping the cabin altitude low enough that the alveolar oxygen partial pressure holds arterial saturation above about 90% - which is what a cabin altitude of 6,000-8,000 ft achieves. nsfQlDgqiZL7fNzgDDct: Above 13 000 ft cabin pressure altitude, 100% of the passengers must be supplied for the entire flight time - no percentage, no grace period. Between 10 000 and 13 000 ft only 10% need be supplied, and then only after the first 30 minutes.
nsl3lCjqgV6HdKh6xjVN: The engine burns a MASS of fuel per hour, not a volume: 220 l/h at 0.80 is 176 kg/h. If the density falls to 0.75, that same 176 kg/h occupies 176 / 0.75 = about 235 litres. nsx6siZf2hzfaZgIyaH5: Apparent drift is 15° per hour times the sine of the latitude: 15 x sin 60° = 13°/h, and in the northern hemisphere the apparent movement is to the right. The latitude nut is set to cancel it for the latitude being flown.
ntEbkUiabqtsQ6IsilIs: The modes cover excessive descent rate (1), excessive terrain closure (2), altitude loss after take-off (5), an unsafe configuration near the ground (6) and descent below the glideslope (7). ntn4lOa2x10EDlOTRDwU: Climbing at a constant IAS, the falling temperature reduces the local speed of sound while the falling density raises the TAS for that IAS - both effects drive the Mach number up continuously. MMO is therefore the limit that will be reached. This is why climb schedules are flown at constant IAS only up to a crossover altitude, then at constant Mach.
nuLhZh7PhbUa4xbd272l: First-aid oxygen is undiluted oxygen given to a passenger who, for physiological reasons, needs it after a decompression - treatment once the aeroplane is at a safe level. Supplemental oxygen protects everyone during the descent, and protective breathing equipment protects the crew from smoke and fumes.
nuRrrDvrmCdbf58f13pR: A non-return or check valve passes flow one way and blocks it the other, exactly as a diode does with current. It is used to stop fluid returning towards a failed pump or leaking back out of a pressurised part of the system.
nuWhuOJnOcdw38aJjLmj: A preventive advisory tells the crew what NOT to do - it restricts the vertical speed band, typically 'monitor vertical speed', without asking for any change to the flight path. The current rate is already safe; the system is simply preventing it from being made unsafe.
nudzEjoG8stknsYjWIGo: Checklists matter most where memory and habit are least reliable: on an unfamiliar type, where the stored routine either does not exist or belongs to a different aeroplane, and under mental pressure, which is exactly when items are skipped and negative habit transfer occurs. Familiarity and recency are when the checklist is most often skimped.
nuwjcdHD7RplGRM6Raje: With the pitot blocked the total pressure is trapped while the static pressure keeps changing, so the difference the instrument sees varies purely with altitude: the airspeed indication rises in a climb and falls in a descent, exactly like an altimeter.
nwFTheIUfH3jfaUyXB3Z: For a 3 degree glide path the rate of descent in feet per minute is about five times the groundspeed in knots: 90 x 5 = 450 ft/min. Always use groundspeed, not TAS, since it is the ground distance that sets how quickly the path descends beneath you.
nwHfzR6cxZtccXpctbUm: The layer's temperature falls 2 C in 100 m, an environmental lapse rate of 2 C per 100 m. That exceeds even the dry adiabatic rate of 1 C per 100 m, so a displaced parcel - saturated or not - always ends up warmer and less dense than its surroundings and keeps accelerating upward. The layer is therefore ABSOLUTELY unstable. Conditional instability would require the ELR to lie between the saturated and dry rates, i.e. below 1 C per 100 m.
nwb06maeQ2b4NIv2okcF: A parallel of latitude cuts every meridian at 90 degrees, a constant angle, so it is a rhumb line. It is not a great circle (except the equator), and following it does not mean a constant heading, because drift means heading and track are only equal in still air.
nwb5vv3MGVRLmHwhHw6s: Every smoke and fumes drill starts the same way: oxygen mask on and set to 100%, smoke goggles on, crew communication established. Only then does the crew begin isolating systems to find the source - fumes can incapacitate a crew during the time it takes to diagnose them.
nwhAimMbjuliCjsFRPfb: If the skin is not stressed it can carry nothing, so the whole bending moment goes into the spars - their booms taking it as tension in one and compression in the other. The ribs then shape the aerofoil and transfer the air load into the spars.
nwyNfwjoobAPHzigLSKc: NAT MNPS airspace runs from 27N to the North Pole, between FL285 and FL420. The southern boundary at 27N takes in the whole organised track structure together with the routes to the Azores and the Canaries.
nxAIm3g5BgE8ESXswL7g: The accumulator stores energy: gas is compressed as fluid is forced in, and that energy comes back to smooth surges, to supplement the pump on a heavy demand and to work the brakes after the pumps have failed. Storing fluid is the reservoir's job.
nxVkMZitzru63lBsRBWD: The apparent solar day is the interval between two successive transits of the REAL (apparent) sun across the same meridian, and it varies through the year because the earth's orbit is elliptical and its axis tilted. The mean solar day, defined by the fictitious mean sun, is the constant one and is what clocks keep.
nygCqf4vZTzIKlHk30Ec: The autothrottle holds a speed - IAS (1) or Mach (2) - or a thrust, expressed as N1 or EPR (4). Angle of attack and flight path are controlled with the elevator by the autopilot, not with the thrust levers.
nynwtDhXOM0RB8YEiNNL: A thunderstorm requires three ingredients together: sufficient moisture, an unstable lapse rate so a saturated parcel keeps accelerating upward through a deep layer, and a trigger to lift the air to its condensation level. Stability is fatal to convection - it damps the vertical motion - and surface pressure is not a requirement at all; airmass thunderstorms form quite happily within a high.
nzBkH1n2PinvDO3OXiqj: Note the current PANS-OPS figure: no noise abatement procedure - including the power reduction - may be initiated below 800 ft above aerodrome elevation, because below that height an engine failure is at its most critical and take-off thrust must not be traded for noise relief. nzqM1Z505Pza6lAP52jL: The yaw damper exists to suppress Dutch roll and damp oscillatory yaw; it has no sideslip target and does not know the turn is unbalanced. Keeping the ball centred remains the pilot's job, or that of a separate turn coordination function.
nzxKl2fJF6pO79PFaeZm: Hyperventilation blurs vision through the alkalosis and cerebral vasoconstriction it produces (1), hypoxia degrades acuity and narrows the field because the retina is highly oxygen-dependent (2), and fatigue impairs accommodation so that instruments become hard to focus on (4). Hypertension does not produce acute visual disturbance in the same way.
o0jQ3FcT7ZflTTNkQYef: The compensation is set for 30°S, so it applies 7.5°/h in the wrong sense for the northern hemisphere; the real earth rate at 60°N is 15 sin 60° = 13°/h to the right, giving 20.5°/h right in total. o0mxFKmIeJYbpi549Dyg: The body clock shifts only slowly - about one to one and a half hours a day - so a six-hour time change takes the better part of a week to complete. o20hkwhLxjEpJO0EPDHV: Air is fed to the cabin at an essentially fixed rate, so the pressure inside is set entirely by how much is allowed to escape - the outflow valve modulating the discharge. Engine speed changes the supply available but is not the controlling element.
o2CX4oaE3vmWYmfwClXB: The wind from 350 is on the port bow of the 100 heading, so it pushes the aircraft right and adds a little speed along track. Resolving the vectors gives a track of about 109 and a groundspeed of about 182 kt, i.e. about 9 degrees of starboard drift.

o30p9KtrsKJ7HhiDDTic: ICAO Annex 17: States should introduce specific security measures for three categories of potentially disruptive passengers: deportees, inadmissible persons, and persons in lawful custody.
o3J40xxzqyQ4k0YqTyLE: All four bear on the choice. o3lUZM3uugbyJV1ww1mW: A series of red flashes from the tower to an aircraft on the ground means 'taxi clear of the landing area in use.' The aircraft must vacate the active landing area.
o405MzzDJHxCywYF9j8M: Before flight the crew uses the CDU to type in what the aircraft cannot know for itself: present position and alignment data for the IRSs, then the route, cruise level, cost index and the mass and centre of gravity for the FMC. o4r5SJKdYWlNQVGX41mv: On a polar stereographic the parallels are concentric circles round the pole, and a rhumb line, which cuts every meridian at the same angle, spirals in towards the pole. It therefore appears as a curve CONCAVE to the pole. Only the meridians themselves are straight.
o5bz75C93rRHeYxo2alO: Flying into a tailwind gust means the aeroplane's airspeed momentarily FALLS - its inertia keeps its groundspeed while the air mass now moves with it. Less airspeed means less lift, so the aeroplane sinks until it accelerates back to its trimmed speed.
o62ZylVfc285BwMG1cjq: ICAO Doc 8168: the obstacle clearance at the departure end of runway (DER) equals 0 ft. Obstacle clearance increases after the DER at the specified climb gradient (typically 3.3%).
o6Nk53AvYX9bYZ6fvIQK: Category IIIA requires an RVR of not less than 200 m, with a decision height below 100 ft or none at all. Category IIIB goes to 75 m, and 300 m belongs to Category II.
o7fPs0FQg9YtkL59hVt9: Pulling out of a dive raises the load factor, and stall speed increases with the SQUARE ROOT of n - so the wing can stall at a speed far above its 1g value. The other options all reduce the stall speed: retracting spoilers restores lift, and less weight needs less lift.
o7g8aqJ11SKKXgbNMNyc: Airborne fuel is block minus taxi = 136 - 9 = 127 kg, made up of trip fuel plus a reserve of 30 percent of it, so trip = 127 / 1.3 = about 98 kg and the fuel flow is 98 / 2.7 = about 36 kg/h. o8Q7meTCE7MTOWAEYCAB: Category IIIB is a decision height below 50 ft, or none, with an RVR below 200 m but not less than 75 m. Below that only Category IIIC remains, which has no RVR limitation at all and requires the taxi route to be usable in the same conditions.
o9gZHwYM9LEs1szvw2th: Emergency extension uses whatever needs no hydraulic power: a nitrogen bottle blowing the gear down (2), a separate auxiliary hydraulic supply (4), or simple free fall under gravity with the uplocks released mechanically (5). oAVPxQbz4aGpZGwinBJi: An axial piston pump can be destroked, so it delivers only what the system is drawing and consumes engine power in proportion. That variable delivery at constant high pressure is why it has displaced the fixed displacement pump and its cut-out valve.
oAW7ogOgAY2xxScmdYlc: The needle shows the direction of turn, so a needle to the left means the aeroplane is turning left. oBYT3EGJ6LZ6i6CCVUHR: Hypoxia is a shortage of oxygen relative to what the tissues need, and because the brain has almost no reserve the effects are mental before they are physical: impaired thinking, poor judgement, slowed reactions and loss of coordination, with euphoria masking all of it. Heart rate rises rather than falls as the body tries to compensate.
oC2uH4OMLMfsCQhrihI7: At or above the transition level with the altimeter set to 1013.2 hPa (standard pressure), vertical position is reported as a Flight Level. Below the transition altitude, altitude on QNH is used.
oCcF8OSSrxRUy5bxexTf: Material held in short-term memory decays within roughly 10-20 seconds unless it is actively rehearsed or deliberately transferred to long-term memory. That is why a clearance not written down or read back is simply gone, and why an interruption during a checklist destroys the item being held.
oClSCOcE0ajSge4GKjtW: Detectability is what the system provides for catching a problem: the automatic monitoring, detection and warning facilities (2), the alerting capability of the man-machine interface that actually gets the crew's attention (4), and the tolerance of the systems, which determines how long there is to detect the problem before it matters (1). oDJrkm3369GjEyuVcEMs: Headwind = wind speed x cosine of the angle between the wind and the runway. The angle is 083 - 035 = 48 degrees, so the headwind is 35 x cos48 = 35 x 0.67 = about 24 kt. oDdTNGt2pGbTgBvsKXsY: Take the pressure error first. oF6TNKvwadGCuwhpMWHM: Large jets have abundant hot air available from the engine compressors, so the wing leading edges are anti-iced thermally, with bleed air ducted through piccolo tubes inside them. oFCgeouQOe8hqLWfMPmf: B is north and west of A, so the track lies in the north-west quadrant, and an angle of 35 degrees with the meridian gives a true course of 360 - 35 = 325. oFjLBdMxrtwpxd0W8L9I: Work outwards. Magnetic heading = compass heading plus deviation = 270 - 2W = 268. The 30E variation is a distractor, because QDM and QDR are both magnetic.
oFwuLpGgZD2IV3XpA5vy: Vortices sink below the generating aircraft's path and then drift downwind, so a wind from the right carries them to the LEFT. Staying to the right - upwind - and above the preceding aircraft's path avoids both the sink and the drift.
oIjbxINbmgGoX5lhie7C: A high aspect ratio wing has a smaller proportion of its span influenced by the tip vortices, so downwash and INDUCED DRAG are reduced - the primary benefit. It also stalls at a LOWER angle of attack: a low aspect ratio wing is strongly influenced by tip effects that keep some flow attached to much higher angles, which is why delta-winged aircraft can be held at very high alpha.
oItY2sgpzMB1Y3mTDE2k: Lift bends the wing upwards, so the upper boom of the spar is shortened and goes into compression while the lower boom is stretched into tension. It reverses on the ground and under negative g, which is why both booms must be designed for both cases.
oJNPaGBFuNTLeYYoIbCV: The GPWS warns of unsafe terrain clearance when the aeroplane is not configured for landing (2) and, in its later versions, of windshear (4). Climb rate is not monitored, and the descent path angle in isolation is not one of its modes.
oJtay41il94vGeXPD6KK: Above the friction layer the wind blows parallel to the isobars and there is no net inflow. Near the surface, friction slows the air, weakening the Coriolis force so that the unchanged pressure gradient force turns the flow inward across the isobars. That cross-isobaric component is what produces convergence at the centre of the low, and hence the ascent that gives its cloud and rain. Without friction there would be no low-level convergence.
oKCdBtG56AsrPIh6YWsw: The altitude alerting system does two things: it warns as the aeroplane approaches the selected altitude, and it warns again if it subsequently deviates from it. Excessive vertical speed and ground proximity are GPWS functions, belonging to a different system entirely.
oKFsgQJCJFjxTGvKkRBm: As a cell discharges its internal resistance rises and its terminal voltage sags as soon as any current is drawn, even though it may read almost normally off load. That is why a battery is capacity tested under load and not judged by an open circuit voltage.
oKX27IUePmzfvUvbMICe: A hot wheel fails along the AXLE line: a fuse plug releasing or a tyre bursting throws its energy sideways. The landing gear is therefore approached from the front or the rear, never from abeam - inboard and outboard are both in the danger arc.
oLX4EyZZ50EtifsOSQab: In a gas turbine all four processes happen at the same time in different parts of the engine, so the cycle is continuous rather than intermittent. oLgGElwyO4heohks4q3o: A directional gyro must hold its axis fixed in space while the aircraft manoeuvres, which needs two degrees of freedom, and that axis has to be kept horizontal by an erection system so that heading is read about the vertical. oM86CitYwUIv1OvlKY2B: Generators are paralleled so that their outputs add at the same voltage, giving more current and therefore more power for the busbar. Connecting them in series would raise the voltage above what the equipment is designed for.
oMW4V2U6pyG20entB0yM: Total temperature is the static temperature multiplied by (1 + 0.2 M²), so recovering the static temperature means dividing by that factor. It is the relationship the air data computer uses to strip the ram rise out of the measured temperature.
oMc2hetJi8YGOQE5Uq8I: Fibres in a resin describes a composite, not a sandwich - a sandwich is two facing skins bonded to a light core, so the first statement is wrong. The second is right: the core crushes under a concentrated load, so fittings need a local insert or a solid doubler.
oMnM9WDeMqhY2AOWpk6y: The two systems are separate and serve different people: a gaseous system with diluter demand regulators for the flight deck, which the crew may need for hours, and chemical generators or a separate low pressure supply for the cabin, which need only cover the descent. Keeping them independent means a failure in one cannot deprive the other.
oN4rlQomGfwhMCIeLOTh: The basic or inner loop does what the pilot's hands do: it stabilises and controls the aeroplane's rotation about its centre of gravity in pitch, roll and yaw. Taking it somewhere - a level, a heading or a beam - is the outer loop's job and works by commanding this one.
oO81563izEFicDI3utrL: Pressure falls exponentially, so the same 5,000 ft costs far more pressure low down than high up: roughly 170 hPa between sea level and 5,000 ft, but only a few hPa between 45,000 and 50,000 ft. oP9B1DI5leZmyN4cX3xk: Detonation is caused by too much pressure and temperature in the cylinder, so the remedy is to reduce the manifold pressure and enrich the mixture, the extra fuel evaporating and cooling the charge directly. Leaning further or raising the boost would destroy the engine.
oPqwjDzDtUSmYnFKZCfS: Turning the cockpit lighting up reduces the contrast between the flash and the ambient level, so the eyes are less dazzled by lightning and recover faster. Dark adaptation is sacrificed deliberately, on the grounds that being blinded at the wrong moment in a thunderstorm is the greater risk.
oQUUol8z0LqaEkYzuLoR: The air cycle machine's purpose is refrigeration: bleed air is compressed, cooled in a heat exchanger and then expanded through a turbine, where doing work against the compressor takes a large amount of heat out of it. The pressure drop is the means, not the object.
oQjjs1XaMAITZSmgXqx1: Isogonals join places of equal magnetic variation. Isoclinals join places of equal dip, isogrives join places of equal grivation (grid north to magnetic north), and isotachs are lines of equal wind speed on a met chart.
oQp8vHDtJZyPl6KGUqYo: A bird hazard is reported to the local ATS unit IMMEDIATELY, because the next arrival or departure faces the same flock within minutes and ATS can pass a warning and call out bird control. The written report comes afterwards and does not replace the call.
oQwHt1r1bImHlUjgOfgk: ICAO Doc 4444: a departing aircraft can be radar-identified when its position indication is observed within 1 NM (2 km) of the departure runway end using PSR or SSR.
oR6WczZs6KutU9NAazDB: The angle between the great circle and the rhumb line at either end is the conversion angle, which is half the convergency. oS14s6ucYqbeKYHp5EU2: The crank assembly is the group that turns gas pressure into rotation: the crankshaft, the connecting rods and the pistons. The crankcase houses it and the valve gear is a separate assembly driven from it.
oSTf3l1is3M4Cm6qEAxO: The normal start-up sequence is IDENT, to confirm the model and that the navigation database is the current AIRAC cycle, then POS INIT, to give the IRSs their starting position, then RTE to enter the route. DEPARTURE and PERF INIT follow once a route exists to attach them to.
oSocSA1JwnOm5Bl7tUtT: True altitude needed is 10 600 + 1500 = 12 100 ft. oSrSAMq3TVIXFsQNUZPu: In Class G above 10,000 ft MSL, VMC minima are 8 km visibility, 1500 m horizontal, 1000 ft vertical from clouds. These are the same as for all airspace classes above 10,000 ft.
oTZgiyQffgnqcya953Xl: The wind from 205 is on the port quarter of the 316 track, giving about 14 kt of crosswind and about 5 kt of tailwind. The drift correction is therefore about 4 degrees into wind, so the heading is about 312, and the groundspeed is about 232 kt.
oTah5TdfdIKPgWSKRpXb: On a polar stereographic the projection plane touches at the pole, so the scale is correct there and expands with distance from it, as the secant squared of half the co-latitude.
